At a matched offloading rate, giving the router session history improves task pass rate over the same router without history, with gains for every model pair; history-aware routing remains within one point of always using the expensive model. We also found that cost depends on execution dynamics rather than token prices alone: the cheaper model's per-task cost advantage narrows from 6.8x to 3.2x on longer sessions. A closed form cache analysis further shows that downward switches (expensive to cheap) recover their cache cost within two LLM calls, whereas upward switches do not break even under the evaluated conditions. Together, these results show that agent routing is a sequential decision problem: effective policies must account for what happened earlier in the session and for the asymmetric cost of switching models.

title: Qwenfant: Train Big Character-level BabyLMs on Concise Parallel Text
summary: This work concerns our submission for the Multilingual track of the 2026 BabyLM Challenge. We improve on our baseline using data that has been summarized and translated by an LLM, showing that higher-quality data can come from synthetic sources. We further improve with 2 simple changes: using a larger model, and using a character-level vocabulary. Both of these changes require LoRA-style fine-tuning for realizing their full potential. We dub our final Qwen3-based model Qwenfant, which, at the time of submission, ranks 1st in the Multilingual track.

title: Learning Keypoint Constraints from Visual Demonstrations for Safe Motion Planning
summary: We present Keypoint Constraint Learning (KCL), a framework for learning task-relevant motion constraints from visual demonstrations and for planning safely with the extracted constraints. To make constraint learning tractable from RGB-D observations, we represent demonstrations using sparse 3D object-centric keypoints and semantic mask centroids extracted through segmentation, visual feature clustering, and point tracking. In this reduced geometric space, we learn keypoint dynamics and infer distance- and orientation-based constraints that make the expert trajectories feasible and approximately locally optimal by enforcing KKT optimality conditions in the reduced state space. We then plan with the learned constraints under uncertainty, using robustness margins derived from accumulated prediction error, and provide a theoretical analysis of how keypoint perception error and learned dynamics error affect the recovered constraints. We evaluate KCL on visual demonstrations from navigation to rigid/deformable manipulation, showing that it recovers multi-stage geometric constraints and outperforms baselines in downstream safe planning.

title: Variationally correct loss functions for nonlinear parametric problems and their neural approximations
summary: We construct computable a posteriori error estimators for parametric families of nonlinear elliptic problems by measuring the residual of a variational formulation in the dual norm of a closed subspace of the test space. A single abstract theorem shows that the resulting estimator is bounded above and below by the error in the trial norm, i.e., it is a variationally correct loss function. Two instances are covered. The first considers an $L_2$-like test space, yielding a nonlinear first-order system least-squares loss function that certifies arbitrary, possibly meshless, approximations. The second breaks the test space, yielding a nonlinear discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin loss function computed by element-local problems. All assumptions are verified for quasilinear diffusion, including monotone fluxes and semilinear problems, and a nonlocal Kirchhoff model. Numerical studies train neural networks approximating the parameter-to-solution maps with the latter loss and measure the ratio of loss to squared error.

title: Verifier-Grounded Agentic RL for Provably Correct Code
summary: Reinforcement learning for code usually rewards passing tests, which a model can do while remaining wrong on the inputs the tests do not cover. A program verifier instead decides whether a program satisfies a formal specification for all inputs. Language models are almost always paired with verifiers at inference time only, and turning a verifier into a reward raises two difficulties. It reports only acceptance or rejection, which gives no gradient when every attempt fails, and a policy can cheat it, most simply by telling it to assume what the proof was supposed to establish. We build an agentic environment and reward that address both. The reward reads the verifier's diagnostics rather than its verdict, scoring a candidate by the weighted fraction of proof obligations it discharges, extended with hidden probes from a reference proof's annotations. An integrity audit outranks the verifier, rejecting any candidate that alters the specification or assumes what it was meant to prove. The model works as an agent against a live verifier over many turns, with a separately trained proof specialist as a frozen collaborator. Across Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 14B and a 35B Qwen3.6 mixture-of-experts model, held-out verification on code generation rises from 66.1% to 93.5% on DafnyBench and from 56.3% to 100% on SWE-Proof. This reward leads every other training signal we compare, including a binary pass-or-fail reward trained under otherwise identical settings, with the widest margin on code generation. When the agent must also deliver the repository patch, graded by each project's withheld tests, the fraction of held-out issues it resolves rises from 59.6% to 72.5%. Evaluated unchanged on three verification suites withheld from training, the checkpoints improve on all of them, including one whose language and verifier are absent from training.

title: The Capacity of the Noisy Torn Paper Channel and the Noisy Shuffling Channel
summary: The torn paper channel breaks a codeword into fragments and returns all fragments without their original order. The noisy torn paper channel additionally introduces bit substitution errors to each fragment. Recovering the message therefore requires accounting for both bit errors and uncertainty about the fragment order. We establish a capacity upper bound for the noisy torn paper channel that matches the achievable rate of Ravi, Vahid, and Shomorony and resolves their conjecture. Our results also determine the capacity of the noisy shuffling channel of Shomorony and Heckel, in which all fragments have the same length, and resolve their open question.

title: Beyond ICD Codes: Semantic IDs for Generative Medical Coding
summary: Generative approaches to automatic International Classification of Diseases (ICD) coding use large language models (LLMs) to predict ICD codes from clinical documents. However, original ICD code strings are not ideal generation targets because the ICD hierarchy does not always reflect clinical relationships, and LLMs struggle to interpret and generate these codes. We introduce SemICD, a framework that trains LLMs to generate Semantic IDs (SIDs) instead. SemICD constructs SIDs by hierarchically clustering embeddings of textual code profiles, allowing semantically related codes to share prefixes while each complete SID uniquely identifies one ICD code. To align the SID tokens with clinical semantics, we employ two auxiliary tasks for bidirectional generation between textual code profiles and SIDs. Experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV with four LLMs show that SemICD outperforms direct code generation, improving Micro-F1 by 1.34-8.00 points. Our code is available at https://github.com/youwillbethebest/SemICD.

title: DTDD: Divergence-Triggered Dynamic Distillation for Reliable On-Policy Supervision
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level supervision on student rollouts, but this supervision can become unreliable when the student and teacher diverge, either because of a large initial policy gap or compounding errors in long-horizon reasoning and tool use. We introduce Divergence-Triggered Dynamic Distillation (DTDD), an adaptive OPD framework that uses segment-level student-teacher divergence to trigger teacher takeover during training. When divergence triggers an intervention during reasoning, the student prefix continues to receive standard OPD supervision. The teacher then generates a recovery suffix, which the student learns through behavior cloning, using cross-entropy on the teacher-generated tokens. We evaluate DTDD in three regimes: long-horizon reasoning, distillation from a base initialization without offline supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and multi-turn agents. We also compare alternative trigger designs and teacher-intervention rates. DTDD reduces the post-warmup peak gradient norm by $8.6\times$ and, from a base initialization, reaches $21.3\%$ held-out math accuracy in $2.6\times$ fewer optimizer updates than OPD; both methods finish near $22\%$. It improves best-observed performance by $4.8$ and $4.1$ percentage points on ALFWorld with LoRA and agentic code, respectively. Ablations show that segment-averaged triggers outperform token-spike triggers. Behavior cloning is also more effective than the tested OPD surrogate for training teacher-generated recoveries. Across 23 experimental arms, takeover tends to help when the teacher substantially outperforms the OPD-trained student, provided that the teacher can recover from student-visited states, the student can learn those recoveries, and teacher intervention is neither excessive nor insufficient.

title: Data-free Multistep Diffusion Distillation
summary: One-step diffusion distillation achieves strong performance on small datasets but remains insufficient for high-resolution or complex text-to-image settings. Extending to multistep distillation often requires training data, suffers from early-step degradation, inconsistent outputs across sampling budgets, and incurs high computational cost. We identify that these limitations stem from simultaneous training, where a single adapted network approximates multiple score functions of different student distributions at once, causing biased distribution matching and unstable optimization. Therefore, we propose Progressive Multistep Data-free Distillation (PMDD), which assigns a dedicated adapted network per student distribution while avoiding the memory overhead of maintaining multiple adapted networks. Combined with a stage-wise unforget loss to preserve earlier-step generations, PMDD reduces optimization bias in the student, provides faster convergence, and a single unified model that supports multiple inference budgets. Extensive experiments show that PMDD matches or outperforms data-free few-step baselines at every multistep budget, reaches FID 1.99 on ImageNet 64x64 in two steps, below its 512-NFE teacher (2.32), and achieves FID 7.76 on zero-shot COCO 512x512, while requiring 4-5x less training compute than data-free DMDv2 to support three inference budgets.

title: Did the LLM Answer the Question? A Semantic Reconstruction Game for Jailbreak Evaluation
summary: Jailbreak attacks against large language models (LLMs) are evaluated using attack success rate (ASR), which depends on correctly identifying responses that fulfill prohibited requests. Existing evaluators can mistake refusals or topically related responses for successful attacks. We show that changing only the judge LLM can alter reported ASR by up to $82$ percentage points. We introduce the semantic reconstruction game, a training-free evaluator that decomposes compliance judgments into constrained semantic comparisons. Given only a response, an LLM reconstructs the request answered by its substantive content, excluding information merely repeated or refused. The game compares this reconstruction against similar decoy requests to determine whether it matches the original request, allowing abstention when neither candidate matches. Across three off-the-shelf LLM judges, the game achieves the lowest mean error against human labels among evaluated methods and reduces variation in reported ASR. It prioritizes avoiding false positives, even at the cost of missing some successful jailbreaks.

title: Parallel Sparse Outputs for Tensor Compilers
summary:
Sparse tensor compilers are commonly used high-performance tools that optimize tensor algebra programs over notoriously complex sparse data structures. Despite the ever-increasing size and scale of sparse datasets, there exists astonishingly little research on developing a parallel sparse tensor compiler. Existing approaches fail to parallelize or make assumptions about access patterns or output formats that limit generality.
  This paper presents Birdseed, the first tensor compiler to support all loop orderings over any standard sparse format in parallel. More specifically, Birdseed supports parallel sparse scatters and directly writes into list, bytemap, hash, and dense levels of fibertree sparse formats. Our approach exhibits asymptotic memory and time improvements over all previous work. We additionally demonstrate empirical speedups on challenging kernels to parallelize, such as histogram construction and SpMSpV.

title: PersEvalBench: Can LLM Evaluators Judge Contextually Appropriate Use of Persona Information?
summary:
Large language model (LLM) evaluators are increasingly used to assess personalized assistants, yet whether they can reliably judge personalization has rarely been tested. We introduce PersEvalBench, a benchmark testing whether an evaluator can recognize appropriate and inappropriate uses of user history. It contains 403 multi-episode scenarios where user information should persist, transfer, or cease to apply. The benchmark covers nine controlled error subtypes across three families: under-personalization, over-personalization, and misapplied-state errors. Human audits confirm that generated errors match their intended types and that the prescribed uses of user information are reasonable.
  Across five LLM evaluators, recognition of controlled personalization errors remains limited even with the full dialogue history. On the human-evaluated subset, under-personalization shows the largest gap: humans recognize 94.4% of these errors, compared with 63.9% for the strongest reported evaluator. Evaluators often recognize that a response is problematic but reverse the error direction, mistaking failure to follow an applicable preference (UNDER) for use of an inapplicable preference (OVER). Easier evidence access offers little help: highlighting the relevant history turns raises error recognition only slightly, suggesting that the remaining difficulty lies in judging what role that information should play in the response.

title: Historical-Feature Residual Adaptation for Sequential Screening
comments: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Agentic AI for Biological Discovery Workshop
summary: Sequential screening policies must use acquired feedback effectively under a fixed experiment budget. We study acquisition-time residual adaptation: a small ranking correction built from fixed historical features and anchored to base scores recorded before feedback is revealed. The interface accepts a history-conditioned scorer and a candidate feature table; its primary instantiation augments AssayFormer's ten-dimensional representation with 64 historical directions while retaining the pretrained model. In retrospective evaluation on 20 official-test screens from 15 recorded sources, a comparison fixed before target-outcome access increased source-macro fraction of hits recovered from 22.58% to 28.61%, exceeding all six prespecified comparators. A same-feature ordinary ranking head achieved 25.73%. Supplementary strong logistic, rank-fusion, and unprojected controls achieved 26.42%, 26.02%, and 26.78%, respectively. A separate model-independent pilot on 13 reused development screens reconstructs the features without AssayFormer assets. Across three seeds, residual adaptation improves random-forest hit recovery from 28.87% to 31.27%, while logistic recovery changes from 30.22% to 29.78%. The results show effective pretrained-policy adaptation and useful transfer to an independent nonlinear base, with gains that depend on the base model.
comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Agentic AI for Biological Discovery Workshop

title: Truthful and Expected-Payment-Optimal Model Routing in Graph-Based Agentic Workflows
summary: Assigning routine tasks to cheaper large language model (LLM) providers can reduce generation cost, but switching providers may require processing accumulated context again. Keeping dependent tasks with the same provider can instead reuse eligible context. Graph-based workflows therefore couple routing decisions across tasks. Independent providers may also privately know their real-time unit costs and strategically misreport them. We formulate this routing problem as a single-parameter procurement auction and propose STAR (Strategy-proof Topology-aware Agent Routing), which minimizes virtual-cost-weighted graph workloads. Its allocation rule and payments, computed by integrating workload over possible cost reports, make truthful reporting utility-maximizing regardless of other providers' reports and cover each truthful provider's execution cost. With independent cost distributions and non-decreasing virtual costs, STAR additionally minimizes the user's expected total payment to providers. Controlled synthetic experiments separate the execution-cost benefit of topology awareness from the payment benefit of virtual-cost optimization: the former grows with fan-out and transferred payload, while the latter increases gradually along the tested prior-shape heterogeneity path. A paired sensitivity study quantifies how payment savings vary with prior misspecification while strategy-proofness is preserved.

title: Hopfield Networks in Non-volatile Memory
summary: Many important computational workloads are bound by the performance of the memory system that supplies data to conventional processors. Compute in Memory (CiM) promises to circumvent this bottleneck by performing the processing within the memory. Neural Networks are memory-bound, and a notable example of such is the Hopfield Network. This work explores the design space of non-volatile computing-in-memory (NV-CiM) architectures using an instruction-level simulator to evaluate application mappings and workload-driven architectural adaptations. The exploration examines the resulting design trade-offs and includes theoretical comparisons with representative CPU and GPU architectures.

title: Generalization Analysis of Biased Stochastic Gradient Methods for Minimax Problems
summary: Minimax optimization refers to a class of optimization problems with some variables to minimize and other variables to maximize. Biased stochastic gradient methods have shown practical success in solving minimax problems to either improve robustness, enhance communication efficiency, or decrease computational costs. These successes motivate a lot of theoretical works to study the convergence of biased stochastic gradient methods, while their generalization analysis remains untouched. In this paper, we present the first framework to study the stability and generalization of biased stochastic gradient methods for minimax problems. We establish a connection between stability and generalization for minimax problems by relaxing the existing bounded gradient assumption to a bounded second moment condition. We then introduce a generalized Lipschitz-type condition on bias and gradient estimators, and derive a general stability bound to clarify the connection among bias, gradient estimators, and stability. We apply our general analysis to Zeroth-order and Clipped stochastic gradient descent ascent (SGDA), and derive stability bounds that match those of SGDA under appropriate smoothing/clipping parameters. We combine stability and convergence analyses together, and derive optimal excess risk bounds of order $1/\sqrt{n}$, where $n$ is the sample size.

title: TopicMerge: A Divide and Conquer Approach to Topic Modeling
summary: Recent advancements in topic modeling have split into two main paths: efficient embedding-based methods that offer scalability but are often outperformed on standard clustering metrics, and Large Language Model (LLM) approaches that achieve state-of-the-art clustering performance but at the cost of prohibitive computational expense and poor scalability. This paper introduces TopicMerge, a novel multi-stage pipeline that bridges these approaches to achieve both state-of-the-art clustering performance and computational efficiency. TopicMerge first employs an efficient clustering pipeline to deliberately over-segment a document corpus into a large set of fine-grained, semantically pure micro-clusters, which are then given initial semantic labels. It then introduces a novel, iterative merging algorithm where an LLM, guided by local neighborhood context, arbitrates on consolidating candidate pairs. These approved merges are then selectively executed and semantically relabeled by the LLM, hierarchically building broader, more coherent topics. Extensive experiments on the Bills and Wiki datasets show that TopicMerge achieves state-of-the-art clustering performance while reducing required LLM calls by over 92% compared to document-level methods, offering a practical and scalable solution.

title: Why don't Graph Transformers attend to the same token?
comments: Accepted at the Geometric Distributional Deep Learning (GDDL) workshop at NeurIPS 2026. 8 pages, 1 figure. Code: https://github.com/alexandre-bismuth/graph-transformer-sinks
summary: In large language models (LLMs), attention concentrates heavily on the first token. This 'attention sink' is believed to protect deep models against over-mixing. Even though graph transformers face a related pressure, we find that a SoTA graph transformer, GRIT, rarely forms sinks on molecules, and that it sinks less when trained on larger graphs, the opposite of the trend in LLMs. In principle, a graph can prevent sinks: we prove and show empirically that its symmetry and locality limit the attention any node can receive. On molecules, however, with distinguishable atoms and global attention, neither limit prevents sinks; what stops them lies in the model. We find that the attention scoring function is the main cause. Replacing GRIT's gated logit with a dot product raises its sink rate from 0.09 to 0.68 on identical graphs. In Graph Transformers using dot-product attention, removing the sink gives about the same error as removing a random node, while GRIT's most-attended nodes matter to its predictions. Attention sinks are therefore a property of dot-product attention rather than of Transformers. In our experiments, they form when dot-product scoring has a distinguishable node to concentrate on.
comment: Accepted at the Geometric Distributional Deep Learning (GDDL) workshop at NeurIPS 2026. 8 pages, 1 figure. Code: https://github.com/alexandre-bismuth/graph-transformer-sinks

title: AutoPoly-HE: Autonomous Design of Polynomial Activations for Privacy-Preserving Encrypted Inference
summary: Privacy-preserving machine learning has become critical for deploying artificial intelligence in sensitive domains such as healthcare, finance, and infrastructure monitoring. Homomorphic encryption (HE) enables secure inference on encrypted data. Despite its advantages, HE is not compatible with nonlinear activation functions found in machine learning models. Existing methods mitigate this problem by manually designing polynomial approximations for these activation functions. However, these functions do not account for the differences in dataset characteristics or model architecture. Furthermore, these functions are also limited to the accuracies of convolutional neural network (CNN) models. In this work, we propose an autonomous framework that selects polynomial activation functions tailored to each dataset and model. Using this framework, we analyze the interdependence between polynomial activation design and model architecture by evaluating several CNN ResNet and Vision Transformer models across multiple datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework generalizes across multiple architectures, including ResNet-18, ResNet-34, ResNet-50, ViT-S/16, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/16. Across all datasets, transformer-based models maintain higher accuracy under polynomial approximation, while convolutional models exhibit increased degradation as task complexity grows. In addition, latency analysis reveals that the proposed CLS token based inference pipeline significantly reduces computational overhead by eliminating depth-dependent operations, shifting the primary cost to encryption and decryption. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method not only adapts polynomial activations across architectures, but also enables efficientencrypted inference through both activation design and pipeline optimization.

title: Solving a sequence of eigenvalue problems using snapshot and row subsampling
summary: A sequence of eigenvalue problems requires solving $A_i\vec{x}_i= λ_i\vec{x}_i$ where $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $N \gg 1$ and (usually) $λ_i$ is the largest or smallest eigenvalue of $A_i$. Often, the matrices $A_i$ come from a discretization of a smooth map depending on a parameter $p \rightarrow A(p)$, that is $A_i = A(p_i)$, so the matrices $A_i$ change gradually along the sequence. Under this latter assumption, we introduce an efficient algorithm for solving sequences of eigenvalue problems. Our algorithm combines the ideas of reduced order model and row subsampling, as done in [E. Jones and Y. Nakatsukasa, arXiv, 2025] for linear systems. In addition, in our approach, the same set of rows is guaranteed to work well independently of the value of the parameter $p$ or the matrix $A(p)$ as long as the snapshot matrix is unchanged and given that the row subset was chosen well at the beginning. Furthermore, we implement an update strategy of the snapshot matrix. Along these results, we present theoretical analysis of the snapshot matrix for eigenvalue problems, showing an exponential decay of the singular values, and we give bounds on the error on eigenvectors for unseen value of the parameter. This analysis generalizes that in [M. Guido, D. Kressner, and P. Ricci, J. Sci. Comput., 2024] and shows that, regardless of the distribution of the snapshot points, the convergence is always (asymptotically) exponential in the number of snapshot points if the function $A(p)$ admits an analytical extension. We further generalize our algorithm for computing largest or smallest singular values and relative singular vectors and to generalized eigenvalue problems. We conclude with numerical results showing the efficiency of our approach.

title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models
summary: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. We propose SonoWorld, a causal ultrasound world model that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them to 6-DoF control using a small set of freehand clinical scans tracked with an EM sensor. SonoWorld is trained in three stages: pretraining a latent-action-conditioned video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames; grounding the learned video dynamics to metric probe poses with a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset; and applying distribution matching distillation to enable causal, long-horizon autoregressive generation with selectively caching eviction tokens at inference time. We evaluate controllability through pose-following fidelity, round-trip consistency, and axis-specific control under synthetic actions on held-out tracked scans, and further validate it with a user study. In model-based action discrimination, SonoWorld correctly ranks the target-directed probe motion over an equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8% of trials. To our knowledge, SonoWorld is the first causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model learned primarily from freehand clinical videos, providing a data-driven interactive environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation.

title: NavAble: A Large-Scale Dataset and Synthetic Data Generation Pipeline for Blind Navigation
summary: Reliable recognition of accessibility-critical objects (e.g., audible pedestrian signals, door-activation buttons, and handrails) is essential for assistive navigation technologies that support safe, independent mobility for blind and low-vision (BLV) users. Yet these categories are underrepresented in existing large-scale vision datasets, and the few datasets that include them suffer from limited class coverage, inconsistent annotations, and poor diversity. We introduce NavAble, a large-scale dataset spanning 11 accessibility-critical object classes, combining 41K curated open-source images with 8K newly collected, densely annotated real-world images. To extend scale and diversity, we develop a synthetic data generation pipeline that renders high-fidelity 3D assets across 37 environments under diverse styles and viewpoints, yielding 452K frames with rich ground-truth annotations from 565 assets. The pipeline minimizes manual effort by combining automated web image crawling, VLM-based filtering, SAM 3D-based asset generation, and convenient camera trajectory configuration, enabling large-scale data generation at a diversity unattainable through manual collection. Experiments show that fine-tuning existing segmentation models on the NavAble Dataset achieves reliable accessibility-object segmentation (>80% mIoU on our held-out test set). We also demonstrate the effectiveness of synthetic data augmentation, which yields up to +3.5 mIoU over real-world-only fine-tuning. Beyond benchmark evaluation, validation on egocentric data from two mobility-assistive robots demonstrates improved perception reliability in real-world navigation scenarios. Together, NavAble establishes a scalable foundation for BLV navigation perception, directly addressing the data scarcity and embodiment gaps. The dataset and pipeline are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/NavAble/NeurIPS_2026_BLV.

title: LLM-jp-4 Technical Report
comments: Results for the LLM-jp-4 33B dense model are not included in this version and will be added in a future revision
summary: This paper presents LLM-jp-4, a family of Japanese sovereign large language models (LLMs) developed with an emphasis on transparency, reproducibility, and practical usability. LLM-jp-4 comprises an 8B dense model and a 32B-A3B mixture-of-experts model, both trained from scratch on approximately 12 trillion tokens. To support independent verification and reproduction, we establish explicit criteria for selecting training data, external models, and software, and make the development process publicly available. Evaluation results demonstrate substantial improvements over previous LLM-jp models and competitive performance against open-weight models of similar scale. By documenting the development principles, training procedures, and empirical findings of LLM-jp-4, we aim to provide a reference for future sovereign AI development.
comment: Results for the LLM-jp-4 33B dense model are not included in this version and will be added in a future revision

title: Probabilistic Physics Digital Twin for Human-Robot Interaction
summary: Digital twins are increasingly used in robotics to simulate interactions, predict action outcomes, and support planning. However, constructing accurate digital twins requires precise estimates of physical properties such as mass, friction, and center of mass, which are often difficult to obtain in real-world environments. We propose probabilistic digital twins, which represent uncertain physical properties as probability distributions rather than fixed values. By simulating actions across these distributions, the twin predicts a range of possible outcomes and their likelihoods. These probabilistic simulations can guide both human and robot actions by identifying actions that are effective despite physical uncertainty. We demonstrate this framework through human-robot interaction scenarios, including interfaces that communicate simulated outcomes to users and robot planning strategies that explicitly account for uncertainty.

title: Beyond Initial Creation: Two Decades of Community-based Chart Revisions from Wikimedia Commons
comments: 5 pages, 2 figures, accepted by IEEE VIS 2026
summary: Open online communities like Wikipedia offer a rich space for understanding the organic evolution of public-facing artifacts, but little is known about how these communities collectively edit chart images. We investigate the phenomenon of "community editing" of visualizations by exploring chart revision patterns on Wikimedia Commons. We introduce a novel dataset of 7,786 longitudinal chart revisions across 1,664 images, labeled with edit categories using an LLM pipeline. Initial data analysis uncovered several novel findings. Multi-contributor revision is associated with more edits to mark styling and text content compared to single-contributor revision. Temporally, mark and text edits occur in more "bursty" cadences than data edits. In addition, while SVG charts attract more unique contributors and revisions than raster charts, their edit histories involve more tightly scoped and less diverse changes. This dataset enables a wide range of analyses of chart change over time.
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, accepted by IEEE VIS 2026

title: Can We Believe AI Peer Review?
summary: As large language models become widely used in scientific review and manuscript revision, AI scores are increasingly serving as feedback for assessing paper quality and guiding edits. Yet whether a single AI score reliably reflects the reviewer's judgment, and whether revision gains based on that score are endorsed by other reviewers, remain understudied. Using 200 papers from ICLR 2025 and 2026 and approximately 14,000 AI reviews, we study score reliability, score-distribution estimation, and cross-model agreement on revision gains. Repeated reviews fluctuate even under identical conditions. Finer-grained scoring protocols reduce score variance but also systematically shift mean scores, while the gains assigned to manuscript revisions depend strongly on the reviewer.

title: MMKG-R1: Constructing Multimodal Knowledge Graphs via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Multimodal knowledge graphs (MMKGs) organize information across different modalities to support multimodal Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which aims to improve the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The effectiveness of these multimodal Graph RAG methods largely depends on the quality of the constructed MMKGs. However, most existing methods construct MMKGs without explicit guidance on graph quality, while reinforcement learning (RL)-based methods that rely on final-answer correctness may provide only indirect feedback on MMKG quality. To address these limitations, we propose MMKG-R1, a novel MMKG-quality-driven RL framework for training an MLLM as a multimodal knowledge constructor. To be specific, MMKG-R1 introduces multiple quality-aware rewards to directly evaluate both the quality of information extracted from individual knowledge sources and the quality of the assembled MMKG. These rewards are then used to guide the RL training. Experiments across multiple datasets show that MMKG-R1 constructs MMKGs that improve downstream question-answering accuracy.

title: Why Do Agent Teams Fail Across Boundaries? A Failure Taxonomy for Agent-to-Agent Systems with Private States
summary: Agents are increasingly interacting with other agents that act for different principals -- people or organizations on whose behalf they work -- e.g., a buyer's personal agent negotiating with an enterprise's seller agent. In such agent-to-agent (A2A) scenarios, each agent has its own environment and holds information and authority that the other cannot see. Moreover, the interests of each agent may be aligned (cooperative), partly aligned (mixed-motive), or opposed (competitive). Existing multi-agent system failure studies assume only one orchestrator, shared workspace, or principal. We ask how A2A systems fail when these assumptions are removed. We study more than 2,500 recorded runs of A2A systems built from different agent harnesses and models, spanning 488 scenarios across eight families (legal, CRM, security, commerce, etc.). From these traces, we derive $A^2$-Failures, a taxonomy of 20 A2A failure modes in four categories: (i) discovery and delegation, (ii) grounding and record consistency, (iii) verification, and (iv) conduct and fidelity. Three observations hold across the harnesses, models, and scenarios studied: (1) Agents match tasks to peer names mentioned in the prompt rather than actively searching for available peers; (2) Agents never fact-check each other unprompted; (3) Scoring only the final output rewards the lead agent while hiding internal coordination, verification, and behavioral breakdowns. Our study makes a case for comprehensive evaluations where agents are scored individually against their own objectives in addition to task outcome. We release the run logs behind the taxonomy at https://huggingface.co/datasets/a2a-salesforce/a2-failures.

title: Counterfactual Gate-Support Decomposition: Separating Selection from Redistribution in Training-Data Filtering
summary: A training-data quality gate changes both which examples survive within regions of the input space and how training mass is distributed across those regions, so a gate-versus-random comparison does not isolate these mechanisms. We introduce Counterfactual Gate-Support Decomposition (CGSD), a four-arm, budget-matched design that crosses gate eligibility with support distribution and decomposes the observed gate effect into within-support selection, between-support redistribution, and their interaction. The practical constraint is finite-pool realizability: we characterize mass and token-assembly conditions under which the required arms can be constructed, together with a support-extinction case in which the ordinary design is undefined. On Korean-English and Korean-Japanese retrieval, the mean within-support selection component is the only one that exceeds its calibrated null band (+29.7 and +5.6 holdout items; 30/30 positive replicates), decisively in Korean-English and marginally in Korean-Japanese; redistribution and interaction remain unresolved at the available power. The same pattern holds for a second, unrelated gate family -- a model-confidence threshold rather than a deterministic verifier -- judged against its own null (+27.3 items, 9/9 positive), so the result is not a property of one gate's mechanism. On a mathematics gate, zero-eligibility supports leave the ordinary design undefined at every budget, while the extended design is constructible only inside narrow budget bands that an exhaustive scan locates and that the natural operating point misses -- the assembly condition separating a property of the pool from a limitation of the packer. CGSD therefore returns a decomposition, a constructible-but-underpowered design, or an explicit non-constructibility result, and says which; it prevents support redistribution from being silently interpreted as sample-level gate quality.

title: Target-Token Asymmetry Can Masquerade As Depth Specialization
summary: Layer-ablation studies often perturb early or late layers of a language model, compare the damage to prediction on two corpora, and read a larger early-layer effect on one corpus as early-layer specialization for its task. Such a comparison averages over the tokens that each corpus asks the model to predict, and these target tokens differ: math solutions, for example, ask for far more whitespace and numbers than encyclopedia prose. We show that this difference can create the appearance of depth specialization. We split a cross-corpus early--late damage interaction by target-token type and recompute it under a target mixture shared by both corpora. Between GSM8K and Wikitext, a positive interaction replicates across five model instances. In the three fully decomposed models, only whitespace has a positive interaction. Removing whitespace reverses the pooled effect in all three, and matching the full target mixture reverses it in two. The diagnosis holds under position matching, adversarial reassignment of token types, and a continuous readout. The risk can also be anticipated from the tokenizer alone. A screen computed before any model runs places every held-out pair it scored in the region its label predicts, and on the pairs it rates at high or medium risk, removing whitespace reverses every positive pooled estimate. A smaller content-word effect one token ahead follows the share of content targets that the unablated model already predicts. A cross-corpus depth effect therefore supports an interpretation of task specialization only after the target-token mixture is reported, the effect is decomposed by token type, and a mixture-matched summary keeps its sign.

title: When Is Smaller Greener? Right-Sizing Language Models for Agentic AI
summary: AI agents use large language models (LLMs) to plan and act over multiple steps, yet models are usually compared per call rather than per completed task. This paper asks: which model should an agent use to complete tasks reliably while minimising energy, cost and time? We show that per-call comparisons can be misleading for agentic AI. Because a task succeeds only if all required steps succeed, small differences in per-step reliability can produce large differences in overall task success. Failed attempts also consume resources. We therefore evaluate models using energy, cost and time per successfully completed task, treating the completed task as the functional unit. On this basis, we develop a decision model for choosing LLMs in agentic workflows. The model applies to tasks with binary or graded outcomes and to settings with or without retries. We show that each resource has a crossover task length at which a smaller, less reliable model ceases to be the greener, cheaper or faster option. These crossovers divide tasks into three regimes: for short tasks smaller models are preferred, for long tasks larger models are preferred, and only between these extremes do preferences among objectives matter. We embed these results in a two-stage framework that separates efficiency from preference. A Pareto screen first removes models that are never competitive; a weighted decision is required only when a genuine trade-off remains. A pilot study of 15 open-weight models from five developers, ranging from 0.6B to 27B parameters, on two multi-step agent tasks with measured GPU energy supports the predicted structure. The model with the lowest energy per completed task changes with task length and task type, and observed crossover points generally match those predicted from per-step measurements. These findings provide a practical framework for right-sizing language models in agentic AI.

title: Integrated Novelty Detection Systems: From Sensor Networks to Multi-Novelty Computer Vision
summary:
Novelty detection is crucial in various technological and scientific domains. Its importance spans from ensuring the reliability of sensor networks to enhancing the adaptability of computer vision systems. As AI systems become increasingly sophisticated and complex, effective anomaly detection is essential for maintaining reliability and accuracy. This work addresses novelty detection in weather sensor networks and computer vision. In weather sensor networks, particularly for monitoring rainfall, detecting blocked rain gauges can significantly impact data reliability, food security, and disaster management. This work evaluates four existing quality control methods for detecting blocked rain gauges and demonstrates their limitations, particularly in detecting clusters of faulty sensors. By comparing methods such as the Conditional Mixture Model (CMM), PSWQ (Fz-filter), Kernel Regression, and Gaussian Method, we identify their shortcomings and propose three novel quality control techniques that integrate probabilistic fault detection and consistency-based diagnosis framework to improve timely detection of blocked sensors, while reducing false alarms.
  In the realm of computer vision, current systems often fail to handle multiple types of novelty due to their focus on single-novelty scenarios. We highlight the need for integrated systems capable of handling multiple types of novelty. To support this, we introduce the Novel Snapshot Serengeti (NOVEL-SS) dataset, derived from the Snapshot Serengeti camera trap data, which includes various forms of novelty. We also present the DCA (Detect, Characterize, and Accommodate) baseline system, designed to handle multiple novelty by detecting, characterizing, and accommodating them. This work aims to advance the robustness and adaptability of novelty detection systems across both weather sensor networks and computer vision applications.

title: Where to Start, How to Move: Analyzing Curricula under GRPO for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
comments: 7 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Minchan Kim and Sungho Bae contributed equally
summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) provides no reward-relative learning signal when all rollouts receive identical rewards. In long-horizon tasks that require multiple interactions, rewards are given only upon successful task completion, making all-fail groups common early in training and limiting opportunities to practice later steps. Guide Assisted GRPO replays a successful reference prefix before the learner continues. We study how initial positions, handoff units, and movement rules affect unassisted task completion. Across three model sizes on BFCL, starting near completion is more effective under a fixed turn-level threshold rule. Finer handoffs alone do not consistently help, but outcome-informed tool-call selection outperforms GRPO on trained and untrained task categories. Guided starts also improve AppWorld success on both evaluation splits. These findings highlight where learning starts and how starting positions move as key curriculum choices.
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Minchan Kim and Sungho Bae contributed equally

title: BFHD: Bidirectional Feature Harmonization Decomposition for Heterogeneous Clinical Assessments
comments: 17 pages, 2 figures, 9 tables. Extended version of the paper published in IJCAI-ECAI 2026, including additional supplementary material in the appendices
summary: Clinical assessments are often collected using heterogeneous assessment systems across centers and time, leading to records that mix different but related sets of measurements. This motivates harmonization beyond total-score linking. We formulate clinical harmonization at the measurement level as a bidirectional recoverability problem: given paired observations from two assessment systems, the goal is to identify which measurements can be reliably translated in both directions within an application-defined tolerance, while separating non-translatable components. We propose Bidirectional Feature Harmonization Decomposition (BFHD), a feasibility-driven framework that enforces bidirectionally coupled translation and uses feature-wise output gating to produce an explicit decomposition in the original measurement space. Experiments on synthetic data and real clinical assessment pairs show that BFHD achieves broader feasible harmonization coverage and improved subset stability compared to baselines.
comment: 17 pages, 2 figures, 9 tables. Extended version of the paper published in IJCAI-ECAI 2026, including additional supplementary material in the appendices

title: Discrete Edge Multiscale Space based Hybrid Schwarz Preconditioner for High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
summary: In this work, we develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed as edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz (EMs-HS), for solving the Helmholtz problem with large wavenumbers. The problem is discretized using $H^1$-conforming nodal finite element methods on meshes of size $h$ decreasing faster than $k^{-3/2}$ such that the discretization error can be bounded by the data uniformly with respect to $k$. EMs-HS consists of a one-level Schwarz preconditioner (RAS-imp) and a coarse solver in a multiplicative way. The RAS-imp preconditioner solves local problems on overlapping subdomains with impedance boundary conditions in parallel, and combines the local solutions using partition of unity. On the PDE level, this coarse space corresponds to an edge multiscale space proposed in {[S. Fu, G. Li, R. Craster, and S. Guenneau, \emph{Multiscale Model. Simul.}, 19(4):1684-1709, 2021]}. The approximation properties of this coarse space to the discrete solutions from the primal and adjoint problems are derived by a novel conforming Galerkin finite element method based upon a nonstandard variational formulation. This work represents the first theoretical analysis of an edge multiscale space at the discrete level. We prove that the EMs-HS preconditioner leads to a convergent fixed-point iteration uniformly for large wavenumbers, by rigorously analyzing the approximation properties of the coarse space to the global Helmholtz harmonic extension part and to the solution of the adjoint problem. We provide extensive numerical results on the sharpness of the theoretical findings and also demonstrate the method on challenging heterogeneous models.

title: Asymptotic Behavior of Transformers
summary: In this paper we study the behavior of transformer networks generating text over long periods of time. We show that even a three-token, single-layer attention-only transformer can fail to converge. We then study a rich class of transformers with arbitrary finite depth, layer normalization, MLPs, RoPE encodings, and an arbitrary mix of local and global layers. Every transformer in this class has a softmax temperature threshold above which its empirical cache distribution converges to a unique limit, independent of initial conditions. We show further that, while each transformer has a temperature threshold, the supremum of this set is infinite, so there is no global minimal temperature that forces all transformers to converge.

title: Steering Vectors for Competing Ethical Frameworks Are Interchangeable: A Competing-Target Test for Activation Steering
summary: Activation steering adds a vector to a model's hidden states to control a named behaviour. A gain on that behaviour, however, does not show that the vector controls it directly: it may act through a component shared with neighbouring behaviours, which unsteered and random baselines cannot separate. We introduce the competing-target test: a vector is compared with the vector built the same way for a competing target, and an equivalence test states when their difference is below a useful margin. We apply it in open-weight models to vectors for Kantian deontology, which judges an act by the rule it follows, and act utilitarianism, which judges it by the welfare it produces. On held-out situations, prompting a framework raises its score and lowers the other's, whereas vectors for either framework move both scores alike, and none reaches the margin. The two vectors share most of their direction, a request to apply some framework; the same construction separates an optimistic from a pessimistic tone, whose vectors share much less. What a vector shares with its competitors therefore sets what it controls: steering a perspective can deliver a mixture, and measuring a disposition can measure its neighbours, unless tested against the competing target.

title: VLX-Go: Robust Embodied Tracking through Multi-Stage Learning and On-Policy Refinement
summary: Embodied visual tracking requires a robot to identify a designated target from visual observations and control its own motion to follow that target through an environment. Following an isolated person is a comparatively simple demonstration of embodied visual tracking, but following the intended person among distractors remains challenging. Existing methods exhibit a substantial drop in success from single-target to distractor tracking, motivating a focus on the shared spaces that person-following robots must navigate. We present \method{}, a vision--language waypoint policy built around the hypothesis that visual and language representations should be aligned before tracking-specific motion is learned. The policy combines complementary frozen visual encoders, multiscale temporal context, a transformer backbone, and a lightweight head for robot-centric waypoint prediction. Its training progresses through vision--language alignment, multimodal reasoning mid-training, and tracking specialization on 19,532 oracle episodes. Compared with 41.54\% distractor-tracking success for our earlier OmTrackVLA model, the complete multi-stage recipe achieves 55.80\%. We then explore on-policy refinement using filtered oracle labels for states visited by the policy. This preliminary study adds 2.42 percentage points of distractor-tracking success, reaching 58.22\%, while reducing collision rate by 1.99 pts. The final policy records the highest distractor- and ambiguous-tracking success rates among the compared methods. These results support staged multimodal learning as a promising direction for tracking among distractors and motivate further study of on-policy refinement for person following in shared spaces.

title: Tail Competition Explains Scaling in Best-of-N Sampling for Verifiable Problems
summary: Best-of-N sampling is a simple inference-time scaling strategy for large language models, yet its behavior under incomplete reward models remains poorly understood. We study Best-of-N as a competition between the extreme reward tails of correct and incorrect responses. This view shows that success depends not only on the probability of sampling a correct response, but also on whether correct responses dominate incorrect ones in the upper tail. Using extreme value theory, we characterize three asymptotic regimes: correct-tail-dominant, incorrect-tail-dominant, and critical explaining both monotonic gains and reward-hacking-induced degradation. We further derive finite-sample scaling laws for representative reward distributions, showing that, under Gaussian rewards, incorrect responses with sufficiently large variance can dominate selection even when their mean reward is lower. Unlike oracle selection, convergence with an incomplete selector can be polynomial rather than exponential. Finally, we propose a lightweight tail-tension criterion to estimate when additional sampling may become harmful. Experiments on synthetic data and real reward model scores are consistent with the theoretically predicted regimes, scaling laws, and diagnostic behavior, suggesting that tail competition provides a unified lens on Best-of-N sampling for verifiable problems.

AI.title_translation: 尾部竞争解释可验证问题中Best-of-N采样的缩放现象
AI.tldr: 本文利用极值理论将Best-of-N采样建模为正确与错误答案的高奖励尾部竞争，解释了其缩放法则与奖励欺骗现象，并提出了检测采样退化的诊断判据。
AI.motivation: Best-of-N采样是大语言模型常用的推理时缩放策略，但在不完备奖励模型（incomplete reward models）下的行为表现与缩放机制仍缺乏深入的理论理解。
AI.method: 利用极值理论将Best-of-N建模为正确与错误响应在上尾奖励分布上的竞争，刻画出三种渐近状态（正确尾部占优、错误尾部占优、临界状态），推导了代表性奖励分布下的有限样本缩放法则，并提出了轻量级的尾部张力（tail-tension）判据。
AI.result: 揭示了在不完备选择器下收敛速度可能是多项式而非指数级的；发现高斯奖励下即使错误响应的均值较低，只要其方差足够大也能主导选择；实验（包括合成数据与真实奖励模型评分）验证了理论预测的机制、缩放法则及有害采样的诊断效果。
AI.conclusion: 尾部竞争视角为可验证问题中的Best-of-N采样提供了统一的理论解释框架，揭示了不完备奖励模型下性能增益与退化的内在机制。
AI.translation: Best-of-N采样是大语言模型一种简单的推理时缩放策略，但其在不完备奖励模型下的行为表现仍未被充分理解。我们将Best-of-N视为正确与错误响应在极端奖励尾部之间的竞争。该视角表明，采样成功不仅取决于采样到正确响应的概率，还取决于正确响应是否在上尾区域占优于错误响应。利用极值理论，我们刻画了三种渐近机制：正确尾部主导、错误尾部主导以及临界状态，从而解释了单调增益和奖励欺骗引发的性能下降。我们进一步推导了代表性奖励分布的有限样本缩放法则，表明在高斯奖励分布下，方差足够大的错误响应即便平均奖励更低也能在选择中占据主导地位。与预言机选择不同，不完备选择器下的收敛速度可能是多项式的而非指数级。最后，我们提出了一个轻量级的“尾部张力”判据，用于评估额外的采样在何时可能变得有害。在合成数据和真实奖励模型得分上的实验结果与理论预测的机制、缩放法则及诊断行为一致，表明尾部竞争为可验证问题中的Best-of-N采样提供了一个统一的分析视角。
AI.summary: 本文基于极值理论，将大模型推理时的Best-of-N采样重新表述为正确与错误响应在极端奖励尾部的竞争。研究推导了有限样本缩放法则，揭示了奖励欺骗和收敛速度减慢的机理，并提出了预测采样退化的诊断指标，通过实验验证了该视角的有效性。
AI.keywords: Best-of-N采样, 极值理论, 奖励模型, 缩放法则, 奖励欺骗
AI.comments: 该研究从极值理论出发，将大模型推理阶段的Best-of-N采样行为建模为正确与错误响应奖励分布的上尾竞争，为解释测试时缩放（test-time scaling）中的性能饱和及奖励欺骗（reward hacking）现象提供了坚实的理论框架。提出的尾部张力判据具有很好的实用诊断价值。

title: Dynamic Graph World Modelling: Learning Future Dynamics from Temporal Context
summary: Dynamic graph learning models how entities and their relations evolve from historical observations to predict future graph states. Existing methods do not fully address dynamic graph world modelling, which requires learning transitions from temporal context to future latent graph states. This is difficult for three reasons: nodes and relations rely on different historical evidence, structural evolution is path-dependent, and future snapshots provide sparse and realization-specific targets. We propose Dynamic Graph World Modelling (DyG-WM), the first framework to jointly predict future node and relation representations from temporal context by answering three questions: what has evolved, how it evolved, and what will evolve next. To capture what has evolved, a historical node-relation context encoder summarizes node-neighborhood trajectories and pair-specific histories. To characterize how it evolved, a node-relation path-signature encoder captures ordered structural changes. To predict what will evolve next, a dual-level joint-embedding objective predicts target-snapshot node and relation representations without reconstructing the raw graph. Experiments on 12 link-prediction and two node-classification datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of DyG-WM across both tasks.

AI.title_translation: 动态图世界建模：从时间上下文中学习未来动力学
AI.tldr: DyG-WM是首个动态图世界模型，通过联合嵌入目标和路径签名编码直接预测未来节点与关系表示，无需重构原始图。
AI.motivation: 现有动态图方法无法充分解决从时间上下文转移至未来潜在图状态的‘世界建模’问题，面临节点与关系依赖不同历史证据、结构演化具有路径依赖性，以及未来快照目标稀疏且具有具体实现特异性三大挑战。
AI.method: 提出动态图世界建模框架（DyG-WM），无需重构原始图即可联合预测未来节点与关系表征：1. 利用历史节点-关系上下文编码器总结节点邻域轨迹和节点对历史；2. 采用节点-关系路径签名编码器捕获有序的结构演变；3. 使用双层联合嵌入目标直接预测未来快照中的节点和关系表征。
AI.result: 在12个链路预测数据集和2个节点分类数据集上的实验充分验证了DyG-WM在两种任务中的有效性。
AI.conclusion: DyG-WM成功将世界建模引入动态图学习，能够有效捕捉时间上下文与路径依赖性，直接预测未来潜在图状态，在动态链路预测和节点分类任务上均展现出优越的性能。
AI.translation: 动态图学习建模实体及其关系如何从历史观测中演化，以预测未来的图状态。现有方法未能充分解决动态图世界建模问题，该问题要求学习从时间上下文向未来潜在图状态的转变。这面临三大困难：节点和关系依赖于不同的历史证据、结构演变具有路径依赖性，以及未来快照提供了稀疏且针对特定实现的目标。我们提出了动态图世界建模（DyG-WM），这是首个通过回答三个问题（演变了什么、如何演变以及下一步将演变什么）从时间上下文中联合预测未来节点和关系表示的框架。为了捕获‘演变了什么’，历史节点-关系上下文编码器总结了节点邻域轨迹和特定节点对的历史；为了表征‘如何演变’，节点-关系路径签名编码器捕获了有序的结构变化；为了预测‘下一步将演变什么’，双层联合嵌入目标在不重构原始图的情况下预测目标快照的节点和关系表示。在12个链路预测和2个节点分类数据集上的实验证明了DyG-WM在两项任务中的有效性。
AI.summary: 本文针对动态图状态预测面临的异质证据、路径依赖与稀疏目标等挑战，提出了首个动态图世界模型DyG-WM。该模型通过上下文编码器、路径签名编码器与双层联合嵌入目标，分别建模演化内容、演化方式并预测未来潜在表示，在14个基准数据集上均取得了有效表现。
AI.keywords: 动态图学习, 世界模型, 路径签名, 联合嵌入预测, 链路预测
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将世界模型（特别是基于联合嵌入预测而非直接像素/图结构重构的思想）引入动态图领域，针对节点与关系的差异性、路径依赖性及未来状态稀疏性提出了系统性的建模方案，避免了重构原始稀疏图的高昂开销。不过，摘要未提及模型在大规模图上的计算复杂度与扩展性。

title: DANGERLENS: Probing Dangerous Representations Hidden by Safety Alignment
summary: Safety alignment teaches language models to refuse harmful requests, yet the internal accessibility of hazardous concepts can retain traces of earlier training. Can checkpoints with equally safe behavior differ in what remains accessible behind their refusals? In this work, we investigate this question through paired training histories and a direct audit of intermediate representations. We introduce DANGERLENS, a probe that maps hidden states into vocabulary space and uses blinded semantic judgments to distinguish harmful goals and operational means from hazard recognition and safety control. Experiments on three Qwen1.5 scales show that checkpoints with prior harmful exposure generally retain greater hazardous concept accessibility after the same safety alignment, with the strongest separation in intermediate and later layers. The same harmful update also produces different behavioral trajectories from closely matched starting points. Human relevance validation and readout ablations reinforce the measured accessibility contrast. Our findings show that training history remains visible inside behaviorally matched models and motivate internal accessibility audits alongside output safety evaluations.

AI.title_translation: DANGERLENS：探测安全对齐所隐藏的危险表征
AI.tldr: 本文提出了 DANGERLENS 探针，揭示了表面输出同样安全的模型在经过相同的安全对齐后，其内部表征依然会残留早期有害训练的历史痕迹与危险概念。
AI.motivation: 安全对齐可以促使模型拒绝有害请求，但危险概念的内部可访问性仍可能保留早期训练的痕迹。研究旨在探究具有相同安全表现的检查点在其拒绝行为背后的内部可访问内容是否存在差异。
AI.method: 通过成对训练历史直接审计中间表征。提出了 DANGERLENS 探针，将隐藏状态映射到词表空间，并利用盲测语义判断将有害目标和操作手段与危险识别和安全控制区分开。此外还进行了人工相关性验证和读出消融实验。
AI.result: 在三种不同规模的 Qwen1.5 模型上的实验表明，曾接触过有害内容的检查点在经过相同的安全对齐后，普遍保留了更高的危险概念内部可访问性，且差异在中间层和后层最为显著；相同的有害更新在高度匹配的起点上也会产生不同的行为轨迹。
AI.conclusion: 模型的训练历史在其内部表征中依然清晰可见，即使其外部行为表现一致安全。这一发现表明除了评估模型的输出安全性外，还需要对模型内部表征的可访问性进行审计。
AI.translation: 安全对齐使语言模型学会拒绝有害请求，然而危险概念的内部可访问性仍可能保留早期训练的痕迹。行为同样安全的检查点在其拒绝背后所保留的可访问内容是否存在差异？在本文中，我们通过成对训练历史和对中间表征的直接审计来探究这一问题。我们引入了 DANGERLENS，这是一种将隐藏状态映射到词表空间并使用盲测语义判断将有害目标和操作手段与危险识别及安全控制区分开的探针。在三种规模的 Qwen1.5 上的实验表明，曾有有害接触史的检查点在经过相同的安全对齐后，普遍保留了更高的危险概念可访问性，且在中间层和较深层中差异最显著。相同的有害更新在紧密匹配的起点上也会产生不同的行为轨迹。人工相关性验证和读出消融进一步证实了测得的可访问性对比。我们的研究结果表明，训练历史在行为匹配的模型内部仍然清晰可见，并促使在输出安全评估之外开展内部可访问性审计。
AI.summary: 本研究探讨了安全对齐模型内部是否会隐藏危险表征。作者提出了 DANGERLENS 探针，通过将中间隐藏状态映射到词表空间来分析内部概念。实验发现，外部拒绝行为同样安全的模型，若此前接触过有害训练，其内部中间层和深层仍会残留更高水平的危险概念可访问性，表明单纯的输出评估不足以完全反映模型的真实安全性。
AI.keywords: 安全对齐, 表征探测, DANGERLENS, 危险概念可访问性, 内部审计
AI.comments: 该研究具有重要的安全警示意义和创新性。它指出了现有基于输出行为的“黑盒”安全评估的局限性，揭示了即使模型在表面上表现出一致的安全拒绝行为，其内部深层表征仍可能牢固保留既往有害训练的历史痕迹。其局限在于摘要中仅展示了在 Qwen1.5 系列模型上的验证，对其他模型架构的普适性以及内部危险表征是否容易被特定对抗攻击重新激活未在摘要中展开详述。

title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
summary: Multimodal models and agents have emerged to enable AI systems to learn from and interact with the real world more like humans by integrating information across multiple modalities. However, enabling multimodal agents to continually acquire useful information from complex, heterogeneous multimodal data remains a significant challenge as they move toward long-horizon tasks and lifelong settings. Addressing this challenge requires effective memory mechanisms that can maintain continuity across sessions, adapt to changing users and environments, and refine memory-management policies through accumulated experience. We introduce a two-axis analytical framework for multimodal agent memory structured around two key questions: how multimodal information is formed and represented (Axis I, Formation and Representation), and how its management adapts with accumulated experience (Axis II, Memory Management). Axis I, Formation and Representation, characterizes what information is retained and how it is encoded (e.g., modality-specific embeddings, textual and structured records, latent and parametric representations) to support subsequent reasoning and action. Axis II, Memory Management, distinguishes three tiers: T1 Static Memory reuses fixed memory; T2 Dynamic Memory updates memory through a stable policy; and T3 Self-Evolving Memory updates memory through an evolving policy. Based on this framework, we synthesize recurring design patterns and derive principles for balancing source fidelity with abstraction, maintaining temporal validity and provenance, grounding memory use in recoverable evidence, and evolving memory policies over time. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and potential future directions for the memory mechanism of multimodal agents.

AI.title_translation: 看见、维护与学习：多模态智能体记忆的演进
AI.tldr: 本文系统提出了多模态智能体记忆的双轴分析框架（表征形成与三级管理演进），并总结了关键设计原则与未来方向。
AI.motivation: 多模态智能体在迈向长周期任务和终身学习场景时，亟需有效的记忆机制以从复杂异构数据中持续获取信息、维持跨会话连续性，并自适应变化的环境与用户。
AI.method: 提出包含两个维度的多模态智能体记忆分析框架：轴I（形成与表征）关注信息的编码与保留方式（如模态嵌入、结构化记录、隐空间参数）；轴II（记忆管理）划分为静态记忆（T1）、动态记忆（T2）和自进化记忆（T3）三个层级，并总结了设计模式与原则。
AI.conclusion: 多模态智能体记忆机制需兼顾信息的高效表征与管理策略的自适应演进；本文构建的框架和设计原则为长周期、终身多模态智能体的记忆系统设计指明了方向。
AI.translation: 多模态模型和智能体的出现使人工智能系统能够通过整合多种模态的信息，以更像人类的方式感知真实世界并与之交互。然而，当多模态智能体走向长周期任务和终身学习场景时，如何从复杂、异构的多模态数据中持续获取有用信息仍是一大挑战。应对该挑战需要有效的记忆机制，以跨会话保持连续性、适应不断变化的用户和环境，并通过积累的经验不断优化记忆管理策略。我们提出了一个围绕两个核心问题构建的多模态智能体记忆双轴分析框架：多模态信息如何形成与表征（轴I，形成与表征），以及其管理如何随经验积累而自适应演变（轴II，记忆管理）。轴I刻画了保留哪些信息以及如何进行编码（例如特定模态嵌入、文本和结构化记录、隐空间及参数化表征），以支持后续的推理与行动。轴II将记忆管理划分为三个层级：T1 静态记忆（复用固定记忆）、T2 动态记忆（通过稳定策略更新记忆）和T3 自进化记忆（通过演化策略更新记忆）。基于该框架，我们总结了常见的设计模式，并提出了在源保真度与抽象性之间取得平衡、维护时间有效性与可追溯性、使记忆使用立足于可恢复证据以及随时间演化记忆策略等原则。此外，我们还探讨了多模态智能体记忆机制所面临的挑战与潜在的未来研究方向。
AI.summary: 本文针对多模态智能体在复杂异构数据下的长程记忆难题，构建了围绕“形成与表征”和“记忆管理（静态、动态、自进化）”的双轴分析框架，归纳了关键设计原则，并展望了未来挑战与发展方向。
AI.keywords: 多模态智能体, 记忆机制, 记忆管理, 自进化记忆, 终身学习
AI.comments: 本文的前瞻性在于针对多模态智能体在长程和终身交互场景中的核心瓶颈——记忆机制，首次提出了清晰的双轴演进框架，尤其是将记忆管理划分到“自进化”层级，极具系统性与启发性。局限性在于摘要表明该工作偏向框架综述与概念设计原则，未提供具体的实证实验或统一评估基准。

title: Beyond Corrected Actions: Training LLM Agents on Textual Critiques
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for multi-turn agentic tasks that require interactions with users and environments over extended sequences of actions. A common approach to improving LLM agents is to use more capable expert models to provide training supervision, either by behavior cloning the expert's trajectories or by using the expert to correct the actions in trajectories generated by the weaker student model. However, expert LLMs can provide richer supervision than actions alone: they can directly generate textual critique that explain why specific actions are incorrect. We study whether training on such feedback benefits LLM agents and propose Critique-Augmented Agentic Fine-Tuning (CAFT), a framework that elicits textual expert feedback on student-generated trajectories. For each incorrect action, the expert yields both a corrected action and a textual critique explaining the student's mistake--which we then use as the training target for fine-tuning. Across four student models from the Nemotron 3 and Gemma 4 families on the agentic domains $τ^2$-Bench Airline+Retail and WebShop, adding critiques to action-level supervision improves performance by 8% on average over action-only distillation. Additionally, CAFT checkpoints can also provide a better warm start for reinforcement learning than expert-trajectory distillation. Our results demonstrate that textual critiques can strengthen supervision for multi-turn LLM agents.

AI.title_translation: 超越纠正动作：基于文本评论训练LLM智能体
AI.tldr: LLM智能体训练可以通过专家模型提供的文本评论（解释错误原因）来增强。CAFT框架结合纠正动作和文本评论进行微调，平均性能提升8%，并为强化学习提供更好的热启动。
AI.motivation: LLM智能体在多轮任务中需要与用户和环境交互。现有方法通常使用专家模型提供纠正动作作为监督。然而，专家LLM可以提供更丰富的监督形式，即文本评论，解释为什么特定动作是错误的。本文研究训练LLM智能体是否能从这种反馈中受益。
AI.method: 提出Critique-Augmented Agentic Fine-Tuning (CAFT) 框架。该框架在学生模型生成的轨迹上引出专家文本反馈。对于每个不正确的动作，专家会提供纠正动作和解释学生错误的文本评论。这些纠正动作和文本评论被用作微调的训练目标。
AI.result: 在Nemotron 3和Gemma 4系列的四个学生模型上，针对$τ^2$-Bench Airline+Retail和WebShop智能体领域，将评论添加到动作级监督中，相比仅基于动作的蒸馏，性能平均提高了8%。此外，CAFT检查点可以为强化学习提供比专家轨迹蒸馏更好的热启动。
AI.conclusion: 文本评论可以增强多轮LLM智能体的监督。
AI.translation: 大型语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地用于多轮智能体任务，这些任务需要与用户和环境进行长时间的动作序列交互。改进LLM智能体的一种常见方法是使用能力更强的专家模型提供训练监督，通过行为克隆专家的轨迹，或使用专家纠正较弱学生模型生成的轨迹中的动作。然而，专家LLMs可以提供比单纯动作更丰富的监督：它们可以直接生成文本评论，解释为什么特定动作是错误的。我们研究了对这种反馈进行训练是否有利于LLM智能体，并提出了评论增强智能体微调（CAFT）框架，该框架旨在从学生生成的轨迹中引出文本专家反馈。对于每个不正确的动作，专家会同时提供纠正动作和解释学生错误的文本评论——我们随后将其用作微调的训练目标。在Nemotron 3和Gemma 4系列的四个学生模型上，针对$τ^2$-Bench Airline+Retail和WebShop智能体领域，将评论添加到动作级监督中，相比仅基于动作的蒸馏，性能平均提高了8%。此外，CAFT检查点还可以为强化学习提供比专家轨迹蒸馏更好的热启动。我们的结果表明，文本评论可以加强对多轮LLM智能体的监督。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了一种名为Critique-Augmented Agentic Fine-Tuning (CAFT) 的新框架，旨在通过利用专家LLM生成的文本评论来改进多轮LLM智能体的训练。与仅依赖纠正动作的传统方法不同，CAFT要求专家不仅提供正确的动作，还提供解释学生模型错误原因的文本评论。实验结果表明，在Nemotron 3和Gemma 4系列模型上，结合文本评论的训练方法在代理任务中平均性能提升了8%，并且为后续的强化学习提供了更好的初始状态，证明了文本评论在增强LLM智能体监督方面的有效性。
AI.keywords: LLM智能体, 文本评论, 微调, 专家反馈, 多轮任务
AI.comments: 该论文的创新点在于引入了文本评论作为LLM智能体训练的监督信号，超越了传统的行为克隆或动作纠正。通过提供错误原因的解释，专家反馈变得更加丰富和有指导性，这对于学生模型学习更深层次的推理和纠错能力至关重要。这种方法不仅提升了模型性能，还可能为未来的可解释AI和更高效的RL预训练提供了新的思路。

title: OS-Bench: Evaluating SWE Agents on Cross-OS Code Migration
summary: Language-model (LM) agents are increasingly evaluated on repository-level software engineering (SWE) benchmarks derived from GitHub issues and pull requests. Although these benchmarks cover a broad range of development tasks, they provide limited insight into a common yet technically distinct challenge: migrating an existing implementation from one operating system (OS) to another while preserving behavior on both. We introduce OS-Bench, an executable benchmark for cross-OS code migration between Linux and Windows. Motivated by case studies showing that cross-platform features are frequently implemented on one OS before support is added for another, OS-Bench identifies migration opportunities by comparing execution coverage collected from the same repository on both systems. Platform-specific regions are then verified, organized into five migration scenarios, and transformed into repository-level tasks with target-platform tests and source-platform regression tests. The resulting benchmark contains 140 validated tasks from 111 repositories across C, C++, C#, Go, and Rust, comprising 91 Windows-to-Linux and 49 Linux-to-Windows migrations. We evaluate six models with SWE-agent, Claude Code, OpenHands, and Win-agent. The best configurations achieve only 26.4% success on Linux-target tasks and 20.4% on Windows-target tasks while preserving correctness across both systems. These results indicate that cross-OS migration is a challenging and underexplored capability, and OS-Bench is a testbed for improving platform-aware SWE agents.

AI.title_translation: OS-Bench：评估SWE智能体在跨操作系统代码迁移中的表现
AI.tldr: OS-Bench是一个新的可执行基准测试，用于评估语言模型智能体在Linux和Windows之间进行跨操作系统代码迁移的能力。现有智能体在此任务上的表现不佳，表明这是一个具有挑战性且未充分探索的领域。
AI.motivation: 现有的软件工程（SWE）基准测试在评估语言模型智能体在跨操作系统代码迁移这一常见但技术上独特的挑战方面存在局限性。研究发现，跨平台功能通常在一个操作系统上实现后才增加对另一个操作系统的支持，这促使研究者开发一个专门的基准测试来解决这一问题。
AI.method: OS-Bench通过比较同一代码库在Linux和Windows上收集的执行覆盖率来识别迁移机会。然后，验证平台特定区域，组织成五种迁移场景，并转换为带有目标平台测试和源平台回归测试的代码库级别任务。该基准包含来自111个代码库（C, C++, C#, Go, Rust）的140个已验证任务，包括91个Windows到Linux和49个Linux到Windows的迁移。使用SWE-agent、Claude Code、OpenHands和Win-agent评估了六个模型。
AI.result: 在Linux目标任务上，最佳配置的成功率为26.4%；在Windows目标任务上，成功率为20.4%，同时需要保持两个系统的正确性。这些结果表明跨操作系统迁移是一个具有挑战性且尚未充分探索的能力。
AI.conclusion: 跨操作系统代码迁移对于当前的语言模型（LM）智能体来说是一个具有挑战性的任务，成功率较低。OS-Bench提供了一个重要的测试平台，用于改进和评估具有平台感知能力的软件工程智能体。
AI.translation: 语言模型（LM）智能体越来越多地通过GitHub问题和拉取请求衍生的代码库级软件工程（SWE）基准进行评估。尽管这些基准涵盖了广泛的开发任务，但它们对一个常见但技术上独特的挑战——在保持两个操作系统行为一致性的前提下，将现有实现从一个操作系统迁移到另一个操作系统——提供的见解有限。我们引入了OS-Bench，一个用于Linux和Windows之间跨操作系统代码迁移的可执行基准测试。受案例研究的启发，这些案例研究表明跨平台功能通常在一个操作系统上实现后才增加对另一个操作系统的支持，OS-Bench通过比较在两个系统上从同一代码库收集的执行覆盖率来识别迁移机会。然后，验证平台特定区域，组织成五种迁移场景，并转换为带有目标平台测试和源平台回归测试的代码库级别任务。由此产生的基准包含来自111个代码库（C、C++、C#、Go和Rust）的140个已验证任务，其中包括91个Windows到Linux和49个Linux到Windows的迁移。我们使用SWE-agent、Claude Code、OpenHands和Win-agent评估了六个模型。最佳配置在Linux目标任务上仅达到26.4%的成功率，在Windows目标任务上达到20.4%的成功率，同时保持了两个系统的正确性。这些结果表明，跨操作系统迁移是一项具有挑战性且尚未充分探索的能力，OS-Bench是改进平台感知SWE智能体的一个测试平台。
AI.summary: 本研究介绍了OS-Bench，这是一个专为评估语言模型智能体在Linux和Windows之间进行跨操作系统代码迁移能力而设计的可执行基准测试。该基准通过分析同一代码库在不同操作系统上的执行覆盖率来识别迁移机会，并将其转化为具有平台特定测试的仓库级任务。OS-Bench包含了来自多种编程语言的140个验证任务。对现有智能体的评估显示，它们在跨操作系统迁移任务上的成功率较低（Linux目标任务26.4%，Windows目标任务20.4%），这突显了该领域的挑战性和未充分探索性，并表明OS-Bench是未来改进平台感知SWE智能体的重要工具。
AI.keywords: OS-Bench, 跨操作系统代码迁移, 语言模型智能体, 软件工程, 基准测试
AI.comments: OS-Bench的创新之处在于它专注于跨操作系统代码迁移这一独特且重要的软件工程挑战，而现有基准测试对此关注不足。通过自动化识别迁移机会和提供可执行的测试环境，它为评估和改进语言模型智能体在处理平台特定代码方面的能力提供了一个宝贵的工具。其重要性在于揭示了当前智能体在此任务上的显著局限性，并为未来研究指明了方向。

title: The Impact of Detector Architecture, Model Scale, and Scene Density on Multi-Pedestrian Tracking
summary: Pedestrian tracking in video is important for applications such as surveillance and scene analysis, but it becomes more challenging in crowded scenarios with frequent occlusions and rapid motion. This paper analyzes how detector architecture, model scale, scene density, and inference regime affect the tracking of multiple pedestrians. We compare the YOLO11, RT-DETR, and YOLO26 detector families with the ByteTrack and BoT-SORT trackers on sequences from the MOT17, MOT20, and SOMPT22 benchmarks. For YOLO26, we also compare traditional overlap filtering via Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) with end-to-end inference. The RT-DETR family achieved the highest mean scores on the HOTA tracking quality metric across all three benchmarks with both trackers, with a more pronounced advantage on MOT20, albeit at a higher computational cost. On MOT17 and SOMPT22, YOLO26 variants, especially YOLO26-L with NMS, offered favorable combinations of quality and speed compared with RT-DETR. In the YOLO26 inference comparison, the end-to-end mode did not yield consistent tracking gains over the NMS-based regime. Taken together, these results provide a practical guide for selecting detectors and trackers for this task based on application priorities.

AI.title_translation: 检测器架构、模型规模和场景密度对外挂多行人追踪的影响
AI.tldr: 本文对比了多种检测器和追踪器组合在多行人追踪任务中的性能，发现RT-DETR追踪质量最高但计算成本大，而YOLO26-L在多数场景下实现了优秀的质量与速度平衡。
AI.motivation: 视频中的行人追踪在拥挤场景、频繁遮挡和快速运动下极具挑战性，目前缺乏关于检测器架构、模型规模、场景密度和推理机制如何系统性影响多行人追踪性能的深入分析。
AI.method: 对比了YOLO11、RT-DETR和YOLO26检测器家族与ByteTrack和BoT-SORT追踪器在MOT17、MOT20和SOMPT22基准上的表现，并对YOLO26的传统NMS与端到端推理进行了对比。
AI.result: RT-DETR在所有三个基准测试的HOTA指标上均取得最高平均分（尤其在MOT20上优势明显），但计算成本更高；YOLO26-L加NMS在MOT17和SOMPT22上实现了质量与速度的最佳平衡；端到端推理相较于NMS未能带来一致的追踪增益。
AI.conclusion: RT-DETR在HOTA指标上表现最优但计算成本较高，而YOLO26-L等变体在速度和精度上取得了良好的平衡；端到端推理模式并未带来一致的追踪增益。研究为特定应用需求下的模型选择提供了实用指南。
AI.translation: 视频中的行人追踪对于监控和场景分析等应用至关重要，但在存在频繁遮挡和快速运动的拥挤场景中变得更具挑战性。本文分析了检测器架构、模型规模、场景密度和推理机制如何影响多个行人的追踪。我们在MOT17、MOT20和SOMPT22基准的序列上，将YOLO11、RT-DETR和YOLO26检测器家族与ByteTrack和BoT-SORT追踪器进行了比较。对于YOLO26，我们还比较了通过非极大值抑制（NMS）进行的传统重叠过滤与端到端推理。RT-DETR家族在使用这两种追踪器的所有三个基准测试中的HOTA追踪质量指标上均获得了最高平均分，在MOT20上的优势更为明显，尽管计算成本更高。在MOT17和SOMPT22上，与RT-DETR相比，YOLO26变体（尤其是带NMS的YOLO26-L）提供了质量和速度的有利组合。在YOLO26推理比较中，端到端模式并未比基于NMS的机制产生一致的追踪增益。综上所述，这些结果为根据应用优先级选择该任务的检测器和追踪器提供了实用指南。
AI.summary: 本文系统研究了检测器架构、模型规模、场景密度和推理机制对多行人追踪的影响，通过对比多种最新检测器与追踪器在多个基准测试上的表现，为实际应用中的模型选择提供了实用的指导方案。
AI.keywords: 多行人追踪, 检测器架构, 模型规模, 场景密度, 端到端推理
AI.comments: 该论文全面分析了检测器架构、模型规模、场景密度和推理模式对多行人追踪性能的影响，对实际应用中的模型选择具有很高的指导意义。其创新点在于跨多个基准测试对比了最新的检测器（如YOLO11, RT-DETR, YOLO26）与主流追踪器的组合。

title: Policy-Verified Self-Training: Learning Agent Compliance from Verifiable Policy Rewards
comments: 16 pages, 3 figures, 13 tables. Companion paper: arXiv:2610.11030
summary: Runtime policy verifiers can prevent agents from executing disallowed actions, but their decisions are typically used only for enforcement and discarded afterward. We ask whether these decisions can instead become verifiable policy rewards for training the agents they guard. We introduce Policy-Verified Self-Training (PVST), a post-training paradigm in which an agent generates its own interaction trajectories and an executable policy verifier, here a deterministic gate compiled from a written policy, evaluates whether each action complies. Compliant trajectories are reinforced, and violations become negatives for preference optimization; beyond the gate and the benchmark's task-success signal, PVST needs no stronger teacher model, no human preference labels and no attack-specific supervision, although rollouts are collected in the benchmark's attacked environment. On held-out AgentDojo tasks under prompt injection, policy-verified preference training of Qwen3-8B reduces violating trajectories from 37.2% to 10.3 $\pm$ 0.9% (three seeds) and successful attacks from 12.4% to 0.5% at equal or higher pooled task utility, although utility falls on travel, compared with 22.0% when negatives are selected by an attack oracle and 31.9 $\pm$ 0.9% with negatives that contain no violation. The learned behavior holds under an attack template never used in training (37.7% to 11.0%) and on a suite excluded from training (34.8% to 16.7%), and the retained verifier's intervention rate falls from 39.2% to 8.8% (seed 0). Our analysis identifies two conditions under which the verdict is most informative: success must not already imply compliance, and guarded actions must appear in both permitted and forbidden contexts.
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 13 tables. Companion paper: arXiv:2610.11030

AI.title_translation: 策略验证自训练：利用可验证策略奖励学习智能体合规性
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种名为PVST的自训练范式，利用运行时策略验证器的决策作为奖励来训练智能体，在不需要人类标签的情况下大幅降低了AI智能体在对抗环境中的违规行为和攻击成功率。
AI.motivation: 现有的运行时策略验证器通常仅用于拦截违规动作，决策过程随后被丢弃。论文旨在探讨如何利用这些验证决策作为可验证的策略奖励，来训练和引导它们所保护的智能体，从而无需依赖人类偏好标签或更强大的教师模型。
AI.method: 引入策略验证自训练（PVST）后训练范式：智能体生成交互轨迹，通过可执行策略验证器（确定性门控机制）评估动作合规性；对合规轨迹进行强化，违规轨迹则作为偏好优化中的负样本进行训练。
AI.result: 在 AgentDojo 的提示词注入任务上，使用 Qwen3-8B 进行策略验证偏好训练后，违规轨迹从 37.2% 降至 10.3%，成功攻击率从 12.4% 降至 0.5%，并在保持同等或更高任务效用的同时，展现出良好的泛化能力（跨攻击模板和跨任务集）。
AI.conclusion: 策略验证自训练（PVST）是一种有效且无需人类或强教师监督的后训练范式，能显著提升智能体在对抗环境中的合规性和安全性，同时保持任务效用。
AI.translation: 运行时策略验证器可以阻止智能体执行被禁止的动作，但它们的决策通常仅用于执行，随后就被丢弃。我们探讨了这些决策是否可以转变为用于训练它们所保护的智能体的可验证策略奖励。我们引入了策略验证自训练（PVST），这是一种后训练范式，其中智能体生成自己的交互轨迹，并且可执行策略验证器（这里是一个从书面策略编译而来的确定性门控）评估每个动作是否合规。合规的轨迹得到强化，而违规行为则成为偏好优化的负样本；除了门控和基准测试的任务成功信号之外，PVST不需要更强大的教师模型、不需要人类偏好标签，也不需要特定攻击的监督，尽管是在基准测试受到攻击的环境中收集Rollout的。在提示注入下的未公开 AgentDojo 任务中，Qwen3-8B 的策略验证偏好训练将违规轨迹从 37.2% 降低到 10.3 $\pm$ 0.9%（三个随机种子），成功攻击从 12.4% 降低到 0.5%，且任务效用池相等或更高（尽管在 travel 任务上效用下降），相比之下，当由攻击预言机选择负样本时为 22.0%，而没有违规的负样本为 31.9 $\pm$ 0.9%。所学习到的行为在训练中从未使用过的攻击模板（从 37.7% 到 11.0%）以及排除在训练之外的一套测试集（从 34.8% 到 16.7%）上依然有效，并且保留的验证器干预率从 39.2% 下降到 8.8%（随机种子 0）。我们的分析确定了裁决最具信息量的两个条件：成功不能已经暗示合规，并且被保护的动作必须同时出现在允许和禁止的上下文中。
AI.summary: 本文提出了策略验证自训练（PVST）范式，利用运行时策略验证器的决策作为奖励信号来训练智能体。该方法无需人类标签或强教师模型，通过强化合规轨迹并将违规轨迹用作偏好优化的负样本，显著降低了智能体在对抗环境下的违规率与攻击成功率。
AI.keywords: Policy-Verified Self-Training, Policy Verifiers, Agent Compliance, Preference Optimization, Prompt Injection
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将运行时策略验证器与自训练（Self-Training）相结合，提出了一种无需强大教师模型或人类偏好标签的高效对齐与安全加固范式（PVST），显著降低了智能体的违规行为和攻击成功率。其局限性可能在于特定任务（如 travel）上的效用下降，且依赖于高质量的策略验证器。

title: Evaluating Compressed Memory: Dependence, Utility, and Content Benefit
summary: Does a language model answer better because its compressed memory contains useful document information? Replacing memory vectors with zeros can lower a trained model's score without showing that it outperforms a model trained without memory. We combine zeroing with separately trained models that cannot access stored text or receive the same constant input for every document. Across nine systems, some models rely on memory yet perform worse than the trained alternative. For example, in experiments that predict states in generated stories, zeroing memory worsens a model's prediction loss, yet a model trained without memory achieves lower loss than the original model with intact memory. On TriviaQA, giving xRAG memory from another question's passage raises F1, which measures word overlap with accepted answers, from 19.38 without a document to 24.78. Its effect on how often outputs contain an accepted answer is statistically uncertain. The question's retrieved passage scores higher still (29.88 F1). Thus a gain over no document alone does not establish that the gain requires the question's passage. Evaluations must therefore specify the comparison model, absolute performance, and generation and scoring conditions.

AI.title_translation: 评估压缩记忆：依赖性、效用和内容效益
AI.tldr: 本文通过实验证明，语言模型中压缩记忆的效用评估需要更严格的基线和对比，简单地替换记忆可能无法证明其优势，有时甚至表现不如无记忆模型。
