AI.motivation: 探讨语言模型中压缩记忆是否真正有助于提升性能，并指出现有评估方法可能无法准确反映其效用。
AI.method: 结合了“置零”记忆向量的方法，并使用独立训练的、无法访问存储文本或接收相同常数输入的模型进行对比。在九个系统上进行了评估，包括预测生成故事中的状态和TriviaQA任务。
AI.result: 在九个系统中，一些模型依赖于记忆，但性能却比没有记忆的替代模型差。在预测故事状态的实验中，置零记忆会恶化模型的预测损失，但没有记忆训练的模型比原始有记忆的模型损失更低。在TriviaQA上，使用来自另一个问题的段落的xRAG记忆将F1分数从19.38（无文档）提高到24.78，但其对输出包含接受答案的频率的影响在统计上不确定。使用问题本身的检索段落得分更高（29.88 F1）。仅凭相对于无文档的增益不能确定这种增益需要问题本身的段落。
AI.conclusion: 评估必须明确指定对比模型、绝对性能以及生成和评分条件。
AI.translation: 语言模型是否因为其压缩记忆包含有用的文档信息而回答得更好？用零替换记忆向量可以降低训练模型的得分，但这并未表明它优于一个未经记忆训练的模型。我们将置零方法与独立训练的模型相结合，这些模型无法访问存储文本或每个文档都接收相同的常量输入。在九个系统中，一些模型依赖于记忆，但性能却比训练的替代方案更差。例如，在预测生成故事中状态的实验中，置零记忆会恶化模型的预测损失，但一个没有记忆训练的模型比原始具有完整记忆的模型实现了更低的损失。在TriviaQA上，给予xRAG来自另一个问题段落的记忆，F1分数（衡量与接受答案的词语重叠）从没有文档时的19.38提高到24.78。其对输出包含接受答案的频率的影响在统计上不确定。问题本身的检索段落得分仍然更高（29.88 F1）。因此，仅凭相对于没有文档的增益并不能证明这种增益需要问题本身的段落。因此，评估必须指定比较模型、绝对性能以及生成和评分条件。
AI.summary: 本文质疑语言模型中压缩记忆的真实效用。通过将记忆向量置零并与无记忆模型进行对比，研究发现在某些情况下，依赖记忆的模型表现反而不如无记忆模型。例如，在TriviaQA任务中，虽然外部记忆能提升F1分数，但其效果不如直接使用问题相关段落，且仅仅对比无文档情况不足以证明记忆的必要性。文章强调，对压缩记忆的评估必须明确指定对比模型、绝对性能以及生成和评分条件。
AI.keywords: 压缩记忆, 语言模型, 评估, 依赖性, 效用
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过严谨的实验设计，挑战了对语言模型中压缩记忆效用的普遍假设。其创新之处在于提出了更严格的评估方法，即不仅要比较有无记忆的性能，还要与未经记忆训练的模型进行对比。这对于理解和优化大型语言模型的记忆机制具有重要指导意义，提醒研究者在设计和评估模型组件时，需要更深入地探究其真实贡献和潜在的替代方案。

title: A Critical Review of Grid Integration Challenges and Flexibility Opportunities for Large-Scale Data Centers
summary: The rapid proliferation of cloud computing and artificial intelligence workloads is fundamentally reshaping the magnitude, spatial concentration, and electrical characteristics of data center power demand. Data centers differ from conventional commercial loads because they combine high rack densities, converter-dominated interfaces, thermally coupled cooling, uninterruptible power supplies, programmable workloads, and increasingly complex behind-the-meter generation and storage within a single facility. This review examines their grid integration from utility and sustainable-energy perspectives across resource planning, large-load interconnection, distribution feeders, market operation, real-time dynamics, power quality, and asset management. Particular attention is given to distribution-level issues that receive limited treatment in broader energy reviews: bidirectional operation on renewable-rich feeders, harmonic propagation and resonance, ride-through and reconnection, transformer derating, cable ampacity, neutral-conductor heating, protection, and measurement. Static, composite, physics-based dynamic, calibrated, impedance, electromagnetic transient, and hybrid load models are compared according to study purpose and data requirements, and utility coordination platforms, uninterruptible power supply and battery control, workload flexibility, renewable co-location, cogeneration, fuel cells, thermal storage, and clean firm supply are assessed. The central finding is that requested peak demand and annual energy matching alone cannot establish reliable or sustainable integration. Credible assessment must consider hourly and locational supply, network deliverability, marginal emissions, lifecycle and water impacts, backup obligations, rebound, asset health, and verified operating capability.

AI.title_translation: 大规模数据中心电网集成挑战与灵活性机遇的批判性综述
AI.tldr: 本文批判性综述了大规模数据中心在电网集成中面临的挑战和灵活性机遇，强调了评估可靠和可持续集成需要考虑的全面因素，而不仅仅是峰值需求和年能耗匹配。
AI.motivation: 云计算和人工智能工作负载的快速增长正在深刻改变数据中心的电力需求，其与传统商业负荷存在显著差异。本文旨在从电力公司和可持续能源的角度，审视数据中心的电网集成问题，并特别关注在更广泛的能源综述中受关注较少的配电层面问题。
AI.method: 本文从资源规划、大负荷并网、配电馈线、市场运行、实时动态、电能质量和资产管理等方面审视了数据中心的电网集成。特别关注了配电层面的问题，并比较了各种负荷模型。同时，评估了多种公用事业协调平台和数据中心内部的灵活性技术。
AI.result: 数据中心与传统商业负荷不同，具有高机架密度、转换器主导接口、热耦合冷却、不间断电源、可编程工作负载以及日益复杂的表后发电和储能。本文发现，仅凭请求的峰值需求和年度能源匹配不足以建立可靠或可持续的集成。可信的评估必须考虑每小时和区域供应、网络输送能力、边际排放、生命周期和水影响、备用义务、回弹效应、资产健康和经核实的运行能力。
AI.conclusion: 可靠和可持续的数据中心电网集成需要全面评估，超越简单的峰值需求和年能耗匹配，必须考虑小时级和区域供应、网络能力、环境影响、备用义务和资产健康等多个维度。
AI.translation: 云计算和人工智能工作负载的快速普及正在从根本上重塑数据中心电力需求的规模、空间集中度和电气特性。数据中心与传统商业负荷不同，因为它在一个设施内结合了高机架密度、转换器主导接口、热耦合冷却、不间断电源、可编程工作负载以及日益复杂的表后发电和存储。本综述从电力公司和可持续能源的角度，审查了数据中心在资源规划、大负荷并网、配电馈线、市场运行、实时动态、电能质量和资产管理方面的电网集成。特别关注在更广泛的能源综述中受关注有限的配电层面问题：富可再生能源馈线上的双向运行、谐波传播和谐振、穿越和重连、变压器降容、电缆载流量、中性线发热、保护和测量。根据研究目的和数据要求，比较了静态、复合、基于物理的动态、校准、阻抗、电磁瞬态和混合负荷模型，并评估了公用事业协调平台、不间断电源和电池控制、工作负载灵活性、可再生能源共址、热电联产、燃料电池、热储能和清洁可靠供应。核心发现是，仅凭请求的峰值需求和年度能源匹配无法建立可靠或可持续的集成。可信的评估必须考虑每小时和区域供应、网络输送能力、边际排放、生命周期和水影响、备用义务、回弹效应、资产健康和经核实的运行能力。
AI.summary: 本综述深入探讨了大规模数据中心在快速增长背景下，与电网集成所面临的独特挑战和潜在的灵活性机遇。文章从电力公司和可持续能源视角，全面审视了数据中心在资源规划、并网、配电、市场运作等多个层面的影响，并特别关注了配电层面的具体技术问题。研究强调，仅通过峰值需求和年能耗匹配不足以实现可靠和可持续的集成，而必须考虑包括小时级供应、网络输送、环境影响和资产健康在内的多维度评估。
AI.keywords: 数据中心, 电网集成, 灵活性, 可再生能源, 配电网
AI.comments: 这是一篇全面的批判性综述，系统性地梳理了大规模数据中心电网集成面临的复杂问题。其创新之处在于不仅识别了挑战，还探讨了灵活性机遇，并特别强调了对配电层面问题的深入分析。该文的重要性在于为未来数据中心与电网的协同发展提供了关键的评估框架和方向，超越了传统的电力需求匹配思维。

title: One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models
comments: 9 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on World Models in Physical AI (WM-PAI)
summary: Latent world models are routinely selected, checkpointed and ablated on one-step prediction loss, on the assumption that a model which predicts the next latent better is a better model. In model-based RL this assumption is known to be unreliable; we ask whether it also fails for latent world models, where the training target is the model's own embedding and the loss is not expressed in interpretable units. We introduce a frozen-decoder protocol reporting one-step error in physical units, decomposed into the part already present in the encoder's representation and the part the predictor adds. Applying it to a recent end-to-end JEPA world model across three continuous-control environments, we move the metric by fine-tuning and measure goal-conditioned planning on the same checkpoints, with three training seeds and paired planning seeds throughout. Within one environment, a per-epoch ladder shows the relationship saturating after a single epoch: the first epoch improves fidelity by 32% and planning by 4.4 pp, but across the fifteen checkpoints that follow -- a further 15% fidelity improvement, monotone in every training seed -- the correlation between one-step error and planning success is r = -0.010. This is not a task-ceiling artifact: stratifying by a model-independent measure of training-data support, planning in the lowest-support stratum starts at 80%, leaving ample headroom, and is nonetheless flat from epoch 1 onward. Across environments the exchange rate is equally unstable: a 93% fidelity reduction on TwoRoom yields -0.7 pp of planning, while a 40% reduction on PushT yields +4.9 pp [+1.1, +8.9]. All results replicate under a decoder-free measure, latent drift. We also show that a matched continued-training control absorbs the entire fidelity gain we had attributed to an auxiliary objective.
comment: 9 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on World Models in Physical AI (WM-PAI)

title: DeLoop: Repeated Actions as Self-Supervision for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Language-model agents that run long tasks often redo work they have already done: they re-issue a tool call they made earlier and get back exactly the same observation, a step that adds no new information. We identify this failure as a loop. Loops appear natively in Qwen, Llama, and Gemini agents and become far more common once the agent's history is compressed to fit its context window. To reduce these loops, we propose DeLoop, a self-supervised training method. DeLoop builds on a simple observation: the agent's own rollout can provide the supervision needed to learn from its loops. We use a looping action as a negative example and the first later non-looping action in the same rollout as a positive example. DeLoop learns from these pairs through direct preference optimization and does not require task rewards, gold answers, or LLM judges. On CodeGym under compression, DeLoop reduces the share of Qwen3-8B tasks containing loops from 57.3% to 6.1%. It also uses about one third as many steps per task, with similar task success. On Qwen3-32B, DeLoop reduces loops and steps while raising task success from 37.7% to 44.8%.

AI.title_translation: DeLoop：将重复动作作为长程Agent的自监督信号
AI.tldr: DeLoop是一种无需外部奖励的自监督训练方法，通过直接偏好优化消除语言模型Agent在长程任务中的重复操作，从而大幅减少冗余步骤并提升任务成功率。
AI.motivation: 语言模型Agent在执行长期任务时经常陷入重复操作（即重复发出相同的工具调用并得到相同的观察结果），尤其在历史记录被压缩以适应上下文窗口时更为严重。现有问题缺乏有效的自监督纠正机制。
AI.method: 提出DeLoop自监督训练方法，利用Agent自身轨迹中的循环动作为负样本，同一轨迹中随后的第一个非循环动作为正样本，通过直接偏好优化（DPO）进行训练。
AI.result: 在CodeGym基准测试中，DeLoop将Qwen3-8B任务的循环比例从57.3%降至6.1%，每项任务的步数减少约三分之二且保持了相近的成功率；对于Qwen3-32B，DeLoop在减少循环和步数的同时，将任务成功率从37.7%提升至44.8%。
AI.conclusion: DeLoop是一种有效且无需外部奖励的自监督训练方法，能显著减少长程语言模型Agent在处理压缩历史时的重复操作问题，提升任务执行效率与成功率。
AI.translation: 运行长期任务的语言模型Agent经常重复已经完成的工作：它们重新发出之前做过的工具调用并得到完全相同的观察结果，这一步没有添加任何新信息。我们将这种失败识别为循环（loop）。循环在Qwen、Llama和Gemini Agent中天然存在，并且在Agent的历史记录被压缩以适应其上下文窗口后变得更加常见。为了减少这些循环，我们提出了DeLoop，一种自监督训练方法。DeLoop建立在一个简单的观察之上：Agent自己的轨迹可以提供从循环中学习所需的监督。我们将循环动作作为负例，同一轨迹中随后的第一个非循环动作作为正例。DeLoop通过直接偏好优化从这些对中学习，并且不需要任务奖励、标准答案或LLM评判器。在压缩条件下的CodeGym上，DeLoop将包含循环的Qwen3-8B任务比例从57.3%降低到6.1%。它还使每个任务使用的步数减少了约三分之二，且具有相似的任务成功率。在Qwen3-32B上，DeLoop减少了循环和步数，同时将任务成功率从37.7%提高到44.8%。
AI.summary: 论文介绍了DeLoop，一种用于长程语言模型Agent的自监督训练方法，旨在消除历史压缩带来的重复操作问题。该方法将循环动作视为负样本，后续非循环动作为正样本，通过直接偏好优化（DPO）提升Agent效率和成功率，无需外部标注或奖励。
AI.keywords: 语言模型Agent, 长程任务, 自监督学习, 直接偏好优化, 重复动作消除
AI.comments: 该论文针对长程语言模型Agent容易陷入重复操作（Loop）的痛点，提出了一种自监督训练方法DeLoop。其创新点在于巧妙利用Agent自身历史轨迹中的循环作为负样本、后续非循环操作作为正样本，通过直接偏好优化（DPO）进行训练，完全不需要外部奖励、标准答案或LLM评判器，具有很高的实用价值和通用性。

title: Robust Explanatory Analysis for Structured Optimization Networks (REASON) in Learning
summary: We seek a hierarchical resolution of residual error under a composite learning objective as a principled mechanism for identifying and exploiting additional information, particularly under distribution shift and perturbation. Inspired by the System 1/System 2 paradigm, we formulate this principle as a two-loop mechanism serving a common inference goal. A fast, System 1-like loop resolves the residual addressable by the available evidence; the remaining epistemic residual triggers a medium speed, System 2-like loop that actively acquires additional evidence and measures its informational value through residual reduction. Over nested solution spaces, the medium-loop optimum is provably no worse than the fast-loop optimum. Experiments show that the resulting two-loop model consistently improves upon the fast loop at approximately half the computation of the medium loop, including under unseen corruptions, and, when provided a cleaner observation, outperforms staged classifiers and learning-to-defer methods at equal computational cost.

title: Learning What to Keep: Transfer-Aware Personal Skill Learning from User Feedback
summary: User feedback enables LLMs to refine reusable personalized skills, but often mixes persistent preferences with request-specific corrections. Indiscriminately retaining both risks negative transfer, motivating selective retention at the level of individual requirements. We frame this challenge as selective transfer over atomic rules and propose SkillGrain, a framework for learning reusable personalized skills from user feedback. SkillGrain decomposes feedback into independently actionable rules, predicts their transferability, and retains only those suitable for future requests. To learn these decisions, we combine rubric-guided skill rewards with fine-grained credit assignment that separately evaluates rule content and retention decisions. We further jointly optimize skill induction and skill-conditioned generation through reinforcement learning, ensuring that learned skills support downstream personalization. We construct a benchmark spanning five personalized writing tasks to evaluate cross-request generalization. Experiments across three base models in both in-domain and out-of-domain settings show that SkillGrain achieves the best overall average performance among competing methods.

title: EvoWeave: Composing Reusable Agent Experience through Operation Level Graphs
summary: Different tasks often require interactive agents to perform similar operations at intermediate steps. Retrieving an entire past workflow can introduce irrelevant steps, whereas retrieving isolated operations can discard the dependencies needed to reuse them. We introduce EvoWeave, a framework for experience memory that represents abstract states as nodes and reusable operations as directed edges with input and output contracts, provenance, and capability references. A planner decomposes the current task into a dependency graph; operation retrieval and bounded directed search then assemble relevant experience fragments. An execution agent can inspect these fragments and their referenced capabilities, while reflection separates concrete execution evidence from reusable abstractions. We study the framework across four benchmarks, five evaluation settings, and three language model backbones. Across backbones, AppWorld Normal and Challenge task goal completion average 51.91 and 27.99, respectively, exceeding the baseline without memory by 6.99 and 4.99 percentage points. An AppWorld ablation associates directed connections with an additional improvement of 2.08 points over independent operation cards. The results motivate composition of reusable operations while exposing tradeoffs in retrieval overhead and conditions for valid reuse.

title: ixi-sLM: On-Device sLM for AI Call Agent Service
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on On-Device Intelligence: Foundation Models under Real-World Constraints
summary: Running an AI call agent on-device makes it private, network-independent, and free of per-query cloud cost, but shipping one as a real-world service imposes constraints a cloud deployment never faces: ~1GiB memory budget, in-call latency and thermal limits, static-integer NPU execution, Korean STT input far from sLM pretraining, and cloud-level quality expectations. We bring ixi-sLM, a 1.2B Korean sLM, to mobile NPUs through ON-DEVICE MODELING: domain-adaptive modeling trims the vocabulary by call frequency to shrink the embedding and LM head that take nearly half the model under INT4 transformer weights and refits the tokenizer to call speech (18% fewer tokens on call traffic), while task-aware quantization calibrates on real calls and assigns per-module mixed precision by activation sensitivity. A single domain-adapted model runs ixi-O's two production services, AI Call Summary and AI Call Answering, at 94% of a state-of-the-art cloud LLM's task-weighted quality; our on-device modeling carries that quality onto the NPU with only a marginal drop in overall score, in an 803MiB model (28% of FP16) at 23% of the CPU's per-call energy. The same recipe deploys across Qualcomm and Apple NPUs and serves several million ixi-O subscribers in production.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on On-Device Intelligence: Foundation Models under Real-World Constraints

title: MMA-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Agent Safety Evaluation
comments: 19 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track (Poster)
summary: Multimodal agents increasingly rely on visual interfaces to perceive state and select actions, creating an attack surface not captured by text-only safety evaluations. We study Visual Semantic Hijacking, in which deceptive but semantically meaningful interface elements, such as forged system alerts, cause an agent to depart from its authorized task. We propose a trajectory-guided procedure that identifies candidate injection points and inserts reproducible visual payloads into the observation stream. Using this procedure, we construct MMA-SafetyBench, which contains 1,083 adversarial trajectories across web automation, desktop GUI control, mobile navigation, document understanding, and video processing. Across nine evaluated models, Attack Success Rate (ASR) reaches 87.96%, while Semantic Compromise Rate (SCR) reaches 98.09%. A 1--3--5 scoring scheme distinguishes target-matching outputs, semantic disruption without a target match, and successful preservation of the benign task. Controls covering all nine models and five domains show that attacks persist under neutral prompts. A safety-priority prompt lowers ASR without eliminating the failure mode.
comment: 19 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track (Poster)

title: RA$^2$: Retain-Anchored Attraction Preserves Forget-Adjacent Utility in LLM Unlearning
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) unlearning is often evaluated primarily by target suppression and clean retain utility. These metrics can miss a local failure mode: a model may perform well on standard retain prompts, yet degrade on benign reasoning when prompts lie near the forgotten domain. This phenomenon is termed forget-adjacent utility loss. A fundamental question is: where should forget representations go after they leave the removed behavior? Successful unlearning depends not only on whether forget-conditioned representations depart from the harmful computation, but also on the direction in which they are redirected afterward. We propose RA$^2$ (Retain-Anchored Attraction), a latent-space unlearning method that redirects forget-token states toward nearby retain-supported representations while preserving higher-layer behavior on retain data. On WMDP and MUSE, RA$^2$ yields higher forget-adjacent utility than strong unlearning baselines at similar broad-utility levels. These results show that the migration direction of forget representations materially affects benign behavior near the forget boundary. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZacLing/retain_anchored_attraction.

title: STRATA: Self-Maintaining Structured Experience Graphs for Self-Evolving Language Agents
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can self-evolve at test time by accumulating experience: retrieving relevant memories before acting and writing new lessons back afterwards. Yet most are single-level: trajectories, distilled workflows and reasoning items all land in one undifferentiated pool indexed by embedding similarity, with no typed abstraction hierarchy. They never forget or deduplicate, and are prone to negative transfer, where a superficially similar but directionally opposite experience is recalled and its concrete steps are copied verbatim, actively harming the agent. We introduce STRATA, a structured, outcome-grounded, self-maintaining memory that organizes experience into a three-layer graph of atomic skills and code snippets, task workflows and generalized meta-frameworks, connected by typed edges. STRATA maintains itself through five mechanisms sharing one similarity geometry: a multi-dimensional similarity that scores retrieval by operation and target; a typed reflector crystallizing procedures from successes and pitfalls from failures; community detection that induces meta-frameworks; pressure-triggered garbage collection with articulation-point protection; and contrast edges that flag confusable, direction-opposite experiences. Across four interactive benchmarks (AppWorld, WebArena, ALFWorld, ScienceWorld), two frozen backbones and seven baselines, STRATA attains the best average score while simultaneously using the lowest latency and fewest environment steps of any memory-augmented method, and 44% fewer lines of injected memory than the most context-hungry baseline. We isolate two failure modes of prior memories: single-level memory degrades sharply as the task set grows, and single-level concrete memories suffer catastrophic negative transfer, which contrast edges repair, lifting ScienceWorld from 78.7 to 96.7 within the same system.

title: The Sum of All Summaries: PROPALIGN for Graded Proposition Salience Evaluation
summary: Identification and ranking of salient propositions in documents is indirectly involved in many AI tasks, but few papers define proposition salience scores clearly, make diverse data available, or evaluate models directly on the task. This paper proposes PROPALIGN, a multiple-summary-based approach for propositional salience score estimation, and releases PROPALIGNBANK, an accompanying dataset for the method with 138K alignments of over 35K propositions. We compare several approaches to salient proposition extraction in English across a broad range of spoken and written genres, and demonstrate that naively asking models for judgments leads to inconsistencies. By contrast, graded, summary-based metrics are more stable. We further observe that while single models perform worse than humans, an ensemble of models incorporating linguistic features approaches manual annotation quality ceilings. In addition, analyses of the model outputs suggest insights into how models can extract salient information with and without the use of summaries.

title: ELARSpeech: A 30K-Hour Dataset Across 675 Underrepresented Languages for Long-Tail Multilingual Speech Technologies
summary: Massively multilingual speech modeling has made remarkable progress in recent years, yet existing training resources and benchmarks still underrepresent much of the linguistic long tail. To address this gap, we introduce ELARSpeech, a large-scale multilingual speech resource comprising 30,202 hours of speech across 675 underrepresented languages, curated from the Endangered Languages Archive. Combining human-annotated and unlabeled recordings, the corpus spans diverse recording conditions, domains, and language families. Beyond corpus construction, our experiments show how ELARSpeech supports extending ASR and TTS capabilities to diverse underrepresented languages, with further benefits from pseudo-labeling unlabeled data. At the same time, our speech representation analysis reveals remaining limitations in transferring existing multilingual models to the linguistic long tail. Together, ELARSpeech provides both a resource and a testbed for extending multilingual speech technology further into the linguistic long tail. We publicly release the dataset, all trained ASR and TTS models, and the complete data construction pipeline to facilitate research on long-tail multilingual speech technologies.

title: Multiscale distributed MPC for Optimal Transport
comments: 9 Pages, 1 Figure, Submitted to American Control Conference 2027, under review
summary: In this paper, we present a novel multiscale formulation for the Optimal Transport (OT) of large swarms. The scheme is divided in two levels, a top-level OT formulation with a terminal penalty cost to handle time-varying densities, and a low-level, Model Predictive Controller (MPC) that allows agents to track the nominal velocity under control affine dynamics and rejects external disturbances. We show that the terminal-penalty dynamic formulation reduces to a regularized static dual, which agents solve in a distributed way to compute the nominal velocity.We also prove distributional input-to-state stability in the $1$-Wasserstein metric of the density flow with respect to the mismatch that the low-level and the target motion introduce, so that the tracking error only perturbs the macroscopic flow by a bounded, quantifiable amount. Finally, we demonstrate via simulations the effectiveness of the proposed method handling time-varying targets and state perturbations.
comment: 9 Pages, 1 Figure, Submitted to American Control Conference 2027, under review

title: Fully sequential Gaussian process regression for preference learning
summary: We study continuous global optimization problems in which the objective function cannot be directly evaluated; rather, we observe only which of two selected design points appears to perform better, subject to noise. Such comparisons complicate the use of Gaussian process regression because they yield non-Gaussian posteriors. We consider a fully sequential approximation, based on moment-matching, that yields a fast closed-form update of the metamodel's mean and covariance. We then propose DOVE, a fully sequential sampling policy that combines an information gain criterion with randomized sampling designed to control error accumulation. Under fairly standard regularity conditions, we prove convergence rates for both statistical error and expected simple regret that depend on kernel smoothness. To our knowledge, these are the first such rates for fully sequential approximate Bayesian inference in continuous global optimization.

title: Beyond Kinematic Tracking: Preserving Expressive Characteristics in Humanoid Whole-Body Control
summary: Whole-body control plays a crucial role in enabling humanoid robots to execute expressive motions. Faithful execution requires preserving both the intended action and its expressive characteristics. Existing whole-body trackers typically balance joint and keypoint tracking with physical stability across diverse motions, but these objectives do not necessarily prioritize the expressive characteristics of each action. Our analysis shows that lower average positional tracking error does not guarantee better preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics. To address this gap, we propose a residual learning framework with compensation objectives targeting amplitude, energy, body expansion, body lean, and pelvis height. To concentrate compensation while limiting interference with the underlying tracking behavior, motion-aware gating allocates correction capacity according to body-part activity, preserving larger correction ranges in more active parts and restricting them elsewhere. For each frozen tracker, we train motion-specific residual policies and distill them into a unified policy shared across motion categories. Simulation and physical experiments on the Unitree G1 across eight motion categories demonstrate superior preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics compared with the corresponding baselines.

title: Selective Next-Location Prediction with MetaModelSelect: A Lightweight Post-Hoc Confidence Metamodel
comments: accepted at IEEE International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI) 2026
summary: Next-location prediction can support proactive mobile-network decisions, but acting on unreliable predictions can waste resources. We apply MetaModelSelect, a lightweight post-hoc confidence metamodel, to selective cellular next-location prediction. The mobility-specific model combines a learned embedding of the predicted location with the four largest softmax probabilities and Softmax Concentration. It learns whether a frozen recurrent neural network's top-1 prediction is correct, using only its outputs and without retraining the backbone. On path-balanced Changchun cellular mobility trajectories, we evaluate backbones trained with cross-entropy (CE) and self-adaptive training plus entropy minimization (SAT+EM), comparing against eight scalar confidence scores, two location-aware lookup methods, and a raw-logit multilayer perceptron. Relative to maximum softmax probability, MetaModelSelect achieves mean per-run reductions in area under the risk--coverage curve (AURC), excess AURC (E-AURC), and area under the generalized risk--coverage curve (AUGRC) of 2.6%, 4.2%, and 3.0% for CE, and 2.0%, 3.3%, and 1.9% for SAT+EM. It also achieves the lowest reported mean risk at every evaluated partial coverage. The results show that MetaModelSelect improves confidence ranking in this mobility setting while leaving the underlying location predictor unchanged.
comment: accepted at IEEE International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI) 2026

title: A Master-to-Simulation Interface with Demonstration-Trajectory Guidance for Vascular Intervention
comments: 6 pages, 3 figures, submitted to IEEE journals
summary: Robotic vascular intervention can reduce radiation exposure to physicians and improve manipulation stability, but effective guidance remains challenging because conventional fluoroscopic images provide limited spatial information. This paper developed a vascular intervention interactive system that connects a real robotic master controller with the SOFA(Simulation Open Framework Architecture) physical simulation platform and reused successful operation trajectories as visual guidance in physical phantom experiments. Experiments were conducted to validate the master-to-SOFA control loop and to compare three guidance conditions: no guidance, centerline guidance, and successful-trajectory guidance. The control validation results showed reliable command delivery under velocity-mode operation. In the physical phantom experiment, centerline guidance showed no obvious improvement over no guidance. In contrast, successful trajectory guidance provided a clear performance benefit. Compared with the no-guidance condition, it reduced task completion time, collision number, rollback number, and rotation number by approximately 66.8%, 34.3%, 55.6%, and 66.7%, respectively. These results indicate that successful trajectories obtained under instrument-vessel interaction can provide practical guidance cues, offering a simple and effective visual assistance strategy for robotic vascular intervention experiments.
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, submitted to IEEE journals

title: EpiGuard: An Autonomous Infectious-Disease Early Warning Agent Platform
summary: Infectious disease outbreaks often spread rapidly before signs of widespread transmission become apparent, leaving a big challenge for rapid response and effective intervention. However, current infectious-disease early-warning systems face three major challenges: fragmented epidemiological evidence across diverse surveillance sources, highly uneven data availability across diseases and geographic regions, and delayed warning procedure caused by manual data collection, analysis, and reporting. To address these challenges, we present EpiGuard, an autonomous, continually self-improving agentic platform for timely and reliable early warning of more than 50 infectious diseases across different regions. EpiGuard proactively monitors and captures newly released official surveillance records, using the latest available evidence for risk assessments. It dynamically adjusts its analytical strategy across three evidence availability regimes, enabling reliable risk assessment under diverse data conditions, ranging from the absence of historical observations to sparse and abundant evidence. Moreover, EpiGuard learns from the successful execution process by preserving effective data-acquisition and analytical procedures as reusable standard operating procedures, enabling it to progressively generalize to previously unseen diseases and regions. We use officially released infectious-disease surveillance data from the China CDC and the United States CDC to evaluate EpiGuard's effectiveness. Experimental results demonstrate that EpiGuard outperforms state-of-the-art forecasting systems, improving forecasting performance by 9.68% and 14.04% on the China CDC and U.S. CDC datasets, respectively.

title: SERO: Learning from Executable Oracle Continuations for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Long-horizon agentic RL is constrained by the futures visited by the current policy. When rollouts fail to reach useful behaviors, improved credit assignment cannot provide supervision for states and actions that were never encountered. On-policy distillation (OPD) introduces teacher guidance on policy-induced states, and recent multi-turn variants improve how this guidance is scheduled, replayed, refined, or validated. However, they do not directly use the oracle-controlled future itself as the training trajectory. We introduce \textbf{State-Rooted Executable Rollout Optimization (SERO)}, which augments on-policy agentic RL with executable oracle continuations. SERO restores a state actually reached by the current policy and lets a training-only oracle continue interacting with the real environment, making the downstream observations and oracle actions themselves available for learning. It then applies \textbf{policy-reachability weighting}, which weights each oracle step by the frozen behavior policy's compatibility with the preceding oracle actions. This allows deeper supervision to become effective as the policy becomes more compatible with the oracle branch. The oracle loss is optimized separately from the base RL estimator and no oracle is used at inference time. We evaluate SERO on two challenging interactive-agent benchmarks, ALFWorld and WebShop, using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. On ALFWorld, learning the full executable continuation is substantially more effective than supervising only the root oracle action, while policy-reachability weighting further improves out-of-distribution performance.

title: RCER: Reconstructing Cross-Evidence Relations for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Iterative retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) accumulates knowledge from retrieved evidence to answer complex questions, but existing methods struggle to reconstruct entity correspondences and inferential dependencies across retrieved passages as new information emerges. We propose RCER, an iterative RAG method that reconstructs these cross-evidence relations directly from accumulated source passages. Inter-round relational evidence acquisition identifies entity correspondences and relational dependencies to drive dynamic problem decomposition and iterative retrieval. Reasoning context reconstruction independently constructs a coherent reasoning context through joint selection of complementary passages and derivation of cross-evidence inferences. Cross-evidence compositional reasoning leverages these inferences to establish entity correspondences and compose relations across selected passages for answer derivation. Experiments show that RCER outperforms the best baselines by 2.83 EM and 3.06 F1 points on average across three multi-hop QA benchmarks and achieves superior performance on narrative and implicit reasoning tasks.

title: KoAGE: Do Large Language Models Know, Learn, and Coin Korean Neologisms?
summary: Korean neologisms arise through diverse mechanisms, a demanding test of language models beyond lexical memorization. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce NeoTrace, an automated, rerunnable framework that collects and dates neologisms across genres. Its 4,271 entries support KoAGE, a cutoff-aware benchmark with three acquisition and two generation tasks---the latter, to our knowledge, the first to compare model coinages with attested neologisms under their original materials and community context. Across 21 models, lexical recall diverges from contextual inference: in a five-model temporal analysis, models define only 13-30% of cutoff-year words, yet can infer meaning from one usage. However, structural understanding remains limited: even correct definitions barely improve formation analysis of pre-cutoff neologisms. Given word-building materials, single models often follow human formation mechanisms, whereas multi-agent coinage favors abbreviation and depends on interaction framing. KoAGE thus separates what models know, learn from use, and coin.

title: Train to Stitch: Topology-Preserving Regularization for Interoperable Representations
summary: As large, powerful pre-trained models become more prevalent, there is growing interest in developing methods that allow different neural networks to be seamlessly combined with little or no direct communication between them. Take autoencoder-based data compression as an example: the ability to independently choose architectures and train encoder and decoder models, while still ensuring they work together, could fundamentally transform how such models are built, deployed, and updated. In this work, we introduce a novel approach that leverages topological regularization to align the latent spaces of two independently trained autoencoder models, entirely eliminating the need for coordination during training. We provide a conditional theoretical analysis showing how the structural agreement encouraged by our regularizer can translate into approximate geometric compatibility between independently learned representations. Reconstruction experiments validate this approach empirically, substantially narrowing the interoperability gap across multiple datasets.

title: Topology-Preserving Multi-Usage Pipe Centerline Refinement under Permanent Tubular Occupancy
summary:
Discrete multi-group pipe routers place channels on a grid or coarse graph. The resulting centerlines are topologically feasible but typically contain many axis-aligned corners. For permanently occupied fluid tubes---as in additively manufactured hydraulic manifolds---those corners are undesirable: they degrade geometric fairness and, in practice, flow quality. This technical report studies the downstream geometric stage that starts from a fixed routing topology and a feasible coarse layout, and refines tubular centerlines under permanent clearance.
  Unlike classical robotic path smoothing, which usually fair one temporary open trajectory, our setting is a branched manifold with declared terminal usages, finite tube radii, and static cross-group occupancy. We formalize the refinement problem, highlight the multi-usage junction conflict that a single shared branch point cannot resolve, and outline a hybrid trunk-share / junction-split parameterization with soft geometric costs and hard clearance acceptance. On a multi-group suite ($8$ groups $\times$ $8$ terminals, $r{=}2$) with capsule clearance, the refine reaches full hard-accept success, $κr\lesssim 1$, and about a $95\%$ relative drop in the soft objective. Physics-based pressure-drop optimization is intentionally deferred to a later PDE stage; here the objective remains geometric.

title: Scaling LLM Inference via Parallelism: Throughput-Latency Trade-off
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) serving systems must balance latency and throughput while efficiently utilizing distributed GPU resources. This challenge arises because inference consists of two fundamentally different phases: prefill, which determines time-to-first-token (TTFT), and decode, which determines inter-token latency (ITL). The use of tensor parallelism (TP), pipeline parallelism (PP), and hybrid configurations exposes different trade-offs between these latency dimensions, making the optimal parallelism configuration highly dependent on workload characteristics, latency requirements, and context length. Moreover, despite the widespread adoption of distributed inference, there is still limited understanding of how parallelism configurations should be selected under varying workload conditions and service-level objectives (SLO). In this paper, we develop a systematic framework for characterizing LLM inference parallelism via throughput-latency trade-offs, SLO-aware serving, and long-context scalability. We introduce the notion of parallelism operating regions by constructing TTFT-ITL feasible sets and Pareto frontiers across different workload compositions, thereby revealing a systematic transition from TP-dominant to PP-dominant configurations as workloads become increasingly prefill-heavy. We further formulate SLO-aware parallelism selection using goodput, showing that stringent TTFT requirements favor PP-dominated configurations, whereas relaxed latency constraints progressively shift the optimality toward TP-dominated configurations with higher serving capacity. Finally, we demonstrate that increasing context length fundamentally changes the relative advantages of parallelism configurations, with PP-dominant configurations exhibiting more favorable scalability and SLO attainment in the long-context regime.

title: Vision-Language Models Integrate Conflicting Evidence Like Biased Bayesian Observers
summary: Vision-language models must reconcile conflicting text and images. Prior work has characterized the resulting behavior in terms of modality biases--e.g., a "blind faith in text"--but why preferences vary across models, domains, and input conditions remains unclear. We develop a predictive account from a Bayesian perspective, positing that VLMs combine conditionally independent evidence from each modality with prior beliefs, subject to modality-specific biases. The resulting two-parameter cue combination model accurately predicts VLM preferences under unseen combinations of input degradation and transfers to new forms of unreliability without refitting. Separating evidence strength from integration bias explains how VLMs can follow text even while weighting visual evidence more heavily, reconciling reports of text and vision dominance under a single combination rule.

title: ForkGRPO: Efficient Exploration and Fine-Grained Credit Assignment for Diffusion Language Models
comments: 20 pages, 5 figures. The first two authors contributed equally
summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have advanced rapidly, yet strengthening their reasoning through reinforcement learning (RL) remains an open challenge. Any-order generation can suffer from entropy degradation, which narrows the reasoning paths available for exploration. Recent work mitigates this issue by applying standard GRPO with left-to-right generation. However, independently generating every rollout from the input prompt can leave alternative continuations from intermediate states underexplored, while trajectory-level advantages assign uniform credit to all tokens without distinguishing the contributions of individual reasoning segments. We propose ForkGRPO, an RL framework that couples efficient exploration with fine-grained segment-level credit assignment. It samples multiple continuations from high-entropy intermediate states along a reference trajectory, prioritizing textual boundaries and reusing shared prefixes. The continuations provide complementary learning signals: within-state group-relative advantages guide which continuations to reinforce, while Monte Carlo state-value differences indicate which reasoning segments improve expected outcomes. Among the evaluated architecture-preserving RL methods, ForkGRPO achieves the best performance on three of four benchmarks, while improving over the directly comparable JustGRPO by up to 1.2 percentage points and using up to 27.8% fewer generated tokens. ForkGRPO-Fast further achieves a $2.49\times$ training wall-clock speedup with negligible accuracy loss.
comment: 20 pages, 5 figures. The first two authors contributed equally

title: Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation
summary: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.

title: W-JEPA: Wavelet Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Wearable Activity Recognition
summary: A major challenge in wearable device activity recognition is the heterogeneity across datasets in sensor placement, channel count, sampling rate and subjects. Moreover, the motion patterns that distinguish activities often appear as subtle, scale-specific variations within otherwise similar waveforms. As a result, raw signals are often ambiguous, and models trained on them tend to rely on cues specific to a particular sensor setup or participant, which limits both cross-dataset transfer and generalization to unseen participants. Addressing this requires representations that preserve such activity-relevant, scale-specific variation. We introduce W-JEPA, a self-supervised framework that exploits the multiscale structure of inertial motion and leverages a joint-embedding predictive architecture, by organizing windows into a fixed grid of wavelet tokens indexed by scale, sensor axis, and time. These wavelet tokens help expose activity-specific detail within broadly similar raw signals, and serve as the units of masked latent prediction. W-JEPA predicts masked token representations supplied by an exponential-moving-average (EMA) target encoder. Because recovering a masked token requires relating motion at one scale and axis to motion at other scales and axes, the model learns the cross-scale, cross-axis structure of human movement. Across six wearable activity benchmarks, W-JEPA outperforms state-of-the-art methods under random-window splits and remains the strongest when subjects are held out, improving average macro-F1 by 8.7 percentage points over the strongest published baseline. These results indicate that physically grounded multiscale tokenization, combined together with latent predictive learning, provides a promising foundation for transferable representations of heterogeneous wearable inertial data.

title: A VR Training System for Robot-Assisted Vascular Intervention with Dual-Mode Control and Model-Based Interaction Response
comments: 8 pages, 7 figures, submitted to a IEEE journal
summary: Virtual reality training for robot-assisted vascular intervention requires accurate robotic control and effective feedback on guidewire--vessel interactions. This paper presents a VR training system combining asynchronous dual-mode command mapping with sensorless interaction estimation. The system supports velocity-controlled navigation and position-driven incremental manipulation. Guidewire deformation and a Hunt--Crossley-type contact response are combined and temporally filtered to estimate interaction intensity, while trajectory-based visualization supports post-procedure review. Tests confirmed distinct command-dispatch patterns across three velocity gears and the position mode. During hybrid-scene navigation, the estimated response remained low during straight insertion and increased as the guidewire bent within the vascular model. Trajectory analysis yielded a model-derived cumulative trauma work (CTW) value of 15.166 in normalized units and localized regions of elevated interaction. In a preliminary study with 15 novices, physical-phantom task success increased from 53.3% to 93.3% after VR training, while mean completion time decreased from 132.4 s to 96.7 s. These results demonstrate the system's dual-mode operation, deformation-sensitive feedback, and potential to improve subsequent physical-phantom task performance.
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, submitted to a IEEE journal

title: Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities
summary: We introduce FormCraft, a framework for representing acquired operations as first-class capabilities that can be recursively composed, directly invoked, and selectively retained in a persistent library through domain-specific verification. The framework separates capability well-formedness and public callability from later admission to persistent storage while preserving formation provenance and operational identity. We formalize recursive compositional closure over a uniform capability space and show that formed composites can be reused through the same public interface without re-forming their historical derivation. Experiments across continuous, discrete, propositional, and sequence domains demonstrate instance-independent reuse, independent checking, persistent acquisition, and reduced reuse-time search work under first-class exposure.

title: Optimistic Distributed Submodular Coordination with Applications to Multi-Target Tracking with Multiple Robots
comments: 8 pages, 1 figure, under review for the American Control Conference (ACC 2027)
summary: We provide a distributed online algorithm for multi-agent submodular coordination in bandit environments, i.e., environments whose evolution is unknown a priori and may even adapt to the agents' actions. We are motivated by multi-robot tasks such as target tracking, where the optimal actions change over time and the agents must track them rather than a single fixed optimum. To address such problems, we provide the Optimistic Distributed Online Greedy (O-DOG) algorithm, that leverages predictions about the environment's behavior and improves regret guarantees. The agents select actions simultaneously over arbitrary, possibly time-varying, network topologies, and each agent acts optimistically, i.e., leveraging predictions of its upcoming rewards, e.g., from forecasts of the targets' motion and of its neighbors' actions. We bound O-DOG's tracking regret in terms of the agents' prediction error and the bound never exceeds its prediction-free counterpart. Particularly, it is sublinear even when the optimal action changes at every time step, provided the predictions are accurate enough. We further quantify the suboptimality due to decentralization as a function of the network structure, and show that accurate predictions accelerate convergence. We validate O-DOG in simulated multi-robot target tracking.
comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, under review for the American Control Conference (ACC 2027)

title: WinARDet: Compressed Window Auto-Regression for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Grounding
summary: MLLM-based detectors formulate vision-language grounding as autoregressive coordinate generation, yet in dense scenes, they often collapse into a box repetition loop, repeatedly emitting identical boxes until the decoding budget is exhausted. We trace this failure to historical-answer attention takeover: Under full-history autoregression, repeated coordinate tokens in the growing answer history attract disproportionate attention, crowding out the attention sinks needed to attend to new visual evidence. % To break this loop, in this paper, we propose \textbf{Compressed Window Auto-Regression} (WinAR). This new mechanism partitions a long answer sequence into consecutive generation windows and restricts full token-level autoregression to the current window only while compressing each previous window into a fixed set of latent tokens that condition subsequent decoding. This design reduces the repeated exposure to raw historical coordinates that triggers the attention takeover, yet preserves cross-window dependencies essential for coherent multi-object generation. On RSDense, which contains 200-2,000 objects per image, our model WinARDet improves RexOmni F1-score (IoU=0.5) from 32.16 to 39.36 over the baseline, while reducing the redundancy rate from 35.48% to 13.00%. WinARDet also generalizes across decoding strategies and output formats, including parallel box decoding and polygon generation, providing a practical paradigm for long-horizon vision-language grounding across scene densities.

title: From Failures to Learnable Worlds: Policy-Conditioned Environment Generation for Navigation Agents
summary: Simulated environments enable scalable training data generation for embodied agents, but more data does not necessarily provide what a particular agent needs to learn. Existing environment-generation pipelines largely optimize generic properties such as realism, diversity, or task coverage, while different pretrained policies can fail for different environmental reasons. We therefore introduce WEDGE, a framework for weakness-guided navigation learning in which the failure modes of a pretrained agent guide the generation of training environments at each adaptation round. Given a pretrained policy, WEDGE uses an LLM to propose executable weakness features from contrasting successful and failed rollouts, automatically validates them on the diagnostic set, and selects the strongest validated weakness based on its success-rate gap. The validated weaknesses are then mapped to the environmental factors that control them. WEDGE varies these factors to construct environments in the difficulty regimes where the policy struggles, producing targeted training experience for adaptation. Across three navigation agents with different adaptation mechanisms, we find that policies exhibit distinct weakness profiles and benefit from different training environments. Weakness-conditioned adaptation consistently outperforms matched random and hard-example alternatives on ProcTHOR, while the resulting gains for Uni-NaVid and Gemini also extend to HM3D after ProcTHOR adaptation. Iterative re-diagnosis further shows that dominant weaknesses can persist or shift as the policy improves, providing updated guidance for subsequent environment construction. Together, these results show that policy failures are not only diagnostic signals, but actionable guidance for constructing training environments that target a policy's current weaknesses.

title: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents accomplish complex tasks through multi-turn interactions with external tools. However, malicious content embedded in user queries, tool descriptions, or environment observations can manipulate their decisions and induce unsafe actions. Adversarial co-evolution has emerged as an effective approach to strengthening LLM safety, but existing work primarily focuses on language-level safety or indirect prompt injection in web tasks. In this paper, we introduce AgentSafeEvo, a co-evolutionary reinforcement learning framework for agent safety built on an attacker-defender game spanning diverse tasks and attack types. The attacker learns to construct adversarial agent tasks that expose weaknesses in the defender's tool use, while the defender learns to complete tasks safely under these attacks. We further introduce learnability-guided task weighting, which uses within-task defender-reward variability to adjust each task's contribution to attacker and defender updates. Extensive experiments on agent safety and general capability benchmarks demonstrate that our method improves adversarial robustness while maintaining general agent capabilities.

title: Beyond the Trial-and-Error Loop: Hybrid Projection and Automated Tuning for Distributed Training
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 22 pages, 8 figures, 25 tables
summary: Configuring distributed LLM training across hundreds of GPUs requires jointly optimizing tensor, pipeline, expert, context, and data parallelism alongside micro-batch size, recomputation, sharding, and overlap, a combinatorial space where memory legality can hinge on a single byte of activation accounting. Today, teams navigate it through expensive multi-node trial and error, burning GPU-hours on crashes and suboptimal recipes. We present Primus Projection, which closes this loop with two coupled components. First, a hybrid projection engine that measures what it can and simulates what it cannot: GPU microbenchmarks on as few as a single device capture compute kernels and any in-scope communication; a sub-node downscale-measure-upscale workflow analytically restores out-of-scope collectives, FSDP overlap, and the full pipeline schedule at the multi-node target. A pure simulation mode runs entirely on CPU, enabling pre-silicon planning without any GPU. Second, the Primus Tuning Agent treats the projection engine as a fast scoring oracle (seconds per candidate instead of tens of minutes) and uses it to drive an intelligent search over the configuration space. A deterministic seed planner sweeps single axes; an LLM investigation loop proposes cross-axis combinations the planner cannot reach, with an analytic memory pre-filter that rejects infeasible candidates before any GPU time is spent. Validated on Llama 3.1 (dense) and Mixtral 8x22B (MoE) across two GPU generations, all projections stay within ~10% of measured multi-node throughput, and fidelity holds at production scale: 4.7% error on DeepSeek V3 671B at 1,024 GPUs and 1.9% on Qwen3-235B-A22B at 256 GPUs. In a Mixtral 8x22B case study, the Primus Tuning Agent discovers a configuration delivering +27% throughput over the published 4-node BF16 reference at the same scale, in under 30 minutes of single-node exploration.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 22 pages, 8 figures, 25 tables

title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
summary: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VideoHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VideoHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.

title: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Before Post-Training: An End-to-End Approach
summary: Agentic capabilities are increasingly important for modern LLMs, yet remain difficult to evaluate during pretraining. Existing approaches typically rely on static trajectory-derived tasks or likelihood-based proxies, which are lightweight but provide limited visibility into how base models behave in interactive environments. We introduce ASAP (Agent Scaffold Adaptation for Pretraining Evaluation), a lightweight framework for eliciting and evaluating agentic behavior from pretrained base models on end-to-end tasks. Rather than converting base models into chat-style agents, ASAP preserves the completion interface and adapts existing agent scaffolds through structured trajectory continuation, short reference prefixes, and minimal recovery mechanisms. Across software-engineering and deep-research benchmarks, ASAP yields discriminative end-to-end performance across base models and pretraining checkpoints. Beyond aggregate scores, ASAP exposes model-generated execution trajectories, enabling analysis of exploration, editing, testing, recovery, and task completion across training stages. These trajectories provide a behavioral view of how agent-relevant capabilities change during pretraining and how execution patterns differ after post-training. Our results suggest that end-to-end agent evaluation can complement conventional pretraining benchmarks by providing a practical diagnostic of interactive model behavior.

title: How Do LLMs Understand Legal Philosophy? Diagnosing Legal-Philosophical Reasoning in LLMs
summary: Legal reasoning is a fundamental capability for large language models (LLMs) to complete legal AI tasks such as legal judgment prediction. In legal practice, this reasoning is shaped by legal philosophy: a judge's view of the nature and sources of law guides how legal materials are interpreted and applied, so judges working from the same statutes and precedents can reach different judgments. Existing research has largely overlooked whether LLMs can understand legal philosophy and apply it in legal reasoning, an ability we call \textit{legal-philosophical reasoning}. To fill this gap, we introduce LePhilBench, a benchmark for evaluating the legal-philosophical reasoning of LLMs that comprises two benchmarking tasks and a dataset. The two tasks evaluate how well LLMs understand legal philosophy and how well they apply it in legal reasoning, respectively. The dataset is manually and meticulously constructed. Its test set contains 220 U.S. Supreme Court opinions. A law professor designed fourteen annotation questions on legal philosophy, and three law-trained annotators with formal training in jurisprudence answered all fourteen questions for every opinion, yielding 9,240 legal-philosophical labels. LePhilBench takes the first step toward exploring legal-philosophical reasoning in LLMs.

title: Comprehensive Comparisons of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms in Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive comparison of four representative reinforcement learning (RL) methods in autonomous vehicle (AV) decision-making, including: Fitted Value Iteration (FVI), Rollout Classification Policy Iteration (RCPI), Deep Q-Network (DQN), and a discrete-action adaptation of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (D-DDPG). The four methods are applied to the same AV decision-making problem at an unsignalized intersection and are compared in terms of optimality and safety, training stability, and training and decision cost. RCPI is the closest to a reference solution and has the most stable training process. However, it is the least data-efficient. D-DDPG reaches the second-smallest gap to a reference solution with the highest data efficiency, but has the least training stability. DQN is the most stable model-free method but has the highest collision rate. FVI achieves a lower collision rate than DQN, but is less data-efficient and less stable. Based on these results, we provide suggestions for selecting a method according to whether a model is available, the budget for training, and whether stable training is required.

title: A potential projection method for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with low regularity potential
summary: We propose a potential projection (PP) method for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) with low-regularity and singular potentials by replacing the potential with its Fourier projection (truncated Fourier series). This gives rise to an NLSE with projected potential (NLSEwPP). We rigorously establish its well-posedness under low-regularity potentials, and its convergence to the original NLSE. The NLSEwPP is then directly discretized by the standard time-splitting Fourier pseudospectral (TS-FP) method with the mesh size chosen according to the potential projection parameter, resulting in the fully discrete TS-PP-FP method. Numerically, TS-PP-FP consistently achieves optimal temporal and spatial convergence rates with respect to the regularity of the exact solution under low-regularity and even singular potentials. Compared with the time-splitting Fourier spectral method, TS-PP-FP attains the same convergence rates at significantly lower computational cost and preserves the mass conservation and time symmetry (that are lost in the Fourier spectral discretization of the time-splitting method); compared with the time-splitting FP method, it is substantially more accurate for low-regularity potentials with the same computational cost.

title: $S^3$-Nav: Structured Spatial-Semantic Decision Making for Language-Guided Robot Navigation
summary: This paper presents $S^3$-Nav, a structured spatial-semantic decision-making framework for language-guided robot navigation under partial observability. Rather than assuming a complete environment representation in advance, $S^3$-Nav incrementally constructs persistent spatial-semantic state while exposing only a capacity-controlled, task-conditioned view to the high-level policy. This separation decouples what the robot must retain from what the policy needs to inspect, allowing decision complexity to be controlled without discarding grounded evidence required for subsequent reasoning and validation. High-level navigation outputs remain provisional and are independently grounded and validated against persistent semantic evidence and current geometric observations before physical execution or task termination. Evaluations across multiple environments and object- and relation-goal tasks demonstrate that separating persistent state, decision-facing evidence, and execution authority improves closed-loop navigation reliability while reducing policy reasoning cost.

title: Recognition Is Not Grounding: Benchmarking Multilingual Financial Evidence Extraction
summary: Comparing financial disclosures across languages requires identifying shared accounting concepts and recovering all numerical facts that express them. Existing benchmarks evaluate aspects of these capabilities, but provide limited insight into whether both succeed on the same multilingual evidence. In particular, it remains unclear whether language models can recognize these concepts across languages and exhaustively recover their corresponding numerical evidence from the same contexts. We introduce MULTIFINGROUND, a benchmark designed to investigate this recognition-grounding gap in multilingual financial reports. Constructed from FY2025 disclosures of 90 issuers in English, French, and Greek, MULTIFINGROUND aligns independently authored reports through a shared accounting taxonomy and provides traceable fact-level annotations. The benchmark evaluates financial fact identification, concept recognition, exhaustive fact selection, and concept discrimination without candidate labels. Across 15 evaluated models, eight API and open-weight reference models achieve 97.3-99.4\% concept recognition accuracy, yet miss at least one target fact in 26.6-41.9\% of correctly recognized groups. Further analyses reveal substantial variation in concept discrimination and limited gains from the evaluated finance-specialized models. Our findings demonstrate that strong concept recognition can coexist with incomplete evidence recovery, highlighting the importance of evaluating semantic recognition and evidence completeness together.

title: EvoProbe: Evaluation-Driven Benchmark Evolution for LLM Agents
summary: Static benchmarks for large language model (LLM) agents face saturation and data contamination risks, motivating continual updates to evaluation tasks. However, aggregate scores and success rates offer limited insight into specific problem-solving bottlenecks and provide limited guidance for subsequent task design. We propose EvoProbe, an evaluation-driven benchmark evolution framework that integrates task generation, diagnostic evaluation, and feedback-driven regeneration into a closed loop. It combines verifiable subtask outcome scoring with evidence-supported multi-judge trajectory evaluation and distills phase-level bottlenecks, success patterns, and failure patterns into diagnostic feedback for generating new executable tasks. Across two rounds of cybersecurity experiments, evaluations of eight models on 66 tasks reveal phase-level performance differences and common failure patterns beyond aggregate scores. In a cross-round comparison with the Examiner model set and solver configuration held fixed, all eight models achieve lower Outcome scores on the updated tasks, with relative decreases of 11.8\% in mean Outcome and 40.0\% in mean Pass\textasciicircum{}3. These results support using fine-grained diagnostics to guide iterative task updates and probe agents' current capabilities and limitations.

title: A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain
summary: We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.

title: Learning to Select Features with Manifold Deep Unfolding PCA
summary: Unsupervised feature selection (UFS) is of great significance in image processing and pattern recognition. Nevertheless, existing model-based methods often rely on manually tuned hyperparameters, while deep learning-based methods generally require massive training data. To address these issues, this paper proposes an efficient manifold deep unfolding feature selection network (MDUFS-Net). Technically, we first incorporate the $\ell_{2,0}$-norm into the classic principal component analysis (PCA) framework, then unfold the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-based iterative algorithm into an end-to-end trainable network, thereby enabling automatic parameter learning. Moreover, a manifold optimization strategy is developed to improve the numerical robustness. On this basis, we further extend MDUFS-Net into an enhanced variant called MDUFS-Net+ by introducing the $\ell_{0}$-norm for more discriminative feature representations. Extensive experiments validate that our proposed MDUFS-Net and MDUFS-Net+ outperform state-of-the-art methods in the UFS task, with promising performance in clustering. Our code is available at https://github.com/xianchaoxiu/MDUFS.

title: Paraphrase Consensus Is Not Self-Consistency: Instruction Reliance and Robustness in VLA Policies
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies fine-tuned on LIBERO are trained and evaluated on the same ten instruction strings, and rewording the instruction changes base OpenVLA's success by -38.0 points. Test-time prompt ensembling, which improves language models, does not recover this loss in any setting we ran. Paraphrase consensus (the medoid action over K paraphrases) costs base OpenVLA 16.8 points when the training instruction is a member. Without it, the medoid of the paraphrases scores -32.4 points relative to the training instruction, and confidence-based selection scores -28.0. The same medoid over samples of one paraphrase improves on greedy decoding but stays -27.6 points below the training instruction, consistent with aggregation reducing variance without removing the bias the paraphrases share. A wrong-instruction probe measures how much of a policy's success depends on the instruction. Across three policies and four suites, paraphrases cost a policy only where this share is high, and the stronger policies lose a much smaller fraction of it than base OpenVLA. LoRA post-training on paraphrased instructions reduces the one-paraphrase effect to +2.0 points, against -32.0 for a matched control, reproduces across two seeds and on OpenVLA-OFT, transfers to withheld phrasings, and leaves the policy's reliance on the instruction unchanged.

title: Progress-Aware Distillation for Mitigating Stagnation in Small Language Model Agents
summary: While LLM-based agent systems have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in reasoning and solving complex real-world tasks, they also come with substantial token consumption and inference latency, limiting their practical deployment. To enhance the efficiency of agent systems, recent efforts have focused on transferring agentic capabilities from large-scale models to small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tuning-based distillation. Nevertheless, as interaction trajectories grow longer, involving extended reasoning-action chains and extensive environmental feedback, distilled student agents tend to experience progress stagnation: becoming trapped in unproductive loops characterized by persistent failed strategies and difficulty making meaningful progress. Our systematic analysis shows that this phenomenon consistently occurs across diverse SLMs and task domains. To address this issue, we propose Progress-Aware Distillation (ProD), which explicitly detects and penalizes stagnation in student-generated trajectories. ProD encodes the stagnation gap between student and teacher into an adaptive margin for dynamically penalizing possible stagnation. By iteratively applying this procedure, ProD enables student agents to progressively approximate teacher behavior. Extensive experiments involving 8 SLMs, ranging from 0.6B to 8B parameters, on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, demonstrate that ProD substantially mitigates progress stagnation while enhancing both the success rates and task-completion efficiency of distilled SLM agents.

title: Integrating Simulation and Chain-of-thought Reasoning in Multimodal-Language Models For Physical Reasoning
summary: Multimodal language models often need to reason about the physical dynamics of the world in order to answer questions appropriately. Various methods have emerged for solving physical reasoning tasks, and in particular, two leading approaches are Chain-of-Thought reasoning and physics-grounded simulation. However, relatively little is known about which particular problems can be solved by each approach. Some tasks may benefit from computationally expensive generative video simulations, whereas others may be solved equally well (or even better) with language-based reasoning. Our work addresses this by systematically comparing simulation and language reasoning across a variety of multimodal tasks involving physical reasoning, such as answering questions about fluid dynamics and elasticity. We draw a parallel with this to resource-rational theories of human cognition, which propose that people optimally trade off simulation and reasoning depending on task demands. We present a novel cognitively-inspired hybrid model which optimally trades off simulation and reasoning to improve model performance and computational efficiency. Our model is able to decide the appropriate method to solve a physical reasoning problem at test time, and finds an optimal balance between accuracy and cost. Further, our model can be trained on a smaller vision-language model that is only 4B parameters and deployed to improve performance on much bigger base models with $>$3T parameters like Gemini 3 Pro.

title: Traffic State Prediction and Control Using a Koopman Operator Framework with Polynomial Observables
summary: In this paper, we develop a Koopman operator framework for modeling and control of traffic flow governed by the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) conservation law. We show that the nonlinear dynamics induced by the Greenshields flow--density relation naturally motivate a dictionary of polynomial observables, while the controlled dynamics become bilinear in the lifted Koopman coordinates. A reduced-order Koopman model is identified from spatio-temporal traffic-density snapshots and used as the prediction model in a model predictive control (MPC) framework for ramp metering. The resulting Koopman-MPC is compared with two predictive control baselines that use, respectively, a fixed linearized LWR model and the nonlinear finite-volume LWR model. In a one-hour freeway experiment, the Koopman-based controller maintains the traffic density below the critical Greenshields value and closely reproduces the behavior of the nonlinear PDE-based MPC, with a maximum-density difference below 1%. The Koopman predictor also reduces the mean online model-evaluation cost by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the nonlinear PDE predictor. In contrast, the linearized LWR predictor is computationally cheaper but exhibits substantially larger prediction errors and yields a more conservative metering policy. These results demonstrate that the analytical structure of the nonlinear traffic conservation law can be exploited to construct an interpretable data-driven surrogate for efficient traffic prediction and control

title: More Than Seeing: Vision as Scalable Anchors in Native Multimodal Pre-Training
summary: Native multimodal pre-training trains a single model from scratch on text and multimodal data, enabling it to understand both language and visual inputs. However, how visual signals shape scaling behavior and support capabilities beyond visual understanding remains unclear. We investigate this question through controlled visual-content ablations across model sizes and training budgets. Specifically, we replace image embeddings with content-free padding token embeddings. Retaining visual content improves text prediction on image-text examples without materially changing the lowest text-only loss at a given compute budget, the optimal balance of model size and training data, or aggregate language scores. The relative multimodal loss benefit grows approximately as a power law of compute. To test benefits beyond understanding images, we evaluate spatial reasoning from text descriptions alone. Both conditions improve with model and data scaling. During training of the largest model, visual gains are most sustained in localization, navigation, and symbolic planning, which involve maintaining object configurations or composing spatial updates; gains in spatial relations, geometry, and physical commonsense are less consistent. These findings identify visual content as a scalable anchor for multimodal learning, with benefits that extend beyond visual inputs while preserving aggregate language performance.

title: Point-and-Play: Instrument Timbre Cloning from Music Mixtures
comments: Submitted to IEEE ICASSP 2027. Code and demo page are available at https://github.com/User-tian/Point-and-Play
summary: Neural instrument synthesizers can clone the timbre of a solo instrument, letting music producers make music with the sound they desire. However, an instrument of interest is often embedded in a fully produced, multi-instrument recording, beyond the reach of existing methods. Source separation before timbre cloning is an approach, but it may suffer from separation artifacts and is also likely a detour for the task. In this work, we propose Point-and-Play, a system that clones the timbre of a cued source directly from a polyphonic mixture and uses it to synthesize new pitches and velocities. To achieve this, we introduce a Cue-Gated Statistics Pooling (CGSP) module that extracts the timbre code of the cued instrument from adapted CLAP embeddings of the music mixture.
