AI.title_translation: 基于印刷忆阻器的低延迟有态逻辑加法器跨层协同设计
AI.tldr: 通过器件-逻辑-架构跨层协同设计，结合混合MAGIC与FELIX逻辑原语，将印刷忆阻器32位加法周期降低60-88%，实现最高16.4倍的工作负载加速。
AI.motivation: 数据中心型系统中存储与处理单元之间的数据搬运存在严重瓶颈，而现有的忆阻有态逻辑加法器通常将器件、逻辑和架构层割裂优化，难以兼顾逻辑原语、操作依赖与数据通路映射，导致算术执行效率受限。
AI.method: 提出跨层协同设计方案：在印刷电化学金属化（ECM）忆阻器上实验验证混合MAGIC和FELIX逻辑原语集，推导优化位间进位传播的全加器操作序列，并将其映射到位串行、位并行和位流水线数据通路架构中。
AI.result: 位并行和位流水线架构下的n位加法周期缩减至2n+6；32位加法所需周期较以往有态逻辑加法器减少60%至88%；在四种代表性工作负载中实现了3.7倍至16.4倍的加速比。
AI.conclusion: 跨层协同设计能够有效消除忆阻有态逻辑的延迟瓶颈，大幅减少运算周期并显著提升系统及工作负载级性能。
AI.translation: 在以数据为中心的应用系统中，存储单元与处理单元之间的数据搬运依然是主要瓶颈。忆阻有态逻辑（SL）通过直接在存储的阻态上执行布尔逻辑运算来解决这一问题。然而，其算术运算效率共同取决于器件所支持的逻辑原语集、操作序列的依赖结构以及其向数据通路架构的映射。以往的设计通常分别独立优化器件、逻辑和架构层，而本文将它们联合考量，协同设计了一种有态加法器。我们在印刷电化学金属化（ECM）忆阻器上实验验证了混合MAGIC和FELIX逻辑原语集，并推导出了针对位间进位传播进行优化的全加器操作序列。将该序列映射到位串行、位并行和位流水线数据通路中，使后两者的n位加法周期减少至2n+6。对于32位加法，该方案比以往的有态逻辑加法器减少了60%至88%的周期。在四个代表性工作负载中，相比以往设计实现了3.7倍至16.4倍的加速比。这些结果表明，跨层协同设计能够切实转化为工作负载层面的性能提升。
AI.summary: 本文针对忆阻有态逻辑算术效率受限的问题，提出了器件、逻辑和架构的跨层协同设计加法器。通过在印刷ECM忆阻器上组合MAGIC与FELIX原语并优化进位传播，将n位加法周期降至2n+6，在32位加法中减少了60-88%的运算周期，并在多种工作负载中实现了3.7-16.4倍的性能加速。
AI.keywords: 忆阻器,有态逻辑,全加器,跨层协同设计,存算一体
AI.comments: 该论文的创新点在于打破了器件、逻辑原语和微架构之间的层级壁垒，通过跨层协同设计有效解决了忆阻有态逻辑加法中进位传播延迟高的核心痛点；并在低成本的印刷ECM忆阻器上进行了实验验证，对存算一体系统及柔性/印刷电子领域的算术逻辑设计具有重要指导价值。局限在于摘要未详细说明该设计在硬件面积与能耗开销方面的权衡。

title: RepForcing: Representation-Space Initialization for Autoregressive Video Distillation
summary: Distilling pretrained video diffusion models into few-step autoregressive (AR) generators typically combines student initialization with distribution matching distillation (DMD). An intermediate AR teacher can provide causally compatible targets for ODE initialization. However, causally compatible targets alone do not ensure high-quality generation under a short sampling schedule. We analyze the posterior-mean predictions favored by direct latent regression and empirically find that causal ODE initialization alleviates blur but still leaves fine detail unresolved. To address this limitation, we propose Representation Forcing, which learns few-step causal initialization through representation-space supervision rather than intermediate-teacher trajectory regression. The student is trained with teacher forcing by comparing clean predictions and training targets through normalized features of a frozen video diffusion transformer. This phase reuses the synthetic videos generated by a bidirectional model for AR teacher training and replaces both teacher training and causal ODE distillation, without generating additional causal ODE trajectories. The subsequent asymmetric DMD procedure remains unchanged. Empirical results show that, at four sampling steps, RepForcing better preserves generation quality than intermediate-teacher-based initialization before DMD. After DMD, our four-step chunk-wise model improves VBench Total from 84.04 to 84.66 (+0.62 points) and VisionReward from 6.326 to 10.074 (+59.25%) over the reported causal-ODE-based baseline.

AI.title_translation: RepForcing：自回归视频蒸馏的表示空间初始化
AI.tldr: 本文提出了RepForcing，一种用于自回归视频蒸馏的表示空间初始化方法，通过表示空间监督学习少量步骤的因果初始化，在少量采样步骤下显著提高了生成质量和细节保留，优于现有方法。
AI.motivation: 将预训练视频扩散模型蒸馏成少量步骤自回归生成器时，结合学生初始化和分布匹配蒸馏(DMD)的方法，特别是因果ODE初始化，在短采样计划下，仍无法解决精细细节和模糊问题，导致生成质量不佳。
AI.method: 论文提出了“表示强制”（Representation Forcing, RepForcing）方法。该方法通过表示空间监督来学习少量步骤的因果初始化，而不是通过中间教师轨迹回归。学生模型采用教师强制训练，通过冻结的视频扩散Transformer的归一化特征来比较干净的预测和训练目标。此阶段重用双向模型生成的合成视频用于AR教师训练，并取代了教师训练和因果ODE蒸馏，无需生成额外的因果ODE轨迹。随后的非对称DMD过程保持不变。
AI.result: 在四步采样下，RepForcing在DMD之前比基于中间教师的初始化更好地保留了生成质量。在DMD之后，四步分块模型相对于报告的基于因果ODE的基线，将VBench Total从84.04提高到84.66（+0.62点），VisionReward从6.326提高到10.074（+59.25%）。
AI.conclusion: RepForcing通过引入表示空间监督进行因果初始化，有效解决了少量步骤自回归视频蒸馏中精细细节未解决和模糊的局限性，与现有的基于因果ODE的方法相比，在生成质量和量化指标上取得了显著改进。
AI.translation: 将预训练视频扩散模型蒸馏成少量步骤自回归（AR）生成器通常结合了学生初始化和分布匹配蒸馏（DMD）。中间AR教师可以为ODE初始化提供因果兼容的目标。然而，仅因果兼容目标并不能确保在短采样计划下生成高质量内容。我们分析了直接潜在回归所偏好的后验均值预测，并经验性地发现因果ODE初始化可以减轻模糊，但仍无法解决精细细节。为了解决这一局限性，我们提出了表示强制（Representation Forcing），它通过表示空间监督而非中间教师轨迹回归来学习少量步骤的因果初始化。学生模型通过教师强制进行训练，通过冻结视频扩散Transformer的归一化特征比较干净的预测和训练目标。此阶段重用双向模型生成的合成视频用于AR教师训练，并取代了教师训练和因果ODE蒸馏，无需生成额外的因果ODE轨迹。随后的非对称DMD过程保持不变。经验结果表明，在四步采样下，RepForcing在DMD之前比基于中间教师的初始化更好地保留了生成质量。在DMD之后，我们的四步分块模型相对于报告的基于因果ODE的基线，将VBench Total从84.04提高到84.66（+0.62点），VisionReward从6.326提高到10.074（+59.25%）。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种创新的自回归视频蒸馏方法RepForcing，旨在解决现有因果ODE初始化在短采样计划下难以保留精细细节和生成质量的局限性。RepForcing通过表示空间监督学习少量步骤的因果初始化，利用冻结视频扩散Transformer的归一化特征进行训练，从而取代了传统的教师训练和因果ODE蒸馏。实验结果表明，RepForcing显著提高了生成质量和VBench Total、VisionReward等量化指标，尤其是在四步采样下，表现优于基于因果ODE的基线。
AI.keywords: 自回归视频蒸馏, 表示强制, 因果初始化, 扩散模型, 少量步骤生成
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于用表示空间监督取代了轨迹回归，进行因果初始化，通过重用现有合成视频并避免生成额外的ODE轨迹，简化了过程。这种方法有效增强了少量步骤自回归视频蒸馏中的细节保留和整体生成质量，这对于高效视频生成至关重要。

title: From Spectral to Frobenius: When Muon Loses Its Spectral Implicit Bias
summary: Prior work on implicit bias shows that gradient descent selects the Frobenius max-margin direction on linearly separable problems, whereas Fan et al. (2025) established spectral max-margin behavior for spectral-norm steepest descent methods, including idealized Muon with exact orthogonalization. In practice, however, Muon approximates orthogonalization using finite Newton-Schulz iterations and a positive stabilization constant. We prove that these implementation choices cause Muon to select the Frobenius rather than the spectral max-margin direction in linear classification with separable data. We also establish this behavior for both exponential moving average and Nesterov-style momentum. The key technical ingredient is a summable perturbation argument showing that the resulting parameter trajectories remain at bounded distance from those of gradient descent. We then disentangle the roles of Newton-Schulz iteration count, the stabilization constant, and the Newton-Schulz polynomial, revealing distinct asymptotic behaviors, including directions that achieve neither Frobenius nor spectral max-margin. Finally, we show that Muon can recover its spectral max-margin bias with Newton-Schulz iterations growing logarithmically over training.

AI.title_translation: 从谱到弗罗贝尼乌斯：当Muon失去其谱隐式偏置时
AI.tldr: 实践中，由于有限的牛顿-舒尔茨迭代和正稳定常数，Muon算法失去了其理想化的谱最大裕度隐式偏置，转而选择弗罗贝尼乌斯最大裕度方向。
AI.motivation: 先前的研究表明，理想化的Muon算法具有谱最大裕度行为，但实际实现中Muon的行为与此不同。本文旨在解释为何实践中的Muon会失去其谱隐式偏置，并揭示其背后的机制。
AI.method: 通过可求和扰动论证，证明了实际Muon的参数轨迹与梯度下降的轨迹保持有界距离。研究了牛顿-舒尔茨迭代次数、稳定常数和牛顿-舒尔茨多项式的作用，揭示了不同的渐近行为。
AI.result: 证明了在可分离数据的线性分类中，Muon的实现选择（有限牛顿-舒尔茨迭代和正稳定常数）导致其选择弗罗贝尼乌斯而非谱最大裕度方向，这对于指数移动平均和Nesterov动量也成立。分析揭示了不同的渐近行为，包括既非弗罗贝尼乌斯也非谱最大裕度的方向。最后，发现当牛顿-舒尔茨迭代次数随训练对数增长时，Muon可以恢复其谱最大裕度偏置。
AI.conclusion: 实际实现中的Muon算法因其特定的实现选择而失去了谱隐式偏置，转而表现出弗罗贝尼乌斯隐式偏置。然而，通过调整牛顿-舒尔茨迭代次数，可以使其恢复谱最大裕度偏置。
AI.translation: 隐式偏置的先前工作表明，梯度下降在线性可分离问题上选择弗罗贝尼乌斯最大裕度方向，而Fan等人（2025）为谱范数最速下降方法（包括具有精确正交化的理想化Muon）建立了谱最大裕度行为。然而，在实践中，Muon使用有限的牛顿-舒尔茨迭代和正稳定常数来近似正交化。我们证明，这些实现选择导致Muon在具有可分离数据的线性分类中选择弗罗贝尼乌斯而非谱最大裕度方向。我们还为指数移动平均和Nesterov式动量建立了这种行为。关键的技术要素是可求和扰动论证，表明所得的参数轨迹与梯度下降的轨迹保持有界距离。然后，我们解开牛顿-舒尔茨迭代次数、稳定常数和牛顿-舒尔茨多项式的作用，揭示了不同的渐近行为，包括既非弗罗贝尼乌斯也非谱最大裕度的方向。最后，我们表明，当牛顿-舒尔茨迭代次数随训练对数增长时，Muon可以恢复其谱最大裕度偏置。
AI.summary: 本研究探讨了Muon算法在实践中如何失去其理想化的谱隐式偏置。以往理论认为Muon具有谱最大裕度行为，但本文证明，由于实际实现中有限的牛顿-舒尔茨迭代和稳定常数，Muon转而选择弗罗贝尼乌斯最大裕度方向。该行为也适用于带有动量的Muon。通过扰动论证，论文分析了不同实现参数对渐近行为的影响，并指出通过对数增长的牛顿-舒尔茨迭代次数，Muon可以恢复其谱偏置。
AI.keywords: 隐式偏置, Muon, 谱最大裕度, 弗罗贝尼乌斯最大裕度, 梯度下降
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过严谨的数学证明，弥合了Muon算法理论行为与实际实现之间存在的差距。它揭示了看似微小的实现细节（如近似正交化）如何显著改变算法的隐式偏置，从谱最大裕度转向弗罗贝尼乌斯最大裕度。这一发现对于理解和设计鲁棒的优化算法具有重要意义，并为如何在实践中恢复或控制特定隐式偏置提供了指导。

title: ACR-Net: Mitigating Semantic Dominance via Contrastive Acoustic-Semantic Decoupling
comments: 5 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables. Published in Interspeech 2026
summary: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) models and Audio LLMs fail when vocal tone contradicts textual semantics. Extensive training on congruent data engenders a rigid semantic prior, causing "Semantic Dominance", a severe text bias during cross-modal conflicts. We introduce the ASPIRE benchmark of adversarial audio-text pairs across four conflict types, alongside two metrics: Semantic Overconfidence Penalty (SOP) and Latent Decoupling Degree (LDD). Unlike fusion methods that merely re-weight collapsed features, our Acoustic Conflict Resolution Network (ACR-Net) uses Cross-Modal Attention and Contrastive Decoupling Loss to disentangle contradictory representations into orthogonal latent spaces. Experiments show existing models fail under polarity conflicts due to extreme semantic overconfidence. Conversely, ACR-Net preserves acoustic fidelity, maintaining high LDD to drive SOP near zero, achieving superior Acoustic Accuracy (ACC) in both adversarial and standard scenarios.
comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables. Published in Interspeech 2026

AI.title_translation: ACR-Net：通过对比声学-语义解耦减轻语义主导效应
AI.tldr: 现有语音情感识别（SER）模型和音频大型语言模型（Audio LLMs）在语音语调与文本语义冲突时因“语义主导效应”而失效。ACR-Net通过对比声学-语义解耦，将矛盾表示解耦到正交空间，有效减轻语义过自信，在对抗性和标准场景下均实现卓越的声学准确性。
AI.motivation: 语音情感识别（SER）模型和音频大型语言模型（Audio LLMs）在语音语调与文本语义矛盾时会失效。这是因为在一致性数据上进行大量训练会产生僵化的语义先验，导致在跨模态冲突中出现严重的文本偏差，即“语义主导效应”。
AI.method: 本文引入了ASPIRE基准，包含四种冲突类型的对抗性音频-文本对，并提出了两种度量标准：语义过自信惩罚（SOP）和潜在解耦度（LDD）。ACR-Net（声学冲突解决网络）通过使用跨模态注意力（Cross-Modal Attention）和对比解耦损失（Contrastive Decoupling Loss）将矛盾的声学和语义表示解耦到正交的潜在空间中，以减轻语义主导效应。
AI.result: 实验表明，现有模型在极度语义过自信的情况下，在极性冲突下会失败。ACR-Net能够保持声学保真度，维持高LDD，并使SOP接近零，在对抗性场景和标准场景中均实现了卓越的声学准确性（ACC）。
AI.conclusion: ACR-Net通过对比声学-语义解耦，能够有效减轻语音情感识别和音频大型语言模型中的“语义主导效应”，显著提升模型在处理跨模态冲突时的性能和准确性。
AI.translation: 语音情感识别（SER）模型和音频大型语言模型（Audio LLMs）在语音语调与文本语义矛盾时会失效。在一致性数据上进行大量训练会产生僵化的语义先验，导致“语义主导效应”，即在跨模态冲突中出现严重的文本偏差。我们引入了ASPIRE基准，其中包含四种冲突类型的对抗性音频-文本对，以及两种度量标准：语义过自信惩罚（SOP）和潜在解耦度（LDD）。与仅重新加权塌缩特征的融合方法不同，我们的声学冲突解决网络（ACR-Net）使用跨模态注意力（Cross-Modal Attention）和对比解耦损失（Contrastive Decoupling Loss）将矛盾的表示解耦到正交的潜在空间中。实验表明，现有模型在极度语义过自信的情况下，在极性冲突下会失败。相反，ACR-Net保持了声学保真度，维持高LDD以使SOP接近零，在对抗性场景和标准场景中均实现了卓越的声学准确性（ACC）。
AI.summary: 该论文旨在解决语音情感识别（SER）和音频大型语言模型（Audio LLMs）中因文本偏见导致的“语义主导效应”，即当语音语调与文本语义冲突时模型失效的问题。为此，作者提出了ASPIRE基准，并引入了语义过自信惩罚（SOP）和潜在解耦度（LDD）两种评估指标。核心贡献是ACR-Net（声学冲突解决网络），它利用跨模态注意力和对比解耦损失将矛盾的声学和语义表示解耦到正交的潜在空间。实验结果表明，ACR-Net能够有效降低语义过自信，保持声学保真度，并在对抗性和标准场景下均表现出优于现有模型的声学准确性。
AI.keywords: 语义主导效应, 语音情感识别, 音频大型语言模型, 对比解耦, 跨模态冲突
AI.comments: ACR-Net的创新之处在于其通过对比解耦明确地将冲突的声学和语义特征分离，超越了简单的特征融合方法。引入ASPIRE基准和SOP、LDD等新颖的评估指标，对于解决跨模态冲突问题具有重要意义。这项工作对于开发更鲁棒、更可靠的语音情感识别和音频大型语言模型具有重要价值。

title: Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents
summary: Long coding agent sessions outgrow the model's context window, so agents compact: older history is replaced by something shorter, usually a model-written summary. A summary selects and rewords, and the agent cannot see what was lost. Existing work has explored a range of compaction techniques, but comparatively little attention has been paid to their effectiveness with lightweight models, including those deployed locally or used for high-volume workloads. Here, we present transparent-compact, a simple deterministic method for the open-source Pi coding agent, designed specifically for use with such models and with the purpose of maximising the transparency of the agent's view of its own compacted context. It guarantees that user and assistant prose in its context is unchanged by a model or algorithm, and explicitly flags where compaction has stripped information. We compare it with Pi's default model-written summary compaction and with pi-vcc, a popular deterministic method with similar methods but without verbatim retention of prose. Our benchmarks run on four models of varying performance levels, with emphasis on Qwen3.8-27B: a lightweight model at the top end of what consumer hardware can serve locally. On sets probing commitments (rules the user set which exist only in the conversation) and recall of facts, transparent-compact matched or outperformed both alternatives. In particular, it showed an advantage in avoiding confident blunders, i.e. assertion of false information as opposed to recognizing that something was not recalled. Even with a frontier model, its advantage was present but smaller. We argue that transparent-compact spares lightweight models from reasoning or searching their way around what compaction lost, and results in improved recall and application of information as a result, without the need for task or context-specific structuring of the session history.

AI.title_translation: 最大化上下文压缩的透明度提升轻量级编程智能体对事实与约定的留存能力
AI.tldr: 论文提出了一种确定性上下文压缩方法 transparent-compact，通过完全保留原对话文本并明确标记信息缺失位置，大幅提升了轻量级编程智能体对事实和规则的保留能力，显著减少了盲目幻觉。
AI.motivation: 在长会话编程中，现有的模型生成摘要等上下文压缩方法会重述并丢失细节，导致智能体无法感知丢失的内容；而现有研究较少关注这些压缩方法在消费级或高吞吐的轻量级模型上的表现与有效性。
AI.method: 为开源 Pi 编程智能体提出了一种确定性上下文压缩方法 transparent-compact。该方法严格保持上下文中的用户与助手原始文本不被模型或算法篡改，并显式标记压缩过程中被剥离信息的位置，最大化智能体对压缩状态的透明度感知。
AI.result: 在事实召回与用户约定规则的评测中，transparent-compact 在以 Qwen3.8-27B 为重点的四种不同水平模型上均持平或优于默认摘要压缩及 pi-vcc 方法；其最突出的优势在于显著减少了“盲目犯错”（即捏造错误事实而非意识到未被召回）的情况，在前沿模型上也展现出了稳定优势。
AI.conclusion: transparent-compact 使得轻量级模型无需费力推测或搜寻压缩中丢失的上下文，在无需针对任务或上下文进行特殊历史结构化处理的前提下，显著提升了对事实与规则的召回及运用能力。
AI.translation: 长时间的编程智能体交互会超出模型的上下文窗口，因此智能体会执行上下文压缩：较早的历史记录会被更短的内容所替代，通常是模型生成的摘要。摘要会进行筛选和转述，导致智能体无法得知丢失了什么信息。现有工作探索了多种压缩技术，但相对较少关注它们在轻量级模型（包括本地部署或用于高吞吐工作负载的模型）上的有效性。在本文中，我们提出了 transparent-compact，这是一种专为开源 Pi 编程智能体设计的简单确定性方法，专门用于此类模型，旨在最大化智能体对其自身压缩上下文的透明度。它保证了上下文中的用户和助手文本不会被模型或算法篡改，并明确标记压缩剥离信息的位置。我们将该方法与 Pi 默认的模型生成摘要压缩以及 pi-vcc（一种流行且机制相似但不逐字保留文本的确定性方法）进行了对比。我们在四种不同性能水平的模型上进行了基准测试，重点关注 Qwen3.8-27B（消费级硬件本地部署的高端轻量级模型）。在测试约定（仅在对话中存在的用户设定规则）和事实召回的数据集上，transparent-compact 达到或优于两种对比方法。特别是，它在避免“盲目犯错”（即断言虚假信息而非意识到某事未能召回）方面表现出优势。即使使用前沿模型，其优势依然存在但有所缩小。我们认为，transparent-compact 使得轻量级模型免于在压缩丢失的内容中进行盲目推理或搜索，从而提升了信息的召回和应用能力，且无需对会话历史进行针对特定任务或上下文的结构化处理。
AI.summary: 本文针对轻量级编程智能体上下文受限与长会话压缩容易丢失信息的问题，提出了 transparent-compact 方法。该方法通过确定性地保留原始对话文本并明确标记信息截断位置，提升了上下文透明度，显著改善了事实和规则的记忆留存，并大幅降低了模型的盲目幻觉。
AI.keywords: 上下文压缩 (Context Compaction), 编程智能体 (Coding Agents), 轻量级模型 (Lightweight Models), 事实召回 (Fact Retention)
AI.comments: 该研究切中端侧/本地大模型落地的关键痛点：轻量级模型因推理与语义纠错能力较弱，在面对模糊或有损的摘要压缩时极易产生盲目自信的幻觉。transparent-compact 放弃了传统的“二次模型摘要”思路，采用确定性的“原样保留+显式标记缺失”策略，方法简单直接、计算开销小且工程落地友好。局限在于其主要针对 Pi 智能体测试，且当对话极度冗长而导致大量文本必须彻底截断时，单纯的原文本保留策略是否能平衡足够长跨度的宏观上下文仍有待进一步验证。

title: KANLab: TensorFlow Playground for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
summary: KANLab is a browser-based visualization tool designed to interactively teach the core concepts of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN), forked from the widely successful TensorFlow Playground. To maximize educational clarity, KANLab omits residual connections and learnable scaling parameters found in modern KAN implementations, ensuring that displayed B-spline activation curves directly correspond to their underlying trainable control points. Users can inspect and modify activation functions, initialization schemes and observe gradient descent correcting manual disruptions. Furthermore, user can explore phenomena such as activation variance, interactive pruning, and re\-/training within a compact 2D machine learning setting. KANLab is open-source and available at https://kanlab.app/

AI.tldr: KANLab 是一个基于浏览器的可视化工具，用于交互式地教授 Kolmogoro-Arnold 网络 (KAN) 的核心概念，它简化了现代 KAN 的实现，以便于教育和探索。
AI.motivation: 旨在通过交互式可视化工具，清晰地教授 Kolmogoro-Arnold 网络 (KAN) 的核心概念，特别是通过简化其实现以最大化教育清晰度。
AI.method: KANLab 是一个基于浏览器的可视化工具，它从 TensorFlow Playground 分叉而来。为了教育清晰度，它省略了现代 KAN 实现中的残差连接和可学习的缩放参数，确保 B 样条激活曲线直接对应于可训练的控制点。它允许用户检查和修改激活函数、初始化方案，观察梯度下降，并探索激活方差、交互式剪枝和再训练等现象。
AI.result: KANLab 允许用户交互式地学习 KAN 的核心概念，观察激活函数、初始化和梯度下降的行为，并探索 KAN 相关的现象，如激活方差、剪枝和再训练，所有这些都在一个紧凑的 2D 机器学习环境中进行。
AI.conclusion: KANLab 是一个有效的教育工具，通过简化的可视化界面，帮助用户深入理解 Kolmogorov-Arnold 网络的工作原理和相关现象。
AI.translation: KANLab 是一个基于浏览器的可视化工具，旨在交互式地教授 Kolmogorov-Arnold 网络 (KAN) 的核心概念，它从广受欢迎的 TensorFlow Playground 分叉而来。为了最大化教育清晰度，KANLab 省略了现代 KAN 实现中发现的残差连接和可学习的缩放参数，确保所显示的 B 样条激活曲线直接对应于其底层的可训练控制点。用户可以检查和修改激活函数、初始化方案，并观察梯度下降纠正手动干扰。此外，用户可以在紧凑的 2D 机器学习环境中探索激活方差、交互式剪枝和再训练等现象。KANLab 是开源的，可在 https://kanlab.app/ 获取。
AI.summary: KANLab 是一个开源的、基于浏览器的交互式可视化工具，旨在简化 Kolmogorov-Arnold 网络 (KAN) 的教学和理解。它借鉴了 TensorFlow Playground，通过简化 KAN 模型（移除残差连接和可学习缩放参数）来提高教育清晰度，使用户能够直接观察 B 样条激活曲线与其控制点的对应关系。该工具允许用户探索激活函数、初始化、梯度下降、激活方差、剪枝和再训练等 KAN 核心概念和现象。
AI.keywords: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, KAN, 可视化工具, TensorFlow Playground, 教育
AI.comments: KANLab 的创新之处在于它将复杂的新型神经网络模型 KAN 简化并可视化，使其更易于理解和学习。通过借鉴 TensorFlow Playground 的成功经验，并针对 KAN 的特点进行定制化，它为研究人员和学生提供了一个直观的探索平台。其局限性可能在于为了教育目的而进行的简化，可能无法完全展示现代 KAN 实现的所有复杂性和性能。

title: The Cost of Executability: Temporal Margins for Continuous-Time Multi-Agent Path Finding under Closed-Loop Control
summary: Multi-agent path finding (MAPF) solvers are evaluated on the schedules they produce, not on how well those schedules can be executed. Specifically, continuous-time optimal solvers can achieve even lower cost than their discrete counterparts by scheduling agents with near-zero temporal/spatial separation, and by exploiting graphs with higher connectedness; however, such schedules may prove hard to execute under a realistic controller. We integrate AOC-CBS, an anytime-optimal continuous-time MAPF solver, into a fleet coordination framework in which each agent tracks its timed path using model predictive control, and we evaluate the resulting system on congested MovingAI benchmark instances with 21 to 40 agents. Without intervention, only a fraction of the instances complete execution. We then apply T-robustness by adding a time-margin, i.e., a minimum temporal gap between agents at shared locations, as well as spatial inflation of the agent footprint. Increasing either margin raises execution success, for a relatively small increase in the schedule's sum-of-costs; it also improves how closely agents adhere to the schedule: when tracking each agent's position throughout execution and comparing it against the position it should occupy according to the schedule, the mean discrepancy falls significantly as the margin increases. In general, the two margins have different effects; temporal margin decreases deviation, giving the controller room to stay on schedule. Spatial margin affects deviation less and instead increases the clearance between agents, so that the same deviation no longer leads to a blocking stall. They are nonetheless substitutes rather than complements: spatial inflation is almost free in schedule cost, but its effect on execution success is small and does not compound with a temporal margin already in place.

AI.title_translation: 可执行性的代价：闭环控制下连续时间多智能体路径规划的时间裕度
AI.tldr: 连续时间多智能体路径规划（MAPF）的调度方案在实际执行中面临挑战。本研究通过引入时间裕度或空间膨胀来提高执行成功率和调度依从性，尽管会带来较小的成本增加，但两者是替代而非互补关系。
AI.motivation: 多智能体路径规划（MAPF）求解器生成的调度方案在理论上表现优异，但其在实际控制器下执行时面临挑战，尤其是在连续时间最优求解器中，由于代理之间近乎零的时间/空间间隔，导致调度难以执行。本研究旨在解决调度最优性与可执行性之间的差距。
AI.method: 本研究将连续时间最优MAPF求解器AOC-CBS集成到一个车队协调框架中，其中每个代理使用模型预测控制来跟踪其定时路径。系统在包含21至40个代理的拥挤MovingAI基准实例上进行评估。为了提高可执行性，研究应用了T-鲁棒性，通过增加时间裕度（即共享位置处代理之间的最小时间间隔）以及代理足迹的空间膨胀。然后，比较了在不同裕度设置下执行成功率、调度总成本以及代理对调度依从性的差异（通过跟踪代理位置与调度位置的平均偏差）。
AI.result: 在没有干预的情况下，只有一小部分实例能够成功执行。增加时间裕度或空间膨胀都能提高执行成功率，并且能以相对较小的调度总成本增加来改善代理对调度的依从性（平均偏差显著下降）。两种裕度有不同的效果：时间裕度能减少偏差，为控制器提供保持调度的空间；空间裕度对偏差影响较小，但能增加代理之间的间隙，从而使相同的偏差不再导致阻塞停滞。两者是替代品而非补充品：空间膨胀在调度成本上几乎是免费的，但其对执行成功的影响很小，并且不会与已有的时间裕度产生复合效应。
AI.conclusion: 为连续时间多智能体路径规划（MAPF）的调度方案引入时间裕度或空间裕度能显著提高其在闭环控制下的可执行性和对调度的依从性。尽管两者都是有效的策略，但它们是替代关系而非互补关系，各自以不同的方式影响执行表现，系统设计者应根据具体需求进行选择。
AI.translation: 多智能体路径规划（MAPF）求解器是根据其生成的调度方案进行评估的，而不是根据这些调度方案的执行效果。具体而言，连续时间最优求解器通过安排代理以接近零的时间/空间分离，并利用具有更高连通性的图，可以实现比其离散对应物更低的成本；然而，这种调度方案在实际控制器下可能难以执行。我们将AOC-CBS（一种随时最优的连续时间MAPF求解器）集成到一个车队协调框架中，其中每个代理使用模型预测控制来跟踪其定时路径，并我们在包含21至40个代理的拥挤MovingAI基准实例上评估了所得系统。在没有干预的情况下，只有一小部分实例能够完成执行。然后，我们通过添加时间裕度（即共享位置处代理之间的最小时间间隔）以及代理足迹的空间膨胀来应用T-鲁棒性。增加任一裕度都会提高执行成功率，而调度总成本的增加相对较小；它还会改善代理对调度的依从性：在整个执行过程中跟踪每个代理的位置并将其与调度应占用的位置进行比较时，平均偏差随着裕度的增加而显著下降。总的来说，两种裕度有不同的效果；时间裕度减少了偏差，为控制器提供了保持调度的空间。空间裕度对偏差的影响较小，而是增加了代理之间的间隙，从而使相同的偏差不再导致阻塞停滞。然而，它们是替代品而不是补充品：空间膨胀在调度成本上几乎是免费的，但其对执行成功的影响很小，并且不会与已有的时间裕度产生复合效应。
AI.summary: 本论文研究了闭环控制下连续时间多智能体路径规划（MAPF）调度方案的可执行性。研究将最优连续时间MAPF求解器AOC-CBS与模型预测控制相结合，并在基准实例上进行了评估。结果表明，最优连续时间调度方案在无干预情况下难以成功执行。通过引入时间裕度（最小时间间隔）和空间膨胀（代理足迹），显著提高了执行成功率和调度依从性，且调度成本增加较小。论文进一步区分了时间裕度和空间裕度的作用，指出它们是增强可执行性的替代而非互补策略。
AI.keywords: 多智能体路径规划, 连续时间, 时间裕度, 空间膨胀, 可执行性, 闭环控制
AI.comments: 该论文解决了连续时间多智能体路径规划中理论最优性与实际可执行性之间的关键鸿沟。通过引入和分析时间裕度与空间裕度，为实际系统部署提供了实用的策略，并揭示了调度成本与鲁棒性之间的权衡。发现这些裕度是替代而非互补关系，对于系统设计具有重要的指导意义。

title: A Bregman Proximal Viewpoint on Neural Operators
summary: We present several advances on neural operators by viewing the action of operator layers as the minimizers of Bregman regularized optimization problems over Banach function spaces. The proposed framework allows interpreting the activation operators as Bregman proximity operators from dual to primal space. This novel viewpoint is general enough to recover classical neural operators as well as a new variant, coined Bregman neural operators, which includes the inverse activation operator and features the same expressivity of standard neural operators. Numerical experiments support the added benefits of the Bregman variant of Fourier neural operators for training deeper and more accurate models.

AI.tldr: 本文通过将算子层的动作视为Banach函数空间上Bregman正则化优化问题的最小化器，提出了神经算子的新进展，并引入了Bregman神经算子变体，数值实验表明其在训练更深、更准确模型方面的优势。
AI.motivation: 论文旨在通过Bregman正则化优化问题的视角，对神经算子进行深入理解和改进，从而提升模型的深度和准确性。
AI.method: 将算子层的动作视为Banach函数空间上Bregman正则化优化问题的最小化器，并将激活算子解释为从对偶空间到原始空间的Bregman近端算子。在此框架下，恢复了经典神经算子并提出了一种新的变体，即Bregman神经算子，它包含逆激活算子。
AI.result: 提出的Bregman神经算子变体（包括逆激活算子）具有与标准神经算子相同的表达能力。数值实验支持Bregman变体傅里叶神经算子在训练更深、更准确模型方面的额外优势。
AI.conclusion: 通过Bregman近端视角，不仅能够统一解释经典神经算子，还提出了一种新的Bregman神经算子，该算子在数值实验中表现出训练更深、更准确模型的潜力。
AI.translation: 我们通过将算子层的动作视为Banach函数空间上Bregman正则化优化问题的最小化器，对神经算子提出了几项进展。所提出的框架允许将激活算子解释为从对偶空间到原始空间的Bregman近端算子。这种新颖的观点足够通用，可以恢复经典的神经算子以及一种新的变体，即Bregman神经算子，它包括逆激活算子并具有与标准神经算子相同的表达能力。数值实验支持Bregman变体傅里叶神经算子在训练更深、更准确模型方面的额外优势。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种通过Bregman正则化优化问题视角来理解和改进神经算子的新框架。该框架将算子层动作解释为Bregman正则化问题的最小化器，并将激活算子视为Bregman近端算子。在此基础上，不仅能解释现有神经算子，还引入了Bregman神经算子，该算子包含逆激活算子且具有同等表达能力。实验证明，Bregman变体傅里叶神经算子在训练深度和精度方面具有显著优势。
AI.keywords: 神经算子, Bregman正则化, 近端算子, Banach函数空间, 傅里叶神经算子
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过引入Bregman近端视角为神经算子提供了一个新颖且统一的理论框架。其创新之处在于将算子层的动作与Bregman正则化优化问题联系起来，并由此推导出了Bregman神经算子。这不仅加深了对现有神经算子的理解，还为设计更深、更准确的模型提供了新的方向。该方法有望在处理复杂函数空间问题上展现出重要性。

title: HM3D-M3: A Benchmark for Multi-Agent, Multi-Modal, Multi-Object Goal Navigation
summary: Rapid progress in AI agents and robotics makes it a matter of the near future that humans are served by a team of robots. Such a team will receive several goals at once, each specified in whatever form is convenient for the human, such as a category name, a photo, or a spoken description. Existing benchmarks study multi-agent, multi-modal, and multi-object goal navigation in isolation, and a benchmark that places all three in one episode is missing. To fill this gap, we introduce HM3D-M3. A team of K agents starts at distributed locations in a photorealistic indoor scene and searches for an unordered set of M object goals, each given as an open-vocabulary category, an instance image, or an instance description. HM3D-M3 provides 1,000 validation episodes over 3,926 goals from 379 open-vocabulary categories, 100K observation-assignment training samples, and two team-level metrics, goal-level SR and makespan-normalized SPL. We further contribute two baselines. HiGA is a trained hierarchical goal assigner on top of a frozen open-vocabulary navigation policy, and LaViRA-M3 is a training-free team of VLM agents with shared mapping and progress analysis. Adapted multi-robot and zero-shot methods reach 16--27% SR, while our baselines reach 38--41% with complementary strengths and distinct failure modes. Furthermore, we deploy LaViRA-M3 on a heterogeneous three-robot team. Project page: https://robo-lavira.github.io/hm3d-m3/

AI.title_translation: HM3D-M3：一个用于多智能体、多模态、多目标目标导航的基准
AI.tldr: 本文推出了 HM3D-M3 基准，旨在解决多智能体、多模态和多目标目标导航的集成难题，并提出了两种有效的基线方法。
AI.motivation: 现有的基准通常孤立地研究多智能体、多模态和多目标目标导航，缺乏将这三者结合在单个评测 episode 中的统一基准。为此需要一个综合基准来促进多机器人团队在真实场景中的协同工作能力。
AI.method: 引入了 HM3D-M3 基准，并提出了两个基线方法：HiGA（基于冻结开放词汇导航策略的层次化目标分配器）和 LaViRA-M3（免训练的 VLM 智能体团队，具备共享建图与进度分析功能）。
AI.result: 现有适应的多机器人和零样本方法的成功率（SR）在 16-27% 之间，而作者提出的基线方法达到了 38-41% 的成功率，展现出互补的优势和不同的失效模式，同时还在异构三机器人团队上成功部署了 LaViRA-M3。
AI.conclusion: HM3D-M3 成功填补了集成多智能体、多模态和多目标导航的基准空白，为未来具身 AI 团队的研究提供了坚实的基础和评估标准。
AI.translation: 人工智能代理和机器人的快速进展使得人类在不久的将来会被机器人团队服务。这样一个团队将同时接收几个目标，每个目标可以由人类方便的任何形式指定，例如类别名称、照片或口头描述。现有的基准孤立地研究多智能体、多模态和多目标导航，缺乏将这三者结合在一个 episode 中的基准。为了填补这一空白，我们引入了 HM3D-M3。一组 K 个智能体从光度真实感室内场景中的分布式位置开始，搜索无序的一组 M 个目标，每个目标给定的形式为开放词汇类别、实例图像或实例描述。HM3D-M3 提供了来自 379 个开放词汇类别的 3,926 个目标的 1,000 个验证 episode、100K 个观察-分配训练样本以及两个团队级指标：目标级 SR 和 makespan 归一化的 SPL。我们进一步贡献了两个基线。HiGA 是一个在冻结的开放词汇导航策略之上的训练得到的层次化目标分配器，LaViRA-M3 是一个免训练的 VLM 智能体团队，具有共享建图和进度分析功能。适应后的多机器人和零样本方法达到了 16--27% 的 SR，而我们的基线达到了 38--41% 的 SR，具有互补的优势和不同的失败模式。此外，我们在异构的三机器人团队上部署了 LaViRA-M3。项目页面：https://robo-lavira.github.io/hm3d-m3/
AI.summary: 本文提出了 HM3D-M3，这是一个全新的基准，用于评估多智能体、多模态和多目标导航。该基准要求一组智能体在真实室内场景中协作，寻找一组通过类别名、图像或描述指定的无序目标。论文还提供了评估指标、训练样本以及两个创新的基线方法。
AI.keywords: Multi-Agent Navigation, Multi-Modal Goal, Multi-Object Goal, Embodied AI, Benchmark
AI.comments: HM3D-M3 是一个极具挑战性的多智能体、多模态、多目标导航基准，填补了该领域的空白，并通过两个强有力的基线推进了具身智能在复杂真实场景中的应用。

title: XViewRank: Overlap-Conditioned Score Fusion for LLM-Augmented Sparse Retrieval
summary: Large language models can reduce vocabulary mismatch in sparse retrieval by generating alternative views of a query. Once these views are searched independently, however, their ranked lists may be complementary, redundant, or affected by query drift, making fixed fusion suboptimal. We present XViewRank, a lightweight retrieval-side method for conditionally fusing BM25 results from an original query, a hypothesis view, and a step-back view. For each pooled candidate, XViewRank retains three normalized BM25 scores and three query-level overlaps between the retrieved result sets. A small nonlinear scorer uses the overlaps as context that changes how the view-specific scores are interpreted, without jointly encoding query and passage text. Under a matched-input protocol, XViewRank improves nDCG@10 and MAP numerically over reciprocal rank fusion on both TREC DL 2019 and 2020, with a statistically significant MAP gain on DL19. Additional analyses show that the clearest benefit occurs when the view rankings have low agreement, while the evidence on DL20 is weaker. The results support overlap-conditioned score fusion as a compact retrieval-side alternative to fixed fusion, while also delimiting where its advantage is empirically established.

title: DreamHMR: From Video Generation to Human Motion Modeling via Structural Focusing
summary: Human mesh recovery (HMR) provides a geometric foundation for understanding human motion, but accurately reconstructing both body motion and fine hand articulation from videos remains challenging, especially in real-world scenes where occlusion and partial visibility are common. Video generation pretraining offers rich spatial and temporal priors for this task, but its focus on visual synthesis leaves a gap between these representations and explicit human geometry. We present DreamHMR, a general framework that adapts video generation priors for complete body-and-hand reconstruction. It follows a global-to-local strategy, first grounding video representations in human geometry and then refining body and hand detail with reliable local evidence. Global Body Representation Transfer trains the video backbone to predict complete human renderings, turning its native prediction task into a means of learning surface correspondence and posed geometry. Local Joint Feature Enhancement combines contextual estimates with reliable local evidence to recover fine body and hand detail, while limiting interference from occluders and background. Experiments on five datasets with four video backbones demonstrate strong reconstruction performance across backbone families. Under a unified evaluation protocol, our best model outperforms the best existing methods on all reported metrics of 3DPW, EMDB-1, and RICH, reducing body MPJPE by 4.2%, 4.7%, and 6.1%, respectively. In more challenging occlusion settings on held-out BEDLAM and EgoBody sequences, DreamHMR reduces overall body and hand MPJPE by 7.0% and 10.0%, respectively. Our code will be made publicly available.

title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
summary: We present eMOOD, an entropy-guided evolution of the Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection (MOOD) framework for high-order finite-volume methods on unstructured meshes. A novel troubled-cell indicator based on numerical entropy production replaces the classical relaxed discrete maximum principle. Using entropy generation as a physically motivated measure of non-smoothness, the detector targets shocks, contact discontinuities and under-resolved flow features with a compact stencil. Compared with conventional MOOD detection, eMOOD reduces flagged cells by up to 75%, improving efficiency and reducing memory-access overhead. The detector is used within both the classical MOOD cascade of progressively reduced-order schemes and a novel MOOD-CWENO hybrid, which retains inexpensive linear reconstruction in smooth regions and activates nonlinear high-order reconstruction only where needed. Implemented in the open-source parallel solver UCNS3D, the methodology is assessed on the Shu-Osher shock-entropy-wave interaction, double Mach reflection, supersonic forward-facing step, shock-helium-bubble interaction and triple material point problems. These benchmarks encompass strong shock interactions, shock-induced instabilities, multi-material interfaces and vortex-dominated flows, testing robustness, shock capturing and accuracy on unstructured meshes. Results show that eMOOD preserves the accuracy and robustness of reference CWENO and MOOD formulations while achieving speed-ups of up to 20% without loss of solution quality. Its compact detection stencil, reduced memory footprint and improved localisation offer a more scalable and efficient framework for massively parallel high-order compressible-flow simulations. title: Tactile-Guided Robot Learning: From Representation Learning to Foundation Models
summary: Tactile sensing is becoming central to robust, adaptive, and dexterous robotic manipulation. Beyond its traditional role in contact detection and reactive control, touch is increasingly used to learn transferable representations, condition manipulation policies, and support embodied physical reasoning. Yet existing surveys largely emphasize tactile hardware and perception, leaving the rapid shift toward learning-based tactile manipulation insufficiently synthesized. This paper reviews tactile-guided skill learning from a learning-centric perspective, organized by the functional role of touch across the learning and control pipeline. We examine tactile representation and policy learning, tactile foundation models, predictive and adaptive control, and generalization across objects, tasks, sensors, embodiments, and simulation-to-real transfer. Across these directions, we identify common design principles and remaining challenges in learning transferable physical representations, integrating semantic reasoning with contact-level control, and scaling tactile learning across heterogeneous data and hardware. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward tactile foundation and world models that can predict, reason about, and adapt physical interactions. Together, this review characterizes the transition of touch from a task-specific feedback signal toward a core modality for general-purpose embodied intelligence. An accompanying database of the reviewed literature and associated resources is available at https://sites.google.com/view/touch-in-robot-learning-review.

title: Seeing at the Edge: Energy Characterization of Vision-Language Model Inference on Edge Platforms
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are moving onto edge devices, but little is known about how much energy they draw on single-board computers with NPU or GPU accelerators, or where that energy goes. We measure total-system energy, latency, and thermal behavior of Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct and its text-only sibling on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-10H NPU and on a Jetson Orin Nano Super, on both CPU and accelerator, and separate the fixed energy of each request from the energy that grows with output length. Because the accelerators use different quantization and serving software, we compare deployment stacks rather than silicon. Three findings stand out. First, NPU offloading makes the Pi a much more efficient VLM platform: it cuts energy per generated token by about two-thirds, leaves the host CPU largely free, and avoids the thermal throttling that the CPU backend reaches in sustained use. Second, an image adds both fixed and per-token energy, but at typical response lengths generating the answer costs far more than processing the image. Third, the Jetson GPU favors short responses through its lower fixed cost per request, whereas the Pi NPU favors longer ones through its lower cost per output token; their energy curves cross near 40 output tokens.

title: StreamErase: Towards Ultra-Fast Streaming Video Erasing
summary: Current video object removal methods suffer from prohibitive latency (minutes per video) and non-causal processing that prevents real-time interaction. We present StreamErase, enabling sub-second latency with up to 26 FPS streaming generation on a single GPU. Our approach first augments a text-to-video model with mask input to generate high-quality videos that erase target objects and synthesize coherent backgrounds, but does not perform inference on the fly. As such, we progressively transfer the erasing capability from a powerful bidirectional foundation model to an efficient unidirectional streaming eraser, enabling long-horizon erasing without sacrificing visual fidelity. Several key challenges arise when generating videos over long, potentially infinite horizons: (1) bridging the domain gap from training on finite length and extrapolating to long horizons, (2) sustaining high quality by preventing error accumulation, and (3) maintaining fast inference, without increasing computational cost as the context grows. To address these challenges, we carefully designed sliding-window causal attention with attention sinks. By incorporating self-rollout with attention sinks and KV cache rolling during training, we simulate inference-time extrapolations with a fixed context window, enabling constant-speed generation of arbitrarily long videos. Finally, we establish a dedicated benchmark, LongErase, for streaming long-video object removal. Our model achieves strong performance compared to existing video object erasing models and generalizes well to real-world video scenarios, uniquely enabling infinite-length streaming. With StreamErase, users can input a mask and see the erasing results unfold in real-time, delivering a truly interactive experience.

title: In-Context Batch Black-box Optimization via Flow Matching
summary: Batch black-box optimization is important for expensive systems where many candidates can be evaluated in parallel, yet only a few rounds of evaluation are affordable. In this regime, effective batch construction must identify multiple promising regions while avoiding redundant evaluations, and conventional Bayesian optimization can require increasingly difficult batch-selection procedures as the batch size grows. We introduce Flow Matching for Thompson-Sampling Refinement (FMTR), an amortized approach that learns offline a continuous, history-conditioned proposal distribution from which variable-size batches can be sampled. FMTR is trained offline by conditional flow matching on Thompson-sampling argmaxes refined toward high-value regions via a horizon-dependent Langevin pushforward map, adapting the exploration-exploitation tradeoff over the optimization horizon. At test time, the model parameters remain fixed and batch generation requires neither task-specific surrogate refitting nor numerical acquisition optimization. FMTR achieves strong performance against batch BO and in-context baselines on synthetic and real-world benchmarks, while substantially reducing the computational cost of batch selection.

title: Sparse Autoencoders for Mechanistic Interpretability in NLP: A Critical Survey of Recoverability, Interpretability, and Utility
summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have emerged as a promising approach to mechanistic interpretability by decomposing language-model activations into sparse, potentially interpretable features. However, differences in design assumptions, evaluation objectives, and experimental settings complicate conclusions about their effectiveness. We present a critical survey of 138 studies on SAEs in natural language processing. Our contributions are fourfold: (1) we propose a task-grounded taxonomy connecting dictionary design, feature operations, and NLP functions; (2) we examine how sparsity allocation, geometry, data coverage, and inference affect feature recoverability; (3) we assess evidence for semantic interpretability, mechanistic faithfulness, and behavioral utility; and (4) we synthesize findings across multilingual processing, retrieval, reasoning, classification, and behavioral regulation, highlighting the roles of objectives, baselines, supervision, and intervention pipelines. Through comparative analyses of published results, we reconcile apparent disagreements, identify unresolved questions, and propose directions for more rigorous evaluation. An anonymous research register https://anonymous.4open.science/r/sae-research-register-C331/register.html accompanies the survey.

title: An Analytic 0.48-Approximation for Non-Monotone k-Submodular Maximization under a Matroid Constraint
summary: We give a randomized polynomial-time $0.48$-approximation for maximizing a nonnegative non-monotone $k$-submodular function under a matroid constraint, for every $k\ge2$. The algorithm combines a top-two label rule with a nested-chain potential and maximum-weight matroid bases. Its analysis reduces the approximation guarantee to a one-dimensional time allocation: a uniform local lower bound leads to a linear differential equation, concavity closes the remaining interval, and two elementary budgets complete the proof. A strict saving in the time budget absorbs sampling and discretization errors, yielding the exact $0.48$ guarantee in the value-oracle model.

title: Attention-Based Spatio-Temporal Approach for Fire and Smoke Detection
summary: In various industries, smoke and fire are two of the most important threats in the workplace. One of the common methods for detecting smoke and fire is the use of infrared thermal and smoke sensors, which cannot be used in outdoor applications. Therefore, the use of vision-based methods seems necessary. The problem of smoke and fire detection is spatiotemporal and requires spatiotemporal solutions. This paper presents a method that uses spatial features along with temporal-based features to detect smoke and fire in the scene. It consists of three main parts; the task of each part is to reduce the error of the previous part so that the final model has a robust performance. This method also uses transformer modules to increase the accuracy of the model. The results of our model show the proper performance of the proposed approach in solving the problem of smoke and fire detection and can be used to increase workplace safety.

title: Structural Dependence, Imitation or Herding? A Multi-Agent Simulation of Global Intermedia Agenda Setting
comments: 20 pages, 3 figures, 15 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/hellowyousuf/dependence-imitation-herding, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23330238
summary: News outlets in poorer countries cover the world much as the leading outlets of rich countries do. Two explanations compete. One says they depend on Western news agencies for lack of resources. The other says they choose to copy prestigious outlets or whoever moves first. Observation cannot tell these apart. This study measured how closely 18 national outlets in Bangladesh, Kenya, South Africa, India, Malaysia and Nigeria followed four core outlets in how much attention they gave, which angle they took and when they published, on the wars in Ukraine and Gaza and two UN climate conferences in 2022-2024. It then ran a simulation in which language models acted as the outlets' editors and dependence, imitation and herding were switched on and off. Of nine tests, one held: outlets that relied more on wire copy published sooner after the core did. Tier and local stake showed no effect distinguishable from none. The herding test was supported and the imitation test was not. The simulation did not decide between the mechanisms, because the dependence rule, as fitted, reduced to publishing wire copy. Wire copy sets the clock of the periphery's foreign news. Whether it sets the agenda stays open.
comment: 20 pages, 3 figures, 15 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/hellowyousuf/dependence-imitation-herding, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23330238

title: Model order reduction of HDG discretizations for harmonic wave propagation
summary: We propose and analyze a projection-based model reduction method for the rapid and reliable solution of time-harmonic acoustic wave propagation problems over a frequency band, with particular emphasis on seismic applications. The high-fidelity model is based on a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) discretization, formulated as a generalized saddle-point system coupling the volume and trace unknowns. The basis construction combines residual-based greedy sampling of the frequency parameter, enrichment with frequency derivatives of the HDG solution, and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) compression. We establish the well posedness of both the high-fidelity and reduced problems and characterize their stability with inf-sup constants. We investigate the interaction between static condensation, inherent to the HDG discretization, and projection onto the reduced spaces, characterizing its implications for the reduced formulation and approximation errors. Since these operations do not commute in general, we derive a priori error estimates for both the trace and volume variables to quantify the gap between the two operations. We further identify a lifting condition on the volume reduced space that eliminates these gaps and yields a trace error estimate independent of the volume approximation error. Numerical experiments on the two-dimensional Marmousi model and a three-dimensional heterogeneous medium, with more than $10^{7}$ unknowns, illustrate the theoretical estimates and show that the reduced model achieves speedups of several orders of magnitude compared to the high-fidelity solver.

title: Enabling Tidying Tasks in Robotic Vacuum Cleaners via a Geometry-Induced Self-Locking Deployable Linkage
summary: Robotic vacuum cleaners must extend their functionality within tight limits on size, cost, and durability. Deployable linkages with few actuators meet these limits, but their backdrivability makes it difficult to hold a load-bearing posture without continuous motor torque. We introduce a two-stage deployable linkage that is self-locking, in the sense used for toggle and singularity-based linkages, through its own geometry: at full deployment an internal three-link subchain approaches a collinear, near-singular configuration where the input--output transmission ratio approaches zero, so that plate loads produce a small residual back-driving torque, absorbed by drive-train friction and a lightweight magnetic detent. A single actuator performs deployment and locking, a passive chassis-mounted trigger releases the lock for retraction, and a second actuator adjusts only the deployment height. We integrate the mechanism into a commercial robotic vacuum cleaner and validate it through a 100-cycle repeatability test, a quasi-static load test in which the locked plate held 50\,N with the motor de-energized, and 140 pushing-type tidying trials on seven household objects against a commercial arm-equipped vacuum robot under a documented protocol. We derive the analytical holding condition and discuss its limits as an intermediate design point between passive compliance and articulated manipulation.

title: LLM-Based Policy Compliance Verification of Loan Applications
summary:
Banks rely on extensive internal policy frameworks to ensure that corporate lending decisions comply with regulatory requirements and internal risk standards. Reviewing loan applications against these policies is a largely manual and knowledge-intensive process, which can lead to overlooked policy violations or exceptions. This report presents a prototype of an LLM-based policy checker that automatically verifies loan applications against internal lending policies.
  The proposed approach follows a two-step architecture. First, compliance-relevant rules are automatically extracted from policy documents and converted into structured, machine-readable representations. Second, loan applications are evaluated against the extracted rules to identify policy exceptions, non-compliant findings, missing information, and cases requiring manual review.
  Evaluation results demonstrate that the rule extraction process is highly stable across multiple runs and consistently captures rules identified as critical by a domain expert. When evaluated on 11 real loan applications with known policy exceptions, the system successfully detected the majority of these exceptions and identified additional compliance issues that had previously been overlooked during manual reviews. While the approach produces false positives and cannot fully replace human judgement, the results indicate that LLM-based policy compliance verification can provide valuable support in the loan application verification process by highlighting potential compliance risks.

title: Atomic-WAM: Execution-Grounded Atomic-Motion Reasoning for World Action Models
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) typically adapt video foundation models to robotic control through joint video and action prediction. However, task-level instructions may leave the next physical interaction underspecified, requiring semantic grounding and state-dependent motion selection. To this end, we introduce Atomic-WAM, an understand-then-execute framework that connects task reasoning to action generation through atomic-motion descriptions. Specifically, a vision-language reasoner describes the next local motion from the task instruction and visual context, guiding a WAM to predict future video and an action chunk. Furthermore, an automatic annotation pipeline curates temporally aligned, contact-enriched supervision from multi-view DROID demonstrations. To make atomic-motion predictions executable by the WAM, we post-train the reasoner with Execution-Grounded GRPO (EG-GRPO). With the WAM fixed, EG-GRPO adapts the reasoner through rewards for motion appropriateness and execution success. Finally, Atomic-WAM achieves 39.6% task success under default instructions and 31.6% under vague instructions in a real-to-sim evaluation on RoboLab. Project page: https://ssj9596.github.io/Atomic-WAM-project

title: Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning
summary: Self-supervised joint embedding learning aligns representations of augmented views while regularizing their distribution to prevent collapse. Regularization aims to shape the overall representation distribution, but most joint embedding methods restrict its computation to the active minibatch. We propose out-of-batch regularization, which maintains a dataset-level state in CPU memory and uses globally constructed per-instance targets during minibatch training. Evaluated on natural images and biomedical datasets, these anchors approximate the full-dataset regularization gradient more faithfully than conventional minibatch estimation at small batch sizes. Applications to contrastive (SimCLR) and non-contrastive (SIGReg) approaches show consistent improvement over the corresponding in-batch objectives for image classification, minority-class performance under controlled imbalance, instance retrieval, and continued self-supervised pretraining, with the largest gains at small batch sizes. These results suggest that dataset-level regularization can be decoupled from minibatch optimization, making batch size an optimization choice that does not affect the geometry of the regularizer.

title: OneLA: Learning Many Worlds from Latent Actions
summary: Learning world models across diverse domains calls for a unified control space, yet ac- tion interfaces vary across domains and action annotations are often scarce. Latent ac- tions learned directly from videos offer a promising way to establish such a space without explicit action supervision. However, learning shared latent actions across domains re- mains challenging, as variations in appearance, embodiment, and dynamics can entangle domain-specific visual cues with transferable transition structure. To this end, we intro- duce OneLA, a simple framework that learns continuous latent actions through a shared orthogonal dictionary and a common predictive objective, without task-specific designs or cross-domain alignment losses during latent action pretraining. These latent actions pro- vide a shared conditioning interface for world models, with lightweight adapters mapping native control commands into the same space. Conditioned on latent actions and the cur- rent visual state, the world model predicts context-dependent transitions for controllable rollout. OneLA improves action readout across domains and reduces action cycle-transfer rotation error by 24.8% over the strongest evaluated baseline. A joint-training comparison further shows a 20.5% improvement in Human Preference Score v3 (HPSv3) for real- scene generation. These results suggest a path toward general-purpose world models that learn from diverse videos and support flexible control through latent action space.

title: The Body-Algorithm-Emotion Loop: Making Emotion AI Misrecognition Visible through Artistic Practice
comments: In Proceedings of Explainable AI for the Arts Workshop 2026 (XAIxArts 2026) arXiv:2607.20131
summary: This pictorial presents The Body in Algorithmic Colonialism, a screen-based interactive installation that critically examines Emotion-AI through artistic practice. The work uses facial tracking to simulate how commercial Emotion-AI systems translate facial movement into emotional categories and verdicts of compliance or non-compliance. Rather than treating explainability as technical transparency alone, the installation approaches XAI as an embodied encounter with misrecognition: viewers experience how the body is measured, classified, and returned to itself through algorithmic thresholds. Drawing on critical AI studies, affect theory, and practice-as-research, the pictorial positions artistic practice as a method for making affective classification visible and contestable. It documents the conceptual framework, technical process, and critical context of a prototype developed in the first year of a practice-based PhD. No audience responses, interviews, or participant data are analysed in this submission.
comment: In Proceedings of Explainable AI for the Arts Workshop 2026 (XAIxArts 2026) arXiv:2607.20131

title: Gap Detection: Mitigating Homogenization through Demand and Defensibility
comments: 24 pages; submitted to ICLR 2027, under review
summary: Language models often produce semantically similar answers to open-ended questions, even when many plausible alternatives exist. Generating useful alternatives requires identifying both what the query calls for and what existing responses already cover. We introduce Gap Detection, a framework that searches for relevant but unoccupied directions in a shared text embedding space. Its objective, GapScore, combines query relevance (Demand) with dissimilarity to the nearest existing item (Defensibility). The framework optimizes this product on the unit sphere, maps candidate directions to concept words with a language model, and uses task-specific filtering and constrained prompting to turn those concepts into text. On five curated topics and 90 INFINITY-CHAT queries, the reported mean relative reductions in output Collision are 12.8% and 10.8%, respectively. We also instantiate the framework for generative engine optimization over four product markets and for iterative synthetic-data augmentation. In the latter setting, with 100 training examples per method, Gap Detection reduces Collision from 0.324 to 0.298 relative to undirected accumulation and increases the Vendi Score from 27.16 to 29.20; the accuracy difference is one example on a 40-example test set. Component ablations expose the trade-off between semantic separation and relevance, while also showing that better direction scores do not uniformly yield better downstream metrics. These results support explicit gap search as a practical mechanism for diversifying content, with task validity checked separately from geometric novelty.
comment: 24 pages; submitted to ICLR 2027, under review

title: Optimizing Sparse Boolean Rule Networks using Mixed Integer Linear Programming
comments: Preprint (submitted version, prior to peer review) of a paper accepted at RuleML+RR 2026, to appear in LNCS
summary: We study the problem of learning accurate and cognitively simple binary classifiers that are directly interpretable as Boolean rules. We propose mixed integer linear programming (MILP) formulations for training sparse disjunctive normal form (DNF) networks, viewed as small networks with a conjunctive hidden layer and a disjunctive output layer. Contrary to previous work that uses MILP for inductive rule learning, we start with a fixed network structure, for which we then find optimal weights. A regularized objective explicitly trades off misclassification costs against sparsity, yielding globally optimized rule sets. Our main technical contribution is an enhanced formulation that substantially reduces the number of integer decision variables and eliminates redundant constraints, while preserving exact Boolean semantics for all feasible solutions. Furthermore, we develop a combined approach based on initialization and dropout to break symmetries in the weights between rules, mitigating redundancy, and encouraging more diverse and stable rule representations. Experiments on synthetic benchmarks and UCI datasets show that the advanced formulation improves computational efficiency and achieves competitive or superior accuracy compared to established interpretable baselines, including SAT-based DNF learning and well-known rule- and tree-based learners. Overall, our approach provides a principled optimization framework for learning compact Boolean rule sets with explicit control over accuracy and sparsity trade-offs.
comment: Preprint (submitted version, prior to peer review) of a paper accepted at RuleML+RR 2026, to appear in LNCS

title: FreeSBee: A Constant-Time Compilation Pipeline
summary: Constant-time execution is an important security property, especially for IoT devices, that prevents the leakage of sensitive information over timing side-channels. However, achieving constant-time execution is very hard when going down to the cycle level, at least on realistic devices. A lot of research is concerned with producing tools that either determine whether code is constant-time or that ensure it is compiled into a constant-time binary, with various degrees of accuracy. In this work, we present and evaluate a full workflow for hardening against timing side-channels during compilation. It starts with taint analysis to determine the code locations that depend on sensitive information. These are then the object of automated control-flow transformations inside the compiler to seal possible timing side-channels. We evaluate our workflow in detail on a realistic application running on a RISC-V core using both static timing analysis and statistical methods. Even though we do not reach cycle-accurate constant-time execution, our statistical results suggest that our hardened binary is safe against timing attacks.

title: MultiPartyTurnBench: Benchmarking Floor Control in Multi-Party Spoken Dialogue
summary: Full-duplex speech systems must decide when to enter, hold, or relinquish the conversational floor, even as multiple speakers overlap or backchannel without taking it. Existing evaluations study dyadic turn-taking or end-to-end agent behavior, but lack a unified, controlled evaluation of genuine floor transitions against confusable non-events in multi-party settings. We introduce MultiPartyTurnBench (MPTB), a benchmark of 240 synthetically generated, channel-separated conversations spanning two to five speakers and six interaction types. MPTB evaluates two complementary tasks: End-of-Turn (EOT) detection distinguishes genuine turn completion from temporary holds, while Interruption (INT) detection distinguishes successful floor takeovers from non-floor-taking speech. Exact event-conditioned annotations enable causal evaluation using false-positive-constrained recall and signed latency. Across acoustic, semantic, and turn-projection baselines, we find a stark asymmetry: learned systems achieve 82.5-92.6% EOT recall at 4.3-11.8% false-positive rates, while INT detection suffers from missed takeovers or excessive false activations. This asymmetry extends to five full-duplex agents which achieve 86.1-95.8% balanced accuracy on turn entry, yet perform near chance (46.9-54.7%) on selective interruption handling. Gemini-3.8-Live yields to 97.7% of backchannels, whereas MiniCPM-o-4.5 yields to only 1.4% of genuine interruptions. These findings establish selective floor control as a distinct, unresolved challenge for reliable multi-party voice interaction.

title: Secret Sharing from Non-Extractable Randomness
summary:
Bosley and Dodis (TCC 2007) proved that a class of imperfect randomness sources that suffices for information-theoretic encryption of messages longer than the logarithm of the key length must admit deterministic extraction of nearly uniform bits, and asked whether the same is true of two-out-of-two secret sharing. Aggarwal, Chung, Obremski, and Ribeiro (TCC 2022) gave a positive answer for schemes that are in addition leakage-resilient or non-malleable; the original question remained open.
  We answer it in the negative. For every $b\ge2$ we construct a class of flat sources on $\{0,1\}^{b+2}$, each of min-entropy at least $b$, together with a perfectly correct and perfectly private two-out-of-two scheme that shares a $b$-bit secret into two $(b+1)$-bit shares using any source in the class, and we show that every deterministic map from $\{0,1\}^{b+2}$ to $\{0,1\}$ is at statistical distance at least $1/6$ from uniform on some source in the class. This implies that sharing a long enough secret does not require extractable randomness. The proof is a short parity argument. The idea of the construction extends to other thresholds: for two-out-of-$n$ and $r$-out-of-$r$ sharing we give perfect schemes with $(b+1)$-bit shares, private for classes of flat sources from which no single bit can be extracted with error below $1/(4n-2)$ and $1/(2(2^r-1))$, respectively.

title: RM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Generative Reward Models
comments: 34 pages, 4 figures; includes references and appendices
summary: Reinforcement Learning on Mixed-domain preference data (Mix-RL) has become the mainstream approach for training general-purpose Generative Reward Models (GRMs). However, Mix-RL suffers from two critical bottlenecks: the reward sparsity induced by outcome rewards, and the cross-domain interference arising from jointly optimizing heterogeneous capabilities, which together give rise to imbalanced capability acquisition and pervasive reward hacking. Inspired by the success of On-Policy Distillation (OPD) in multi-domain capability integration, we introduce RM-OPD (Reward Modeling via On-Policy Distillation), a two-stage framework that separates specialist acquisition from capability integration. First, we cultivate domain-specialized teacher models via single-domain GRPO fine-tuning, allowing each expert to reach its performance ceiling in isolation; then we consolidate these teachers into one student model through (i) routed on-policy distillation, which provides dense signed token-level supervision on student-generated critiques; (ii) domain contribution reweighting, which reweights token guidance toward target domain shares, preventing specific domains from dominating optimization; and (iii) optional criteria context distillation, which conditions teachers on domain-specific evaluation criteria to sharpen token-level supervision. Across multiple RM benchmarks and two base models, RM-OPD consistently outperforms vanilla Mix-RL and other strong baselines, achieving overall superior performance and exhibiting an emergent "teacher-surpassing" effect. These results establish RM-OPD as a promising paradigm for building generalist GRMs.
comment: 34 pages, 4 figures; includes references and appendices

title: TreeSpark: Learning to Draft the Trees You Verify for Speculative Decoding
summary: Parallel drafters such as DFlash and DSpark reduce proposal latency, but early mismatches limit how much of each block can be accepted. Retaining alternatives introduces parent states and candidate choices that reference-conditioned training does not directly supervise. We introduce TreeSpark, a unified training and inference framework extending the semi-autoregressive DSpark architecture. It constructs parent-conditioned candidate trees from one backbone pass and replays their expansion, pruning, and budgeted packing during training. Survival negative log-likelihood weights retained edges by reference-derived path mass, while a capped coverage hinge promotes target-important alternatives near local selection boundaries. Both objectives reuse reference-chain target distributions without additional target forward passes. We evaluate greedy decoding with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B on nine general benchmarks and six writing domains. Across targets and suites, TreeSpark improves mean acceptance length over DSpark by 23.4% to 31.6% and mean single-request throughput by 15.1% to 25.0%. Batched Qwen3-4B throughput improves by 12.6% to 17.2%. At fixed attention capacity and inference policy, the proposed supervision further improves mean acceptance length by approximately 6.4% and mean system throughput by 4.2% to 5.0% on Qwen3-4B.

title: Cross-Model In-Context Neurofeedback Reveals (Limited) Activation Control in LLMs
comments: 29 pages, 11 figures, 5 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/Dundalia/control-with-neurofeedback
summary: Probes on activation vectors are widely used to detect misbehavior in language models, but their success relies on the assumption that models cannot control what their activations encode. Humans can learn, through neurofeedback, to control the firing of even single neurons, and recent studies investigated whether this ability extends to language models, reaching conflicting conclusions. No experimental design so far disentangles competence at the task from genuine access to one's own activations. We fill this gap with in-context neurofeedback sessions, in which a "subject" model is asked to maximize (or minimize) a score derived from its activations, shown back to it at every turn. In our first experiment, the sentences are generated either by the subject or by a second "writer" model, while the score always derives from the activations of the subject. We test ten open-weight models from five families, with sizes from 9B to 32B. Some models move their own scores considerably, but no more than a writer of comparable competence moves them. Is this because the task requires no privileged access, or because the subject controls its activations while processing the sentences, whoever wrote them? To answer this, we prefill a fixed sentence as the subject's reply at every turn and ask it to increase or decrease the score. Three out of ten models show small but consistent control effects. We further ask whether models can control their activations to the point of fooling an activation monitor. We make models repeat sentences a monitor would flag, such as a deceptive answer for a deception monitor, and ask them to raise or lower the monitor's score. No model learns to lower it, but one model can raise it. In-context control of a model's own activations might not yet be a threat to activation monitors, but it exists in a few models and needs to be tracked as models evolve.
comment: 29 pages, 11 figures, 5 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/Dundalia/control-with-neurofeedback

title: Noise-Aware Lombard Speech Synthesis via Flow-GRPO for Intelligibility Optimization
comments: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing. 14 pages, 6 figures
summary: Voice-based conversational agents are increasingly deployed in real-world settings, where environmental noise often degrades the interactive experience. Therefore, robust acoustic adaptability is essential to maintain natural and intelligible human-computer communication. However, most existing systems remain acoustically insensitive and fail to emulate the human Lombard effect, in which speakers involuntarily adjust their vocal production to preserve intelligibility in the presence of noise. As a result, their communicative reliability degrades under adverse acoustic conditions. To remain intelligible in noisy environments, conversational agents require a mechanism to emulate noise-induced adaptive behavior during synthesis. We propose NIL-TTS, a noise-induced Lombard TTS framework. We integrate a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) mechanism into a flow-matching backbone for dynamic vocal adaptation. A two-stage training paradigm is utilized: initial supervised fine-tuning on paired Lombard corpora, followed by Flow-GRPO post-training to optimize for intelligibility. Evaluations confirm that NIL-TTS autonomously adjusts its output in response to varying noise conditions, exhibiting key correlates of the human Lombard effect. Driven by these adaptive modulations, the synthesized speech achieves significant intelligibility improvements that scale proportionally with noise intensity. Ultimately, this work presents a flow-matching and reinforcement learning-based advancement within the adaptive Lombard speech synthesis paradigm for challenging real-world scenarios.
comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing. 14 pages, 6 figures

title: When Occupation-derived Skills Don't Help: On the Limits of Skill-Augmented Career Path Prediction
summary: Skills are widely assumed to play a central role in career transitions, motivating their use in career path prediction (CPP) systems. In this work, we critically examine whether explicit skill representations provide complementary signal beyond text-based job representations. We evaluate multiple strategies for incorporating skills into CPP models, including score fusion and neural architectures, under two conditions: predicted skills and ground-truth ESCO annotations. Surprisingly, across two benchmark datasets, none of these settings yield substantial improvements over strong text-only baselines. Even when using ground-truth skills, gains remain marginal and inconsistent. Through detailed analysis, we identify key factors underlying this result: high redundancy between textual and skill representations, limited discriminative power of ESCO's taxonomy, and representational collapse in skill embeddings. Furthermore, we find that skill prediction difficulty correlates with overall sample difficulty, limiting the potential for complementary signals. Our findings challenge the common assumption that explicit skill modeling inherently benefits career prediction and suggest that dense text representations already capture most skill-relevant information.

title: Dimension-Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning
summary:
Tracking changing comparators is a central problem in online learning. For exp-concave losses, previous work established the $T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon $T$ and Euclidean path length $P_T$ for fixed dimension, while the optimal cost of dimension remained unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing a sharp $d^{1/3}$ curved dimension factor, improving the $d^{2/3}$ factor of recent switching and interval reductions [1, 2]. To achieve this improvement, we develop a proper, full-information learner on compact convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that adapts to the unknown path length and, under fixed dimension-independent diameter, gradient, and curvature parameters, guarantees
  $$\operatorname{Reg}_T(u_{1:T}) \le \widetilde{O}\left(d+\min\left\{d^{1/3}T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3},\sqrt{TP_T},T\right\}\right).$$
  A matching lower bound on a diameter-one Euclidean ball establishes the minimax frontier up to logarithmic factors when $T\gtrsim d^2$, including the transition from the curved rate to larger path budgets. The lower bound already holds for losses that depend on only one coordinate per round, isolating an unavoidable cost of learning across directions. Our upper bound follows from square-root Gaussian KL control of comparator movement and a cancellation argument that pays for history restarts. The curved learner maintains $O(\log^2 T)$ Gaussian states, uses one gradient per round, and runs in time near-linear in $T$ under a Mahalanobis-projection oracle.

title: Asymmetry and Complexity of Nondeterministic Computations
summary:
Symmetry of Information (SoI) [ZL70] is a fundamental theorem of classical Kolmogorov complexity whose status for time-bounded computation is closely related to central open problems in complexity theory and cryptography. In a recent development, [HMO26] showed that SoI fails for $rKt$ complexity, namely in the setting of randomized computation. By contrast, many basic properties of Kolmogorov complexity are known to remain valid in the presence of nondeterminism [HLO26], suggesting that SoI may provide a fruitful structural principle for exploring the relative power of randomness and nondeterminism in computation.
  Our results reveal that the validity of SoI for nondeterministic computation, namely for $nKt$ complexity, is a subtle question connected to several frontiers. We show that symmetry of information holds on average for randomized extensions of $nKt$, while its worst case validity would imply breakthrough complexity separations. Although the standard cryptographic argument for asymmetry does not extend to the nondeterministic setting, we provide evidence that information remains asymmetric in nondeterministic computations. Among other results, we show that SoI would imply a collapse of exponential time classes to low levels of the polynomial hierarchy.
  Then, building on the work of [Hir22b, GK22, KK26, HMO26], we develop a general framework connecting symmetry of information, meta-complexity, and explicit constructions in the nondeterministic setting. More precisely, we prove that suitable formulations of these three notions are quantitatively equivalent. We apply different aspects of this correspondence to make progress on complexity lower bounds and on the failure of SoI for nondeterministic computation. These consequences are unconditional and provide some of the strongest known lower bounds in meta-complexity.

title: Value-Guided Repulsion for Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: Drifting models have emerged as a highly efficient and stable paradigm for policy design in offline reinforcement learning (RL). However, standard drift policies determine repulsion solely from geometric relationships among generated actions and therefore cannot distinguish them by expected value. To address this limitation, we introduce Value-Guided Repulsion Q-Learning (VRQL) to integrate action value estimates into the particle interaction field. For each state, VRQL combines geometric kernel distance with a normalized Q value scaling. This mechanism assigns greater repulsive influence to particles with lower values while strictly retaining attraction toward behavior action. Consequently, this value-guided interaction field aligns behavior regularization with policy improvement without adding an auxiliary behavior model stage. On 50 OGBench task configurations and 6 D4RL AntMaze configurations, VRQL demonstrates highly competitive performance against established baselines, suggesting that value-guided particle interaction is an effective method for offline RL.

title: HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
summary: Medication recommendation (MR) is critical for clinical decision support. While existing MR methods are mostly designed for single-center learning, where only one independent hospital is involved, multi-center MR with hospitals of different scales has become increasingly demanding in practice. In multi center settings, abundant data from large medical centers can improve recommendation performance for low-resource centers. Despite a few preliminary attempts on this task, two critical gaps remain. Gap 1: Existing multi-center methods fail to disentangle transferable cross-hospital clinical experience from hospital-specific prescribing patterns, limiting clinical feasibility and physician acceptance. Gap 2: They commonly overlook multi label safety constraints of MR, including drug-drug interaction risks and local formulary feasibility, which are essential for safe real-world deployment. To address these gaps, we propose HEM-Med, a novel hierarchical agentic memory framework for multi-center MR. To address Gap 1, we design a disentangled hierarchical memory module that builds patient-level medication context attribution records and disentangles them into cross hospital experience memory and hospital-specific residual memory. To address Gap 2, we introduce a safety-aware medication set generation module, which integrates dual-level experience retrieval with safety-aware set decoding to produce clinically relevant, safer, and locally adaptive medication recommendations. Experiments on a real-world multi-center eICU dataset show that HEM-Med outperforms representative transfer learning, LLM-based, and MR baselines in terms of both recommendation accuracy and safety.

title: SWE-Stream: Scaling Executable Training Data for SWE Agents via Progressive Construction and Elastic Streaming
summary: Software engineering agents have advanced rapidly, but scaling their training remains constrained by the limited availability of high-quality executable tasks. Development histories contain valuable signals for constructing such tasks, yet they often require substantial reconstruction due to incomplete environments, missing tests, and inconsistent artifacts. We present SWE-Stream, a system for scaling executable SWE training data through progressive construction and elastic streaming execution. SWE-Stream progressively validates and refines task candidates, reusing existing artifacts when possible and applying targeted completion only when necessary. An elastic scheduler asynchronously coordinates construction stages under shared resource constraints, adapting execution budgets based on observed workload demands. Using development histories from 10,728 repositories across six programming languages, SWE-Stream constructs 80,874 validated tasks and collects 118,688 successful trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 on these trajectories achieves resolve rates of 69.0%, 49.3%, and 45.42% on SWE-bench Verified, Multilingual, and Pro, respectively. In a controlled comparison with approximately matched training budgets, SWE-Stream achieves a 45.6% resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming three existing data sources. Moreover, its streaming construction strategy improves efficiency, delivering $1.45\times$ the accepted-task throughput of batch construction and accepting 13.2% more tasks than fixed-limit streaming.

title: What Makes a Social Agent's Interactions Effective? Learning from Verifiable Outcomes in Paired Worlds
summary: Effective social interaction requires more than fluent responses: agents must reach plans that fit the participants' needs and circumstances. Existing evaluations of social agents mainly rely on LLM judges that rate the conversation, without checking the resulting plan. We introduce HICO-Bench, a benchmark of 180 everyday coordination scenarios, such as resource allocation, scheduling, and authorization, in which two agents with private information converse and then independently record the plan they agreed on. A program checks Feasibility (the two records match and satisfy both participants' private conditions), and an LLM judge checks Integrity (the conversation supports the recorded plan); passing both is a Verified Success. Each scenario has two versions that share the same public context but differ in one private condition, so the correct plan differs between them. Across thirteen LLMs, 36% of conversations rated highly for goal completion fail Verified Success. To learn from outcomes that arrive only at the end of a conversation, we propose Paired-Credit Policy Optimization (PaCPO). After each turn, PaCPO asks the agent for a tentative plan, checks it in both versions of the scenario, and rewards the turns after which the tentative plans fit their respective versions. PaCPO raises Qwen3-8B's Verified Success from 20.4% to 28.3%.

title: Drivers of LLM Consensus Formation Under Competing Incentives: A Simulation Study
summary:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent environments that produce unanimous agreement, both in intended interactions that need coordination and in unintended emergent interactions. Consequently, understanding how LLMs with competing incentives reach consensus is crucial to better interpret and design LLM collectives. We introduce an evaluation, based on the Network Consensus game, to assess the mechanisms driving this process. Here, a network of agents must agree on one of two colours to receive a payoff, but agents are offered different payoffs for the agreed colour. We vary components such as communication access and network structure and assess six open-source models and one closed model (ChatGPT 5.6-sol).
  We find that open-source LLMs reach consensus less often than humans in comparable experiments and only if messages are communicated across the global network. ChatGPT 5.6-sol, however, is able to reach consensus with communication limited to its neighbours and with no communication ability. This is achieved through lower stubbornness and higher majority-following tendencies, and by providing more information about its neighbours' states in messages. However, situating agents in a highly clustered graph reduces consensus, regardless of these traits, demonstrating that both system design and individual model traits drive collective outcomes.

title: Investigating Behavior Cloning from Few Demonstrations for Autonomous Driving based on Bird's-Eye View in Simulated Cities
comments: 14 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Accepted manuscript (author version) of the paper published in the proceedings of BRACIS 2024 (34th Brazilian Conference on Intelligent Systems, Belém, Brazil, 17-21 November 2024). Project page: https://sites.google.com/view/weighted-bc
summary: This paper investigates the use of Behavior Cloning (BC) for autonomous driving from a bird's-eye view (BEV) perspective in simulated urban environments.
