title: Scaling Multilingual Mixture-of-Experts: How Language Coverage Changes Capacity and Compute Allocation
summary: Multilingual models share capacity across languages, so adding languages can hurt performance on existing ones. Mixture-of-experts models expand this capacity with little additional per-token computation. Given this extra capacity, does adding experts reduce what each additional language costs? To answer this question, we propose a repetition-aware joint scaling law relating number of active parameters, training tokens per language, number of experts, and language coverage. Fitted on 26,300 per-language loss observations from 64 pretrained configurations, our law reduces prediction error on held-out configurations by 28% relative to the strongest evaluated baseline. At matched number of active parameters and training tokens per language, 32 experts reduce the loss penalty of expanding from 12 to 200 languages by 83% compared with a dense model. Our law further shows that broader language coverage favors more experts across a wider range of compute budgets, guiding capacity allocation as multilingual models scale.

title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
authors: Maurice W. P. M. H. Heemels
summary: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. The effectiveness and computational efficiency of the approach are demonstrated using experimentally obtained frequency response data from industrial-grade semiconductor equipment. The synthesized controller is implemented on the physical setup, and its performance is validated in real-time experiments.

title: Subexponential Parameterized Approximation for Group-Fair Euclidean $k$-Center
summary:
Clustering is a basic tool for grouping data into meaningful classes, but in many applications the resulting clusters must also respect the fairness conditions among different groups. We study this direction for the group-fair Euclidean $k$-center problem in fixed dimension, where the input points are partitioned into disjoint color classes, and every cluster must satisfy given lower and upper bounds on the fraction of each color.
  We give a separator-based recursive approximation algorithm for the continuous-center setting. The main idea is to first reduce the continuous search space to a finite candidate center set and then use the geometric sphere separators to break the instance into smaller subproblems.
  Our algorithm gives a bicriteria approximation: the clustering radius is within a factor of $(1+ε)$ of the optimum exactly fair solution, while the fairness bounds are relaxed only by a multiplicative factor. For fixed dimension, number of colors, and approximation parameters, the running time is polynomial in input size and subexponential in $k$. A recent IJCAI-ECAI2026 result gives a $(1+ε)$-approximation for group-fair $k$-center in bounded doubling metrics with running time $(k/ε)^{\mathcal{O}(k)}n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}$. In the fixed-dimensional Euclidean setting considered here, we improve the dependence on $k$ to subexponential, while allowing continuous centers. The fairness guarantees of the two results are different: the previous work allows an additive fairness violation, whereas our algorithm uses a controlled multiplicative relaxation.

title: Contrastive uncertainty learning for robust multi-structure segmentation in lower-pelvic MR
summary: Boundary delineation of anatomical structures in prostate MRI is often compromised by regional ambiguity. Automated segmentation methods relying on global overlap loss functions tend to be insensitive to surface deviations, leading to significant errors in ambiguous regions. Most existing uncertainty-aware methods treat uncertainty as a post-hoc quality indicator or prediction filter. We propose Contrastive Uncertainty Learning (CUL), a supervised framework that uses predictive uncertainty to directly guide representation learning. Using Monte Carlo Dropout, CUL identifies voxel-wise uncertainty and structures the embedding geometry accordingly: low-uncertainty, correctly predicted features form stable voxels while high-uncertainty or misclassified features are actively repelled, preventing feature collapse at difficult boundaries. We evaluate CUL on a 589-scan 3D prostate MRI multi-structure segmentation task (8 anatomical structures) using a ViT with UperNet decoder architecture. Average Dice ($83.38\%$) remains comparable to the baseline ($83.35\%$), while surface distance decreases significantly ($p<0.001$) across 6 of 8 anatomical structures. A hard-case analysis reveals a $22{\times}$ asymmetry between significantly improved and degraded cases ($18.8\%$ vs $0.9\%$). Ablation studies show that removing uncertainty-guided sample selection eliminates improvements for the transition zone, while replacing the contrastive objective with a boundary loss additionally removes bladder improvements, demonstrating that both uncertainty-guided sampling and the contrastive objective are essential for the observed gains. These findings demonstrate that the proposed uncertainty-guided representation learning is a useful mechanism for reducing the risk of extreme errors in safety-critical medical segmentation

title: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Robust Planetary Landing
summary: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies for planetary landing and other aerospace guidance, navigation, and control tasks are commonly trained under randomized disturbances to improve robustness. However, typical stochastic perturbation sampling assumes independent variations, whereas real mission disturbances often exhibit spatial and temporal correlation and cannot be reproduced through independent random draws. This work investigates adversarial reinforcement learning to discover challenging off-nominal conditions. A secondary agent generates physically constrained perturbations that degrade the performance of a landing controller, forming an asymmetric sequential zero-sum game. Training proceeds in three stages: baseline controller learning, robustness enhancement with stochastic perturbations, and an iterative adversarial phase in which the controller and disturbance generator are alternately optimized. Preliminary experiments in a three-degree-of-freedom landing environment show that adversarial disturbances reveal vulnerabilities missed by conventional randomization and provide early indications that, with a more extensive training campaign, the approach can yield improved robustness and stronger generalization under previously unseen perturbation regimes.

title: Repairing Speech Access After Text Updates with Frozen Affine Fields
summary: Speech-capable language models inherit most of their knowledge from text-rich language backbones, and continued model maintenance is likewise dominated by text updates. Knowledge acquired through a text update can nevertheless remain difficult to access when the same query is spoken. We formulate this mismatch as post-update speech access repair, where the knowledge-bearing checkpoint stays frozen and a detachable operator repairs speech-only access in one model pass. We introduce Affine Fields for Interface Repair across Modalities (AFFIRM), which first learns and freezes a base correction for speech hidden states, then adds query-specific corrections with zero mean over the operator-training queries. Paired speech and text states provide the coordinates that condition these corrections on each query. On balanced synthetic-speech PopQA, paired comparisons do not establish a clear advantage for AFFIRM over global SALSA steering or low-rank ReFT interventions under the same frozen single-state constraint. On recorded SLUE-SQA-5 questions with text passages, a full-scale PopQA-fitted AFFIRM operator transfers without refitting and improves ROUGE-L by 0.0941 over its paired No Repair baseline. Low-rank ReFT interventions also transfer positively, whereas the matched SALSA variant falls 0.0707 below its paired baseline. These results show that text acquisition and speech access can diverge after an update and should be verified and repaired separately.

title: GLoD-LVSM: Learning Geometry-Grounded Continuous-LoD Scene Representations for Large View Synthesis Models
summary: Large view synthesis models (LVSMs) reconstruct scenes from sparse views and render novel views quickly, but they incur unnecessary storage and rendering costs due to token redundancy. We present GLoD-LVSM, a compact, geometry-grounded scene representation for LVSMs with continuous levels of detail. First, instead of learning a fixed set of scene anchor initializations, GLoD-LVSM learns a continuous field that initializes a flexible number of anchors to match the desired budget. A condenser then aggregates scene information into these anchors, with both the field and condenser trained end-to-end. Second, the condenser infers reference-token and anchor geometry to guide compression through geometry-grounded attention, improving rendering quality and enabling frustum culling during decoding. Compared with existing LVSM scene-compression baselines, GLoD-LVSM achieves the best trade-off between rendering quality and scene token count. Compared with the uncompressed base model, GLoD-LVSM reduces the scene-token count by 33.4% and accelerates rendering by $1.23\times$ with no quality loss. Under a relaxed quality-loss budget, the reduction increases to 85.5%, with $3.00\times$ rendering speedup. Further analysis reveals that view-synthesis supervision yields emergent scene depth and self-organized anchors that align with surfaces and adapt their density to local texture complexity. Beyond rendering, we further show that our scene representation also supports scene-semantic understanding, highlighting its potential for broader downstream tasks.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Receding-Horizon Safety Critic and Differentiable Action Shields
summary: Despite the Markov assumption, safety failures in robot reinforcement learning rarely occur instantaneously; they typically emerge over several steps as the policy enters unfamiliar states under disturbances and domain shift. We address this limitation by learning a receding-horizon safety critic that predicts whether a state will remain non-terminating over the next receding horizon, enabling anticipatory detection of impending locomotion failures. The critic is trained from rollout-derived horizon labels with a composite objective that combines horizon classification, control-barrier-function-inspired temporal consistency, and smoothness regularization, and we aggregate an ensemble of critics with a conservative Conditional Value at Risk estimate to account for uncertainty. Building on the learned critic, we derive a closed-form, differentiable CBF-style safety filter that minimally modifies the policy action to improve predicted safety, and integrate it into PPO with an anticipation loss to reduce policy-filter mismatch during training. In simulated quadruped locomotion, our method improves robustness under action noise, external perturbations, and terrain shifts, reducing catastrophic failures while maintaining competitive returns.

title: Long-Horizon RL Needs Muon
summary: Long-horizon agents must coordinate reasoning, tool use, and environment feedback over extended interactions. Learning from sparse outcome rewards requires weighting trajectories of different lengths and updating the policy while rollouts are still being collected. We examine a single-rollout asynchronous recipe combining Muon, token-averaged loss, truncated importance sampling, and auxiliary length and tool-error penalties. Single-rollout sampling allows asynchronous learning without waiting for multiple trajectories for the same issue. We study optimizer choices and recipe components for repository-level issue resolution across two model families. The evaluated training runs show higher training success with the full recipe than with the baselines.

title: Harness Policy Distillation: Aligning Agent Policies with Runtime Semantics
summary: Deploying a general-purpose model as an agent means running it inside a product-specific runtime harness that decides which actions are executable, how state advances, and when the loop may terminate. Ordinary trajectory supervision shows which action was taken but leaves the runtime semantics behind that action implicit. We introduce Harness Policy Distillation (HPD), which makes these runtime control semantics an explicit training target alongside actions to align the harness policy. HPD replays reference trajectories through the harness to recover the runtime semantics that are implicit in ordinary trajectory data, and represents them as control documents at each model-call boundary. These documents provide privileged information for a teacher to generate actions, while harness verification ensures that the resulting targets are executable under the runtime contract. We jointly train a shared model on the runtime semantics recovered from control-state privileged information and native history, thereby internalizing these semantics into the model policy. At deployment, the trained model uses the original harness interface without requiring the control document or any additional supplement. On TRAJECT-Bench with the Pi harness, Qwen3-8B trained with HPD reaches 22.98% autonomous task success and 49.23% runtime compliance, against 3.09% and 19.90% for the unadapted model. Harness-verified teacher actions substantially improve the native deployment policy, while joint control-state supervision provides further gains in task completion and runtime compliance. HPD turns executable runtime semantics into dense supervision for learning harness-compatible actions at each decision boundary.

title: Anuvani-LID: Robust and Calibrated Spoken Language Identification for Indian Languages
summary: Every multilingual speech pipeline begins with a language decision, an error there propagates silently through recognition, translation and routing. In India it spans 22 scheduled languages across four language families, heard over short, noisy, narrowband and code-mixed audio. Foundational speech models increasingly present language identification (LID) as an inherent latent, generalized capability. Autoregressive decoders in speech models emit a special language ID token, and modern LLMs with audio capabilities can name the language when prompted. We test this assumption on identical clips and find that whisper and similar speech models has tokens for only 15 of the 23 languages, on one second inputs Gemini 3.5 Flash reaches 0.52 macro-F1 and GPT-audio 0.14. We present Anuvani LID, a dedicated 115M parameter LID conformer model trained on 54,643 hours of Indian speech spanning 22 Indian languages and Indian accented English. Along with designed and controlled studies on 102 condition benchmark with speaker and corpus held out tests. Across 37 conditions, it reaches 0.914 mean macro-F1, 5.2 points above Gemini 3.5 Flash and ahead of 14 other systems. It is 24 points ahead of Gemini at one second, scores 0.897 on all 23 languages where no other system exceeds 0.713, and is calibrated to an ECE of 0.008. Reliable Indian LID still requires a robust, dedicated and calibrated model.

title: FUSE: Fairness-aware Update Screening against Byzantine Exploitation in $q$-Fair Federated Learning
summary: Client-level fair federated learning, in the form of $q$-fair federated learning ($q$-FFL), agnostic federated learning, or tilted empirical risk minimization, has emerged as an attractive solution to equalize utility across heterogeneous clients. This paradigm grants high-loss clients greater relative influence, while a central server aggregates their loss-weighted updates into a single shared model. Yet, the Byzantine robustness of $q$-fair federated learning has been largely neglected, leaving the server unable to tell legitimate fairness-induced amplification from malicious update scaling. To address this critical gap, we formalize the problem of Byzantine-robust $q$-fair federated learning under an \emph{update-only interface}, in which the server observes nothing but the fairness-scaled client updates. Our analysis under shared class-conditional label skew shows that fairness scaling preserves the nonnegative class-mixture structure of honest updates, while replacing their unit-sum constraint by a client-dependent radial scale. Moving beyond magnitude-based screening, we show that this warped geometry supplies two complementary tests, one radial and one structural, that a single norm cannot provide. We then introduce FUSE, a structure-aware robust aggregator that uses a small trusted labeled dataset for coefficient recovery, scale and cone-consistency screening, and post-screening step-size control. Across four benchmarks and seven Byzantine attacks, FUSE improves seed-wise worst-attack accuracy over the strongest baseline on each benchmark by 3.9--30.1 percentage points, while largely preserving the influence of the high-loss honest clients that fairness is meant to protect.

title: Wavelet compression for sampling deep Gaussian processes
summary: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) use iterative sampling to create non-stationary random fields. This is notoriously expensive because the covariance at each non-initial layer depends on the realised field from the layer below, so it changes with every sample. Moreover, standard fast sampling techniques like circulant embedding or matrix compression fail since the underlying kernel usually lacks the necessary regularity and structure. We develop and analyse a wavelet compression method for convolution Matérn DGPs. At each layer the covariance matrix is compressed using wavelets and a Lanczos algorithm computes the random sample. For specific parameter ranges involving the smoothness of the Matérn kernel as well as the smoothness of the wavelets, we show that the accumulative compression and sampling errors through all layers decay exponentially with increasing truncation parameter. We obtain a practical DGP sampling algorithm by choosing a truncation that gives log-linear covariance storage and matrix-vector costs, enabling DGP sampling at nearly linear computational cost.

title: CSWBench: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Code-Switching in Creative Writing
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated multilingual capabilities across diverse language generation and understanding tasks. Yet effective code-switching requires more than multilingual proficiency: models must decide when, where, and why to switch languages in ways that fit the surrounding context. This context-sensitive ability remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce CSWBench, a benchmark for evaluating context-sensitive code-switching in creative writing through two complementary settings: Focused Narrative and Extended Narrative. We further propose CSWEval, a theory-informed framework with two complementary levels: event-level evaluation of Licensing, Contextual Appropriateness, and Functional Gain, and whole-text evaluation of task-specific quality---overall literary and narrative quality in Focused Narrative and quality emphasizing multilingual organization in Extended Narrative. Evaluating twelve LLMs, we find that models exhibit meaningful but uneven code-switching competence across narrative contexts. Model differences are particularly pronounced in multilingual literary integration, while multilingual-focused dimensions show stronger difficulty effects overall than the general narrative dimensions; narratively salient switches are associated with stronger contextual and functional realization; and event-level CS quality is moderately associated with whole-text performance.

title: Resolution Allocation with Learnable Resizing and Spectral Filter Parameterization
comments: 5 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to ICASSP 2027
summary: Learnable downsampling and spectral-domain filter parameterizations have each made convolutional networks more flexible, but their interaction has not been systematically examined. We bridge this gap by examining convolutional kernels learned in the spatial and spectral domains, together with learned downsampling ratios under a cropped resizing implementation. We find that spectral and spatial kernels respond differently to learned resolution allocation, with larger gains for the spectral kernel. We observe this consistently on three datasets (EuroSAT, CIFAR-10 and STL-10) and at two model sizes (differences in accuracy gain of +0.013 to +0.028 on held-out test sets). Part of this difference reflects the greater gain of the spectral kernel from retaining more spatial area, but the difference remains positive when total retained area is matched. This pattern is observed across datasets and model sizes, although its magnitude and dependence on the complexity budget vary with model size and the resizing implementation.
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to ICASSP 2027

title: TANGO: RNA Topology and Geometry Co-Design
summary: Designing RNA sequences that satisfy target tertiary-structure objectives is an important problem in RNA engineering, with broad applications in synthetic biology and therapeutics. Existing 3D RNA design methods have made substantial progress, but they largely treat the target fold as a geometry-only objective. This is incomplete for RNA, whose functional folds are specified not only by tertiary geometry but also by secondary base-pairing topology. We therefore formulate RNA inverse design as a topology-and-geometry co-design problem and propose TANGO, a multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for this task. TANGO adopts a staged curriculum: it first learns a topology-aware policy from secondary-structure targets, then transfers this policy to tertiary-structure targets to train a general co-design model, and finally applies frontier-guided fine-tuning to refine target-specific trade-offs among secondary-structure fidelity, tertiary-structure fidelity, and sequence diversity. Experiments show that TANGO generates diverse and novel designs, improving tertiary- and secondary-structure performance by 18.3% and 52.7%, respectively, over the strongest baseline.

title: A Valid Watermark Is Not a Valid Identity: Spatial-Spectral Adversarial Face Evasion with Watermark Preservation
comments: Accepted at IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB 2026)
summary: Facial image watermarking can support traceability and certification in biometric pipelines, but provenance or manipulation detection alone does not guarantee reliable biometric identity. We introduce a watermark-preserving face evasion attack that targets this gap under a black-box watermarking setting, without access to the watermarking components. The proposed PGD-L_2 attack guides adversarial perturbations with spatial and spectral preservation terms to reduce face-recognition similarity while limiting pixel-level distortion and high-frequency changes that may interfere with hidden watermark cues. Evaluated on controlled facial images with two watermarking schemes, two face-recognition models, and two datasets, the attack achieves evasion rates above 92% at operational thresholds while preserving watermark recovery above 93% for StegaFormer and above 99.7% for FaceSigns, with visual quality above 47dB PSNR at epsilon_2=2.0. These results expose a structural gap in watermark-based facial certification: a face image can remain watermark-valid and visually faithful while becoming biometrically unreliable.
comment: Accepted at IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB 2026)

title: Neural POS Tagging for the Low-Resource Saraiki
summary: Part-of-speech tagging is a fundamental sequence labeling task and an important component for many downstream natural language processing applications. However, Saraiki, written from right to left in a Perso-Arabic script, remains an under-resourced Indo-Aryan language, despite being spoken as a mother tongue by 28,849,579 people (approximately 28.9 million) according to Pakistan 7th Population and Housing Census 2023. This paper presents a manually annotated Saraiki Universal POS tagging dataset developed from plain-text. We annotated the text with 17 POS categories. We evaluate three pretrained transformer encoders under the same fine-tuning setup: XLM-RoBERTa base, Urdu RoBERTa small, and multilingual DistilBERT. Experimental results over five random seeds show that XLM-RoBERTa base achieves the best performance, with 87.29% +/- 0.21% development accuracy and 88.60% +/- 0.21% test accuracy. Urdu RoBERTa small and multilingual DistilBERT also provide competitive results, suggesting that multilingual and related-script pretrained encoders are effective for Saraiki UPOS tagging. The dataset, evaluation setup, and baseline results introduced in this work provide a benchmark for future research on Saraiki NLP and low-resource sequence labeling.

title: Learning-Based Adaptive MPC for Magnetorquer-Only Satellite Attitude Control
comments: 8 pages, 8 figures, 1 table, Accepted for publication at the International Conference on Space Robotics (iSpaRo) 2026
summary: Nanosatellites (e.g., CubeSats) have the potential to carry out useful science and exploration activities for outer solar system exploration, but their small size leads to tradeoffs between attitude control and science capabilities. Magnetorquers offer a unique compromise as compact actuators that enable three-axis attitude control, but suffer from a loss of control authority and require full knowledge of the planetary magnetic field. In this work, we present a learning-based adaptive model predictive control (MPC) algorithm that plans rotational trajectories for the satellite while accounting for this loss of control authority. Key to our approach is the inclusion of a learned magnetic field model that is trained in simulation using low-fidelity magnetic field data. Using measurements collected online, our proposed algorithm adapts this learned magnetic field model using a simple last-layer update scheme, allowing the MPC controller to quickly adapt to the true planetary magnetic field model and more effectively plan attitude trajectories. We demonstrate the results of our proposed approach for two use cases, (1) Earth-orbit and (2) Uranus-orbit, and show that our learning-based adaptive MPC algorithm improves controller success for these system simulations by 5% and 61%, respectively.
comment: 8 pages, 8 figures, 1 table, Accepted for publication at the International Conference on Space Robotics (iSpaRo) 2026

title: From Semantic Editing Intentions to Persistent Parametric Controls for AI-Assisted Image Editing
summary: AI-powered image editing increasingly allows users to express high-level editing intentions, yet how these intentions are translated into concrete editing actions often remains difficult to understand. We present Atelier, a semantic image editing tool that uses image semantics and user intent to determine which editing controls to surface and how to initialize them. Guided by a formative study with eight image-editing practitioners, Atelier composes context-specific, directly manipulable controls that users can refine rather than committing AI interpretations directly to finished edits. In a within-subjects study with 12 practitioners, participants preferred AI-composed controls, described them as supporting creative exploration, and actively refined AI proposals. However, experiences of control were mixed, and interviews highlighted limited insight into why particular controls and values were proposed. Our findings suggest that making AI interpretations actionable through manipulable controls can support exploration and refinement, but actionability alone does not make those interpretations transparent to all users.

title: Towards Efficient Threat Intelligence Instruction Tuning via Quality-Aware and Optimal Transport-Guided Data Selection
summary: High-quality data is essential for improving instruction tuning in threat intelligence analysis. However, existing methods for generating cybersecurity instruction data lack reliable quality assessment mechanisms, and gradient influence-based data selection methods primarily focus on single-sample matching, failing to cover diverse and complex security capabilities. To address these issues, we propose CTI-TDS, a Targeted Data Selection method for instruction tuning in Cyber Threat Intelligence analysis. Specifically, we first filter high-quality CTI instructions by integrating instruction style consistency and security knowledge verification. Furthermore, we formulate gradient influence as a distribution alignment problem, learning a gradient subspace of target tasks and applying entropic regularized optimal transport to optimize distribution matching between training samples and target tasks, enabling diversity-aware data selection. We conduct extensive experiments on CTIBench across multiple large language models. Experimental results demonstrate that when fine-tuning with only a small set of high-value instruction data, CTI-TDS outperforms existing data selection methods and achieves competitive performance on threat intelligence analysis tasks.

title: Scaled Companion Linearizations for Coefficientwise Backward Stability
summary:
A central goal in solving a polynomial eigenvalue problem is to compute eigenpairs that are exact for a nearby polynomial, with each coefficient perturbation bounded by a modest multiple of unit roundoff times that coefficient's norm. A backward stable eigensolver for a linearization does not automatically provide this coefficientwise relative guarantee. Scaling can improve accuracy, but a single scaling may not work across a widely spread spectrum.
  We construct a family of scaled companion linearizations that covers the nonzero complex plane. Each linearization is paired with a region and an eigenvector recovery rule for which the backward-error amplification factor is bounded at exact pencil eigenvectors, independently of coefficient norm disparities. Tropical roots guide the construction, and their multiplicities reduce the number of required solves. These results provide a basis for coefficientwise relative backward stability across the spectrum.

title: From Plato to Aristotle: Toward a General Theory of Representation Hypotheses
summary: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) holds that increasingly capable models converge toward a common representation. However, recent studies have shown different views on aligning representations via their neighborhoods, spanning trees, and distances. We show that these views can differ because the alignment criteria behind them sit at different points of one lattice, and we formalize this explanation as the Lattice Representation Hypothesis (LRH). Under the LRH, the convergence claimed by the PRH is agreement at the top of the lattice, whereas its evidence comes from neighbor overlap, a criterion near the bottom. The Aristotelian Representation Hypothesis (ARH) restricts convergence to local neighborhoods because calibration keeps the growth of neighbor overlap with model size but largely removes that of centered kernel alignment. We show that this removal can come from calibrating a maximum over layers, so global convergence remains open. Back into Plato's Cave (BPC) infers coarse shared structure from the collapse of neighbor overlap on larger evaluation sets, whereas we trace it at least partly to a fixed number of neighbors covering shorter distances. We show that the spanning-tree overlap used by Structure over Geometry (SOG) mostly repeats one-nearest-neighbor overlap. The LRH also extends to independently trained models, whose training procedure and objective decide the criteria met reliably across runs. We prove this claim for the training procedure in a linear autoencoder and for the objective in a finite contrastive Gibbs model. Experiments on dozens of pretrained vision and language models and thousands of runs of both theoretical models support these conclusions. We hope this work paves the way toward a general theory of representation hypotheses, with a framework to analyze them and compare their evidence. Project page: https://eethanshi.github.io/LRH

title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
comments: Accepted as an oral at NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: AI Data Readiness for Scientific Discovery (AIDaR). Code: https://github.com/SamGijsen/interaction-flows
summary: Conditional generative models are increasingly used for scientific prediction beyond the direct training support. Yet scientific questions often concern whether one intervention changes the effect of another. Such interactions can be of primary interest while explaining little of the total variation, allowing models to appear accurate overall without recovering the relevant scientific effect. It remains unclear how these models learn interactions and when these successfully extrapolate to unseen conditions. We therefore study interaction recovery in flow-matching models using a physiological time-series simulator, drug dose-response data, combinatorial cell perturbations, and molecular conformer generations, where we separate recovery from hallucinated interaction structure. In the controlled setting, individual effects are learned much earlier than interactions and models hallucinate interactions where none exist. Across settings, we find qualitatively different generalization problems, with successful prediction depending on whether condition structure continues from observed to held-out targets. When it does, interactions are recoverable. If not, models can generate plausible responses while missing the interaction. We furthermore find that hallucinations increase as targets become less identifiable, and that successful interaction recovery in output space can fail under nonlinear readouts. Finally, we show that aggregate fidelity metrics can conceal whether models learn and extrapolate interactions.
comment: Accepted as an oral at NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: AI Data Readiness for Scientific Discovery (AIDaR). Code: https://github.com/SamGijsen/interaction-flows

title: Generating Accurate Microstructures of Anisotropic Magnetorheological Elastomers
summary: Anisotropic magnetorheological elastomers are magnetoactive smart materials whose complex magneto-mechanical behavior is strongly influenced by their underlying microstructure. Efficient and accurate multiscale simulations of these materials rely on small unit cells that reproduce the behavior of the real material. In this work, we present a framework for the generation and validation of such two-dimensional representative volume elements (RVEs) from a given microstructure image, assuming circular particles. The cells are generated through an optimization procedure where the two-point correlation function serves as a differentiable descriptor, while a minimum inter-particle distance is enforced as a constraint. To assess the equivalence of the generated cells, we compare their effective magneto-mechanical response with those of the reference microstructure. We demonstrate that the generated cells reproduce the reference response with high accuracy, also with substantially fewer particles. Consequently, the computational cost of subsequent multiscale simulations is reduced.

title: Asynchronous Distributed Multi-Sensor Fusion Over Sensor Track Hypotheses
comments: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Multisensor Fusion and Integration (MFI), Plzeň. 6 pages, 6 figures
summary: This work proposes a multi-target tracking solution that reasons over combinations of sensor-level tracks to perform distributed multiple hypothesis tracking (MHT) in an asynchronous multi-sensor network. This approach handles clustered target tracking and allows for efficient information pedigree summarization for distributed data fusion (DDF). By decomposing the association problem into partitioned hypothesis sets and fusing across sensor track combinations, the method reduces combinatorial complexity compared to traditional MHT approaches. Evaluation on a satellite constellation-based tracking scenario demonstrates improved estimation accuracy and data association quality compared to a reference target tracker with global nearest neighbor association.
comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Multisensor Fusion and Integration (MFI), Plzeň. 6 pages, 6 figures

title: Taking the PULSE of Medical Reasoning: Step-Level Retrieval Timing for Knowledge-Grounded Inference
summary: Reliable medical reasoning requires LLMs to dynamically access external biomedical evidence to improve factual trustworthiness and reasoning accuracy. However, indiscriminate retrieval can introduce noise and latency, raising a critical retrieval-timing problem: at each reasoning step, the system must decide whether the model's internal knowledge is reliable or external evidence is needed. We propose PUlSE, a lightweight probing method that uses the model's internal representations as intrinsic signals for step-level retrieval control. Our posterior trajectory analysis reveals that erroneous steps exhibit substantially higher inter-layer volatility than correct ones, suggesting unstable internal knowledge. Based on this finding, PUlSE trains a compact probe on inter-layer geometric features to detect factual errors upon step completion, and uses it as an adaptive trigger for retrieval and step regeneration. Across four medical benchmarks, PUlSE-timed retrieval matches exhaustive per-step retrieval in accuracy while reducing retrieval calls by 72%, and can transfer to an unseen legal domain, indicating potential domain-agnostic generality. Overall, our study provides an initial step toward shifting retrieval-trigger design from surface-level confidence estimates to internal activation dynamics for adaptive access.

title: CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval
summary: Large language models increasingly generate multiple retrieval actions jointly, while downstream systems often provide only one reward for the resulting set. Broadcasting this reward provides a valid score-function gradient estimator for the expected set-level objective, but does not determine a coalition-dependent within-set attribution. We introduce CASI (Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval), which constructs the missing counterfactual information through snapshot-grounded set intervention: generate and retrieve once, hold replayable snapshot components fixed, and evaluate alternative subsets under common conditions. Shapley aggregation converts these marginals into within-set credit, which bounded zero-sum advantage shaping incorporates into policy optimization. For m >= 4, singleton, leave-one-out, and full-set endpoints do not generally determine the Shapley allocation; under additive set values, extra coalition evaluations are redundant. In a five-action sponsored-search setting, exhaustive auction replay over 1,200 requests reveals substantial coalition dependence. Under the training-time evaluator, CASI achieves the highest median cosine similarity to a replay-defined Shapley reference among evaluated credit rules; under a sensitivity backend, CASI does not outperform Singleton. Across five independent training runs, CASI-trained policies achieve higher held-out auction-replay set value than Singleton- or Broadcast-trained policies. In a randomized seven-day production A/B test on 10% of traffic, the CASI-trained policy yields an observed 3.51% lift in the primary advertiser-value metric over production control.

title: MMLA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through RTT and RTMA
summary: An agent can improve its behavior within an unresolved problem by changing how it acts and which experience it retains. We propose MMLA-RSI, a recursive self-improvement scheme with two implementations in Memory-Mediated Learning Architecture: Reasoning-Time Training (RTT) changes the policy state $Φ$, while Reasoning-Time Memory Adaptation (RTMA) changes authoritative memory $M$. Each route also makes its adaptation method an object of improvement. A current numerical updater trains the policy proposing its successor; a current memory manager chooses the records available to the process proposing its successor. An independently admitted successor takes over the same role in the next generation. We give bounded executable rule languages, shared task/proposal interfaces, and one algorithm for either route or their composition. The RTT instance changes scalar schedules in a clipped-momentum update. The RTMA instance chooses NULL or a complete-row write with possible eviction. A fixed interpreter, trusted committer, and independent evaluator bound what can change. State versions, read closures, and conditional properties describe causal execution, accepted transitions, and finite work. Existing numerical-component studies motivate the construction. In four-candidate program selection, retaining LARC feedback updates reduces expected error by 24.65 and 36.65 percentage points for two trained initializations. In chronological continuous-integration replay, feedback binding is positive while retention increases loss. Completed SQL studies improve substantially over an unadapted substrate but do not establish the required additional online benefit. These results characterize their declared components. The two recursive routes and their joint realization are specified here; their beneficial recursive chains and discovery efficiency remain to be evaluated.

title: Simple, Faster (min, +) Matrix Multiplication and APSP
summary: In this note, we provide a deterministic algorithm that computes the $(\min, +)$-Matrix Product $C = A * B$ of two $N \times N$ matrices $A$ and $B$ with polynomially bounded integer entries in $\tilde{O}(N^{2.9964})$ time, improving upon the exponent of $O(N^{2.9995})$ time obtained in the recent breakthrough by Anthropic (Alman and Vassilevska Williams, 2026). Our algorithm uses a phased approach first proposed by Bringmann, Grandoni, Saha, and Vassilevska Williams in 2016. The phased approach produces an approximation $\tilde{C}$ of $C$ in truly subcubic time such that the number of remaining triples $(i,k,j): A_{i,k}+B_{k,j} < \tilde{C}(i,j)$ is truly subcubic. This provided strong evidence that a truly subcubic $(\min, +)$-Matrix Product and therefore, a truly subcubic algorithm for All Pairs Shortest Paths (APSP) may exist. However, to find the remaining triples in subcubic time, a sparse certificate is needed whose construction was not known. We use the thin matrix product theorem of the recent breakthrough to provide such a certificate. This gives a simple modular subcubic algorithm for APSP.

title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization
summary: Orthogonal transforms have emerged as an effective tool for low-bit quantization of large language models (LLMs), as they reshape activation distributions without changing the underlying model function. Existing approaches typically rely either on fixed data-agnostic transforms, such as Hadamard rotations, or on calibration-time optimization of learned rotations. We study rotation selection from first principles and show that maximizing covariance leads to spectral alignment and provides a principled criterion for constructing quantization-friendly orthogonal transforms. Based on this insight, we propose SpectrumQuant, a closed-form rotation method that estimates activation covariance from calibration data and uses it to construct a covariance-aware orthogonal transform for post-training quantization. Our formulation characterizes quantization-friendly rotations as compositions of alignment and mixing components, while recovering Hadamard matrices as a special case. Interestingly, a class of butterfly matrices belongs to this category. In the realm of LLM quantization, SpectrumQuant bridges the gap between data-agnostic structured rotations and learned rotations, providing an effective and efficient data-aware alternative for post-training quantization. Experiments on Llama and Mistral models show that SpectrumQuant is competitive with state-of-the-art rotation strategies while requiring less than one-third of the GPU memory and significantly less time than learned rotations approaches like SpinQuant and DartQuant.

title: Event Cameras versus Frame Cameras for Synthetic-Aperture Imaging: A Simulation Study
summary: Synthetic-aperture imaging (SAI) removes occluders such as foliage by integrating many views of a scene along a camera path. It has so far been used mainly with frame cameras. We ask whether an event camera has advantages for SAI, and answer the question in simulation, where both sensors see exactly the same scene and the same camera movement. A densely rendered Blender sequence is turned into frames with an EMVA~1288 noise model of an industrial global-shutter camera, and into an event stream with the v2e simulator parameterized like a Sony IMX636. The frames are integrated with the existing airborne optical sectioning renderer. For the events we add a new integration path that projects every single event onto the focal plane at its own interpolated pose, so no events have to be binned into frames. We compare the two sensors in three main runs and an additional dark high-speed test. In a bright scene at 25,m/s the frame camera records only three images on the path and cannot remove the occluder, while the event camera reconstructs the target, even after an event-rate controller drops most of its events to fit the camera link. At the same speed in a 5,lux scene the event camera no longer resolves the target either. In a 5,lux scene at 5,m/s both sensors reconstruct the target at similar quality. We also compare the data one traversal of the aperture costs. At high speed the capped event stream still shows the target at the same data volume as the three frames. At 1,m/s we compare both cameras at two matched data budgets, and there the event camera has no advantage over the frame camera in reconstruction quality. The data rate of the event camera depends on the scene and is highest exactly in the fast bright scenes where it is needed most.

title: MUSEBENCH: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Music Detection and Artifact Analysis
summary: Advances in generative AI have made it possible to produce music that is nearly indistinguishable from human compositions, raising the question of whether such works can be reliably distinguished from human compositions. We present MUSEBENCH, a large-scale benchmark for AI-generated music detection and artifact analysis, comprising over 361K tracks. The dataset includes human compositions, stylistically matched music generated by ten state-of-the-art open-source and commercial models, such as Suno and Udio, as well as human-AI co-creations and variants processed with adversarial perturbations, compression, and acoustic post-processing. Using MUSEBENCH, we benchmark 11 automated detectors and evaluate their accuracy, generalization, and robustness, under default, out-of-domain, and transformed-variant experiment settings. We further conduct a comprehensive artifact analysis through acoustic feature inspection, identifying recurring signatures such as non-idiomatic harmonic progressions, upsampling induced spectral periodicities, and violations of physical performance constraints. Our findings reveal key strengths and vulnerabilities of existing detectors and provide practical insights for building more reliable AI music detection systems.

title: Reflect After Failure: Brain-Inspired Self-Evolving Agents for Embodied Spatial Intelligence
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in spatial reasoning, and self-evolving agents further extend these capabilities to embodied environments by learning from interactions. However, current self-evolution remains particularly challenging in embodied spatial tasks, complex and multi-step decisions from partial visual evidence making it difficult to determine why an execution fails. The failure may stem from misperception, insufficient exploration, or incorrect planning, yet execution feedback alone rarely reveals which component is responsible. As a result, simply accumulating interaction experience can reinforce ineffective strategies. To address this, we propose HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent for embodied spatial intelligence, inspired by metacognitive monitoring and hippocampal memory consolidation. Through Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection, HiMeco diagnoses failures in perception-exploration-planning (PEP), then compares execution attempts to derive reusable strategies and guidance for avoiding recurring errors. It also abstracts interaction programs into parameterized skills, using evidence contracts and execution-based validation to determine their retention and reuse. These strategies and skills guide subsequent interactions, with memory updated only between rounds and model parameters kept frozen. HiMeco achieves state-of-the-art performance on ESI-Bench, and it also improves accuracy on EmbSpatial-Bench by 3.94 percentage points without evolution.

title: Building Sound Evaluation Practices for Rust-Based Security Frameworks
summary: Background: Rust is a modern programming language known for its focus on usability, concurrency, and security. However, empirical studies reveal that Rust is still affected by software vulnerabilities, with hundreds of memory safety issues found in Rust programs, including Rust's standard library. As a result, additional tool-assisted security testing is crucial to enhance the security of Rust code. Evaluating such tools, however, is highly complex. While there is substantial research on evaluating C/C++ security frameworks, including test sets, serious issues in published evaluations have been identified, undermining their scientific soundness and reproducibility. In practice, selecting an inadequate implementation (e.g., a fuzzer) can lead to missed vulnerabilities ultimately compromising a program's security. Aims: Our methodology aims to help researchers to conduct scientifically sound evaluations in order to prevent similar issues with the evaluation of security tools and frameworks in the Rust ecosystem. Method: We systematically analyze existing evaluation literature to develop the first sound methodology for Rust based evaluations. Our guidelines provide enough flexibility to support a variety of use cases. To quantify the performance of a security tool, we introduce an automated approach to inject unsafe code coverage oracles, which require no forward porting, avoid overfitting, and allow updating test sets in the future. We also present methods to quantify the diversity of a Rust test set, ensuring that the results are applicable to a large set of existing Rust programs. We practically apply our methodology in our evaluation of the most popular Rust fuzzers. Results: We show the practical applicability of our design and conduct an evaluation with a diverse test set of 20 Rust projects. [...]

title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation For Robot Policies
summary: Reinforcement-learning policies for robot locomotion can fail at deployment when operating conditions shift (e.g., rough or slippery terrain, payload changes, sensing degradation), and retraining or manual recalibration is often infeasible under on-device latency and memory constraints. We study test-time adaptation (TTA) for robotic control: adapting a pretrained policy online and in a self-supervised manner during execution, without access to rewards. Our starting point is a lightweight baseline that updates only the actor using a frozen pretrained critic as a deployment-time performance surrogate. Building on this, we introduce TEMPO, a test-time entropy-regularized, memory-guided policy optimization method that stabilizes critic-driven updates under severe shift. TEMPO combines (i) an entropy-promoting regularizer on the critic's predictive distribution to mitigate overconfident extrapolation, and (ii) a score-based memory, inspired by prioritized replay, that prioritizes low-value ("hard") observations and applies importance sampling to focus limited computation on the most informative deployment conditions. Across Go1, Go2, and G1 in MuJoCo Playground under four representative shifts and multiple architectures, TEMPO yields consistent gains, reaching up to 80% improvement in a single-device setting. We further validate on a physical Unitree Go2 with an added calf payload, where fully on-device adaptation improves performance over the non-adapted baseline across real-world episodes.

title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains, yet their susceptibility to backdoor attacks remains a formidable challenge. While existing defenses have evolved from visual-centric patch cues to unsupervised internal attention statistics, they are fundamentally constrained by a reliance on static snapshots and attack-specific heuristics. Given the intricate interplay between dual modalities, the vast design space for multimodal triggers allows diverse threats, such as textual injections, sub-perceptual noises, and coordinated cross-modal triggers, to easily circumvent such rigid priors, particularly when attack types are unknown in real-world applications. In this paper, we rethink backdoor detection by shifting the diagnostic paradigm from static observations to dynamic output evolution. We observe that a successful attack inevitably hijacks the model's decoding trajectory, skewing internal modal contributions during generation while maintaining an abnormal output invariance despite input perturbations. To capture this behavior, we propose EVO-Detect, a unified detection framework that monitors the dynamic evolution of internal signals during early decoding steps through two complementary channels: Attention Flow and Logits Flow. The attention branch measures how image-text attention allocation evolves during early generation, whereas the logits branch quantifies the sensitivity of the output distribution to modal perturbations through interventional ablations. We then convert these trajectories into compact sample-level metrics and normalize them against negative-control signatures so that natural perturbations are less likely to be mistaken for backdoor evidence. Extensive evaluations show that our approach substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines such as BYE and TCAP across diverse attack families.

title: TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Large-scale robot learning increasingly relies on diverse human demonstrations, yet tactile manipulation data remain difficult to scale, and existing multimodal datasets often lack consistent quality control and structured supervision. We present TacClaw-Infinity, a large-scale structured Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) dataset for contact-rich manipulation, collected with TacClaw, a tactile-enabled UMI-style handheld interface that records synchronized visual observations, fingertip tactile signals, and end-effector trajectories without requiring a target robot during data collection. TacClaw-Infinity is built through a distributed worldwide collection across homes, laboratories, industrial workplaces, retail stores, and outdoor environments including tasks contributed by academic and industrial collaborators. Together, these efforts yield over 10,000 hours, 1 million episodes, and 1 billion frames spanning more than 1,000 task types. We develop a scalable pipeline for trajectory reconstruction, multimodal quality control, embodiment-aware filtering, and structured annotation, covering contact-centric segmentation, subtask description, and spatial grounding. We validate TacClaw-Infinity at both the data and model levels: At the data level, we assess the collection interface, the action-space compatibility of the curated demonstrations, and the structured annotations, while for the model level, we demonstrate cross-embodiment transfer across three heterogeneous robots without robot-specific demonstrations.

title: Delay-Enabled Adaptive Learning of Time-Varying Parameters
summary: This paper proposes a novel adaptive learning method for unknown time-varying parameters by deliberately incorporating a delay into the parameter update. Specifically, a conventional adaptive estimator is augmented with only one additional dynamic state, which estimates the parameter variation rate from the difference between current and previous parameter estimates. The method fundamentally changes the influence of time variation on estimation performance: the resulting estimation error is governed by the second derivative of the unknown parameter rather than its first derivative. Under persistent excitation, a small-gain analysis proves exponential stability of the complete estimation-error system and establishes explicit bounds for the parameter, state-prediction, and parameter-rate errors. In particular, accurate learning of linearly time-varying parameters and their unknown rates can be guaranteed with errors converging exponentially fast to zero. Numerical comparisons with conventional adaptive estimation and a recent timevarying parameter estimator demonstrate superior learning performance in the considered examples. The proposed delay-enabled adaptive estimator requires neither state derivatives nor any assumed model of parameter variation, and its implementation consists of one delayed difference and a first-order filter. These results thus provide a direct extension of adaptive learning from constant to time-varying parameters without sacrificing the simplicity of the conventional adaptive estimation mechanism.

AI.title_translation: 延迟使能的时变参数自适应学习
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种通过在参数更新中引入延迟来学习未知时变参数的新型自适应方法，它能有效估计参数变化率，并实现对时变参数的精确学习。
AI.motivation: 现有的自适应估计方法在处理时变参数时，估计误差通常受参数的一阶导数影响，导致性能不佳。本文旨在提供一种直接将自适应学习从常数参数扩展到时变参数的方法，同时保持传统自适应估计机制的简洁性，并改善时变参数估计的性能。
AI.method: 本文提出了一种新型延迟使能的自适应学习方法。该方法通过在参数更新中引入延迟，将一个额外的动态状态添加到传统的自适应估计器中。这个附加状态通过当前和之前的参数估计之间的差异来估计参数变化率。其实现仅包含一个延迟差分和一个一阶滤波器，无需状态导数或任何参数变化的模型假设。
AI.result: 该方法将估计误差的控制从未知参数的一阶导数转变为二阶导数。在持续激励下，小增益分析证明了完整估计误差系统的指数稳定性，并建立了参数、状态预测和参数率误差的明确界限。特别地，可以保证线性时变参数及其未知速率的精确学习，误差以指数速度收敛到零。数值比较表明，在所考虑的例子中，该方法比传统自适应估计器和最近的时变参数估计器具有更优越的学习性能。
AI.conclusion: 本研究提供了一种直接将自适应学习从常数参数扩展到时变参数的方法，且不牺牲传统自适应估计机制的简洁性。通过引入延迟和估计参数变化率，实现了对未知时变参数的有效和精确学习，显著改善了时变参数估计的性能。
AI.translation: 本文提出了一种通过在参数更新中故意引入延迟来学习未知时变参数的新型自适应学习方法。具体来说，传统的自适应估计器仅通过一个额外的动态状态进行增强，该状态从当前和先前的参数估计之间的差异中估计参数变化率。该方法从根本上改变了时间变化对估计性能的影响：由此产生的估计误差由未知参数的二阶导数而非其一阶导数决定。在持续激励下，小增益分析证明了完整估计误差系统的指数稳定性，并建立了参数、状态预测和参数率误差的明确界限。特别是，可以保证线性时变参数及其未知速率的精确学习，误差以指数速度快速收敛到零。与传统自适应估计和最近的时变参数估计器进行数值比较，结果表明在所考虑的例子中，该方法具有优越的学习性能。所提出的延迟使能自适应估计器既不需要状态导数，也不需要任何假设的参数变化模型，其实现包括一个延迟差分和一个一阶滤波器。因此，这些结果在不牺牲传统自适应估计机制简洁性的前提下，提供了将自适应学习从常数参数直接扩展到时变参数的方法。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种新颖的延迟使能自适应学习方法，用于估计未知时变参数。通过在参数更新中引入延迟并增加一个动态状态来估计参数变化率，该方法将估计误差的控制权从参数的一阶导数转移到二阶导数。理论分析证明了系统的指数稳定性，并保证了线性时变参数的精确学习。数值实验表明其性能优于现有方法。该方法实现简单，无需状态导数或参数变化模型，成功地将自适应学习扩展到时变参数。
AI.keywords: 自适应学习, 时变参数, 延迟, 参数变化率, 指数稳定性
AI.comments: 这项工作创新性地利用延迟来处理时变参数，并通过估计参数变化率，将估计误差的敏感性从参数的一阶导数降低到二阶导数，这在理论上是一个显著的进步。其优点在于实现简单（仅需一个延迟差分和一个一阶滤波器），且无需预设参数变化模型或状态导数，这大大提高了其在实际应用中的可行性。它成功地在保持传统自适应估计机制简洁性的同时，解决了时变参数的自适应学习问题，具有重要的理论和实践意义。

title: Cache-Aided Linear Function Computation
comments: 11 pages, 2 figures. A shorter version has been submitted to the 2027 IEEE Information Theory Workshop (ITW)
summary: We study cache-aided linear computation in distributed systems where each source generates and stores its own data. An external receiver requests a linear combination of these data, and the sources use information cached before the request is known to reduce the communication needed to recover the requested result. In our model, each of the $N$ sources stores its own independent file over a finite field and has an additional cache of normalized size $M$. The receiver must recover any requested linear combination with zero error from the messages sent by the sources over separate noiseless links. We establish a lower bound on the worst-case communication rate over any finite field by analyzing several requests under the same cache placement. This bound determines the optimal rate when no additional cache is available. For binary files, we propose parity-aided placement (PAP), a coded-placement scheme that combines cached parities with uncoded symbols. For every $N\geq3$, we characterize its communication rate for each request and optimize its placement parameters to obtain a closed-form worst-case rate. The resulting achievable rate meets the lower bound for $0\leq M\leq1/(2N-1)$ and $M\geq(N-1)/N$, establishing the optimal memory--rate tradeoff in these two ranges.

AI.title_translation: 缓存辅助线性函数计算
AI.tldr: 该论文研究了分布式系统中缓存辅助的线性函数计算，旨在通过预缓存信息减少通信量，并在特定内存范围内建立了最优的内存-速率折衷。
AI.motivation: 在分布式系统中，当外部接收器请求数据的线性组合时，利用预缓存信息来减少恢复所需结果的通信量。
AI.method: 1. 建立任何有限域上最坏情况通信速率的下界。2. 对于二进制文件，提出了一种结合缓存奇偶校验和未编码符号的编码放置方案——奇偶校验辅助放置（PAP）。3. 描述了PAP方案的通信速率，并优化其放置参数以获得封闭形式的最坏情况速率。
AI.result: 1. 建立了最坏情况通信速率的下界，该下界在没有额外缓存时确定了最优速率。2. 提出的PAP方案在$0 \leq M \leq 1/(2N-1)$和$M \geq (N-1)/N$的范围内实现了与下界相符的可达速率。3. 在这两个范围内建立了最优的内存-速率折衷。
AI.conclusion: 该论文通过提出奇偶校验辅助放置（PAP）方案，并在特定内存范围内达到理论下界，从而建立了缓存辅助线性函数计算的最优内存-速率折衷。
AI.translation: 我们研究分布式系统中缓存辅助的线性计算，其中每个源生成并存储自己的数据。外部接收器请求这些数据的线性组合，源利用在请求已知之前缓存的信息来减少恢复所需结果所需的通信。在我们的模型中，N个源中的每一个都存储其独立的有限域文件，并具有一个归一化大小为M的额外缓存。接收器必须从源通过独立的无噪声链路发送的消息中以零误差恢复任何请求的线性组合。我们通过分析在相同缓存放置下的多个请求，建立了任何有限域上最坏情况通信速率的下界。这个下界确定了没有额外缓存时的最优速率。对于二进制文件，我们提出了奇偶校验辅助放置（PAP），这是一种结合缓存奇偶校验和未编码符号的编码放置方案。对于每个N≥3，我们描述了其每个请求的通信速率，并优化其放置参数以获得封闭形式的最坏情况速率。由此实现的可达速率在0≤M≤1/(2N-1)和M≥(N-1)/N的范围内满足下界，从而在这两个范围内建立了最优的内存-速率折衷。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了分布式系统中缓存辅助的线性函数计算，旨在通过预缓存数据减少通信开销。研究人员建立了一个最坏情况通信速率的下界，并针对二进制文件提出了一种名为奇偶校验辅助放置（PAP）的编码放置方案。该方案在特定内存大小范围（$0 \leq M \leq 1/(2N-1)$ 和 $M \geq (N-1)/N$）内达到了最优的内存-速率折衷，与理论下界相符。
AI.keywords: 缓存辅助计算, 线性函数, 分布式系统, 通信速率, 内存-速率折衷
AI.comments: 该论文通过引入奇偶校验辅助放置（PAP）方案，在缓存辅助的分布式线性函数计算领域取得了重要进展。它不仅建立了理论下界，还在特定内存范围内实现了最优的内存-速率折衷，对于理解和设计高效分布式计算系统具有重要意义。

title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep-Learning based DoA Estimators for Real-Time ISAC Beamforming
summary: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems rely on accurate Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation for effective beamforming and spectral-efficiency enhancement. While numerous classical and deep-learning-based DoA estimation methods have been reported in the literature, their suitability for real-time ISAC operation remains insufficiently understood because practical deployment requires consideration of both estimation accuracy and computational latency. This paper presents a unified evaluation framework for systematically comparing classical and learning-based DoA estimators within an ISAC beamforming pipeline. Representative classical and learning-based DoA estimators, together with an ensemble architecture, are integrated with Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based beamforming and evaluated under identical operating conditions. The impact of DoA estimation accuracy, inference latency, beamforming-weight generation time, and resulting effective spectral efficiency is investigated. Results show that different estimators occupy distinct operating points in the accuracy-latency-performance design space. Although learning-based approaches substantially reduce estimation time compared with MUSIC, the overall processing latency increasingly becomes dominated by the computational cost of SVD-based beamforming. Among the evaluated methods, the Regression Convolutional Neural Network (RCNN) exhibits a favorable balance between estimation accuracy, computational efficiency, and beamforming performance, making it a promising candidate for real-time ISAC deployment. The findings further suggest that future low-latency ISAC systems may benefit from beamforming strategies that reduce or avoid computationally intensive SVD-based beamforming-weight generation.

AI.title_translation: 深度学习方向估计器在实时ISAC波束成形中的比较评估
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一个统一的评估框架，用于系统比较经典和基于深度学习的DoA估计器在实时ISAC波束成形中的性能。研究发现，RCNN在估计精度、计算效率和波束成形性能之间取得了良好平衡，是实时ISAC部署的有希望的候选。同时，SVD波束成形是整体延迟的主要瓶颈。
AI.motivation: 集成感知与通信（ISAC）系统依赖精确的方向到达（DoA）估计来实现有效的波束成形和频谱效率提升。然而，现有文献中对经典和深度学习DoA估计方法在实时ISAC操作中的适用性理解不足，因为实际部署需要同时考虑估计精度和计算延迟。
AI.method: 本文提出了一个统一的评估框架，用于系统比较ISAC波束成形管道中的经典和学习型DoA估计器。将代表性的经典和学习型DoA估计器以及集成架构与基于奇异值分解（SVD）的波束成形相结合，并在相同的操作条件下进行评估。研究了DoA估计精度、推理延迟、波束成形权重生成时间以及由此产生的有效频谱效率的影响。
AI.result: 结果表明，不同的估计器在精度-延迟-性能设计空间中占据不同的操作点。尽管基于学习的方法与MUSIC相比显著减少了估计时间，但整体处理延迟日益由基于SVD的波束成形的计算成本主导。在评估的方法中，回归卷积神经网络（RCNN）在估计精度、计算效率和波束成形性能之间表现出良好的平衡。
AI.conclusion: 回归卷积神经网络（RCNN）在估计精度、计算效率和波束成形性能之间取得了良好平衡，使其成为实时ISAC部署的有希望的候选。研究结果进一步表明，未来的低延迟ISAC系统可能受益于减少或避免计算密集型SVD波束成形权重生成的波束成形策略。
AI.translation: 集成感知与通信（ISAC）系统依赖于精确的到达方向（DoA）估计来实现有效的波束成形和频谱效率提升。尽管文献中报道了许多经典和基于深度学习的DoA估计方法，但由于实际部署需要同时考虑估计精度和计算延迟，它们在实时ISAC操作中的适用性仍未得到充分理解。本文提出了一个统一的评估框架，用于系统比较ISAC波束成形管道中的经典和学习型DoA估计器。代表性的经典和学习型DoA估计器，连同集成架构，与基于奇异值分解（SVD）的波束成形相结合，并在相同的操作条件下进行评估。研究了DoA估计精度、推理延迟、波束成形权重生成时间以及由此产生的有效频谱效率的影响。结果表明，不同的估计器在精度-延迟-性能设计空间中占据不同的操作点。尽管基于学习的方法与MUSIC相比显著减少了估计时间，但整体处理延迟日益由基于SVD的波束成形的计算成本主导。在评估的方法中，回归卷积神经网络（RCNN）在估计精度、计算效率和波束成形性能之间表现出良好的平衡，使其成为实时ISAC部署的有希望的候选。研究结果进一步表明，未来的低延迟ISAC系统可能受益于减少或避免计算密集型SVD波束成形权重生成的波束成形策略。
AI.summary: 本论文旨在评估不同DoA估计器在实时ISAC系统中的适用性，重点关注估计精度和计算延迟。通过一个统一的评估框架，比较了经典和深度学习方法与SVD波束成形相结合的性能。研究发现，深度学习方法可以显著减少估计时间，但整体延迟主要受SVD波束成形计算成本的影响。其中，回归卷积神经网络（RCNN）在精度、效率和性能之间表现出最佳平衡，是实时ISAC部署的理想选择。研究还建议未来低延迟ISAC系统应探索非SVD的波束成形策略。
AI.keywords: DoA估计, ISAC, 深度学习, 波束成形, 实时系统
AI.comments: 本文通过建立统一的评估框架，系统地比较了经典与深度学习DoA估计器在实时ISAC波束成形中的性能，具有较强的实践指导意义。其创新之处在于不仅关注估计精度，还深入分析了计算延迟对整体系统性能的影响。揭示了SVD波束成形作为主要延迟瓶颈的发现，为未来ISAC系统设计提供了关键方向，即寻找更高效的波束成形策略。RCNN的优异表现也为实时系统部署提供了明确的技术选择。

title: Anuvani-Diarization: Zero Shot Speaker Diarization and Annotation Conventions Across 22 Languages
summary: India's 22 scheduled languages are spoken by over a billion people in conversations that mix languages, often within one turn, overlap freely, and take place over telephones, in meetings, and in media. Knowing who spoke when, the task of speaker diarization, is essential to speech applications for such conversation: voice agents conversing with several people at once, speaker attributed transcription of meetings and calls, contact center analytics, and media monitoring. We present a systematic study of speaker diarization across all 22 languages on IndicDiarBench and introduce Anuvani-Diarization, which adapts a self-supervised end-to-end segmentation model to Indian conversation with uncertainty aware silver supervision. Evaluated zero shot alongside nine recent diarization systems, it reaches a duration weighted diarization error rate (DER) of 16.78% on all 1,164 recordings, the lowest of all systems we ran and second only to the best published result (16.0%), and leads the three strongest rivals in 14 of 22 languages. It matches its parent on six international benchmarks. We also show that the benchmark's utterance level annotation convention is a hidden variable worth 1.9 to 4.1 DER points, depending on the system, and that a convention learned from other Indian transcriptions does not transfer.

AI.title_translation: Anuvani-Diarization：跨22种语言的零样本说话人分离与标注规范
AI.tldr: 提出了一种名为Anuvani-Diarization的零样本说话人分离系统，专门应对印度22种复杂官方语言的多语言对话场景，取得了领先的性能。
AI.motivation: 印度拥有22种官方语言，其对话场景高度复杂（包含语码转换、自由重叠说话以及多样化的音频媒介），现有的说话人分离系统难以有效应对这些挑战，亟需开发适用于多语言的鲁棒说话人分离系统。
AI.method: 通过引入具有不确定性感知银标签监督的方法，将自监督端到端分割模型适应于印度对话场景，并在IndicDiarBench上评估了其在22种语言上的零样本性能。
AI.result: 在包含1,164个录音的测试中，Anuvani-Diarization取得了16.78%的持续时间加权说话人分离错误率（DER），在22种语言中的14种表现优于最强竞争对手，并在六个国际基准测试中与其父模型表现相当。此外，研究发现标注规范会带来1.9到4.1 DER点的差异。
AI.conclusion: Anuvani-Diarization系统在印度多语言说话人diarization任务中展现出卓越的零样本性能，证明了自监督端到端模型结合不确定性感知银标签监督在复杂多语言场景下的有效性。
AI.translation: 印度的22种预定语言拥有超过十亿人口，这些对话常包含语言混合（甚至在同一轮对话中）、自由重叠，且发生在电话、会议和媒体中。说话人分离（即知道谁在何时说话）对于此类对话的语音应用至关重要：如同时与多人对话的语音代理、会议和通话的说话人属性转录、呼叫中心分析以及媒体监控。我们对IndicDiarBench上的全部22种语言进行了系统的说话人分离研究，并推出了Anuvani-Diarization，它通过不确定性感知的银标签监督，将自监督端到端分割模型适应于印度对话。在与其他九个最新说话人分离系统一起进行的零样本评估中，它在所有1,164个录音上达到了16.78%的持续时间加权说话人分离错误率（DER），这是我们运行的所有系统中的最低值，仅次于最佳发表结果（16.0%），并在22种语言中的14种语言里超越了三个最强对手。它在六个国际基准测试中与其父模型相匹配。我们还表明，基准测试的 utterance 级标注规范是一个隐藏变量，根据系统的不同，其价值在1.9到4.1 DER点之间，并且从其他印度转录中学习到的规范无法迁移。
AI.summary: 论文介绍了Anuvani-Diarization，这是一个针对印度22种官方语言的零样本说话人分离系统。通过采用自监督端到端模型及不确定性感知银标签监督，该系统在复杂的印度对话场景中取得了领先的错误率，并探讨了标注规范对评估结果的关键影响。
AI.keywords: 说话人分离, 零样本, 印度语言, 自监督学习, 语音识别
AI.comments: 该论文针对印度22种官方语言复杂的语音环境，提出了Anuvani-Diarization系统，实现了零样本说话人 diarization，并在多语言基准测试中取得了领先性能，同时揭示了标注规范对评估结果的重要影响。

title: Argument Graph Uncertainty: Quantifying Uncertainty from the Logical Structure of Reasoning Chains
summary: Reliable uncertainty estimation is essential for deploying large language models in high-stakes reasoning tasks, yet most existing approaches rely on expensive sampling strategies or shallow token-level signals that ignore the internal logical structure of model outputs. We introduce Argument Graph Uncertainty, a post-hoc framework for multiple choice question tasks, that estimates model confidence directly from the logical structure of a single chain-of-thought reasoning trace. Our method uses either a lightweight instruction-tuned model or a simple deterministic rule to segment the reasoning chain into propositional units, then applies a NLI model to infer relational edges and construct two complementary argument graphs over these segments. The resulting edge scores are aggregated into a Dirichlet posterior over answer options, whose concentration yields calibrated uncertainty estimates reflecting both local step-to-step coherence and global logical consistency across the reasoning trace. Evaluated on GPQA, MMLU-Pro and TruthfulQA, our method consistently surpasses token-based and consistency-based uncertainty baselines across multiple reasoning models. We further demonstrate through extensive combination analyses that argument graph uncertainty captures an orthogonal signal to existing approaches, making it a complementary component in uncertainty ensembles. Crucially, our framework requires no additional calls to the evaluated model and relies entirely on small, efficient auxiliary models, producing fully interpretable, per-node uncertainty attributions at low computational cost.

AI.title_translation: 论证图不确定性：从推理链的逻辑结构量化不确定性
AI.tldr: 提出论证图不确定性框架，从单一思维链推理轨迹的逻辑结构直接估计大语言模型置信度，效果优于现有方法且计算成本低。
AI.motivation: 现有大语言模型的不确定性估计方法依赖昂贵的采样策略或浅层token级信号，忽略模型输出的内部逻辑结构，导致在高风险推理任务中部署不可靠。
AI.method: 引入“论证图不确定性”框架，这是一个针对多项选择题任务的后验框架。该方法使用轻量级指令微调模型或简单的确定性规则将推理链分段为命题单元，然后应用NLI模型推断关系边并构建两个互补的论证图。聚合由此产生的边分数得到答案选项的Dirichlet后验，其集中度提供校准的不确定性估计，反映局部逐步连贯性和全局逻辑一致性。
AI.result: 在GPQA、MMLU-Pro和TruthfulQA上评估，该方法一致优于基于token和基于一致性的不确定性基线。它捕捉到与现有方法正交的信号，可作为不确定性集成中的互补组件。该框架无需额外调用被评估模型，仅依赖小型高效的辅助模型，计算成本低，并提供完全可解释的逐节点不确定性归因。
AI.conclusion: 论证图不确定性框架通过利用推理链的逻辑结构，提供了一种有效、高效且可解释的大语言模型不确定性估计方法，优于现有基线，并能作为互补信号提升不确定性估计的整体性能。
AI.translation: 可靠的不确定性估计对于在高风险推理任务中部署大型语言模型至关重要，然而大多数现有方法依赖于昂贵的采样策略或忽略模型输出内部逻辑结构的浅层token级信号。我们引入了论证图不确定性，这是一个用于多项选择题任务的后验框架，它直接从单一思维链推理轨迹的逻辑结构估计模型置信度。我们的方法使用轻量级指令微调模型或简单的确定性规则将推理链分段为命题单元，然后应用NLI模型推断关系边并构建两个互补的论证图。由此产生的边分数被聚合成答案选项的Dirichlet后验，其集中度产生校准的不确定性估计，反映推理轨迹中局部逐步连贯性和全局逻辑一致性。在GPQA、MMLU-Pro和TruthfulQA上评估，我们的方法始终超越基于token和基于一致性的不确定性基线，在多个推理模型上表现出色。我们通过广泛的组合分析进一步证明，论证图不确定性捕捉到与现有方法正交的信号，使其成为不确定性集成中的一个互补组件。至关重要的是，我们的框架无需额外调用被评估模型，完全依赖于小型、高效的辅助模型，以低计算成本产生完全可解释的逐节点不确定性归因。
AI.summary: 本文提出“论证图不确定性”框架，旨在从单一思维链推理轨迹的逻辑结构中直接估计大型语言模型的置信度。该方法通过将推理链分割成命题单元，并构建论证图来捕捉推理的局部连贯性和全局逻辑一致性。实验结果表明，该方法在GPQA、MMLU-Pro和TruthfulQA等基准测试中优于现有的基于token和一致性的不确定性估计方法，且计算成本低、可解释性强，可作为现有不确定性估计方法的有效补充。
AI.keywords: 论证图不确定性, 大语言模型, 不确定性估计, 逻辑结构, 思维链
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于其从推理链的逻辑结构而非表面信号来量化不确定性，提供了一种新颖且高效的方法。它解决了现有方法计算成本高昂和忽略逻辑结构的问题，并提供了可解释的逐节点归因。这对于大语言模型在高风险场景下的可靠部署具有重要意义。其作为正交信号的特性也使其在不确定性集成中具有巨大潜力。

title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
summary: Diffusion and flow matching are now dominant frameworks for generative modeling in continuous domains, but they typically require multiple network evaluations at inference. This has motivated extensive research on one-step generative modeling primarily built on diffusion and flow, though existing approaches often rely on complex training machinery. In this work, we introduce Priming Models, a simple two-stage framework for training one-step generators. Motivated by the difficulty of distributional training from scratch, Priming Models are first trained on a reconstruction objective, e.g., pixel-space denoising at a fixed noise level, before undergoing feature-space distributional post-training. Our central scientific finding is that this simple reconstruction stage is already enough to entirely alleviate the difficulty of distributional training. Empirically, across class-conditional image generation, text-to-image generation, and world modeling, Priming Models significantly advance the Pareto frontier of training compute vs. generation quality. On ImageNet at $256 \times 256$ resolution, we achieve a state-of-the-art FID of $1.19$ among one-step generators using approximately one-tenth the training compute of prior methods with comparable FID. We open-source our codebase at https://github.com/JaeyeonKim01/priming.

AI.title_translation: 我们是否在过度思考单步生成？
AI.tldr: 通过引入一个简单的重构预训练阶段，Priming Models 大幅降低了单步生成模型的训练难度，并以十分之一的计算成本实现了最先进的图像生成效果。
AI.motivation: 现有的单步生成模型（基于扩散和流匹配）通常依赖于复杂的训练机制，且从头开始进行分布训练非常困难。
AI.method: 提出 Priming Models，一个两阶段框架：首先在固定的噪声水平下进行重构目标训练（如像素空间去噪），然后进行特征空间的分布后训练。
AI.result: 在类条件图像生成、文本到图像生成和世界模型任务中，显著推进了训练计算量与生成质量的 Pareto 前沿；在 ImageNet 256x256 分辨率上取得了 1.19 的 SOTA FID，且训练计算量仅为同等质量先前方法的十分之一。
AI.conclusion: Priming Models 显著降低了单步生成模型的训练难度，并以极低的计算成本实现了最先进的生成质量，证明了简单重构预训练在生成建模中的巨大潜力。
AI.translation: 扩散和流匹配现在是连续域中生成建模的主导框架，但它们在推理时通常需要多次网络评估。这激发了主要基于扩散和流的单步生成建模的广泛研究，尽管现有方法通常依赖于复杂的训练机制。在这项工作中，我们介绍了“Priming Models”，这是一个用于训练单步生成模型的简单两阶段框架。受限于从头进行分布训练的困难，Priming Models 首先在重构目标（例如，在固定噪声水平下的像素空间去噪）上进行训练，然后再进行特征空间的分布后训练。我们的核心科学发现是，这个简单的重构阶段已经足以完全缓解分布训练的困难。在经验上，在类条件图像生成、文本到图像生成和世界模型中，Priming Models 显著推进了训练计算量与生成质量的 Pareto 前沿。在 $256 \times 256$ 分辨率的 ImageNet 上，我们在具有可比 FID 的单步生成器中实现了 $1.19$ 的最先进 FID，同时训练计算量仅为先前方法的约十分之一。我们在 https://github.com/JaeyeonKim01/priming 上开源了代码库。
AI.summary: 该论文介绍了“Priming Models”，一个用于训练单步生成模型的简单两阶段框架。通过先进行重构预训练再进行分布后训练，该方法大幅降低了单步生成模型的训练难度，并在多项生成任务中以远低于同类方法的计算成本实现了最先进的生成质量。
AI.keywords: 单步生成, 扩散模型, 流匹配, 图像生成, 预训练
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种简单而高效的两阶段单步生成模型训练框架——Priming Models，通过引入重构预训练阶段，彻底缓解了从头进行分布训练的难度，在图像生成和世界模型等任务中显著提升了训练计算效率与生成质量的Pareto前沿。其创新点在于用简单的预训练替代了复杂的单步生成训练机制。

title: VIGOR-MPC: Vision-Guided Objective Regulation MPC
summary: Controlling an agent in an environment solely perceived through onboard vision is challenging: perception yields noisy, variable-length, and partially occluded context, while onboard compute is shared between perception and control, limiting the planning horizon executable in real time. We propose VIGOR-MPC, a modular student-teacher framework, agnostic to the perception pipeline, which addresses reference tracking across navigation tasks by distilling a privileged, field-of-view-aware long-horizon MPC into a computationally lightweight short-horizon MPC whose cost parameters are determined online from vision. The teacher operates in simulation with full state knowledge and a multi-trajectory formulation that guarantees the agent can stay within its field of view. The student observes only the noisy, occluded context produced by a perception module and learns, via a multi-level recurrent mapping, to infer cost parameters that aim to recover the teacher's behavior despite missing information. We evaluate VIGOR-MPC on vision-based autonomous racing in simulation and on hardware. Using only onboard perception of the track, VIGOR-MPC generalizes to tracks unseen during training and approaches the lap times of the privileged long-horizon teacher while reducing per-step computation by over 90%.

AI.title_translation: VIGOR-MPC: 视觉引导目标调节模型预测控制
AI.tldr: VIGOR-MPC是一个模块化的学生-教师框架，通过将一个具有特权、视场感知的长时域MPC精炼成一个计算轻量级的短时域MPC，其成本参数由视觉在线确定，解决了纯视觉感知环境下代理的参考跟踪问题。它在模拟和硬件上的视觉自主赛车中表现出色，泛化能力强，接近教师性能，同时大幅减少计算量。
AI.motivation: 在仅通过车载视觉感知的环境中控制代理面临挑战：感知数据噪声大、长度可变、部分遮挡，同时车载计算资源在感知和控制之间共享，限制了实时规划时域。
AI.method: 提出VIGOR-MPC，一个模块化的学生-教师框架，与感知管道无关。教师在模拟中运行，具有完整的状态知识和多轨迹公式，确保代理保持在视场内。学生仅观察感知模块产生的噪声和遮挡上下文，并通过多级循环映射学习推断成本参数，以恢复教师行为。其核心是将一个具有特权、视场感知的长时域MPC精炼成一个计算轻量级的短时域MPC，成本参数由视觉在线确定。
AI.result: VIGOR-MPC在训练中未见的赛道上具有泛化能力，在模拟和硬件上进行的视觉自主赛车测试中，其单圈时间接近特权长时域教师，同时每步计算量减少了90%以上。
AI.conclusion: VIGOR-MPC通过结合视觉引导的成本参数在线调节，成功地在纯视觉感知环境下实现了高效、泛化能力强的代理控制，大幅降低了计算成本，同时保持了接近特权教师的性能。
AI.translation: 仅通过车载视觉感知的环境来控制代理具有挑战性：感知会产生噪声、可变长度和部分遮挡的上下文，而车载计算在感知和控制之间共享，限制了实时可执行的规划时域。我们提出了VIGOR-MPC，一个模块化的学生-教师框架，与感知管道无关，通过将一个具有特权、视场感知的长时域MPC精炼成一个计算轻量级的短时域MPC，其成本参数由视觉在线确定，解决了导航任务中的参考跟踪问题。教师在具有完整状态知识和多轨迹公式的模拟中运行，该公式保证代理可以保持在其视场内。学生仅观察由感知模块产生的噪声、遮挡上下文，并通过多级循环映射学习推断成本参数，旨在尽管信息缺失也能恢复教师的行为。我们在模拟和硬件上的视觉自主赛车中评估了VIGOR-MPC。仅使用车载赛道感知，VIGOR-MPC可以泛化到训练中未见的赛道，并接近特权长时域教师的单圈时间，同时将每步计算量减少了90%以上。
AI.summary: VIGOR-MPC是一个针对纯视觉感知环境下代理控制挑战提出的模块化学生-教师框架。它通过将一个在模拟中运行并具有完整状态知识的长时域MPC教师的行为，精炼到依赖在线视觉信息确定成本参数的轻量级短时域MPC学生中。该方法旨在克服视觉感知噪声、遮挡和计算限制。在自主赛车任务中，VIGOR-MPC展示了对未见赛道的泛化能力，并以超过90%的计算量减少实现了接近教师性能的单圈时间。
AI.keywords: MPC, 视觉引导, 学生-教师框架, 自主控制, 实时规划
AI.comments: VIGOR-MPC的创新之处在于其学生-教师框架设计，巧妙地结合了特权长时域规划与实时视觉引导的短时域控制。通过在线调节成本参数，它有效应对了纯视觉感知下的不确定性和计算限制，展示了在资源受限系统中的巨大潜力。其在泛化能力和计算效率上的显著提升，使其在机器人自主导航等领域具有重要应用价值。

title: TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees
summary: A ReAct-style agent accumulates observations, intermediate results, and failed attempts in a single context. As this context grows, stale and off-path information consumes its limited capacity and obscures relevant evidence, making focused reasoning increasingly difficult. We introduce TreeFlex, a framework in which the agent's own policy decides where to search. The agent records each intermediate state, with a short summary, as a node in a search tree maintained by the harness. The policy is a single language model that acts in two roles. In the Reflection role, it has a global view of the tree through these summaries and picks a node to resume, together with an instruction. In the Execution role, the harness restores the path that led to that node, and the model carries out the instruction with the usual task tools until it saves a new node or proposes a solution, which Reflection then approves or sends back to another node. Through these choices, the policy decides whether to deepen the current line, branch from or revisit an earlier state, verify a proposal, or stop, without a fixed traversal order or a score for each node.
