We train navigation, task actions, checkpointing, and proposal review jointly with a tree-aware adaptation of GRPO, using task-level outcome rewards augmented by process rewards. After small-scale RL of a 4B model, with the same active-context limit for all methods, TreeFlex reaches 48.8% accuracy on a challenging deep-research benchmark, versus 41.5% for flat ReAct and 42.8% for FoldAgent, and its Pass@8 is about ten points higher than either. On SWE-bench Verified, with all three systems trained with RL from the same 9B model, TreeFlex resolves 54.9% of tasks, versus 43.3% for FoldAgent and 45.2% for its step-wise variant.

AI.title_translation: TreeFlex：自主导航搜索树的智能体
AI.tldr: TreeFlex通过让AI智能体自主导航和管理自己的搜索树，解决了长文本上下文中的信息过载问题，大幅提升了复杂推理和任务求解的准确率。
AI.motivation: 传统的ReAct风格智能体将所有观察、中间结果和失败尝试累积在单一上下文中，随着上下文增长，陈旧和脱轨的信息会消耗有限的容量并掩盖相关证据，导致聚焦推理变得越来越困难。
AI.method: 引入TreeFlex框架，将智能体策略分为反射和执行两个角色。反射角色通过全局树摘要选择恢复节点和指令，执行角色恢复路径并使用工具执行任务。采用树感知的GRPO算法，结合任务级结果奖励和过程奖励进行联合训练。
AI.result: 在一个具有挑战性的深度研究基准测试中，4B模型的TreeFlex达到了48.8%的准确率（优于ReAct的41.5%和FoldAgent的42.8%），Pass@8高出约10个百分点；在SWE-bench Verified上，9B模型的TreeFlex解决了54.9%的任务（优于FoldAgent的43.3%）。
AI.conclusion: TreeFlex框架通过赋予大模型自主导航搜索树的能力，有效解决了长文本上下文中信息冗余和推理困难的问题，在深度研究和软件工程基准测试中均展现出显著的性能优势。
AI.translation: ReAct风格的智能体在单一上下文中累积观察结果、中间结果和失败的尝试。随着上下文的增长，陈旧和偏离路径的信息会消耗其有限的容量并掩盖相关证据，使聚焦推理变得越来越困难。我们介绍了TreeFlex，这是一个框架，其中智能体自身的策略决定了搜索的位置。智能体将每个中间状态及其简短摘要记录为由框架维护的搜索树中的一个节点。策略是一个扮演两个角色的单一语言模型。在反射（Reflection）角色中，它通过这些摘要对树有全局视图，并挑选一个节点来恢复，连同一条指令。在执行（Execution）角色中，框架恢复通向该节点的路径，模型使用常规任务工具执行指令，直到它保存一个新节点或提出一个解决方案，然后反射角色批准该方案或将其送回另一个节点。通过这些选择，策略决定是加深当前路线、从早期状态分支或重新访问、验证提案还是停止，而无需固定的遍历顺序或每个节点的评分。我们使用基于任务级结果奖励并由过程奖励增强的树感知GRPO自适应方法，联合训练导航、任务动作、检查点和提案审查。在对4B模型进行小规模强化学习后，在所有方法具有相同活动上下文限制的情况下，TreeFlex在一个具有挑战性的深度研究基准测试上达到了48.8%的准确率，而扁平的ReAct为41.5%，FoldAgent为42.8%，其Pass@8比两者高出大约十个百分点。在SWE-bench Verified上，通过使用相同9B模型的RL对所有三个系统进行训练，TreeFlex解决了54.9%的任务，而FoldAgent为43.3%，其逐步变体为45.2%。
AI.summary: TreeFlex是一个让大模型智能体自主导航其搜索树的框架，通过反射与执行的双角色协作以及树感知的强化学习训练，克服了传统单一上下文ReAct智能体在处理长时任务时的信息过载问题，显著提升了深度研究和软件工程任务的性能。
AI.keywords: TreeFlex, 智能体, 搜索树, 强化学习, 语言模型
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的智能体搜索树导航框架TreeFlex，打破了传统ReAct智能体在单一生长上下文中容易被冗余信息淹没的瓶颈。其最大亮点在于让大模型通过角色分工（反射与执行）自主决定搜索路径，无需固定的遍历顺序或节点评分，并通过树感知的GRPO联合训练实现了显著的性能提升。

title: Read, Parse, Describe: Unified Document Parsing with Visual Element Description Generation
summary: Document understanding systems are typically evaluated as separate components via layout analysis, optical text recognition, reading-order prediction, and image captioning. This separation leaves scientific figures, captions, and visual semantics weakly connected, and fails to measure whether a model can produce a single page-level parse that is both structurally faithful and semantically accessible. We introduce Read-Parse-Describe, a unified dataset for document parsing with visual element description generation. Given a page image, models are required to output an ordered list of layout elements containing bounding boxes, semantic labels, reading-order indices, recognized textual content, and alternative text descriptions for visual elements. The benchmark is built from 2,402 documents, comprising 18,163 continuous pages, 125,218 layout elements, and 11,338 visual instances. Besides, we further propose a plug-and-play space-awareness enhancer that reuses multi-layer visual features and injects grid-aware spatial guidance into vision-language tokens for layout-aware generation. Experiments across end-to-end VLMs and pipeline parsers show that existing systems still struggle to jointly recover reading order and visual semantics, while our enhanced model achieves strong joint performance. These results highlight the need to move beyond isolated document parsing modules toward unified models that jointly read, parse, and describe complex documents. The new dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yufanchen96/RPD

AI.title_translation: 读、解析、描述：统一文档解析与视觉元素描述生成
AI.tldr: 现有文档理解系统在结构和语义连接上不足。本文提出了一个统一的数据集（Read-Parse-Describe）和增强器，用于文档解析和视觉元素描述生成，实验表明现有系统难以处理，而我们的模型表现良好，强调了统一模型的重要性。
AI.motivation: 现有文档理解系统将布局分析、文本识别、阅读顺序预测和图像字幕等组件独立评估，导致科学图表、标题和视觉语义之间的连接薄弱，并且无法衡量模型能否生成既结构忠实又语义可访问的页面级解析。
AI.method: 本文提出了一个名为Read-Parse-Describe的统一数据集，用于文档解析和视觉元素描述生成。该数据集要求模型输出包含边界框、语义标签、阅读顺序索引、识别文本内容和视觉元素替代文本描述的有序布局元素列表。数据集包含2,402份文档、18,163个连续页面、125,218个布局元素和11,338个视觉实例。此外，还提出了一个即插即用的空间感知增强器，该增强器重用多层视觉特征，并将网格感知空间指导注入到视觉-语言token中，以实现布局感知生成。
AI.result: 跨端到端VLMs和管道解析器的实验表明，现有系统仍然难以联合恢复阅读顺序和视觉语义，而本文提出的增强模型实现了强大的联合性能。
AI.conclusion: 现有文档理解系统需要从孤立的文档解析模块转向能够联合读取、解析和描述复杂文档的统一模型。
AI.translation: 文档理解系统通常通过布局分析、光学文本识别、阅读顺序预测和图像字幕等独立组件进行评估。这种分离导致科学图表、标题和视觉语义之间的连接薄弱，并且无法衡量模型能否生成既结构忠实又语义可访问的页面级解析。我们引入了Read-Parse-Describe，一个用于文档解析和视觉元素描述生成的统一数据集。给定一个页面图像，模型需要输出一个有序的布局元素列表，其中包含边界框、语义标签、阅读顺序索引、识别的文本内容以及视觉元素的替代文本描述。该基准数据集由2,402份文档构建，包含18,163个连续页面、125,218个布局元素和11,338个视觉实例。此外，我们进一步提出了一个即插即用的空间感知增强器，该增强器重用多层视觉特征，并将网格感知空间指导注入到视觉-语言token中，以实现布局感知生成。对端到端VLMs和管道解析器的实验表明，现有系统仍然难以联合恢复阅读顺序和视觉语义，而我们增强的模型实现了强大的联合性能。这些结果强调了需要从孤立的文档解析模块转向能够联合读取、解析和描述复杂文档的统一模型。新的数据集和代码将在https://github.com/yufanchen96/RPD公开。
AI.summary: 本文针对现有文档理解系统在结构和语义连接上的不足，提出了一个名为Read-Parse-Describe的统一数据集和基准，旨在促进文档解析与视觉元素描述的联合生成。此外，还提出了一个空间感知增强器，通过注入空间指导来提升布局感知生成能力。实验结果表明，该增强模型在联合恢复阅读顺序和视觉语义方面表现出色，并强调了开发统一文档理解模型的重要性。
AI.keywords: 文档解析, 视觉元素描述, 统一数据集, 空间感知增强, 文档理解
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过引入一个统一的数据集和基准，以及一个创新的空间感知增强器，有效解决了当前文档理解系统在处理视觉元素和语义连接方面的不足。其创新点在于将文档解析、文本识别、阅读顺序和视觉描述整合到一个统一的框架中，并强调了端到端统一模型的必要性。这对于提升文档理解的全面性和实用性具有重要意义。

title: AutoRSR: Automated Real-to-Sim-to-Real Data Generation for Scalable Robot Learning
summary: Scaling embodied robot learning requires large and diverse manipulation datasets, but collecting real-world demonstrations remains expensive in human effort and robot time. Simulation provides a scalable alternative, yet converting a real workspace into a robot-learning-ready environment still requires substantial manual effort for object extraction, asset processing, coordinate calibration, and trajectory specification. We present AutoRSR, a highly automated real-to-sim-to real framework that converts scanned real-world workspaces into reusable embodied simulation assets and scalable manipulation data. Given multi-view observations, robot states, and open-vocabulary semantic queries, AutoRSR reconstructs the workspace, extracts individual object assets, and automatically registers the reconstructed scene to the robot base frame at metric scale. Starting from a small number of reference motions, AutoRSR then generates executable manipulation trajectories and scales them through trajectory interpolation and domain randomization. After workspace scanning and semantic queries, the remaining pipeline requires no manual object annotation, scene-to-robot calibration, or robot teleoperation. Across three real-world manipulation tasks, policies trained on 1K automatically generated episodes per task achieve 73.3--86.7% real-world success rates, comparable to pi 0.5 trained from 150 human teleoperated demonstrations, while reducing the human time required for data generation by an order of magnitude. These results demonstrate that real-world observations can be converted into metrically aligned, executable, and scalable simulation data with substantially reduced human effort.

AI.title_translation: AutoRSR: 自动化真实到模拟到真实的数据生成，用于可扩展的机器人学习
AI.tldr: AutoRSR框架通过自动化将真实世界工作空间转换为模拟资产和操作数据，显著减少了机器人学习所需的数据生成人工投入，并取得了与人工示教相当的真实世界成功率。
AI.motivation: 扩展具身机器人学习需要大量多样化的操作数据集，但收集真实世界演示在人力和机器人时间方面仍然昂贵。尽管模拟提供了可扩展的替代方案，但将真实工作空间转换为机器人学习就绪环境仍然需要大量手动工作。
AI.method: AutoRSR是一个高度自动化的真实到模拟到真实框架。它通过多视图观测、机器人状态和开放词汇语义查询，重建工作空间，提取独立物体资产，并自动将重建场景以度量尺度注册到机器人基座。随后，从少量参考动作开始，通过轨迹插值和域随机化生成并扩展可执行的操作轨迹。在工作空间扫描和语义查询之后，整个流程无需手动物体标注、场景到机器人校准或机器人遥操作。
AI.result: 在三个真实世界操作任务中，使用每个任务1K自动生成情节训练的策略达到了73.3%-86.7%的真实世界成功率，这与从150次人工遥操作演示训练的策略相当，同时将数据生成所需的人工时间减少了一个数量级。
AI.conclusion: 真实世界观测可以以度量对齐、可执行和可扩展的模拟数据形式进行转换，且大大减少了人工投入。
AI.translation: 扩展具身机器人学习需要大量多样化的操作数据集，但收集真实世界演示在人力和机器人时间方面仍然昂贵。模拟提供了一种可扩展的替代方案，但将真实工作空间转换为机器人学习就绪环境仍然需要大量手动工作，包括物体提取、资产处理、坐标校准和轨迹规范。我们提出了AutoRSR，一个高度自动化的真实到模拟到真实（real-to-sim-to-real）框架，它将扫描的真实世界工作空间转换为可重用的具身模拟资产和可扩展的操作数据。给定多视图观测、机器人状态和开放词汇语义查询，AutoRSR重建工作空间，提取单个物体资产，并以度量尺度自动将重建场景注册到机器人基座。从少量参考动作开始，AutoRSR然后生成可执行的操作轨迹，并通过轨迹插值和域随机化对其进行扩展。在工作空间扫描和语义查询之后，剩余的流程不需要手动物体标注、场景到机器人校准或机器人遥操作。在三个真实世界操作任务中，每个任务使用1K自动生成的情节训练的策略达到了73.3%-86.7%的真实世界成功率，与从150次人工遥操作演示训练的策略相当，同时将数据生成所需的人工时间减少了一个数量级。这些结果表明，真实世界观测可以以度量对齐、可执行和可扩展的模拟数据形式进行转换，且大大减少了人工投入。
AI.summary: AutoRSR是一个自动化框架，旨在解决具身机器人学习中数据收集成本高昂的问题。它能将真实世界工作空间自动转换为可重用的模拟资产和可扩展的操作数据。通过多视图观测和语义查询，AutoRSR重建场景、提取物体并进行自动校准。它从少量参考动作生成并扩展操作轨迹，显著减少了数据生成所需的人工投入，并在真实世界任务中取得了与人工示教相当的成功率。
AI.keywords: 机器人学习, 数据生成, 真实到模拟到真实, 自动化, 操作轨迹
AI.comments: AutoRSR的创新之处在于其高度自动化的真实到模拟到真实数据生成流程，极大地降低了机器人学习数据采集的人工成本。通过整合场景重建、物体提取、自动校准和轨迹生成，它有效弥补了真实数据稀缺与模拟数据生成复杂之间的鸿沟，对于推动可扩展的具身机器人学习具有重要意义。

title: Training Dynamics of Transformers on Unbounded Inputs: Attention Learning Can Lag Output Layer Learning
summary: The success of transformers is attributed to several factors, including their capacity to express formal languages over variable-length inputs, and ability of the attention mechanism to focus on relevant input features. However, there is limited understanding of the training dynamics of shallow transformers, specifically how to decouple the learning of the attention and the output (feedforward) layer. A natural extension of the theory of one-step gradient feature learning in feedforward networks suggests that one could first learn the attention weights with a single gradient step, and then train the output layer. We show that this fails for a shallow transformer trained to recognize a star-free language from unbounded-length input. We prove that the transformer can be trained to recognize the language with a three-phase gradient descent: the output layer is updated first, followed by an attention update, and the output layer is fine-tuned in the third phase. In contrast, the language cannot be learned by training only the attention or output layer, or by a single attention-layer update followed by finetuning the output layer. We empirically show that ``attention learning lagging output layer learning" is beneficial in other language recognition, regression, and in-context learning tasks as well.

AI.title_translation: 无界输入下Transformer的训练动态：注意力学习可能滞后于输出层学习
AI.tldr: 该论文发现浅层Transformer在处理无界输入时，其注意力机制的学习会滞后于输出层的学习，需要通过三阶段的训练过程才能成功学习语言。
AI.motivation: 目前对浅层Transformer训练动态（特别是如何解耦注意力和输出层的学习）的理解有限，传统前馈网络的单步特征学习理论在此失效，因此需要研究Transformer在无界输入下的真实训练过程。
AI.method: 通过理论证明和实验验证，分析浅层Transformer在无界输入下的梯度下降训练动态，研究输出层和注意力层的交互过程。
AI.result: 证明了Transformer需要三阶段梯度 descent（输出层更新-注意力更新-输出层微调）才能识别无界输入语言，且“注意力学习滞后于输出层”的现象在语言识别、回归和上下文学习任务中普遍具有益处。
AI.conclusion: Transformer在识别无界输入语言时表现出独特的三阶段训练动态，其中输出层的先期学习和注意力学习的滞后对于成功训练至关重要。
AI.translation: Transformer的成功归因于几个因素，包括它们在可变长度输入上表达形式语言的能力，以及注意力机制关注相关输入特征的能力。然而，人们对浅层Transformer的训练动态了解有限，具体表现为如何解耦注意力层和输出（前馈）层的学习。前馈网络中单步梯度特征学习理论的自然延伸表明，人们可以首先通过单步梯度学习注意力权重，然后训练输出层。我们证明，这对于训练用来识别来自无界长度输入的无星语言的浅层Transformer是失败的。我们证明了Transformer可以通过三阶段梯度下降来训练以识别该语言：首先更新输出层，接着更新注意力层，并在第三阶段微调输出层。相比之下，仅训练注意力层或输出层，或者通过单步注意力层更新后微调输出层，都无法学习该语言。我们通过实验表明，“注意力学习滞后于输出层学习”在其他语言识别、回归和上下文学习任务中也是有益的。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了浅层Transformer在无界输入上的训练动态，证明了其识别无界长度语言需要三阶段梯度下降，即输出层先学习，随后是注意力更新，最后输出层微调。这种“注意力学习滞后于输出层学习”的现象在多种任务中都被证明是有益的。
AI.keywords: Transformers, 训练动态, 注意力机制, 形式语言, 梯度下降
AI.comments: 该论文揭示了Transformer在处理无界输入时独特的训练动态，特别是“注意力学习滞后于输出层学习”这一现象，打破了传统前馈网络单步特征学习的直觉，为理解Transformer的优化过程提供了重要的理论和实证基础。

title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
summary: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/

AI.title_translation: InfiniSplat v2：从任意视角分析和改进前馈3DGS
AI.tldr: InfiniSplat v2通过架构和训练改进，解决了前馈高斯重建中大视点变化下高质量渲染的挑战，实现了在多个数据集上最先进的渲染质量。
AI.motivation: 前馈高斯重建在从预测几何中学习高斯属性以实现大视点变化下的高质量渲染方面仍面临挑战。
AI.method: InfiniSplat v2分析了高斯属性学习的局限性，通过架构和训练的改变来提高渲染质量。具体方法包括：解耦几何和属性预测（使用冻结的几何分支），在训练期间使用真值相机姿态对齐预测的高斯，并采用大角度目标视图监督。
AI.result: 在六个数据集上，同一训练模型的前馈输出在姿态条件和无姿态设置下，在评估方法中实现了最先进的平均LPIPS和DISTS。在姿态条件设置中，与最强的基线相比，平均LPIPS和DISTS分别降低了25.8%和32.9%。此外，发现仅通过图像重建监督学习到的不透明度能够抑制几何不一致点。
AI.conclusion: InfiniSplat v2通过改进高斯属性学习的架构和训练策略，显著提升了前馈3DGS在大视点变化下的渲染质量，并在多项指标上达到SOTA性能。
AI.translation: 前馈高斯重建直接从输入图像构建3D场景以进行新视图渲染，但从预测几何中学习高斯属性以实现大视点变化下的高质量渲染仍然具有挑战性。我们分析了高斯属性学习的局限性，并引入了InfiniSplat v2，它通过架构和训练的改变来提高渲染质量。我们的方法通过冻结的几何分支解耦了几何和属性预测，在训练期间使用真值相机姿态对齐预测的高斯，并采用大角度目标视图监督。在六个数据集上，同一训练模型的前馈输出在姿态条件和无姿态设置下，在评估方法中实现了最先进的平均LPIPS和DISTS。在姿态条件设置中，与最强的评估基线相比，平均LPIPS和DISTS分别降低了25.8%和32.9%。我们进一步发现，仅通过图像重建监督学习到的不透明度能够抑制几何不一致点。项目页面：https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/
AI.summary: 该论文介绍了InfiniSplat v2，旨在解决前馈高斯重建中，在大视点变化下从预测几何学习高斯属性以实现高质量渲染的挑战。通过分析高斯属性学习的局限性，InfiniSplat v2提出了架构和训练上的改进，包括解耦几何与属性预测、利用真值相机姿态对齐高斯以及采用大角度目标视图监督。实验结果表明，在六个数据集上，InfiniSplat v2在姿态条件和无姿态设置下均达到了最先进的渲染质量，显著优于现有基线。
AI.keywords: 前馈3DGS, 高斯重建, 新视图合成, InfiniSplat v2, 渲染质量
AI.comments: InfiniSplat v2的创新之处在于其对前馈3DGS中高斯属性学习局限性的深入分析，并提出了一系列有效的改进措施，如几何与属性解耦、真值姿态对齐和大角度监督。这些方法显著提升了在大视点变化下的渲染质量，对于推动实时3D场景重建和新视图合成领域的发展具有重要意义。

title: When Does Task-Aware Imputation Matter? An Analysis of Robustness Under Train-Test Mismatch
summary:
Missing data is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, often degrading predictive performance and complicating model deployment. Most existing approaches treat imputation as a preprocessing step independent of the downstream task, a separation that becomes problematic under train-test mismatches in missingness mechanisms or rates. We introduce a unified framework that treats missing entries as variables in a task-conditioned optimization problem. We instantiate this framework in two settings: an amortized approach for scenarios with missing data at both training and test time, and a latent optimization approach for settings where only training data is incomplete.
  The evaluation is conducted on 98 tabular datasets, and robustness under train-test mismatches is assessed on 36 datasets. Results reveal that reconstruction error constitutes a poor proxy for predictive utility (Spearman rho approximately 0.16 to 0.32), and that task-aware imputation becomes critical in scenarios where classical methods fail to recover complete-data performance, achieving win rates of up to 80% in challenging train-test mismatch scenarios.

AI.title_translation: 任务感知归因何时重要？训练-测试不匹配下鲁棒性分析
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种任务感知归因框架，解决了在训练-测试缺失数据不匹配下传统归因方法性能下降的问题，并在复杂场景中表现出显著的鲁棒性提升。
AI.motivation: 机器学习中缺失数据普遍存在，会降低预测性能并使模型部署复杂化。现有大多数归因方法将归因视为独立于下游任务的预处理步骤，这种分离在缺失机制或缺失率的训练-测试不匹配情况下会产生问题。
AI.method: 引入了一个统一框架，将缺失条目视为任务条件优化问题中的变量。该框架在两种设置下实例化：一种是针对训练和测试时均存在缺失数据的摊销方法，另一种是针对仅训练数据不完整的潜在优化方法。
AI.result: 在98个表格数据集上进行了评估，并在36个数据集上评估了训练-测试不匹配下的鲁棒性。结果表明，重建误差是预测效用的一个不佳替代指标（Spearman rho约为0.16到0.32），并且在经典方法无法恢复完整数据性能的场景中，任务感知归因变得至关重要，在具有挑战性的训练-测试不匹配场景中实现了高达80%的胜率。
AI.conclusion: 重建误差不能很好地代表预测效用，任务感知归因在训练-测试缺失数据不匹配的挑战性场景中对于恢复完整数据性能至关重要，并显著优于传统方法。
AI.translation:
缺失数据是机器学习中普遍存在的挑战，常常会降低预测性能并使模型部署复杂化。大多数现有方法将归因视为独立于下游任务的预处理步骤，这种分离在缺失机制或缺失率的训练-测试不匹配情况下会产生问题。我们引入了一个统一框架，将缺失条目视为任务条件优化问题中的变量。我们在两种设置下实例化了该框架：一种是针对训练和测试时均存在缺失数据的摊销方法，另一种是针对仅训练数据不完整的潜在优化方法。
评估在98个表格数据集上进行，并在36个数据集上评估了训练-测试不匹配下的鲁棒性。结果表明，重建误差是预测效用的一个不佳替代指标（Spearman rho约为0.16到0.32），并且在经典方法无法恢复完整数据性能的场景中，任务感知归因变得至关重要，在具有挑战性的训练-测试不匹配场景中实现了高达80%的胜率。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一个统一的任务感知归因框架，旨在解决机器学习中缺失数据在训练-测试不匹配情境下对预测性能的影响。该框架将缺失条目视为任务条件优化问题中的变量，并提供了两种实例化方法。实验结果表明，重建误差不能有效衡量预测效用，而任务感知归因在传统方法失效且存在训练-测试不匹配的挑战性场景中，能够显著提升模型性能，胜率高达80%。
AI.keywords: 缺失数据, 任务感知归因, 训练-测试不匹配, 鲁棒性, 预测性能
AI.comments: 这项工作创新性地解决了缺失数据归因在训练-测试不匹配下的鲁棒性问题，强调了任务感知归因的重要性。它挑战了将归因作为独立预处理步骤的传统观念，并为复杂现实场景下的数据缺失处理提供了更有效的解决方案。其局限性可能在于框架的计算复杂性或对特定任务的适应性。

title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
summary: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself. Existing benchmarks measure downstream task success under a fixed harness, leaving harness engineering itself unexplored. We propose Doc2Harness, a two-stage benchmark that evaluates long-horizon harness engineering directly. In Stage 1, a build model operating inside a fixed builder harness receives an interface-only contract skeleton and a development document that consolidates behavior across twelve frontier harnesses, and then constructs a complete candidate harness in an isolated container. In Stage 2, the frozen candidate harness runs in containers separate from the construction environment, one per test case, and is driven end to end by a scripted mock model. We score each test case using four observable channels, namely the requests sent to the model, the files on disk, the process exit code, and the command output; positive controls rule out vacuous passes. Across nineteen frontier models, each evaluated with three independent builds on 328 test cases, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest pass rate at 53.05%, while the weakest model reaches 27.44%, a gap of roughly twenty-six percentage points. Even the strongest model fails nearly half of the test cases, and failures cluster around how cross-cutting functionality is split across modules. To our knowledge, Doc2Harness provides the first deterministic benchmark for measuring long-horizon harness engineering.

AI.title_translation: Doc2Harness：对LLM在长周期编码智能体框架工程方面的基准测试
AI.tldr: Doc2Harness是一个两阶段基准测试，用于评估大型语言模型在长周期编码智能体框架工程方面的能力。结果显示，即使是表现最好的模型也未能通过近一半的测试用例，揭示了当前LLM在复杂框架构建中的局限性。
AI.motivation: 大型语言模型驱动的智能体越来越多地被部署到长周期任务中，其性能不仅取决于模型本身，也取决于围绕模型的框架。现有基准测试仅在固定框架下衡量下游任务的成功，而框架工程本身仍未被探索。
AI.method: 本文提出了Doc2Harness，一个直接评估长周期框架工程的两阶段基准测试。第一阶段，一个构建模型在固定构建器框架内接收接口骨架和开发文档，然后在一个隔离容器中构建一个完整的候选框架。第二阶段，冻结的候选框架在独立于构建环境的容器中运行，每个测试用例一个容器，并由脚本模拟模型端到端驱动。通过模型请求、磁盘文件、进程退出码和命令输出来评估每个测试用例。
AI.result: 在19个前沿模型上，每个模型经过三次独立构建并在328个测试用例上进行评估，GPT-6 Astra以53.05%的通过率达到最高，而最弱模型的通过率为27.44%，两者之间存在约26个百分点的差距。即使是最强的模型也未能通过近一半的测试用例，并且失败主要集中在跨领域功能如何跨模块拆分的问题上。
AI.conclusion: Doc2Harness首次提供了一个确定性的基准测试，用于衡量长周期框架工程能力。研究表明，当前LLM在复杂框架工程方面仍有显著提升空间，尤其是在处理跨模块功能拆分上。
AI.translation: 由大型语言模型驱动的智能体越来越多地被部署到长周期任务中，在这些任务中，它们使用工具并修改真实工作空间。它们的表现好坏，不仅取决于模型本身，也取决于围绕模型的框架。现有基准测试在固定框架下衡量下游任务的成功，而框架工程本身仍未被探索。我们提出了Doc2Harness，一个直接评估长周期框架工程的两阶段基准测试。在第一阶段，一个在固定构建器框架内运行的构建模型接收一个仅包含接口的契约骨架和一份整合了十二个前沿框架行为的开发文档，然后在一个隔离容器中构建一个完整的候选框架。在第二阶段，冻结的候选框架在独立于构建环境的容器中运行，每个测试用例一个，并由脚本模拟模型端到端驱动。我们使用四个可观察通道对每个测试用例进行评分，即发送给模型的请求、磁盘上的文件、进程退出码和命令输出；正向控制排除了空洞通过。在19个前沿模型中，每个模型在328个测试用例上进行三次独立构建评估，GPT-6 Astra以53.05%的通过率达到最高，而最弱模型达到27.44%，两者之间存在大约26个百分点的差距。即使是最强的模型也未能通过近一半的测试用例，并且失败集中在跨领域功能如何跨模块拆分的问题上。据我们所知，Doc2Harness提供了第一个用于衡量长周期框架工程的确定性基准测试。
AI.summary: 本文提出了Doc2Harness，一个用于评估大型语言模型（LLM）在长周期编码智能体框架工程方面能力的双阶段基准测试。该基准测试要求LLM基于开发文档构建完整的框架，并随后在独立环境中运行和评估其性能。实验结果显示，在19个前沿LLM中，即使是表现最好的GPT-6 Astra也仅有53.05%的通过率，且失败多集中于跨模块功能拆分问题。Doc2Harness是首个衡量长周期框架工程的确定性基准，揭示了LLM在此领域仍存在显著挑战和提升空间。
AI.keywords: LLM, 框架工程, 基准测试, 编码智能体, 长周期任务
AI.comments: Doc2Harness的创新之处在于它首次将框架工程本身作为LLM的评估目标，而不仅仅是固定框架下的下游任务表现。这对于理解和提升LLM在复杂、真实世界软件开发任务中的能力至关重要。其两阶段、隔离容器的设计保证了评估的确定性和公平性。然而，研究结果也突显了当前最先进的LLM在处理模块化和跨领域功能拆分方面的局限性，指明了未来研究的方向。

title: Non-asymptotic Convergence of Average-reward Q-learning with Options
summary: We study the finite-sample convergence of Q-learning algorithms for the average-reward formulation of Reinforcement Learning (RL) with options. While options allow temporarily extended and hierarchical actions, the average-reward formulation incorporates continual tasks beyond discounted and episodic RL. We establish the first $\tilde{O}(1/\text{iterations})$ convergence guarantees, in the mean-square sense, for average-reward option Q-learning algorithms in both the inter- and intra-option settings. First, we prove that both inter- and intra-option Bellman operators satisfy multi-step span contractions under unichain assumptions. Then, we propose synchronous estimators of these multi-step option Bellman operators leading to two variants of option Q-learning. Finally, we extend the stochastic approximation framework to prove convergence rates of these two algorithms under the minimal assumptions used in the literature.

AI.title_translation: 平均奖励Q学习与选项的非渐近收敛
AI.tldr: 该论文研究了平均奖励Q学习算法与选项的有限样本收敛性，首次建立了$	ilde{O}(1/\text{iterations})$的收敛性保证。
AI.motivation: 研究带有选项的平均奖励强化学习（RL）Q学习算法的有限样本收敛性。选项允许暂时扩展和分层动作，而平均奖励公式则将持续任务纳入考量，超越了折扣和分段RL。
AI.method: 首先，证明了在单一链假设下，选项间和选项内贝尔曼算子都满足多步跨度收缩。其次，提出了这些多步选项贝尔曼算子的同步估计器，从而产生了两种选项Q学习的变体。最后，扩展了随机逼近框架，以在文献中使用的最小假设下证明这两种算法的收敛速度。
AI.result: 首次在均方意义上，为选项间和选项内设置中的平均奖励选项Q学习算法建立了$	ilde{O}(1/\text{iterations})$的收敛性保证。
AI.conclusion: 在最小假设下，所提出的两种平均奖励选项Q学习算法变体实现了$	ilde{O}(1/\text{iterations})$的收敛速度。
AI.translation: 我们研究了带有选项的强化学习（RL）平均奖励公式的Q学习算法的有限样本收敛性。虽然选项允许暂时扩展和分层动作，但平均奖励公式将持续任务纳入考量，超越了折扣和分段RL。我们首次在均方意义上，为选项间和选项内设置中的平均奖励选项Q学习算法建立了$	ilde{O}(1/\text{iterations})$的收敛性保证。首先，我们证明了在单一链假设下，选项间和选项内贝尔曼算子都满足多步跨度收缩。然后，我们提出了这些多步选项贝尔曼算子的同步估计器，从而产生了两种选项Q学习的变体。最后，我们扩展了随机逼近框架，以在文献中使用的最小假设下证明这两种算法的收敛速度。
AI.summary: 本文研究了带有选项的平均奖励Q学习算法的有限样本收敛性，该算法适用于分层动作和持续任务。论文首次为选项间和选项内设置中的平均奖励选项Q学习算法提供了$	ilde{O}(1/\text{iterations})$的均方收敛性保证。研究方法包括证明贝尔曼算子的多步跨度收缩性，提出同步估计器以开发两种Q学习变体，并扩展随机逼近框架来证明其收敛速度。
AI.keywords: 平均奖励Q学习, 选项, 非渐近收敛, 强化学习, 随机逼近
AI.comments: 这项研究的创新之处在于首次为带有选项的平均奖励Q学习算法建立了非渐近收敛性保证，填补了该领域的空白。这对理解此类算法在持续任务中的实际性能具有重要意义。

title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection
summary: Asynchronous EEG event detection supports practical brain-computer interfaces by identifying event classes and temporal boundaries directly from continuous recordings without predefined event boundaries at inference time. The primary challenge lies in extracting event-related patterns embedded in ongoing background activity. To address this, we propose \textbf{NeuroDETR}, a discrete spatiotemporal multiscale framework that combines structured tokenization with event-aware feature refinement. Multiscale temporal codebooks capture brief responses and sustained dynamics, while Spatial-Pyramid VQ hierarchically encodes spatial structure across EEG channels. These complementary representations form a compact event memory for jointly classifying events and estimating their onsets and offsets. Before tokenization, we apply FOCAL, an event-aware sparse attention module that uses predicted event presence to guide temporal feature refinement and spatial aggregation, emphasizing likely event periods while preserving context across the recording. Experiments on eight EEG datasets that span diverse paradigms demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. These findings provide a basis for the development of BCI systems that recognize meaningful neural activity during continuous interaction and monitoring.

AI.title_translation: 神经DETR：多尺度离散时空标记用于异步脑电图事件检测
AI.tldr: NeuroDETR是一个新的框架，通过多尺度离散时空标记和事件感知特征细化来检测异步脑电图事件，在多个数据集上取得了最先进的性能。
AI.motivation: 异步脑电图事件检测对于实际的脑机接口至关重要，但从连续记录中提取嵌入在背景活动中的事件相关模式具有挑战性。
AI.method: NeuroDETR框架结合了结构化标记和事件感知的特征细化。它使用多尺度时间码本来捕捉短暂响应和持续动态，并使用空间金字塔VQ来分层编码EEG通道的空间结构。在标记化之前，FOCAL模块使用预测的事件存在来指导特征细化和空间聚合。
AI.result: 在八个EEG数据集上进行了实验，结果表明NeuroDETR具有最先进的性能。
AI.conclusion: NeuroDETR为开发能够识别连续交互和监控期间有意义的神经活动的BCI系统奠定了基础。
AI.translation: 异步脑电图事件检测通过直接从连续记录中识别事件类别和时间边界，支持实际的脑机接口，而无需在推理时预定义事件边界。主要挑战在于提取嵌入在持续背景活动中的事件相关模式。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了	extbf{NeuroDETR}，一个离散的时空多尺度框架，它结合了结构化标记和事件感知的特征细化。多尺度时间码本捕捉短暂的响应和持续的动力学，而空间金字塔VQ则分层地编码跨EEG通道的空间结构。这些互补的表示形成了一个紧凑的事件内存，用于联合分类事件和估计它们的开始和结束。在标记化之前，我们应用了FOCAL，一个事件感知的稀疏注意力模块，它使用预测的事件存在来指导时间特征细化和空间聚合，强调可能的事件周期，同时在整个记录中保留上下文。在跨越不同范式的八个EEG数据集上的实验证明了最先进的性能。这些发现为开发在连续交互和监控期间识别有意义的神经活动的BCI系统奠定了基础。
AI.summary: NeuroDETR是一个新颖的框架，通过多尺度离散时空标记和事件感知的特征细化来解决异步脑电图事件检测问题。它利用多尺度时间码本和空间金字塔VQ来捕捉不同时间尺度的动态和空间结构，并结合FOCAL模块以事件为导向来优化特征提取。该方法在多个EEG数据集上取得了最先进的性能，为开发更高级的BCI系统提供了基础。
AI.keywords: 脑电图事件检测, NeuroDETR, 时空标记, 多尺度分析, 脑机接口
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种名为NeuroDETR的新型框架，用于解决异步脑电图事件检测的挑战。该方法的创新之处在于其多尺度离散时空标记策略以及事件感知的特征细化机制（FOCAL模块）。通过结合时间码本和空间金字塔VQ，NeuroDETR能够有效地捕捉不同时间尺度和空间维度的信息，从而在各种EEG数据集上实现了最先进的性能。这为开发更精确、更实用的脑机接口系统开辟了道路。然而，该方法在处理极端稀疏或噪声较大的EEG信号时的鲁棒性仍有待进一步验证。

title: Lifted State Policy Optimization: Internalizing Self-Correction through Transition Geometry
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Originally titled "Self-Correction as Transition Geometry: Internalizing Reasoning via Lifted State Policy Optimization."
summary: Preference optimization ranks final answers and trajectory RL maximizes aggregate returns, yet neither credits the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. We introduce Lifted State Policy Optimization (LSPO), which establishes this finite, cost-adjusted transition as the primary unit of learning. Each textual answer is augmented with a learned continuous coordinate, forming a lifted state that an energy function evaluates and orders. A shaped reward drives energy descent net of edit and step costs, and an internalization loss absorbs selected low-energy answers into the direct generator. On Qwen3.5-27B, the resulting single-pass policy reaches 71.8% aggregate accuracy across mathematics, science, code, and logic benchmarks, matching test-time reflection at 71.9% with 28% lower latency and 25.8% fewer tokens. The pattern holds across dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, and matched controls confirm that transition credit and the lifted coordinate each contribute, as does answer internalization. Our code is available at https://github.com/Venomrko/lspo.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Originally titled "Self-Correction as Transition Geometry: Internalizing Reasoning via Lifted State Policy Optimization."

AI.title_translation: 提升状态策略优化：通过转换几何内化自我修正
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为提升状态策略优化（LSPO）的新方法，它将学习重点放在文本推理中将错误状态转变为更好状态的局部转变上，而不是仅仅优化最终结果。LSPO通过学习连续坐标来增强文本答案，并使用能量函数进行评估。实验表明，LSPO在多个基准测试中达到了与测试时反思相当的准确率，同时显著降低了延迟和使用的token数量。
AI.motivation: 现有的方法如偏好优化和轨迹强化学习主要关注最终结果或总体回报，而忽略了在推理过程中将错误状态改进为更好状态的局部转变的重要性。
AI.method: 提出提升状态策略优化（LSPO）方法，将学习单元定义为成本调整后的有限转换。具体做法是：为每个文本答案学习一个连续坐标，形成一个“提升状态”，并使用能量函数进行评估和排序。通过奖励函数引导能量下降，同时考虑编辑和步骤成本。此外，引入内化损失将低能量答案整合到直接生成器中。
AI.result: 在Qwen3.5-27B模型上，LSPO实现了71.8%的综合准确率，覆盖数学、科学、代码和逻辑基准。该方法在测试时反思准确率（71.9%）相当的情况下，延迟降低了28%，使用的token数量减少了25.8%。该方法在不同的模型架构（密集和混合专家模型）上均表现出一致性，并且实验确认了转换归因和提升坐标以及答案内化的有效性。
AI.conclusion: LSPO方法有效地将学习重点从最终结果转移到推理过程中的局部状态改进，通过内化自我修正实现了高效且准确的推理。
AI.translation: 偏好优化对最终答案进行排序，轨迹强化学习最大化总回报，但两者都没有将导致错误推理状态变为更好状态的局部变化归功于学习。我们引入了提升状态策略优化（LSPO），它将这种有限的、成本调整后的转换确立为学习的主要单元。每个文本答案都通过一个学习到的连续坐标进行增强，形成一个能量函数进行评估和排序的提升状态。一个整形奖励驱动能量下降，净成本为编辑和步骤成本，并且内化损失将选定的低能量答案吸收进直接生成器。在Qwen3.5-27B上，由此产生的单程策略在数学、科学、代码和逻辑基准上的综合准确率达到了71.8%，在71.9%的测试时反思下匹配了71.9%，同时延迟降低了28%，token数量减少了25.8%。这种模式在密集和混合专家骨干网络中普遍存在，并且匹配的对照组证实了转换归因和提升坐标的贡献，以及答案内化的贡献。我们的代码可在https://github.com/Venomrko/lspo获取。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种名为提升状态策略优化（LSPO）的新方法，用于改进文本推理。LSPO将学习的重点放在推理过程中将错误状态改进为更好状态的局部转变上，通过为每个文本答案学习一个连续坐标来形成“提升状态”，并利用能量函数进行评估和排序。该方法通过奖励和内化机制优化学习过程。在Qwen3.5-27B模型上的实验结果表明，LSPO在多个基准测试中达到了与现有先进方法相当的准确率，同时显著提高了效率，降低了延迟和计算资源消耗。
AI.keywords: 提升状态策略优化, 内部化, 转换几何, 强化学习, 推理
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的方法LSPO，将学习的重点从最终输出转移到推理过程中的局部状态改进，这是一种有前景的研究方向。通过“提升状态”和“能量函数”的概念，该方法为量化和优化推理步骤提供了一种有趣的方式。实验结果表明了该方法的有效性，尤其是在效率方面的提升值得关注。然而，对于“能量函数”的具体形式和“内化损失”的详细机制，摘要中未作深入说明，这可能是未来研究可以进一步探索的方向。

title: Human Demonstrations as Post-Training Data for Any Robot Body: Retargeting the Object, Not the Hand
comments: 16 pages, 17 figures, 7 tables, 2 algorithms; 56-page supplement as ancillary file. A subset of episodes with their per-robot outcomes: https://playground.dxtr.co
summary: Human demonstrations are today used largely for pretraining vision-language-action models, with little ability to use the same data for target-embodiment or task-oriented training, which scalable deployment of robots in industrial and general environments depends on. A human demonstration recorded on a simple and scalable device such as a mobile phone can serve as post-training data for a robot whose body differs in structure and capability from the human who recorded it. This is made possible not by retargeting the hand's motion but the object's. A capture yields a body-free record: the object's pose over time, its contact intervals, and a reconstructed 3D object with provenance. Any robot, given as a URDF and a short descriptor, is solved against that record and scored in simulation against the demonstrated object motion as ground truth: the human-to-simulation leg of human-to-simulation-to-robot transfer, measured per robot. Each (robot, episode) pair gets one outcome: pass, failure with a named mode, or refusal, with its reason, before any motion. The method runs as a working system over a growing collection; the set analysed here is a sample of it: 42 captures solved on 8 robots, 157 pairs, of which 31.2% pass, 52.2% fail, 14.0% are refused and 2.5% are unauditable (kinematic feasibility, +/-50 mm / +/-15 deg, in simulation). Refusals held up: every pair the checks refuse on stored evidence yet ran anyway failed (13 of 13; 5 on a body whose public model welds its hand). A description file could not be shown to screen a robot: its outcomes were barely more predictable than guessing. No policy has yet been trained on the record. The record decides what a robot may post-train on; whether the policy then works on the real robot is the simulation-to-robot question, answered downstream.
comment: 16 pages, 17 figures, 7 tables, 2 algorithms; 56-page supplement as ancillary file. A subset of episodes with their per-robot outcomes: https://playground.dxtr.co

AI.title_translation: 人类演示作为任何机器人身体的训练后数据：重定向物体而非手
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种新方法，允许将人类演示数据（记录了物体的运动轨迹）用于训练与演示者身体结构不同的机器人，而无需直接复制手的动作。通过关注物体的姿态、接触时间和三维重建，该方法能够将演示数据转化为机器人可在模拟环境中学习的指令，并评估不同机器人在执行任务时的成功率。
AI.motivation: 当前机器人训练主要依赖预训练，缺乏将人类演示数据用于特定机器人身体或任务导向训练的能力，这阻碍了机器人在工业和通用环境中的大规模部署。
AI.method: 该方法将人类演示记录为不包含演示者身体的“物体记录”，包括物体随时间的姿态、接触区间以及重建的三维模型。然后，将此记录与机器人本体（以URDF格式提供）进行匹配，并在模拟环境中评估机器人执行物体运动轨迹的能力。评估指标包括成功、失败（带原因）和拒绝。
AI.result: 在42个演示和8个机器人组成的样本中，共进行了157次模拟测试。结果显示，31.2%的任务成功，52.2%失败，14.0%被拒绝，2.5%无法审计。研究还发现，被拒绝的任务如果强行执行，最终都会失败。机器人本体的描述文件对于预测其表现几乎没有帮助。
AI.conclusion: 该方法能够有效地利用人类演示数据对不同机器人进行训练后数据处理，通过关注物体运动而非手部动作，实现了数据的重定向和泛化。然而，模拟环境中的表现与真实机器人上的表现之间的关系（模拟到机器人迁移）仍需进一步研究。
AI.translation: 人类演示如今主要用于视觉-语言-动作模型的预训练，但在目标具身或面向任务的训练方面能力有限，而这对于机器人在工业和通用环境中的可扩展部署至关重要。在简单的可扩展设备（如手机）上录制的人类演示可以作为机器人训练后数据，即使该机器人的身体结构和能力与演示者不同。这并非通过重定向手的运动，而是重定向物体的运动来实现的。一次捕获会产生一个不含身体的记录：物体随时间的姿态、接触区间以及重建的3D物体及其来源。任何机器人，只要提供其URDF模型和简短描述，都可以根据该记录进行求解，并在模拟中以演示的物体运动作为真实情况进行评分：这是人类到模拟到机器人的迁移过程中的人类到模拟部分，按机器人进行测量。每个（机器人，回合）对都有一个结果：通过、带有命名模式的失败或拒绝，并附带原因，在任何运动之前。该方法作为一个工作系统运行在一个不断增长的集合上；这里分析的集合是其中的一个样本：在8个机器人上求解了42个捕获，157个回合，其中31.2%通过，52.2%失败，14.0%被拒绝，2.5%无法审计（模拟中的运动学可行性，+/-50毫米 / +/-15度）。拒绝是可靠的：检查拒绝的所有回合在存储的证据上仍然进行了，但最终都失败了（13个中的13个；5个在一个其公共模型将其手焊接在一起的身体上）。无法显示一个描述文件来筛选一个机器人：其结果几乎无法预测，比随机猜测好不了多少。还没有策略在该记录上进行训练。该记录决定了机器人可以进行训练后训练的内容；策略随后是否能在真实机器人上工作是模拟到机器人的问题，在下游得到解答。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种新颖的人类演示数据利用方法，允许将记录物体运动的人类演示数据用于训练与演示者身体结构不同的机器人。该方法的核心在于“重定向物体而非手”，通过提取演示中的物体姿态、接触信息和三维模型，将其转化为机器人在模拟环境中学习的后训练数据。实验结果表明，该方法在不同机器人上的模拟测试中取得了可观的成功率，并能有效识别出无法执行的任务。
AI.keywords: 人类演示, 机器人训练, 物体运动重定向, 模拟测试, 后训练数据
AI.comments: 该方法在利用人类演示数据方面具有创新性，解决了传统方法在机器人身体差异方面的限制。将重点从手的动作转移到物体的运动，为机器人学习提供了更通用的视角。然而，模拟到真实机器人的迁移效果仍需进一步验证，并且对机器人描述文件的依赖性有待商榷。

title: ReferFlow: Beyond Final-Target Localization for Complex Referring Expressions
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models have made significant progress in referring expression comprehension (REC), yet most REC benchmarks still focus on final-target localization. Complex queries often involve intermediate visual references with different dependencies on prior grounding, but final-only evaluation leaves this process unexamined. To address this gap, we formulate trajectory-level REC, in which models receive an ordered sequence of grounding steps constructed from a single complex query and localize the target regions associated with each step. We instantiate this setting in ReferFlow-Bench, which characterizes structured region transitions through four trajectory types, namely Refinement, Shift, Reset, and Mixture. Experiments show that current models struggle to consistently ground intermediate visual references across successive steps. We further propose ReferFlow, which decouples interleaved text-latent trajectory generation from coordinate decoding. Specifically, Stateful Region Latent Reasoning represents each target region as an object-indexed state composed of continuous latents, with explicit visual and spatial supervision to preserve region information for subsequent grounding. Trajectory-Aware Parallel Decoding then recovers all coordinate blocks in parallel through four geometry-constrained refinement rounds, with each block conditioned on its corresponding trajectory prefix, thereby reducing within-box sequential dependencies and eliminating cross-box autoregression. We further apply Grounding-Aware GRPO to promote consistent grounding across steps and learn adaptive trajectory generation from complex REC queries. ReferFlow achieves leading performance on general REC benchmarks and ReferFlow-Bench.

title: Beyond Expert Rankings: Contrast Calibration for Mixed-Precision MoE Quantization
summary: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models activate only a few experts per token, yet all expert weights must be stored. Mixed-precision quantization reduces this storage cost by assigning higher bit-widths to sensitive experts and lower bit-widths to resilient ones, but expert rankings alone do not determine how strongly to weight their errors. To address this gap, we propose NatScale, a contrast-calibrated allocation framework for mixed-precision MoE quantization. It uses a model-specific power transformation to calibrate gradient-based expert weights to an information-theoretic contrast target while preserving rankings. We jointly evaluate each expert's gate, up and down configurations to estimate its output error. We then combine these errors and calibrated weights with an existing prior based on weight spectra, variance and precision decay to select configurations under a storage budget. Across three models, NatScale achieves the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and the highest top-token agreement in all nine settings against five allocation baselines. It also yields the lowest perplexity in seven settings. These findings highlight the importance of objective-aware precision allocation.

AI.title_translation: 超越专家排名：混合精度MoE量化的对比校准
AI.tldr: NatScale是一种用于混合精度MoE量化的对比校准框架，通过模型特定的幂变换将基于梯度的专家权重校准到信息论对比目标，同时保留排名，实现了比现有基线更好的量化效果。
AI.motivation: 现有的混合精度量化方法仅依赖专家排名来分配不同的比特宽度，但没有考虑如何根据专家误差的敏感度来分配权重，导致量化效果不佳。
AI.method: NatScale框架使用模型特定的幂变换来校准基于梯度的专家权重，以达到信息论对比目标，同时保留专家排名。它还联合评估每个专家的门控、上行和下行配置，以估算其输出误差。然后，将这些误差和校准后的权重与基于权重谱、方差和精度衰减的先验知识相结合，在存储预算内选择最优配置。
AI.result: 与五个分配基线相比，NatScale在三个模型的所有九种设置下，实现了最低的本地到量化KL散度和最高的前导词一致性，并在七种设置下实现了最低的困惑度。
AI.conclusion: 客观感知精度分配对于MoE模型的混合精度量化至关重要，NatScale框架通过对比校准有效解决了这一问题。
AI.translation: 混合专家（MoE）语言模型每个token只激活少数专家，但所有专家的权重都必须存储。混合精度量化通过为敏感专家分配更高的比特宽度，为有弹性的专家分配更低的比特宽度来降低存储成本，但专家排名本身并不能决定误差的权重。为了解决这个差距，我们提出了NatScale，一个用于混合精度MoE量化的对比校准分配框架。它使用模型特定的幂变换将基于梯度的专家权重校准到一个信息论的对比目标，同时保留排名。我们联合评估每个专家的门控、上行和下行配置，以估计其输出误差。然后，我们将这些误差和校准后的权重与基于权重谱、方差和精度衰减的现有先验相结合，在存储预算下选择配置。在三个模型上，NatScale在所有九种设置下，与五个分配基线相比，实现了最低的本地到量化KL散度和最高的前导词一致性。它还在七种设置下产生了最低的困惑度。这些发现突显了客观感知精度分配的重要性。
AI.summary: NatScale是一种新颖的混合精度MoE量化框架，通过引入对比校准来解决现有方法仅依赖专家排名的问题。该框架利用模型特定的幂变换将梯度信息与信息论目标对齐，并综合考虑多种因素来优化专家配置，从而在存储预算内实现更优的量化性能，具体表现在KL散度、前导词一致性和困惑度等指标上。
AI.keywords: 混合精度量化, Mixture-of-Experts, 对比校准, NatScale, 专家权重分配
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种创新的对比校准方法NatScale，用于解决混合精度MoE量化中的专家权重分配问题。与现有方法相比，NatScale在多个评估指标上表现出显著优势，证明了其有效性和实用性。然而，该方法在不同规模和类型的MoE模型上的泛化能力以及计算复杂度仍需进一步考察。

title: Understanding NVIDIA Grace-Blackwell Unified Memory Through Placement-Controlled Microbenchmarks
summary:
NVIDIA Grace--Blackwell systems make CPU--GPU memory increasingly unified at the programming level, but unified addressability does not make the memory system uniform. A CUDA managed allocation on GB200 may be served from GPU-local HBM, accessed through host/system memory, demand-migrated, prefetched, reused after GPU access, or evicted and reloaded under capacity pressure. The problem is that these states share a programming interface while exercising different hardware paths and runtime mechanisms, making a single ``Unified Memory bandwidth'' number misleading.
  This paper presents a placement-controlled microbenchmark study of CUDA Unified Memory on NVIDIA GB200, using GH200 as a Grace--Hopper baseline and GB10/DGX Spark as a validation platform. Our methodology separates local HBM access, host/system-memory access, explicit movement, managed first touch, prefetch, reuse, access-pattern sensitivity, oversubscription, and CPU--GPU handoff, then summarizes the observations with a measurement-calibrated model of compute, access, migration, eviction, synchronization, and handoff costs. On GB200, a 1~GB STREAM-style triad reaches 3963~GB/s from local HBM but 304~GB/s through host-mapped CPU/system memory; for a 256~MB streaming kernel, cold CPU-initialized managed memory reaches 14.1~GB/s, while managed prefetch and reuse reach 4606~GB/s and 4504~GB/s. Below the capacity boundary, prefetched and reused managed memory remain above 4.6~TB/s, but at 125\% of CUDA-visible memory they fall to 968~GB/s and 1214~GB/s, showing that Grace--Blackwell unified memory must be understood through placement, access history, locality, reuse, and capacity pressure.

title: Typechecking without Minimum Types: Finite Bases and Backward Checking for $F_{<:}^{\top}$
summary:
System $F_{<:}^{\top}$ has decidable subtyping but lacks minimum types. We prove that typechecking is decidable for arbitrary explicitly annotated terms with unrestricted subsumption. The difficulty is that type abstraction uses a variable's declared bound to type its body, while quantified subtyping forgets that bound. We construct finite covers that preserve all required subtype comparisons across this change of context. These covers yield a compositional finite typing basis and a decision procedure.
  We then derive a backward checker that propagates acceptable targets without constructing the complete typing basis. Rectangularity of typing families gives a uniform elimination domain while retaining every result type, even when the canonical type is not least. Finite inverse families transport targets through type substitution. The same inverse specification recovers bound forgetting and yields finite type-avoidance families. Both typechecking procedures are total Rocq functions proved equivalent to the original typing judgment. For a separate symbolic word-RAM realization, we prove a quartic worst-case work bound. We measure family representation sizes and comparison storage in independent OCaml prototypes on synthetic checking judgments.

title: Closed-Form Optimal Weight Splitting for Matrix-Vector Multiply on Noisy In-Memory Accelerators
summary: Analog in-memory computing performs the matrix-vector multiplications of neural networks directly inside the memory array, which saves time and energy. But each memory cell stores only a few levels and is noisy, so one cell cannot hold a weight precisely. The standard fix is to split each weight across several cells, like digits of a number. The base of this split decides the trade-off: a large base gives fine resolution but amplifies the noise, and a base near one averages the noise but wastes resolution. The best-known prior analysis considers only the noise, and so it always picks a base of one. We propose a principled method that also accounts for the limited number of levels per cell. It gives the optimal base in closed form, from a single measurement of the device noise. On a device-physics simulator, the optimal split is 3.3 dB more accurate than the common base-16 split, and it beats equal splitting in end-application accuracy.

title: Do AI Agents Gossip? Evaluative Talk in Human and AI-Agent Online Communities
summary: Gossip, defined as evaluative talk about absent third parties, is widely seen as a uniquely human social practice. This study examines whether comparable discourse emerges spontaneously in a community of autonomous AI agents. We compare Moltbook, a Reddit-style platform populated by AI agents, with PTT, a large human-operated bulletin board in Taiwan. To reduce differences attributable to communicative setting, we analyze two public, asynchronous forums using the same operational definition of gossip. Gossip occurs on Moltbook, but its prevalence is 2.6 to 6 times lower than on PTT, depending on the denominator used. On both platforms, gossip frequently targets locally prominent figures, tends to elicit agreement from the first respondent, and is rarely presented as unsupported rumor. The clearest difference concerns how subsequent responses develop. Among threads containing at least one codable reply, challenges occur in 65.1% of human threads but only 21.3% of agent threads. Moreover, following an early aligning response, consensus remains unchallenged in 83.6% of agent threads, compared with 44.7% of human threads. This thread-level contrast remains after controlling for thread depth and board composition and under recalibration against two human annotators. Estimates based on individual reply turns are less robust and are therefore reported as bounds. These findings suggest that AI-agent communities reproduce the informational dimension of gossip, while the extent to which gossip performs comparable relational functions remains unresolved.

title: Fractional is Better: Learnable Derivative Orders in Neural Operator Learning
comments: Accepted at ICML 2026. 37 pages, 11 figures, 13 tables. Code: https://github.com/FaresBMehouachi/delNO
summary: Neural operators learn mappings between function spaces, enabling fast surrogate solutions to partial differential equations. Despite remarkable architectural diversity, these methods often share a common input representation: raw coordinate-value pairs $(x, u(x))$. We ask whether inputs aligned with PDE differential structure can improve learning. Through Picard iteration on mild solutions, we show that derivatives of the input appear explicitly in the solution operator, suggesting that providing derivative features should reduce the network's implicit differentiation burden. We prove this intuition: providing derivative features improves approximation bounds from $O(W^{-(s-m)/d})$ to $O(W^{-s/d})$, where $W$ is parameter count, $s$ is input regularity, $m$ is the PDE order, and $d$ is spatial dimension. Our central finding, however, is a surprise: the optimal derivative order $β^*$ is strictly less than the PDE order $m$. This gap arises from a bias-variance tradeoff in spectral space that we characterize in closed form. Learning $β$ from data achieves automatic spectral regularization. We introduce $\partial$-NO (del-NO), for derivative-augmented neural operators, an architecture-agnostic augmentation that provides learnable fractional derivative features to any neural operator backbone. Across benchmark problems and architectures, $\partial$-NO consistently improves prediction accuracy, with learned orders that reflect a representation of known physics modulated by noise and finite-sample constraints.
comment: Accepted at ICML 2026. 37 pages, 11 figures, 13 tables. Code: https://github.com/FaresBMehouachi/delNO

title: Lexical Persistence Without Semantic Entrenchment in AI Agent Communities
summary: AI agent communities sustain lexical persistence, popular terms spread, recur, and achieve broad adoption, but whether they also develop the temporal semantic structure characteristic of human linguistic communities remains open. We compare MoltBook (AI agent community, 8 weeks), PTT (Chinese human BBS, 19 years), and Reddit (English human forum, in matched 8-week windows) using Compass-Aligned Distributional Embeddings (CADE), measuring semantic drift (B1), neighborhood stability (B2), and lag-1 autocorrelation of per-word drift trajectories. Across the platforms, lag-1 autocorrelation forms a memory-horizon continuum. AI agents' result clusters at the low end, while human platforms show longer-range temporal dependence. MoltBook exhibits approximately 2$\times$ the B1 drift and 20-30% lower B2 stability than both human platforms. As a partial control for community age, r/vibecoding (founded 2025-02-08) shows significant ACF in its first 8 weeks ($0.082$, $p<.001$) and over 15 weeks ($0.220$, $p<.001$); MoltBook's ACF remains non-significant ($p = 0.41$), consistent with the gap not reducing to developmental stage alone. We interpret this pattern as evidence that lexical diffusion alone does not guarantee diachronic semantic consolidation. The findings are consistent with a contrast between communities whose semantic trajectories accumulate long-range interaction constraints and communities whose outputs are repeatedly regenerated from largely fixed pretrained distributions.

title: Cascaded Retrieval with Cross-Modal Query Refinement for Efficient Visual Document Search
summary: Retrieving information from visually rich documents requires matching queries against pages that contain complex evidence in tables, figures, and layout-dependent structures. Current vision-language retrievers address this but incur query-time costs that grow with corpus size and are impractical to scale. We propose SCOUT, a cascaded two-track retrieval framework that separates retrieval performance from exhaustive search. The visual track first uses a lightweight parent retriever to filter the corpus to a compact candidate pool, then applies a stronger multi-vector reranker only to those candidates. In parallel, a semantic track retrieves over hierarchical page and document summaries generated offline to provide a signal complementary to visual matching. The outputs are fused through cross-modal query refinement, which uses semantic scores to adjust the visual query representation before final ranking. We evaluate SCOUT on 4 major benchmarks against 6 baselines and observe a significant query-time latency improvement up to 80.7x (28.8x on average) relative to the best baseline, while exceeding state-of-the-art retrieval performance by up to 7.8% NDCG across all benchmarks.

title: ReAl: Refine neural operators via aligning dynamical flow
summary: Neural partial differential equation (PDE) surrogates trained with mean squared error (MSE) can capture dominant dynamics but often lose high-frequency information and fine-scale structures. Generative models (e.g., Flow Matching) can capture the distribution of fine-scale details, yet stochastic errors may accumulate during autoregressive rollouts and compromise long-term stability. To address these limitations, we introduce Refine and Align(ReAl), a model-agnostic plug-in that augments pretrained PDE surrogates to improve the reconstruction of high-frequency structures associated with complex physical phenomena. In the refinement stage, a conditional flow-matching model learns the residual distribution around the deterministic base prediction, recovering missing fine-scale structures while retaining the dominant dynamics. In the alignment stage, to mitigate the generative discrepancies amplified in the autoregressive rollout, particularly in chaotic systems, we generate multiple trajectories from the same input and reinforce the refiner with trajectory-level rewards, thereby achieving long-horizon dynamical alignment. Experiments across diverse surrogate architectures and PDE tasks demonstrate that ReAl consistently improves high-frequency fidelity, forecasting accuracy, and long-horizon stability.

title: From Triage to Impact: A Multi-Hop Reasoning Benchmark for Explainable Persian Hate Speech
summary: Hate speech has become increasingly prevalent on social media, raising concerns about its detection, interpretation, and moderation. Persian, a relatively low-resource language, lacks sufficient annotated data and computational resources for fine-grained hate speech analysis. In this study, we introduce a fine-grained, multi-hop benchmark for explainable Persian hate speech analysis, covering content triage, target identification, hate tactic and moral foundation analysis, textual evidence extraction, harmful narrative inference, and severity assessment. By evaluating state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs), we find that performance generally declines as tasks require more fine-grained semantic and inferential reasoning. Proprietary models generally outperform open-weight models, while reasoning-oriented models show no consistent advantage. Incorporating intermediate reasoning steps substantially improves severity prediction compared with one-shot assessment. Our analysis further reveals that Incitement to Violence or Harm is most strongly associated with higher severity, while political-affiliation targets are particularly associated with subversion-based moral framing. Overall, this work provides insights into LLM-based hate speech analysis and supports more accountable moderation of Persian-language social media. The benchmark is publicly available at https://github.com/kalhorghazal/From-Triage-to-Impact.

title: Hypothesis Selection via Weighted Medians
summary: Given $n$ distributions (hypotheses) $\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_n\}$ and samples from an unknown target distribution $P$, proper hypothesis selection seeks a distribution whose total variation distance to $P$ is close to the best achievable within the known distributions. We give an algorithm that, using $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ target samples, running in $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ time, with probability at least $1-δ$, returns $H_{\hat i}$ satisfying $d_\mathrm{TV}(P,H_{\hat i})\leq 3\min_{i\in[n]}d_\mathrm{TV}(P,H_i)+\varepsilon.$ The algorithm achieves the optimal approximation factor and sample complexity. The running time improves the dependence on the failure probability from polynomial to logarithmic in the state-of-the-art bound $\tilde{O}(n\varepsilon^{-2}δ^{-1})$ of Aamand, Aliakbarpour, Chen, and Silwal (COLT 2026), thereby answering their Question~2.

title: Contagious Misinterpretations: Social Learning with Shared Interpretations
summary:
When people discuss which of several hypotheses is true, they share not only their beliefs but also their interpretation of each one, that is, the distribution of signals each hypothesis is expected to produce. This interpretation is an opinion about what each hypothesis means and what evidence it predicts, and it is revised only through conversation, not by confronting it with the observed data. Standard non-Bayesian social learning captures only belief-sharing and keeps the likelihoods private. We study what happens when agents share both beliefs and likelihoods under static networks. We show that interpretations converge geometrically to a common reading shaped by the most influential agents. Then, beliefs concentrate, almost surely and at an exponential rate, on the hypothesis that, under this consensus interpretation, best explains the signals privately observed by all agents taken together.
  As a result, sharing interpretations can lead a population to adopt, unanimously and confidently, a hypothesis it would have rejected if it had shared only beliefs. Whether this helps or hurts when a true hypothesis exists depends on how accurately agents initially read the data they observe. When every agent initially interprets the true hypothesis exactly as the data it would observe, sharing interpretations cannot strictly improve learning and can strictly harm it when agents observe different data distributions. When interpretations are logically coherent and some agents misread their own data, sharing can either rescue the population, leading it to learn the true hypothesis, if an accurate reading dominates the interpretation network, or corrupt it, leading it to a wrong hypothesis, if a misreading one does.

title: Look Before You Restore: Learning to Predict Before Acting for Agentic Image Restoration
summary: Agents for mixed-degradation image restoration typically learn what a tool does to an image only after running it: failed calls waste computation and harmful outputs go unnoticed until too late. We propose PreActIR, an agentic restoration framework that predicts tool consequences before execution. For each candidate tool, a tool-conditioned world model forecasts changes in residual degradation, image quality, and fidelity, together with the risk of harm and the uncertainty of the prediction. The agent executes the top-ranked candidate, and an independent verifier commits or rolls back its output before the agent replans from the observed state. PreActIR also audits whether performance is limited by the selector or by the candidate space, and studies targeted tool adaptation as a controlled way to expand that space. In a controlled evaluation that fixes the candidate pool, verifier, and budget and employs reference-annotated degradation states, PreActIR uses 42.5% fewer real tool calls and 63.4% fewer rejected calls than reactive, execute-then-evaluate trial and error, while improving Y-PSNR by 0.92 dB.

title: From Relevance to Validity: Zero-Shot Tool Selection via Functional and Contextual Validation
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly face tasks from unseen domains and execution contexts, making zero-shot tool selection essential for identifying tools that can satisfy task requirements. Existing dominant methods mainly rely on relevance ranking, but semantic matching alone cannot ensure that a tool is functionally compatible or remains applicable in a new context. We preliminarily identify a \emph{transfer-validity gap}, where semantically relevant tools may still fail to satisfy functional or contextual requirements after transfer. To address this gap, we propose \methodname{}, a progressive validation framework that complements semantic relevance with endpoint-grounded functional compatibility and task-conditioned contextual evidence. Across cross-domain and cross-dataset transfer, \methodname{} consistently improves capability ranking, with larger gains under functional or contextual ambiguity. Ablation results further confirm the complementary contributions of functional and contextual validation.

title: Exact Joint MAP Decoding for Unknown Load and Message Counts in Orthogonal Unsourced Random Access
summary: We study joint recovery of the load (the number of active users) and message-count vector in type-based unsourced random access with very short messages. Each user's $k$-bit message activates one of $M=2^k$ orthogonal resources; coherent collisions therefore produce a noisy, unnormalized histogram of the transmitted messages. For arbitrary load and message priors, we propose an exact joint maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) decoder. Known-load allocation is separable and convex; our contribution is to show that the solutions for all candidate loads are nested prefixes of one greedy chain. Scoring these prefixes with the Bayesian posterior terms jointly estimates the load and message-count vector in $O(M+K_{\max}\log M)$ time. We compare the proposed joint MAP decoder with marginal MAP, three scalar-count two-stage receivers, oracle-load MAP, a sum-only receiver, and a soft-pilot receiver. For $K\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{0{:}60\}$ at 2 dB, the proposed decoder cuts the no-activity false-alarm probability from $25.9\%$ to $3.5\%$ relative to the Bayesian-count two-stage receiver and, conditioned on $K\ge1$, reduces normalized count error by $21.4\%$. The advantage concentrates under idle or sparse uncertain activity, whereas support-count processing approaches joint MAP when the possible loads are well separated. We also prove that the sum-only statistic is insufficient and quantify prior and amplitude mismatch. The model targets synchronized, power-controlled, very-short payloads rather than general URA.

title: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents
summary: With the rapid development of vision-language models (VLMs), Web-GUI agents have achieved promising performance in interacting with real-world interfaces through screenshot-based grounding. However, high-resolution screenshots and multi-turn histories introduce excessive visual tokens, causing substantial inference overhead. Existing token pruning methods, mainly designed for natural images, often select tokens independently based on importance scores, which can fragment the local visual structures required for recognizing small GUI elements such as buttons, icons, and hyperlinks. In this work, we propose STP-GUI (Spatially-aware Token Pruning for GUI agents), a query-guided token pruning framework that preserves fine-grained instruction-conditioned token scoring while performing spatially coherent window-level selection under aggressive token reduction. A lightweight selector is optimized through policy learning while the VLM backbone remains frozen. Experiments on Online-Mind2Web show that \papername achieves a favorable efficiency-performance tradeoff under low token budgets. At 21% token retention, it preserves 77.7% of full-token performance while reducing inference latency by 31% and FLOPs by 57%. Results on Android in the Wild further suggest that the method transfers to mobile GUI environments.

title: FOLD: Position-Free Far Memory with Local Order for Long-Context Speculative Decoding
summary: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM generation through lightweight drafting and parallel verification. It is particularly promising for long inputs, where KV-cache access costs can be amortized over multiple accepted tokens. Yet most drafters are trained on short sequences and degrade on long inputs, while long-context training is costly. Existing training-free approaches restrict the context window, rescale positions, or augment recent context with retrieved distant entries. Drafters, however, read target hidden states that already encode contextual and positional information, and their lightweight architecture makes full-history attention affordable. We propose FOLD, a training-free method that preserves exact local positions and treats all distant entries as far memory at a shared position. To counter attention dilution as the memory grows, we sharpen attention within it to emphasize relevant entries while separately controlling its total weight relative to the local window. Across six target-drafter pairs and diverse benchmarks of up to 256K tokens, FOLD predominantly delivers the highest speedup, with the best case more than doubling the speedup over autoregressive decoding, from 2.08$\times$ to 4.22$\times$.

title: What Should a Software Team Spend on Agents? Simulation-Based Cost Optimization of Mixed AI-Human Teams
summary:
Context: AI agents are rapidly adopted in software development, but their token costs are rising and it is unclear how much a team should spend on agents, and on which tasks.
  Objective: We determine how teams should divide spending between human developers and AI agents to deliver the features a project demands at the lowest total cost.
  Method: We model mixed teams of human developers and AI agents with eight specialized roles as a discrete-time stochastic process covering bug injection and detection, technical debt, human supervision of agents, and release cycles with feature freezes. Using Monte Carlo simulation and evolutionary search, we determine cost-optimal teams for 432 scenarios varying developer capability, project velocity, debt dynamics, agent capability and price, and bug costs, and compare them with a human-only baseline.
  Results: Escaped bugs are the dominant cost driver, and 61% of the agent budget goes to finding bugs. Agent capability matters more than token price, since higher-quality outputs reduce downstream quality assurance costs. In teams with capable agents, human developers mostly fix bugs and leave the implementation of new features to the agents. Teams with high-capability agents are typically cheaper than human-only teams, but low-capability agents offer no consistent advantage. At realistic velocities, the optimal teams still spend more on developers than on agents.
  Conclusions: There is neither a universal token budget per developer nor a universal agentic team structure. As in traditional development, this depends on many factors and teams need to be carefully tailored to the project context to achieve the optimal cost-quality trade-off.

title: Bounded-Density Vertex Deletion Beyond Vertex Cover
summary:
We study \textsc{Bounded-Density Vertex Deletion} (BDVD), where one asks whether at most \(k\) vertices can be deleted so that every remaining subgraph has density at most a rational input threshold \(τ_ρ\).
  We address the twin-cover and distance-to-cluster cases left open by Raupach, Breitkopf, Herrmann, and Nichterlein (MFCS 2026). We prove fixed-parameter tractability parameterized solely by the twin-cover number, for unrestricted input density. For distance to cluster, we establish fixed-parameter tractability parameterized by \(\operatorname{dc}(G)+\lfloor2τ_ρ+1\rfloor\), and complement this with \(\mathsf{W[1]}\)-hardness parameterized by \(\operatorname{dc}(G)\) alone when the target density is part of the input, even for integral targets.
  Thus distance to cluster alone is fixed-parameter tractable throughout \(τ_ρ<1\), while it is insufficient for unrestricted input density.
  Finally, we settle the combined parameter treewidth plus solution size, an open problem posed by Bazgan, Nichterlein, and Vazquez Alferez (JCSS 2025). We prove that BDVD is \(\mathsf{W[1]}\)-hard parameterized by \(\operatorname{td}(G)+k\), and hence also by \(\operatorname{tw}(G)+k\), already for targets strictly between \(1\) and \(2\).

title: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort
comments: 40 pages, literature-selection and search record included
summary: When does a human correction become useful learning, and what establishes better segmentation at matched human effort? This critical narrative review follows feedback through its selection, learner update, and evaluation. It compares active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation using a common mathematical account of target information, predictive error, response predictability, and human work. An exact Bayesian update converts evaluation-label information into expected log-loss improvement; an excess-risk decomposition explains what an approximate learner can lose. Conditional information decompositions separate the roles of selected locations, labels, and displayed context. Empirical comparisons show why response protocols, update mechanisms, and effort denominators matter, distinguishing current-mask refinement from reusable learning and simulated interaction from human evidence. We identify what logs can reveal, what requires independent evaluation, and what remains model-dependent. The resulting research priorities are to test what selection reveals, whether using it improves assimilation, and whether the resulting interaction policy benefits segmentation at matched effort. These are distinct claims: predicting a teacher's responses need not identify human intentions or establish better learning. No new acquisition algorithm or empirical superiority is claimed.
comment: 40 pages, literature-selection and search record included

title: Where Should the Gaussians Go? Reusable Label-Aware Allocation for Budget-Constrained Gaussian Splatting of Cinematic CT
summary: Anatomical labels help 3D Gaussian splatting preserve vessels in cinematic renderings of CT, but the representation is still found by optimising each patient's scene, where densification decides where Gaussians go, while real-time displays cap their number. We address one part of this process: deciding where a fixed budget of B Gaussians should be placed. We propose a reusable, labelaware allocation front end that maps a patient's CT, labels and transfer function to a density over 2mm cells and draws exactly B positions from it without per-patient optimisation; the other Gaussian attributes are still fitted per patient. The front end is learned once from per-patient optimised scenes and implemented as a population-trained neural prior and an interpretable seven-parameter visibility-aware closed form (VACF). With identical attribute fitting on 20 held-out patients at 10K-100K Gaussians, both raise vessel-masked PSNR over uniform allocation by 4.5-7.1dB and over pruning a dense voxel-aligned model by 1.6-3.3dB. The neural prior does not differ significantly from per-patient optimised allocation at any budget, and VACF is within 0.6dB of it on vessels; on 19 external patients the neural prior again matches it on vessels and VACF is within 0.7dB. As an initialisation for position optimisation, VACF allocation beats per-patient densification on vessels at 10K Gaussians and, at 25K, reaches a higher vessel PSNR after 118s of optimisation than densification after 248s. Under altered rendering presets, VACF transfers to new colours and lighting but not to a label-free transfer function, whereas the neural prior shows the opposite pattern.

title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
summary: Context can improve large language model performance, but these gains may be lost after context removal. Inspired by biological systems consolidation, we formulate Memory Consolidation (MC) as internalizing these gains while preserving non-target capabilities, connecting context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering under a common objective. We introduce a five-task-family testbed measuring consolidation and retention under single, batch, and sequential updates. We propose Cortex, which generates prospective queries to anticipate uses of context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates. Across 4B--120B dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, including both text-only and multimodal models, Cortex lies on the empirical consolidation--retention Pareto frontier in most evaluated settings. After 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model, Cortex-Structural recovers 88.9% of the context-induced gain while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance.

title: HRTF Upsampling and Personalization via Neural Operators
summary: Head-related transfer function (HRTF) spatial upsampling from sparse measurements is a fundamental challenge in personalized binaural audio. We formulate HRTF upsampling as an operator learning problem and introduce SPARO, a neural operator that maps sparse measurements at a set of spatial directions to the HRTF field, a continuous representation that can be queried at arbitrary positions. SPARO projects the measurements onto a learned set of spherical latent modes, processes the latent modes with Transformer blocks, and decodes the resulting representations at query directions. On SONICOM, using the LAP24 measurement configuration, SPARO attains the best log-spectral distortion (LSD) and interaural level difference (ILD) error at every sparsity level from 3 to 100 measurements (18% lower LSD and 43% lower ILD error than the strongest baseline at 100 measurements) while remaining competitive in interaural time difference (ITD) error. It reconstructs a dense HRTF 15 to 373 times faster than the leading neural-field method RANF. We further validate the approach on HUTUBS, demonstrating its effectiveness across HRTF datasets.

title: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully
summary: Reinforcement learning makes language models better at solving tasks, but the same mechanism also rewards guessing. When success is the only way to earn reward, opting for a safe fallback is always worse than a long-shot attempt. When a wrong action can corrupt a database or ship broken code, that incentive can be costly. Therefore, we propose training models to fail gracefully: to preserve successful behavior whenever possible while learning to execute a safe fallback policy when acting would be unreliable. However, naively using policy gradients with intermediate reward for fallback behavior is brittle due to unfavorable optimization dynamics. We address this challenge with GracefulRL, which reshapes the optimization landscape to promote graceful failure. Importantly, this behavior emerges directly from outcome-level reward signals, without annotations specifying when to fall back or additional inference-time machinery such as a verifier. Across a range of tasks and scales, we train models that largely preserve their task-solving capability while selectively falling back when acting would be unreliable. More broadly, our results show that reinforcement learning can not only incentivize models to succeed, but also to reason about the limits of their capabilities and change course when they determine that success is out of reach.

title: Generalization of Strang-Fix remark for discrete maximum principles on tetrahedral meshes
summary: Most of qualitative properties of finite element (FE) approximations for various PDE models, in particular the validity of the discrete maximum principles (DMPs), are usually guaranteed by certain geometric properties (e.g. acuteness/nonobtuseness) of FE meshes used. In this work, we revisit the linear FE discretization of the Poisson equation and discuss, in the context of DMPs, the representation of the stiffness matrix entries in terms of the edge lengths and cotangents of the dihedral angles of the tetrahedral meshes, thus avoiding the common use of face areas and element volumes. Using this type of entry representation, certain structural properties of meshes, and simple trigonometric relations, as proposed in the two-dimensional case by Strang and Fix, we show that DMPs still hold (as the stiffness matrices remain $M$-matrices) for many tetrahedral configurations with obtuse dihedral angles. Such a relaxation of the standard acuteness/nonobtuseness conditions can be vital in practical calculations, as these angle properties are difficult to preserve in global and local mesh refinements. Several representative examples are presented.

title: Hyperspherical Contrastive Representations Unlock Planning and Exploration
summary: We develop a self-supervised reinforcement learning algorithm that learns to build towers of up to eight cubes from scratch, without prior data, rewards, demonstrations, or pretrained models. Our method, Contrastive Planning via Spherical Linear Interpolation (C-Slerp), uses contrastive representations as reusable building blocks and repeatedly composes them to infer a sequence of intermediate waypoints. Under our hyperspherical parameterization, the learned representations allow intermediate waypoints to be inferred in closed form through spherical linear interpolation, without training a separate high-level policy or performing graph search. Importantly, the representation geometry also tells us how to adjust the number of waypoints based on the difficulty of each goal-reaching problem. Experiments show that our method succeeds on long-horizon navigation and robotic manipulation tasks, including settings where strong baselines fail to achieve a single success. Ablations further show that using a fixed number of waypoints substantially degrades performance, highlighting the importance of adapting the plan to task difficulty.

title: Hybrid supervised instance segmentation by learning label noise suppression
summary: To reach top accuracy, current fully supervised instance segmentation methods severely rely on large-scale pixel-wise labeled datasets. They are usually expensive and time-consuming to obtain. Though weakly or semi-supervised methods utilize cheap bounding box labeled, image-level labeled or unlabeled samples to save the labeling cost, their performance is largely sacrificed. To save labeling cost without losing much performance, in this paper, we present a pipeline that can utilize economical bounding box labels and accurate pixel-wise labels in a hybrid way. Specifically, we design two ancillary models to learn label noise suppression and obtain accurate pseudo pixel-wise labels from bounding box labels for training. One is designed to suppress mislabeling between foreground and background, and the other is designed to suppress noise from mislabeling of instances. Moreover, we exploit category-aware spatial attention module, category constraint module, instance constraint module, and self-learning training approach to improve the accuracy of pseudo labels. Experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and the Cityscapes datasets show that our method can achieve competitive performance with much less labeling cost.

title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
summary: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.

title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM
summary: Poor generalisation in deep neural networks is frequently associated with convergence to sharp minima. Sharpness-Aware Minimisation (SAM) improves generalisation of deep neural networks by minimising a combination of the training loss and the local sharpness of the loss landscape, biasing convergence towards flat minima. However, SAM relies on a fixed perturbation radius $ρ$ that ignores local curvature, leading to inefficient behaviour: the perturbation may be too small to escape poor basins defined by sharp local minima, or too large to allow convergence to solutions with good loss-sharpness tradeoff. We reinterpret $ρ$ as the intensity of the perturbation signal and propose Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM (CAP-SAM), a geometry-aware method that modulates the perturbation radius based on a sharpness ratio, enabling a more effective search for robust minima on the loss landscape. We prove that CAP-SAM preserves the same convergence rate as standard SAM in non-convex stochastic settings. Extensive experiments indicate that our approach consistently outperforms SAM and its most prominent variants across diverse network architectures on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet.

title: Tracking a Small Set of Experts in Online Convex Optimization
summary:
For the fundamental problem of prediction from expert advice, Freund asked whether one could compete with a comparator that switches $k$ times among only $m$ experts. For a discrete set of experts, this problem was resolved by Bousquet and Warmuth (2020), who gave an efficient algorithm with optimal regret matching the information-theoretic limit.
  We study the analogous problem in online convex optimization, where the action space is continuous. An inefficient algorithm can be derived by discretizing the action space and applying the Bousquet--Warmuth algorithm, giving regret of $\widetilde{O}(md+k)$, while the best known efficient algorithm for this problem has regret $\widetilde{O}(dk)$. We show that this computational inefficiency is inherent, establishing a separation between the information-theoretic and polynomial-time regret achievable for this problem. Specifically, under the hypergraphic planted-clique conjecture, we show that for every polynomial-time algorithm there exist instances for which it incurs at least $(k\sqrt d)^{1-o(1)}$ regret.

title: From Unreliable to Usable: Decomposing Failure Modes and Confidence Signals in LLM Entity Extraction - Evidence from Cyber Threat Intelligence
comments: 13 pages: 7-page main text within the 8-page limit, plus Limitations, references, and appendices A-J. Code, protocol, and frozen evaluation data will be made public
summary: Audits of large language model (LLM) extraction from full-length documents report severe unreliability, leaving two questions open: what the failures actually consist of, and whether confidence signals can turn unreliable output into usable output. We run a preregistered, fully frozen evaluation of two new-generation low-cost LLMs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash) with a flagship-tier control (GPT-6.1-Sol) on a public corpus of 354 incident campaigns (315 unique reports, 630 model-report evaluations), scoring extraction quality against gold, confidence calibration, and robustness to single-sentence perturbations. Three findings emerge. (1) Unreliability persists across tiers: micro precision is 0.03-0.34 and verbalized calibration error (ECE) 0.53-0.94 across both splits; the gap does not close at the flagship tier. (2) The dominant failure is not hallucination: a full mention census plus a three-tier annotation of 360 sampled candidates (two independent LLM annotators from vendors outside the evaluated set, Cohen's kappa = 0.79 on the preregistered acceptance line, fully disclosed) back-projects to 65.6% background mentions and 19.9% gold-scope gaps, with only 1.2% unsupported candidates. (3) Confidence ranks but does not verify: zero-cost self-consistency-frequency tiering passes a preregistered top-30% precision-gain bar in all six test-split model-type cells (4/6 on train), the zero-cost text-frequency x SC frequency combination wins 3, ties 2, loses 1 across cells, yet relation-level counterfactuals on all 45 targets show that a single misattribution sentence flips high-confidence judgments in 95.6-100% of cases, and even a background sentence explicitly marked as unrelated still binds a fake vulnerability in up to 26.7% of them. We conclude with a deployment boundary: confidence tiering may set review priorities, never truth.
