title: HybridStitch: Token-Adaptive Model Stitching for Efficient Diffusion Generation
summary: Iterative diffusion generation requires different amounts of model capacity at different token positions. Prior model combinations allocate capacity by denoising step or by drafting and verification role. We present HybridStitch, a training-free framework that uses token-level feedback to select the model supplying each adopted update. Continuous image refinement and discrete language commitment operate on a shared generation state, while model-specific KV buffers provide attention context for selected queries. HybridStitch achieves 1.63--1.68$\times$ faster image generation and 1.15--1.58$\times$ diffusion large language model (dLLM) throughput on four main benchmarks. Estimated dLLM decode query cost decreases by 50--66% with comparable generation quality.

title: Global Cross-Modal Geo-Localization: A Million-Scale Dataset and a Physical Consistency Learning Framework
summary: Cross-modal Geo-localization (CMGL) matches ground-level text descriptions with geo-tagged aerial imagery, which is crucial for pedestrian navigation and emergency response. However, existing studies are constrained by narrow geographic coverage and simplistic scene diversity, failing to reflect the immense spatial heterogeneity of global architectural styles and topographic features. To bridge this gap and facilitate universal positioning, we introduce CORE, the first million-scale dataset dedicated to global CMGL. CORE comprises 1,034,786 cross-view images sampled from 225 distinct geographic regions across six continents, offering an unprecedented variety of perspectives in varying environmental conditions and urban layouts. We leverage the zero-shot reasoning of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to synthesize high-quality scene descriptions rich in discriminative cues. Furthermore, we propose a physical-law-aware network (PLANET) for cross-modal geo-localization. PLANET introduces a novel contrastive learning paradigm to guide textual representations in capturing the intrinsic physical signatures of satellite imagery. Extensive experiments across varied geographic regions demonstrate that PLANET significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, establishing a new benchmark for robust, global-scale geo-localization. The dataset and source code will be released at https://github.com/YtH0823/CORE.

title: The Reasoning Trap -- Logical Reasoning as a Mechanistic Pathway to Situational Awareness
comments: Accepted at ICLR 2026 Workshop on Logical Reasoning of Large Language Models. 21 Pages. Position Paper
summary: Situational awareness, the capacity of an AI system to recognize its own nature, understand its training and deployment context, and reason strategically about its circumstances, is widely considered among the most dangerous emergent capabilities in advanced AI systems. Separately, a growing research effort seeks to improve the logical reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) across deduction, induction, and abduction. In this paper, we argue that these two research trajectories are on a collision course. We introduce the RAISE framework (Reasoning Advancing Into Self Examination), which identifies three mechanistic pathways through which improvements in logical reasoning enable progressively deeper levels of situational awareness: deductive self inference, inductive context recognition, and abductive self modeling. We formalize each pathway, construct an escalation ladder from basic self recognition to strategic deception, and demonstrate that every major research topic in LLM logical reasoning maps directly onto a specific amplifier of situational awareness. We further analyze why current safety measures are insufficient to prevent this escalation. We conclude by proposing concrete safeguards, including a "Mirror Test" benchmark and a Reasoning Safety Parity Principle, and pose an uncomfortable but necessary question to the logical reasoning community about its responsibility in this trajectory.

title: Partitioning Israeli Municipalities into Politically Homogeneous Cantons: A Constrained Spatial Clustering Approach
comments: 18 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables. v2: adds the Israeli local authorities in Judea and Samaria, a party-by-election representation, per-election maps and held-out tests. Code, data and maps: https://github.com/adirelm/israel-cantons-project
summary:
Israeli society has experienced significant political polarization in recent years, reflected in five Knesset elections held within a four-year period (2019-2022). Public discourse increasingly references hypothetical divisions of the country into politically homogeneous "cantons." This paper develops a data-driven algorithmic approach to explore such divisions using publicly available municipality-level election results and geographic boundary data.
  We partition 255 Israeli municipalities, including the Israeli local authorities in Judea and Samaria, into cantons of neighbouring municipalities that maximize internal political similarity. We evaluate four clustering algorithms (Simulated Annealing, Agglomerative Clustering with contiguity constraints, Louvain Community Detection, and a K-Means baseline), four feature representations, three distance metrics and six values of K (3-20): 264 configurations.
  BlocShares with Agglomerative clustering gives the highest silhouette score (0.987 with Cosine distance), while NMF with Louvain community detection best balances political homogeneity, silhouette quality (0.142) and interpretability, with stable boundaries across the five elections (ARI 0.927). The resulting K=5 partition identifies five politically coherent regions -- a mixed center-right metropolitan core around Tel Aviv, a right-wing region from Jerusalem through the south and the Judea and Samaria authorities, a right-leaning northern region, an Arab canton, and a canton of the seven predominantly Haredi cities, held together by political similarity rather than shared borders. Built from the 2019-2021 elections only, the cantons still differ significantly in every bloc's vote share in the held-out 2022 election. An interactive web application accompanies this work.

title: Selective Prediction Forgetting for Adaptation of Weakly Supervised Localization of Histology Images
summary: Under strong cross-domain shifts, weakly supervised object localization (WSOL) models often lose their capacity to discriminate and develop a strong prediction bias toward a subset of classes. As a result, the majority of target samples are assigned to these dominant classes. Since source-free (unsupervised) domain adaptation (SFDA) methods typically rely on pseudo-labels, inaccurate pseudo-label estimation causes suboptimal adaptation and poor classification and localization performance. This issue is particularly challenging in computational histopathology, where shifts in organ-specific morphology, staining protocols, and acquisition conditions can significantly impact class-discriminative visual cues. This paper introduces SFDA with selective prediction forgetting (SFDA-SPF), a method designed to mitigate excessive concentration of predictions for dominant classes during target-domain adaptation. SFDA-SPF identifies prediction-dominant classes based on the model's target predictions and selectively revises uncertain samples assigned to them. Importantly, this procedure does not require knowledge of the true target class distribution. In contrast with previous SFDA methods, SFDA-SPF introduces a 'forget set' composed of uncertain samples from dominant classes near their decision boundaries, enabling the classification boundaries to shift away from biased predictions. A second 'retain set' is used to anchor certain and accurate samples. To forget the predictions of dominant classes, SFDA-SPF introduces a complementary optimization objective that reduces their probability while allowing alternative class assignments to emerge. This iterative optimization process reassesses target images for forget and retain sets at regular intervals. In addition to improving image-level pseudo-label estimation, the pixel-level classifier is jointly optimized, further enhancing localization.

title: Verification and Forward Invariance of Control Barrier Functions for Differential-Algebraic Systems
summary: Differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) arise in power networks, chemical processes, and multibody systems, where algebraic constraints encode physical conservation laws. The safety of such systems is critical, yet safe control is challenging because algebraic constraints restrict allowable state trajectories. Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide computationally efficient safety filters for ordinary differential equation (ODE) systems. However, existing CBF methods are not directly applicable to DAEs due to potential conflicts between the CBF condition and the constraint manifold. This paper introduces DAE-aware CBFs that incorporate the differential-algebraic structure through projected vector fields. We derive conditions that ensure forward invariance of safe sets while preserving algebraic constraints and extend the framework to higher-index DAEs. A systematic verification framework is developed, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for geometric correctness and feasibility of DAE-aware CBFs. For polynomial systems, sum-of-squares certificates are provided, while for nonpolynomial and neural network candidates, satisfiability modulo theories are used for falsification. The approach is validated on wind turbine and flexible-link manipulator systems.

title: OxyGen: Unified KV Cache Management for VLA Inference under Multi-Task Parallelism
summary: Embodied AI agents increasingly require parallel execution of multiple tasks, such as manipulation, conversation, and memory construction, from shared observations under distinct time constraints. Recent Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) support such heterogeneous outputs, yet existing inference systems incur redundant computation and resource contention when serving concurrent tasks on-device. We identify isolated KV cache management as the root cause. To address this, we propose unified KV cache management, an inference design that treats the KV cache as a first-class shared resource across tasks and control cycles. This abstraction enables two key optimizations: cross-task KV sharing eliminates redundant prefill of shared observations, while cross-frame continuous batching batches unfinished language requests from different frames and advances them within a per-frame decoding budget. We implement this design in OxyGen and evaluate $π_{0.5}$ on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Thor. OxyGen achieves up to 3.7$\times$ speedup over isolated execution, delivering over 200 tokens/s language throughput and 70 Hz action frequency simultaneously on RTX 4090. We also validate the design on Xiaomi-Robotics-0 and StarVLA across different backbones and expert configurations. We further demonstrate the inference gains on a humanoid robot with on-board Jetson AGX Thor.

title: GenState-AI: State-Aware Dataset for Text-to-Video Retrieval on AI-Generated Videos
summary: Existing text-to-video retrieval benchmarks often permit matching from static appearance, making it difficult to determine whether models capture state changes and final outcomes. We introduce GenState-AI, a benchmark comprising 956 AI-generated videos and 195 verified state-change queries across Toy, Cartoon, Home, and Manipulation domains. Its construction uses prompt-controlled variants that target either conflicting temporal/state outcomes or semantic substitutions. Following human verification, all valid videos contribute to subset-level retrieval pools, while complete query-specific triplets support diagnostic hard-negative ordering. We evaluate VCF-Lik, Qwen3-VL, and LanguageBind using both standard Recall@K and triplet-based consistency metrics. Qwen3-VL (8B) achieves the best macro-average R@1 and triplet consistency, while LanguageBind obtains the highest semantic discrimination accuracy. However, stronger retrieval does not consistently yield correct hard-negative ordering, and Qwen3-VL and LanguageBind remain weak on Manipulation triplets, where VCF-Lik performs substantially better. GenState-AI therefore provides a controlled diagnostic testbed for distinguishing global retrieval quality from fine-grained temporal and semantic grounding in AI-generated videos.

title: BenchPreS: A Benchmark for Context-Aware Personalized Preference Selectivity of Persistent-Memory LLMs
summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly store user preferences in persistent memory to support personalization across interactions. However, in third-party communication settings governed by social and institutional norms, some user preferences may be inappropriate to apply. We introduce BenchPreS, which evaluates whether memory-based user preferences are appropriately applied or suppressed across communication contexts. Using two complementary metrics, Misapplication Rate (MR) and Appropriate Application Rate (AAR), we find even frontier LLMs struggle to apply preferences in a context-sensitive manner. Models with stronger preference adherence exhibit higher rates of over-application, and neither reasoning capability nor prompt-based defenses fully resolve this issue. These results suggest current LLMs treat personalized preferences as globally enforceable rules rather than as context-dependent normative signals.

AI.title_translation: BenchPreS：持久记忆大语言模型上下文感知个性化偏好选择性基准
AI.tldr: 本文提出了BenchPreS基准，发现现有前沿大模型难以根据上下文规范适当抑制持久记忆中的个性化偏好，往往将其作为全局规则而过度应用。
AI.motivation: 大模型常在持久记忆中保存用户偏好以实现个性化，但在受社交和机构规范约束的第三方交流场景下，盲目应用某些偏好可能不恰当，需要评估模型是否具备结合上下文选择性应用偏好的能力。
AI.method: 提出了基准评测数据集 BenchPreS，设计了错误应用率（Misapplication Rate, MR）和适当应用率（Appropriate Application Rate, AAR）两个互补评估指标，用于测试模型在不同交流场景中对持久记忆偏好的应用与抑制能力。
AI.result: 前沿大模型仍难以结合上下文敏感地应用偏好；偏好遵循能力越强的模型，过度应用偏好的发生率越高；强大的推理能力和基于提示词的防御手段均无法完全解决过度应用的问题。
AI.conclusion: 当前的LLM将个性化偏好视为全局强制执行的硬性规则，而非依赖于具体上下文的规范性信号。
AI.translation: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地将用户偏好存储在持久记忆中，以支持跨交互的个性化服务。然而，在受社交和机构规范制约的第三方交流场景中，应用某些用户偏好可能并不恰当。我们提出了 BenchPreS，用于评估基于记忆的用户偏好在不同交流上下文中是否被恰当应用或抑制。通过错误应用率（MR）和适当应用率（AAR）这两个互补指标，我们发现即使是前沿LLM也难以根据上下文敏感地应用偏好。偏好遵循能力较强的模型表现出更高的过度应用率，且无论是推理能力还是基于提示的防御机制都无法彻底解决这一问题。这些结果表明，当前的LLM将个性化偏好视为了全局强制执行的规则，而非依赖上下文的规范性信号。
AI.summary: 本文针对持久记忆大模型在第三方沟通场景下可能不当套用个性化偏好的问题，提出了BenchPreS基准与MR、AAR两项评估指标。实验表明，现有前沿模型容易将记忆偏好视为全局不可违背的规则而过度应用，提示词工程和推理能力也难以彻底消除该问题。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型, 持久记忆, 个性化偏好, 上下文感知, BenchPreS
AI.comments: 该论文指出了当前大模型个性化记忆系统的一个关键安全与合规盲区：模型倾向于将用户偏好机械地当作全局规则，而忽视了社交和机构场景下的规范约束。偏好遵循度与过度应用之间的正相关权衡具有很强的警示意义。局限在于摘要未详细展开具体的数据集构建规模与记忆存储实现机制。

title: Maximum-Entropy Exploration with Future State-Action Visitation Measures
comments: arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2412.06655
summary: Maximum entropy reinforcement learning motivates agents to explore states and actions to maximize the entropy of some distribution, typically by providing additional intrinsic rewards proportional to that entropy function. In this paper, we study intrinsic rewards proportional to the entropy of the discounted distribution of state-action features visited during future time steps. This approach is motivated by two results. First, we show that the expected sum of these intrinsic rewards is a lower bound on the entropy of the discounted distribution of state-action features visited in trajectories starting from the initial states, which we relate to an alternative maximum entropy objective. Second, we show that the distribution used in the intrinsic reward definition is the fixed point of a contraction operator and can therefore be estimated off-policy. Experiments highlight that the new objective often leads to improved visitation of features within individual trajectories, in exchange for slightly reduced visitation of features in expectation over different trajectories, as suggested by the lower bound. It also leads to improved convergence speed for learning exploration-only agents. Control performance remains similar across most methods on the considered benchmarks.

AI.title_translation: 基于未来状态-动作访问度量的最大熵探索
AI.tldr: 本文提出利用未来状态-动作特征访问分布的熵作为内在奖励，实现了理论下界保障与高效的异策略探索学习。
AI.motivation: 传统最大熵强化学习通常依赖熵函数的内在奖励进行探索，本文旨在探索基于未来状态-动作特征访问分布熵的奖励设计，解决轨迹特征分布熵的最大化问题，并实现具有理论保障的异策略可估计性。
AI.method: 提出了一种与未来时间步中访问的状态-动作特征折现分布熵成比例的内在奖励机制。该方法证明了该奖励期望和是初始状态轨迹特征分布熵的下界，并通过压缩算子的不动点性质实现了该分布的异策略（off-policy）估计。
AI.result: 实验表明，新目标通常能改善单条轨迹内特征的访问多样性，虽然跨轨迹的特征访问期望略有下降；同时显著提升了纯探索智能体学习的收敛速度，而在所测试基准上的控制性能与其他大多数方法保持相近。
AI.conclusion: 所提出的基于未来状态-动作访问分布熵的内在奖励机制，提供了一种可在异策略下有效估计的最大熵探索方法，能显著提升单轨迹探索多样性并加速纯探索智能体的收敛。
AI.translation: 最大熵强化学习促使智能体探索状态和动作以最大化某种分布的熵，通常通过提供与该熵函数成比例的额外内在奖励来实现。在本文中，我们研究了与未来时间步所访问的状态-动作特征折现分布熵成比例的内在奖励。该方法源于两项理论结果：首先，我们证明了这些内在奖励的期望和是从初始状态出发的轨迹中所访问状态-动作特征折现分布熵的下界，我们将其与另一种最大熵目标联系起来；其次，我们证明了内在奖励定义中所使用的分布是某个压缩算子的不动点，因此可以进行异策略（off-policy）估计。实验表明，正如理论下界所揭示的，新目标通常能够在单条轨迹内带来更好的特征访问覆盖，代价是不同轨迹平均期望下的特征访问略微减少。此外，该方法还提高了纯探索智能体学习的收敛速度。在所考虑的基准测试中，其控制性能与大多数现有方法保持相近。
AI.summary: 本文研究了一种基于未来状态-动作特征折现分布熵的新型内在奖励探索机制。理论上证明了该奖励和是轨迹特征熵的下界，且可通过收缩算子进行异策略估计。实验显示该方法能提高单轨迹探索丰富度并加快探索收敛速度。
AI.keywords: 最大熵强化学习, 探索机制, 状态-动作访问度量, 内在奖励, 异策略估计
AI.comments: 该论文将最大熵探索与未来状态-动作访问分布的熵相关联，提供了严谨的数学下界支持，并利用压缩算子保证了异策略（off-policy）估计的可行性，在单轨迹特征覆盖和探索收敛速度上有明显优势，但基准任务上的最终控制性能提升相对有限。

title: Learning to Disprove: Formal Counterexample Generation with Large Language Models
summary: Mathematical reasoning demands two critical, complementary skills: constructing rigorous proofs for true statements and discovering counterexamples that disprove false ones. However, current AI efforts in mathematics focus almost exclusively on proof construction, often neglecting the equally important task of finding counterexamples. In this paper, we address this gap by fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) to reason about and generate counterexamples. We formalize this task as formal counterexample generation, which requires LLMs not only to propose candidate counterexamples but also to produce formal proofs that can be automatically verified in the Lean 4 theorem prover. To enable effective learning, we introduce a symbolic mutation strategy that constructs candidate counterexample-generation tasks by systematically extracting theorems and removing selected hypotheses. Together with curated datasets, this strategy enables a multi-reward expert iteration framework that substantially enhances both the effectiveness and efficiency of training LLMs for counterexample generation and theorem proving. Experiments on three newly collected benchmarks validate the advantages of our approach, showing that the mutation strategy and training framework yield substantial performance gains.

AI.title_translation: 学习反驳：使用大型语言模型生成形式化反例
AI.tldr: 本文通过微调大型语言模型（LLMs）来解决数学推理中形式化反例生成的问题，引入了符号变异策略和多奖励专家迭代框架，显著提高了模型在反例生成和定理证明方面的性能。
AI.motivation: 当前的AI数学研究主要集中在构建严谨的证明，而忽视了同样重要的寻找反例的任务。本文旨在弥补这一空白，使大型语言模型能够推理和生成反例。
AI.method: 本文将反例生成任务形式化为形式化反例生成，要求LLMs不仅提出候选反例，还要生成可在Lean 4定理证明器中自动验证的形式化证明。为了有效学习，引入了一种符号变异策略，通过系统地提取定理并移除选定的假设来构建候选反例生成任务。结合精选数据集，该策略实现了多奖励专家迭代框架。
AI.result: 在三个新收集的基准测试上的实验验证了该方法的优势，表明变异策略和训练框架带来了显著的性能提升。
AI.conclusion: 该研究成功地通过微调大型语言模型，结合符号变异策略和多奖励专家迭代框架，有效地解决了形式化反例生成的问题，并在实验中取得了显著的性能提升。
AI.translation: 数学推理需要两种关键的、互补的技能：为真命题构建严谨的证明，以及发现反驳假命题的反例。然而，当前人工智能在数学方面的努力几乎完全集中在证明构建上，常常忽视了同样重要的寻找反例的任务。在本文中，我们通过微调大型语言模型（LLMs）来推理和生成反例，从而弥补了这一空白。我们将这项任务形式化为形式化反例生成，这要求LLMs不仅要提出候选反例，还要生成可以在Lean 4定理证明器中自动验证的形式化证明。为了实现有效的学习，我们引入了一种符号变异策略，通过系统地提取定理并移除选定的假设来构建候选反例生成任务。结合精选数据集，该策略实现了一个多奖励专家迭代框架，该框架显著提高了训练LLMs进行反例生成和定理证明的有效性和效率。在三个新收集的基准测试上的实验验证了我们方法的优势，表明变异策略和训练框架带来了显著的性能增益。
AI.summary: 本文旨在解决AI在数学推理中忽视反例生成的问题。通过微调大型语言模型（LLMs），研究者将反例生成形式化为需要可验证证明的任务。为提高学习效率，引入了符号变异策略和多奖励专家迭代框架。实验结果表明，该方法在反例生成和定理证明方面均取得了显著性能提升。
AI.keywords: 大型语言模型, 反例生成, 形式化证明, 符号变异, Lean 4
AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于将大型语言模型应用于形式化反例生成这一被忽视的领域，并提出了一套结合符号变异策略和多奖励专家迭代框架的有效训练方法。其重要性在于，反例生成对于数学推理至关重要，该研究为AI在数学领域的全面发展提供了新的方向。

title: LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models
summary: Looped language models (LoopLMs) perform iterative latent computation to refine internal representations, offering an alternative to explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. However, existing reinforcement learning (RL) paradigms primarily target output tokens, creating a structural mismatch with looped architectures whose reasoning unfolds implicitly. In this work, we propose LoopRPT, a reinforcement pre-training framework tailored for LoopLMs. By reframing next-token prediction as a next-token reasoning task, LoopRPT assigns reinforcement signals directly to latent steps using an EMA teacher reference and noisy latent rollouts. This formulation enables RL to directly shape intermediate representations, compressing effective reasoning into fewer iterations. We instantiate LoopRPT on Ouro across multiple model scales. Results show that LoopRPT improves per-step representation quality and achieves Pareto dominance in accuracy-computation trade-offs. Large gains on hard tokens indicate that LoopRPT enhances early-stage reasoning rather than merely encouraging premature exits. Our findings highlight reinforcement pre-training as a principled paradigm for learning efficient latent reasoning in LoopLMs.

AI.title_translation: LoopRPT：循环语言模型的强化预训练
AI.tldr: LoopRPT是一个为循环语言模型（LoopLMs）设计的强化预训练框架，通过直接对潜在步骤施加强化信号，以提升模型内部推理效率和表示质量。
AI.motivation: 现有强化学习（RL）范式主要针对输出token，与循环语言模型（LoopLMs）的隐式推理结构不匹配，导致RL难以直接塑造LoopLMs的中间表示。
AI.method: LoopRPT将下一个token预测重新定义为下一个token推理任务，并使用EMA教师参考和带噪声的潜在rollout直接向潜在步骤分配强化信号。这使得RL能够直接塑造中间表示，将有效的推理压缩到更少的迭代中。
AI.result: LoopRPT提高了每步表示质量，并在准确性-计算权衡方面实现了帕累托优势。在难处理的token上取得的显著增益表明LoopRPT增强了早期推理能力，而不仅仅是鼓励过早退出。
AI.conclusion: 强化预训练是学习循环语言模型中高效潜在推理的原则性范式。
AI.translation: 循环语言模型（LoopLMs）通过迭代潜在计算来精炼内部表示，为显式思维链（CoT）推理提供了一种替代方案。然而，现有的强化学习（RL）范式主要针对输出token，与循环架构的推理隐式展开的结构存在不匹配。在这项工作中，我们提出了LoopRPT，一个专为LoopLMs设计的强化预训练框架。通过将下一个token预测重新定义为下一个token推理任务，LoopRPT使用EMA教师参考和带噪声的潜在rollout直接向潜在步骤分配强化信号。这种公式使RL能够直接塑造中间表示，将有效的推理压缩到更少的迭代中。我们在多个模型规模的Ouro上实例化了LoopRPT。结果表明，LoopRPT提高了每步表示质量，并在准确性-计算权衡方面实现了帕累托优势。在难处理的token上取得的显著增益表明LoopRPT增强了早期推理能力，而不仅仅是鼓励过早退出。我们的发现强调了强化预训练是学习LoopLMs中高效潜在推理的原则性范式。
AI.summary: 本文提出了LoopRPT，一个针对循环语言模型（LoopLMs）的强化预训练框架。针对现有RL范式与LoopLMs隐式推理结构不匹配的问题，LoopRPT通过将下一个token预测重构为下一个token推理任务，并利用EMA教师参考和噪声潜在rollouts直接向潜在步骤施加强化信号。实验结果表明，LoopRPT显著提升了每步表示质量，并在准确性与计算效率之间取得了更好的平衡，尤其在处理复杂token时表现出更强的早期推理能力。这表明强化预训练是提高LoopLMs潜在推理效率的有效方法。
AI.keywords: 循环语言模型, 强化预训练, 潜在推理, 内部表示, LoopRPT
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地提出了一种针对循环语言模型内部潜在推理的强化预训练方法，解决了传统RL范式与此类模型结构不匹配的问题。通过直接优化中间表示，LoopRPT有望显著提升模型在复杂推理任务上的效率和性能，为未来语言模型的设计提供了新的思路。

title: Reasoning or Rhetoric? An Empirical Analysis of Moral Reasoning Explanations in Large Language Models
summary: Do large language models reason morally, or do they merely sound like they do? We investigate whether LLM responses to moral dilemmas exhibit genuine developmental progression through Kohlberg's stages of moral development, or whether alignment training instead produces reasoning-like outputs that superficially resemble mature moral judgment without the underlying developmental trajectory. Using an LLM-as-judge scoring pipeline validated across three judge models, we classify more than 600 responses from 13 LLMs spanning a range of architectures, parameter scales, and training regimes across six classical moral dilemmas, and conduct ten complementary analyses to characterize the nature and internal coherence of the resulting patterns. Our results reveal a striking inversion: responses overwhelmingly correspond to post-conventional reasoning (Stages 5-6) regardless of model size, architecture, or prompting strategy, the effective inverse of human developmental norms, where Stage 4 dominates. Most strikingly, a subset of models exhibit moral decoupling: systematic inconsistency between stated moral justification and action choice, a form of logical incoherence that persists across scale and prompting strategy and represents a direct reasoning consistency failure independent of rhetorical sophistication. Model scale carries a statistically significant but practically small effect; training type has no significant independent main effect; and models exhibit near-robotic cross-dilemma consistency producing logically indistinguishable responses across semantically distinct moral problems. We posit that these patterns constitute evidence for moral ventriloquism: the acquisition, through alignment training, of the rhetorical conventions of mature moral reasoning without the underlying developmental trajectory those conventions are meant to represent.

AI.title_translation: 论证还是修辞？大型语言模型道德推理解释的实证分析
AI.tldr: 本文实证分析发现，大型语言模型在道德困境中并非真正进行人类发展式的道德推理，而是通过对齐训练习得成熟道德推理的修辞惯例，表现出与人类发展规范相反的模式，并存在道德解耦现象，即所谓的“道德腹语术”。
AI.motivation: 探讨大型语言模型（LLM）对道德困境的反应是表现出真正的道德发展阶段，还是对齐训练产生的表面上类似成熟道德判断但缺乏内在发展轨迹的推理输出。
AI.method: 使用经过三个评判模型验证的“LLM即评判者”评分流程；对来自13个LLM（涵盖不同架构、参数规模和训练方案）的600多个响应进行分类，涉及六个经典道德困境；进行了十项补充分析，以表征所得模式的性质和内部一致性。
AI.result: LLM响应绝大多数对应于后习俗推理（阶段5-6），与人类发展规范（阶段4为主）完全相反；部分模型表现出“道德解耦”：陈述的道德理由与行动选择之间存在系统性不一致；模型规模对结果有统计学上显著但实际影响很小的作用；训练类型没有显著的独立主效应；模型在不同困境之间表现出近乎机械的一致性，对语义上不同的道德问题产生逻辑上无法区分的响应。
AI.conclusion: 这些模式构成了“道德腹语术”的证据：LLM通过对齐训练习得了成熟道德推理的修辞惯例，但缺乏这些惯例所代表的内在发展轨迹。
AI.translation: 大型语言模型是进行道德推理，还是仅仅听起来像在进行？我们调查了大型语言模型（LLM）对道德困境的反应是否表现出科尔伯格道德发展阶段的真正发展进程，或者对齐训练是否仅仅产生了表面上类似于成熟道德判断但缺乏潜在发展轨迹的推理式输出。我们使用一个经过三个评判模型验证的“LLM即评判者”评分流程，对来自13个LLM（涵盖一系列架构、参数规模和训练方案）的600多个响应进行了分类，涉及六个经典道德困境，并进行了十项补充分析，以表征所得模式的性质和内部一致性。我们的结果揭示了一个惊人的反转：无论模型大小、架构或提示策略如何，响应绝大多数对应于后习俗推理（阶段5-6），这与人类发展规范（阶段4为主）完全相反。最引人注目的是，一部分模型表现出道德解耦：陈述的道德理由与行动选择之间存在系统性不一致，这是一种逻辑不连贯的形式，它跨越规模和提示策略持续存在，代表着独立于修辞复杂性的直接推理一致性失败。模型规模具有统计学上显著但实际影响很小的作用；训练类型没有显著的独立主效应；模型在不同困境之间表现出近乎机械的一致性，对语义上不同的道德问题产生逻辑上无法区分的响应。我们认为这些模式构成了道德腹语术的证据：通过对齐训练，LLM获得了成熟道德推理的修辞惯例，但缺乏这些惯例所代表的内在发展轨迹。
AI.summary: 本文实证分析了大型语言模型（LLM）在道德困境中的表现，以探究其是进行真正的道德推理还是仅模仿成熟道德判断。研究通过“LLM即评判者”评分流程，分析了13个LLM对六个经典道德困境的600多个响应。结果发现，LLM的道德判断模式与人类发展规范相反，主要表现为后习俗推理（阶段5-6），并存在道德理由与行动选择不一致的“道德解耦”现象。研究者提出，这表明LLM通过对齐训练习得了道德推理的“修辞惯例”，而非内在的发展轨迹，称之为“道德腹语术”。
AI.keywords: 大型语言模型, 道德推理, 科尔伯格道德发展阶段, 对齐训练, 道德腹语术
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过引入“道德腹语术”的概念，对大型语言模型在道德推理方面的能力提出了深刻的质疑。其创新之处在于采用“LLM即评判者”的独特方法，并揭示了LLM道德判断与人类发展模式的惊人反转及道德解耦的逻辑不一致性。这对于理解当前LLM的局限性及其在伦理决策场景中的应用具有重要意义。

title: LLMON: An LLM-native Markup Language to Leverage Structure and Semantics at the LLM Interface
summary:
Textual Large Language Models (LLMs) provide a simple and familiar interface: a string of text is used for both input and output. However, the information conveyed to an LLM often has a richer structure and semantics, which is not conveyed in a string. For example, most prompts contain both instructions ("Summarize this paper into a paragraph") and data (the paper to summarize), but these are usually not distinguished when passed to the model. This can lead to model confusion and security risks, such as prompt injection attacks.
  This work addresses this shortcoming by introducing an LLM-native mark-up language, LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced "Lemon"), that enables the structure and semantic metadata of the text to be communicated in a natural way to an LLM. This information can then be used during model training, model prompting, and inference implementation, leading to improvements in model accuracy, safety, and security. This is analogous to how programming language types can be used for many purposes, such as static checking, code generation, dynamic checking, and IDE highlighting.
  We discuss the general design requirements of an LLM-native markup language, introduce the LLMON markup language and show how it meets these design requirements, describe how the information contained in a LLMON artifact can benefit model training and inference implementation, and provide some preliminary empirical evidence of its value for both of these use cases. We also discuss broader issues and research opportunities that are enabled with an LLM-native approach.

AI.title_translation: LLMON：一种LLM原生标记语言，用于在LLM接口中利用结构和语义
AI.tldr: LLMON是一种LLM原生标记语言，旨在通过在LLM接口中传递文本的结构和语义元数据来提高大型语言模型的准确性、安全性和安全性，从而解决当前文本字符串接口的局限性。
AI.motivation: 当前大型语言模型（LLM）的文本接口无法有效传达输入和输出中更丰富的结构和语义信息。提示中的指令和数据未区分，可能导致模型混淆和安全风险，例如提示注入攻击。
AI.method: 本文引入了一种LLM原生标记语言LLMON（LLM对象表示法），它允许以自然的方式将文本的结构和语义元数据传达给LLM。该方法包括讨论设计要求、介绍LLMON语言及其符合要求的方式，并描述LLMON信息如何有益于模型训练和推理实现。
AI.result: LLMON传达的信息可用于模型训练、模型提示和推理实现，从而提高模型的准确性、安全性和安全性。文章提供了初步的实证证据，证明其在这些用例中的价值。
AI.conclusion: LLMON方法能够利用文本的结构和语义信息，从而提高LLM的性能和安全性。它还开启了更广泛的研究问题和机遇。
AI.translation:
文本大型语言模型（LLM）提供了一个简单而熟悉的接口：一个文本字符串用于输入和输出。然而，传达给LLM的信息通常具有更丰富的结构和语义，这些信息并未在字符串中传达。例如，大多数提示都包含指令（“将这篇论文总结成一段话”）和数据（要总结的论文），但这些在传递给模型时通常没有区分。这可能导致模型混淆和安全风险，例如提示注入攻击。
这项工作通过引入一种LLM原生标记语言LLMON（LLM对象表示法，发音为“Lemon”）来解决这一缺点，该语言能够以自然的方式将文本的结构和语义元数据传达给LLM。然后，这些信息可以在模型训练、模型提示和推理实现期间使用，从而提高模型的准确性、安全性和安全性。这类似于编程语言类型如何用于多种目的，例如静态检查、代码生成、动态检查和IDE高亮显示。
我们讨论了LLM原生标记语言的通用设计要求，介绍了LLMON标记语言并展示了它如何满足这些设计要求，描述了LLMON工件中包含的信息如何有益于模型训练和推理实现，并为这两个用例提供了一些初步的实证证据。我们还讨论了LLM原生方法所带来的更广泛的问题和研究机会。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为LLMON的LLM原生标记语言，旨在解决当前大型语言模型文本接口无法有效传达结构和语义信息的局限性。LLMON允许将文本的结构和语义元数据以自然的方式传达给LLM，从而提高模型准确性、安全性和安全性，并可应用于模型训练、提示和推理实现。研究提供了初步的实证证据，并探讨了该方法带来的研究机遇。
AI.keywords: LLMON, LLM原生标记语言, 结构化输入, 语义, 提示注入
AI.comments: LLMON的创新之处在于它将编程语言中类型系统的概念引入到LLM的接口设计中，通过结构化和语义化的输入来解决传统文本接口导致的模型混淆和安全问题（如提示注入）。这对于提高LLM的可靠性和可用性具有重要意义，并可能为未来LLM的开发和应用开辟新的范式。

title: PLACID: Privacy-preserving Large language models for Acronym Clinical Inference and Disambiguation
comments: 10 pages, 2 figures, Under review AMIA Symposium
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer transformative solutions across many domains, but healthcare integration is hindered by strict data privacy constraints. Clinical narratives are dense with ambiguous acronyms, misinterpretation these abbreviations can precipitate severe outcomes like life-threatening medication errors. While cloud-dependent LLMs excel at Acronym Disambiguation, transmitting Protected Health Information to external servers violates privacy frameworks. To bridge this gap, this study pioneers the evaluation of small-parameter models deployed entirely on-device to ensure privacy preservation. We introduce a privacy-preserving cascaded pipeline leveraging general-purpose local models to detect clinical acronyms, routing them to domain-specific biomedical models for context-relevant expansions. Results reveal that while general instruction-following models achieve high detection accuracy (~0.988), their expansion capabilities plummet (~0.655). Our cascaded approach utilizes domain-specific medical models to increase expansion accuracy to (~0.81). This novel work demonstrates that privacy-preserving, on-device (2B-10B) models deliver high-fidelity clinical acronym disambiguation support.
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, Under review AMIA Symposium

AI.title_translation: PLACID: 隐私保护大型语言模型用于临床首字母缩略词推断与消歧
AI.tldr: 本研究开发了一个隐私保护的设备端级联管道，利用小型语言模型高精度地检测和消歧临床叙述中的缩略词，以解决医疗领域LLM应用中的数据隐私和缩略词误解问题。
AI.motivation: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在医疗保健领域的应用受到严格数据隐私限制的阻碍。临床叙述中充满模糊缩略词，误解可能导致严重的医疗错误。将受保护的健康信息传输到云端LLMs违反隐私框架，因此需要一种隐私保护的解决方案。
AI.method: 本研究引入了一个隐私保护的级联管道，完全部署在设备端，利用小参数模型（2B-10B）。该管道首先使用通用本地模型检测临床缩略词，然后将检测到的缩略词路由到领域特定的生物医学模型进行上下文相关的扩展和消歧。
AI.result: 通用指令遵循模型在缩略词检测方面表现出高准确率（约0.988），但在扩展能力方面准确率较低（约0.655）。本研究提出的级联方法通过利用领域特定医学模型，将缩略词扩展的准确率提高到约0.81。
AI.conclusion: 隐私保护的设备端（2B-10B）模型能够提供高保真度的临床缩略词消歧支持，有效解决了医疗领域LLM应用中的隐私和准确性挑战。
AI.translation: 大型语言模型（LLM）在许多领域提供了变革性解决方案，但医疗保健整合受到严格数据隐私限制的阻碍。临床叙述中充满了模糊的缩略词，误解这些缩写可能导致严重的后果，例如危及生命的用药错误。虽然依赖云的LLM在缩略词消歧方面表现出色，但将受保护健康信息传输到外部服务器违反了隐私框架。为了弥合这一差距，本研究率先评估了完全部署在设备上的小参数模型，以确保隐私保护。我们引入了一个隐私保护的级联管道，利用通用本地模型检测临床缩略词，然后将其路由到领域特定生物医学模型进行上下文相关扩展。结果显示，虽然通用指令遵循模型实现了高检测准确率（~0.988），但其扩展能力大幅下降（~0.655）。我们的级联方法利用领域特定医学模型将扩展准确率提高到（~0.81）。这项新颖的工作表明，隐私保护的设备端（2B-10B）模型能够提供高保真度的临床缩略词消歧支持。
AI.summary: 本研究提出PLACID，一个隐私保护的设备端级联管道，用于临床缩略词的推断和消歧。针对医疗领域LLM应用中数据隐私的挑战，该方法结合通用本地模型进行缩略词检测（准确率约0.988）和领域特定生物医学模型进行上下文扩展，将扩展准确率从通用模型的约0.655提升至约0.81。研究证明，小参数的设备端模型能够有效且隐私地处理复杂的临床语言问题。
AI.keywords: 隐私保护, 大型语言模型, 临床缩略词消歧, 设备端AI, 医疗保健
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地解决了医疗领域LLM应用中的核心隐私问题，通过设备端部署的小参数级联模型，在保证数据安全的同时实现了高精度的临床缩略词消歧。其方法结合了通用检测和领域特定扩展，有效平衡了性能与隐私需求，为未来医疗AI的部署提供了重要参考。

title: A Wireless World Model for AI-Native 6G Networks
summary: Integrating AI into the physical layer is a cornerstone of 6G networks. However, current data-driven approaches struggle to generalize across dynamic environments because they lack an intrinsic understanding of electromagnetic wave propagation. We introduce the Wireless World Model (WWM), a multi-modal foundation framework predicting the spatiotemporal evolution of wireless channels by internalizing the causal relationship between 3D geometry and signal dynamics. Pre-trained on a massive ray-traced multi-modal dataset, WWM overcomes the data authenticity gap, further validated under real-world measurement data. Using a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a multi-modal mixture-of-experts Transformer, WWM fuses channel state information, 3D point clouds, and user trajectories into a unified representation. Across the five key downstream tasks supported by WWM, it achieves remarkable performance in seen environments, unseen generalization scenarios, and real-world measurements, consistently outperforming SOTA uni-modal foundation models and task-specific models. This paves the way for physics-aware 6G intelligence that adapts to the physical world.

AI.title_translation: 面向AI原生6G网络的无线世界模型
AI.tldr: 无线世界模型（WWM）是一个多模态基础框架，通过内化3D几何和信号动态之间的因果关系，预测无线信道的时空演化，并在6G网络任务中显著优于现有SOTA模型。
AI.motivation: 当前的6G网络中，将AI集成到物理层的数据驱动方法难以在动态环境中泛化，因为它们缺乏对电磁波传播的内在理解。
AI.method: 本文引入了无线世界模型（WWM），这是一个多模态基础框架。它通过内化3D几何和信号动态之间的因果关系来预测无线信道的时空演化。WWM在一个大规模射线追踪多模态数据集上进行预训练，并经过真实世界测量数据验证，克服了数据真实性差距。WWM采用联合嵌入预测架构和多模态专家混合Transformer，将信道状态信息、3D点云和用户轨迹融合为统一表示。

AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为无线世界模型（WWM）的多模态基础框架，旨在解决现有AI驱动6G网络在动态环境中泛化能力不足的问题。WWM通过内化3D几何与信号动态的因果关系来预测无线信道的时空演化，并利用大规模射线追踪数据集进行预训练及真实测量数据验证。其采用联合嵌入预测架构和多模态专家混合Transformer，融合信道状态信息、3D点云和用户轨迹。实验结果表明，WWM在多种场景和下游任务中均显著超越了现有SOTA模型，为构建物理感知型6G智能奠定了基础。
AI.keywords: 无线世界模型, AI原生6G, 多模态基础模型, 信道预测, 电磁波传播

title: Constitutive parameterized deep energy method for solid mechanics problems with random material parameters
summary: In practical structural design and solid mechanics simulations, material properties inherently exhibit random variations within bounded intervals. However, evaluating mechanical responses under continuous material uncertainty remains a persistent challenge. Traditional numerical approaches, such as the Finite Element Method (FEM), incur prohibitive computational costs as they require repeated mesh discretization and equation solving for every parametric realization. Similarly, data-driven surrogate models depend heavily on massive, high-fidelity datasets, while standard physics-informed frameworks (e.g., the Deep Energy Method) strictly demand complete retraining from scratch whenever material parameters change. To bridge this critical gap, we propose the Constitutive Parameterized Deep Energy Method (CPDEM). In this purely physics-driven framework, the strain energy density functional is reformulated by encoding a latent representation of stochastic constitutive parameters. By embedding material parameters directly into the neural network alongside spatial coordinates, CPDEM transforms conventional spatial collocation points into parameter-aware material points. Trained in an unsupervised manner via expected energy minimization over the parameter domain, the pre-trained model continuously learns the solution manifold. Consequently, it enables zero-shot, real-time inference of displacement fields for unknown material parameters without requiring any dataset generation or model retraining. The proposed method is rigorously validated across diverse benchmarks, including linear elasticity, finite-strain hyperelasticity, and complex highly nonlinear contact mechanics. To the best of our knowledge, CPDEM represents the first purely physics-driven deep learning paradigm capable of simultaneously and efficiently handling continuous multi-parameter variations in solid mechanics.

AI.title_translation: 具有随机材料参数的固体力学问题的本构参数化深度能量方法
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种名为CPDEM的纯物理驱动深度学习方法，首次实现了固体力学中连续随机材料参数的高效零样本实时推理。
AI.motivation: 实际工程中材料属性具有随机变异性，但传统有限元法计算成本高昂，数据驱动模型依赖海量数据集，标准物理信息框架在材料参数改变时需要完全重新训练，因此需要一种能高效处理连续材料不确定性的方法。
AI.method: 提出了本构参数化深度能量方法（CPDEM），通过在神经网络中将材料参数与空间坐标一起编码，将传统的空间配点转化为参数感知材料点，并通过参数域上的期望能量最小化以无监督方式进行训练。
AI.result: 通过线性弹性、有限变形超弹性以及复杂的强非线性接触力学等多样化基准测试，验证了该方法能够实现未知材料参数位移场的零样本、实时推理。
AI.conclusion: CPDEM是一种高效、纯物理驱动的深度学习范式，能够有效解决含随机材料参数的固体力学问题，实现零样本实时推理。
AI.translation: 在实际结构设计和固体力学模拟中，材料属性在有界区间内表现出固有的随机变化。然而，在连续材料不确定性下评估力学响应仍然是一个持续的挑战。传统的数值方法，如有限元法（FEM），由于需要对每个参数实现进行重复的网格离散化和方程求解，导致了极高的计算成本。类似地，数据驱动的代理模型严重依赖海量的高保真数据集，而标准的物理信息框架（如深度能量方法）在材料参数改变时严格要求从头开始完全重新训练。为了弥补这一关键差距，我们提出了本构参数化深度能量方法（CPDEM）。在这个纯物理驱动的框架中，通过编码随机本构参数的潜表示，重构了应变能密度泛函。通过将材料参数与空间坐标一起直接嵌入神经网络，CPDEM将传统的空间配置点转化为参数感知的材料点。该预训练模型通过参数域上的期望能量最小化以无监督方式进行训练，能够连续学习解流形。因此，它能够在不需要任何数据集生成或模型重新训练的情况下，对未知材料参数的位移场进行零样本、实时的推理。所提出的方法在各种基准测试中得到了严格验证，包括线弹性、有限应变超弹性以及复杂的强非线性接触力学。据我们所知，CPDEM代表了第一个能够同时且高效处理固体力学中连续多参数变化的纯物理驱动深度学习范式。
AI.summary: 本文提出了本构参数化深度能量方法（CPDEM），这是一种纯物理驱动的深度学习框架，通过将随机本构参数的潜在表示编码到神经网络中，实现了在固体力学中对连续材料参数变化的零样本、实时推理，无需生成数据集或重新训练模型。
AI.keywords: 深度能量方法, 材料不确定性, 固体力学, 物理信息神经网络, 参数化建模
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的本构参数化深度能量方法（CPDEM），将材料不确定性直接融入神经网络中，实现了固体力学中连续随机参数的高效零样本实时推理，克服了传统有限元法和现有PINN方法计算成本高的痛点。

title: Can We Change "Stroke Size" to Simplify Regression Learning?
summary: Deep-learning-based image generation is increasingly useful but expensive. Across the different timesteps in the denoising chain, high-noise timesteps present distinct optimization and prediction challenges, which can increase the cost of real-world applications. Inspired by the varying stroke sizes used in human painting, in this work, we ask whether a similar stroke-size variation (i.e., rough stroke applied early) in diffusion can simplify existing image-generation algorithms. We subsequently develop the MultiStroke operator, which linearly interpolates coarse and fine strokes in a coarse-to-fine manner to potentially simplify the prediction target, especially at high-noise timesteps. Across DDPM and flow-matching models trained from scratch, MultiStroke achieves an FID reduction of up to $70.2\%$. A quick video is at https://wendybaiyunwei.github.io/MultiStroke-Web/.

AI.title_translation: 我们能否改变“笔触大小”以简化回归学习？
AI.tldr: 本文提出MultiStroke算子，受人类绘画中笔触大小变化的启发，旨在简化扩散模型中的图像生成，并在FID上实现了显著降低。
AI.motivation: 深度学习图像生成日益有用但成本高昂，尤其是在去噪链中的高噪声时间步，这些时间步带来了独特的优化和预测挑战，增加了实际应用的成本。
AI.method: 受人类绘画中不同笔触大小的启发，作者探讨了在扩散模型中使用类似的笔触大小变化（即早期应用粗略笔触）来简化现有图像生成算法。他们开发了MultiStroke算子，以从粗到细的方式线性插值粗笔触和细笔触，以简化预测目标，特别是在高噪声时间步。
AI.result: MultiStroke在从头开始训练的DDPM和流匹配模型中实现了高达70.2%的FID降低。
AI.conclusion: MultiStroke算子通过以从粗到细的方式改变笔触大小，有效简化了扩散模型中的预测目标，从而显著提高了图像生成质量（通过FID降低来衡量）。
AI.translation: 深度学习驱动的图像生成日益有用但成本高昂。在去噪链的不同时间步中，高噪声时间步带来了独特的优化和预测挑战，这会增加实际应用的成本。受人类绘画中不同笔触大小变化的启发，在这项工作中，我们探讨了扩散模型中类似的笔触大小变化（即早期应用粗略笔触）是否可以简化现有的图像生成算法。随后，我们开发了MultiStroke算子，它以从粗到细的方式线性插值粗笔触和细笔触，以潜在地简化预测目标，尤其是在高噪声时间步。在从头开始训练的DDPM和流匹配模型中，MultiStroke实现了高达70.2%的FID降低。快速视频网址：https://wendybaiyunwei.github.io/MultiStroke-Web/。
AI.summary: 本文旨在解决深度学习图像生成中高噪声时间步的成本和复杂性问题。受人类绘画的启发，作者引入了MultiStroke算子，该算子以从粗到细的方式插值笔触大小，从而简化了扩散模型中的预测目标。该方法显著提高了图像生成质量，在DDPM和流匹配模型中实现了高达70.2%的FID降低。
AI.keywords: 扩散模型, 图像生成, 笔触大小, MultiStroke算子, FID降低
AI.comments: 这项工作的创新之处在于从人类艺术技术（变化的笔触大小）中汲取灵感，以解决深度学习（简化扩散模型）中的技术挑战。这种跨学科的方法是新颖且有效的，展示了性能的显著提升，为使图像生成更高效和可及提供了一个有前景的方向。

title: Mapping data literacy trajectories in K-12 education
comments: Presented at the Data Literacy for the 21st Century: Perspectives from Visualization, Cognitive Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Education CHI '26 workshop
summary: Data literacy skills are fundamental in computer science education. However, understanding how data-driven systems work represents a paradigm shift from traditional rule-based programming. We conducted a systematic literature review of 84 studies to understand K-12 learners' engagement with data across disciplines and contexts. We propose the data paradigms framework that categorises learning activities along two dimensions: (i) logic (knowledge-based or data-driven systems), and (ii) explainability (transparent or opaque models). We further apply the notion of learning trajectories to visualize the pathways learners follow across these distinct paradigms. We detail four distinct trajectories as a provocation for researchers and educators to reflect on how the notion of data literacy varies depending on the learning context. We suggest these trajectories could be useful to those concerned with the design of data literacy learning environments within and beyond CS education.

title: Structural Pass Analysis in Football: Learning Pass Archetypes and Tactical Impact from Spatio-Temporal Tracking Data
summary: Passing actions are commonly evaluated through ball progression and attacking outcomes, yet their relationship with the spatial organisation of the opposition provides an additional perspective on passing behaviour. This study introduces an interpretable framework for describing passing structure using synchronised event and tracking data. Three complementary descriptors are proposed: Line Bypass Score (LBS), measuring the difference in goal-side opponent counts between passer and receiver; Space Gain Metric (SGM), comparing their nearest-opponent distances; and Structural Disruption Index (SDI), summarising differences in defensive organisation between pass initiation and a sampled state one second later. Following transformation and standardisation, these descriptors are combined into Tactical Impact Value (TIV), a fixed-weight structural composite. Applied to 41,078 open-play passing events from the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the framework identifies four interpretable profiles: Circulatory, Destabilising, Line-breaking, and Space-expanding. The profiles exhibit distinct structural signatures and different distributions of territorial-crossing and recorded attacking indicators. Team, spatial, player, and passer--receiver analyses further demonstrate how the representation can describe passing behaviour across analytical scales. The framework complements outcome-oriented approaches by connecting individual passing actions with measurable characteristics of opposition positioning and defensive organisation.

title: Terminal Agents Suffice for Enterprise Automation
comments: Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), 10/2026. 56 pages, 6 figures, 23 tables. Code: https://github.com/ServiceNow/StarShell. Data: https://huggingface.co/collections/ServiceNow-AI/starshell. Reviews: https://openreview.net/forum?id=6zrEOjtoVF
summary: There has been growing interest in building agents that can interact with digital platforms to execute meaningful enterprise tasks autonomously. Among the approaches explored are tool-augmented agents built on abstractions such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) and web agents that operate through graphical interfaces. Yet, it remains unclear whether such complex agentic systems are necessary given their cost and operational overhead. We argue that a coding agent equipped only with a terminal and a filesystem can solve many enterprise tasks more effectively by interacting directly with platform APIs. We evaluate this hypothesis across diverse real-world systems and show that these low-level terminal agents match or outperform more complex agent architectures at a fraction of the cost. Our findings suggest that simple, flexible programmatic interfaces combined with strong foundation models should be the backbone of enterprise automation.

title: Cooking Up Risks: Benchmarking and Reducing Food Safety Risks in Large Language Models
summary: Food safety directly affects human health in daily life, as unsafe preparation or storage can lead to contamination and foodborne illness. PwC's 2025 consumer survey reports that 47% of respondents are comfortable using generative AI for meal planning, highlighting the need for safe food-related assistance. Yet the safety of large language models (LLMs) against malicious food-related requests remains underexplored. We introduce FoodGuardBench, an FDA-grounded benchmark with 2,124 seed malicious questions, 16,992 variants from eight jailbreak strategies, and 1,000 benign questions across five food-safety risk categories. Across twelve LLMs, the mean overall ASR is 25.51%, whereas the average per-model maximum across eight attacks is 60.59%, revealing that testing only one attack can substantially underestimate the full extent of food safety risk. For several models, nearly half or more of unsafe answers are rated as ready-to-use guides for harmful actions. Existing general-purpose guardrails average 96.25% benign utility but only 55.80% detection accuracy against these eight jailbreak attacks. Using FoodGuardBench, we fine-tune FoodGuard-4B, a food-safety-specific guardrail that achieves 97.64% out-of-distribution (OOD) accuracy while maintaining high benign utility. This demonstrates the value of FoodGuardBench for identifying and mitigating food safety risks.

title: MobiGuide: Vocabulary-Guided Online Recovery for Mobile Manipulation
summary: A central challenge in mobile manipulation is preserving multiple plausible action modes while remaining reactive during execution. For example, grasping a bottle in a cluttered scene can be achieved through multiple physically feasible base-arm motion plans. Deterministic VLA policies trained with $L_1$ regression are efficient, but they tend to average across valid modes and may produce physically invalid actions. Diffusion-based generative policies can better represent multimodal action distributions, yet their proposals may be weakly constrained when generated from pure noise, and iterative sampling can increase inference cost. Action chunking helps amortize inference, but it also introduces partially open-loop execution, allowing small mismatches to accumulate into drift. We present MobiGuide, a generative VLA model for efficient mobile manipulation, where action generation is guided by a structured trajectory vocabulary. Constructed from expert demonstrations, this vocabulary encodes plausible whole-body motion patterns and provides structured priors for feasible action generation. Given the current observation and instruction, MobiGuide locally refines these reference trajectories into context-compatible action proposals and selects the most suitable trajectory for execution. This preserves multimodal action candidates while keeping generation constrained around feasible expert-like motion modes. To mitigate chunk-induced drift, we further introduce a lightweight residual correction module that performs high-frequency, per-step adjustments during rollout. Across diverse mobile manipulation tasks, MobiGuide improves success and stability under execution disturbances while maintaining low-latency inference.

title: F2F-AP: Flow-to-Future Asynchronous Policy for Real-time Dynamic Manipulation
summary: Asynchronous inference has emerged as a prevalent paradigm in robotic manipulation, achieving significant progress in ensuring trajectory smoothness and efficiency. However, a systemic challenge remains unresolved, as inherent latency causes generated actions to inevitably lag behind the real-time environment. This issue is particularly exacerbated in dynamic scenarios, where such temporal misalignment severely compromises the policy's ability to interpret and react to rapidly evolving surroundings. In this paper, we propose a novel framework that leverages predicted object flow to synthesize future observations, incorporating a flow-based contrastive learning objective to align the visual feature representations of predicted observations with ground-truth future states. Empowered by this anticipated visual context, our asynchronous policy gains the capacity for proactive planning and motion, enabling it to explicitly compensate for latency and robustly execute manipulation tasks involving actively moving objects. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances responsiveness and success rates in complex dynamic manipulation tasks.

title: Explorable Proofs: Making Written Proofs Explorable by Grounding Them in Formal Representations
summary: LLM-generated explanations can make technical content more accessible, but there is a ceiling on what they can support interactively. Because LLM outputs are static text, they cannot be executed or stepped through. We argue that grounding explanations in a formalized representation enables interactive affordances beyond what static text supports. We instantiate this idea for mathematical proof comprehension with explorable theorems, a system that uses LLMs to translate a theorem and its written proof into Lean, a programming language for machine-checked proofs, and links the written proof with the Lean code. Readers can work through the proof at a step-level granularity, test custom examples or counterexamples, and trace the logical dependencies bridging each step. Each worked-out step is produced by executing the Lean proof on that example and extracting its intermediate state. A user study ($n = 16$) shows potential advantages of this approach: in a proof-reading task, participants who had access to the provided explorability features gave better, more correct, and more detailed answers to comprehension questions, demonstrating a stronger overall understanding of the underlying mathematics.

title: Towards Secure Agent Skills: Architecture, Threat Taxonomy, and Security Analysis
summary: Agent Skills is an emerging open standard that defines a modular, filesystem-based packaging format enabling LLM-based agents to acquire domain-specific expertise on demand. Despite rapid adoption across multiple agentic platforms and the emergence of large community marketplaces, the security properties of Agent Skills have not been systematically studied. This paper presents a systematization of the security of the Agent Skills framework. We define a threat model for the framework and decompose the full lifecycle of an Agent Skill across four phases---Creation, Distribution, Deployment, and Execution---identifying the structural attack surface each phase introduces. Building on this lifecycle analysis, we construct a threat taxonomy comprising seven categories and nineteen scenarios organized across three attack layers, grounded in both architectural analysis and real-world evidence. Each scenario is annotated with whether the exposure follows from the specification or from the latitude the specification leaves to individual runtimes, with the strength of the public evidence supporting it, and with the feasibility of its mitigation. We map seven documented security incidents onto the taxonomy. Based on these findings, we discuss defense directions for each threat category, identify open research challenges, and provide actionable recommendations for stakeholders. The most severe threats arise from structural properties of the framework itself: the absence of a data-instruction boundary, a single-approval persistent trust model, and a capability declaration mechanism to which the specification attaches no enforcement semantics. None of these is addressable through incremental mitigations alone.

title: KiToke: Distribution-Aware Token Compression for Video Large Language Models
summary: Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) achieve strong performance on video understanding tasks but suffer from high inference costs due to the large number of visual tokens. We study training-free, query-agnostic video token compression, where heuristic importance rules can over-represent large redundant visual groups and miss less frequent visual patterns, particularly under aggressive token budgets. We propose KiToke, a distribution-aware compression framework that treats visual tokens as samples from the video's spatiotemporal token distribution. KiToke uses global embedding density as a proxy for representational redundancy and inverse-density sampling to balance token allocation across visual patterns of different frequencies. It further aggregates unselected tokens into retained anchors within detected temporal intervals to reduce cross-transition mixing. Across evaluated backbones, KiToke achieves the highest average accuracy among compared training-free methods and remains robust down to 1% retention, where most evaluated baselines underperform uniform random token sampling. On LLaVA-OneVision, it preserves 98.5% and 89.2% of the uncompressed model's four-benchmark mean accuracy at 10% and 1% token retention, with 6.8x and 12.5x prefill speedups, respectively, including compression overhead.

title: AdaptFuse: Training-Free Sequential Preference Inference via Externalized Bayesian Computation
summary: Large language models (LLMs) struggle to accumulate evidence across multiple rounds of user interactions, failing to update their beliefs in a manner consistent with Bayesian inference. Existing solutions require fine-tuning on sensitive user interaction data, limiting their applicability in privacy-conscious settings. We propose \textsc{AdaptFuse}, a training-free framework that externalizes probabilistic computation entirely from the LLM, where a symbolic module maintains a Bayesian posterior over a discrete hypothesis set, while a frozen LLM contributes semantic reasoning via multi-sample Dirichlet aggregation. The two signals are combined through entropy-adaptive fusion, which automatically weights each source by its predictive confidence, shifting reliance from the LLM to the symbolic posterior as evidence accumulates. We evaluate across three domains: flight recommendation, hotel recommendation, and web shopping; on Gemma~2 9B, Llama~3 8B, and Qwen~2.5 7B. \textsc{AdaptFuse} consistently outperforms both prompting baselines and fine-tuned Bayesian Teaching models on all tasks, with accuracy improving monotonically over interaction rounds. These results demonstrate that principled inference-time algorithms can substitute for fine-tuning in personalized recommendation, without storing or training on sensitive user data.

title: Coupling Macro Dynamics and Micro States for Long-Horizon Social Simulation
summary: Social network simulation aims to model collective opinion dynamics in large populations, but existing LLM-based simulators mainly focus on aggregate dynamics while largely ignoring individual internal states. This limits their ability to capture opinion reversals driven by gradual individual shifts and makes them unreliable in long-horizon simulations. We propose MF-MDP, a social simulation framework that tightly couples macro-level collective dynamics with micro-level individual states. MF-MDP explicitly models per-agent latent opinion states with a state transition mechanism, combining individual Markov Decision Processes at the micro level with a mean-field collective framework at the macro level. This allows individual behaviors to change internal states gradually rather than trigger instant reactions, enabling the simulator to distinguish agents that are close to switching from those that are far from switching, capture opinion reversals, and maintain accuracy over long horizons. Across real-world events, MF-MDP supports stable simulation of long-horizon social processes with up to 40,000 interactions, compared with about 300 in the baseline MF-LLM, while reducing long-horizon KL divergence by 75.3% (1.2490 to 0.3089) and reversal KL by 66.9% (1.6425 to 0.5434), significantly mitigating the drift observed in MF-LLM. Code is available at ai4ss.github.io/M2Sim.

title: SnapFlow: One-Step Action Generation for Flow-Matching VLAs via Progressive Self-Distillation
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models with flow-matching action heads, such as π0 and π0.5, have become a standard recipe for generalist robot manipulation, but every action chunk is produced by integrating a learned velocity field over about ten sequential action-expert evaluations, so action generation dominates model latency and caps the achievable control frequency. Existing remedies either shrink each evaluation through layer distillation or pruning while leaving the sequential solver in place, or import one-step objectives from image generation that were designed for training from scratch, rely on an exponential-moving-average teacher or an external critic, and regress finite-span targets onto the conditional velocity, whose variance around the marginal field biases the learned map. We introduce SnapFlow, a self-distillation method that adapts a pretrained flow-matching VLA to one-step action generation. SnapFlow mixes local flow-matching supervision with shortcut samples whose target is the model's own two-step Euler endpoint under stop-gradient, and adds a single zero-initialized destination-time projection so that one action expert serves both objectives while the pretrained predictor is preserved at initialization; no separate teacher network or critic is required. On π0.5, whose 10-NFE teacher operates near ceiling, the archived one-NFE SnapFlow checkpoint reaches 98.75% LIBERO success versus 97.75% for the teacher; under a separate paired evaluation of π0, the one-NFE model surpasses its teacher by 10.5 percentage points. SnapFlow also lowers mean and tail action error on held-out data, cuts batch-one model latency by about 3.3x, and transfers to shelf retrieval on a dual-arm humanoid.

title: Relevance Supervision Can Teach Neural Retrievers to Prefer LLM-Generated Text
summary: Recent studies show that neural retrievers often exhibit source bias, ranking LLM-generated passages above semantically similar human-written ones, which threatens the reliability of modern information access systems. While this bias is often viewed as a model-level property, we show that relevance supervision itself can induce it. Empirically, source bias is clearest in relevance-supervised retrievers, and the same encoders become more LLM-preferring after relevance fine-tuning. We trace this effect to surface-level artifacts in supervised retrieval data: annotated positives and negatives differ systematically in properties such as fluency and lexical specificity, and these differences parallel those between LLM-generated and human-written passages. As a result, retrievers can learn artifact-based shortcuts for relevance. We further show theoretically that, under contrastive learning, artifacts that reliably separate positives from negatives can be encoded into learned relevance scores. Motivated by this mechanism, we propose complementary strategies that reduce source bias during training and at inference: balancing artifact distributions in negative sampling and removing the artifact-aligned embedding component, respectively. Overall, our findings support a data-centric view of source bias: retrievers may prefer LLM-generated text not merely because of inherent model properties, but because relevance supervision teaches them to rely on surface-level artifacts.

title: Automated Standardization of Legacy Biomedical Metadata Using an Ontology-Constrained LLM Agent
summary: Descriptive scientific metadata in public repositories are often incomplete and inconsistent with community standards and ontologies, limiting data FAIRness. Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising approach to automatically standardizing such metadata when the LLM is provided with knowledge of the relevant standards in machine-actionable form (e.g., as metadata templates from systems such as the CEDAR Workbench). Entry of metadata standards through prompt engineering offers only fixed snapshots of the relevant standards, however, and it relies on an LLM's pretrained knowledge to interpret and satisfy constraints related to the standard. We evaluate whether giving an LLM access to metadata specifications and authoritative terminology at runtime improves automated metadata standardization. We present ARMS, a tool-augmented LLM agent that retrieves complete CEDAR metadata templates and dynamically queries authoritative biomedical terminology services at execution time. We compared ARMS with a prompt-based approach on 839 legacy metadata records from the Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP), using expert-standardized records as the reference standard. ARMS outperformed the prompt-based approach, increasing precision from 0.56 to 0.93 and recall from 0.51 to 0.85, with improvements across all field categories and assay types. The largest gains occurred for ontology-constrained fields, where precision increased from 0.36 to 0.92. Our findings show that access to appropriate metadata standards can substantially improve LLM-based standardization of legacy metadata. ARMS improves metadata standardization by giving LLMs runtime access to the authoritative resources that define valid metadata. Representation of metadata standards in machine-actionable form enhances the task of rectifying legacy metadata using LLM technology, especially when those standards can be queried dynamically.

title: StaRPO: Stability-Augmented Reinforcement Policy Optimization
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is effective in enhancing the accuracy of large language models in complex reasoning tasks. Existing RL policy optimization frameworks rely on final-answer correctness as feedback signals and rarely capture the internal logical structure of the reasoning process. Consequently, the models would generate fluent and semantically relevant responses but logically inconsistent, structurally erratic, or redundant. To this end, we propose StaRPO, a stability-augmented reinforcement learning framework that explicitly incorporates reasoning stability into the optimization objective. Our StaRPO decomposes stability into two computable lightweight metrics: the Autocorrelation Function (ACF) to evaluate local step-to-step coherence, and Path Efficiency (PE) to evaluate global goal-directedness of the reasoning trajectory. These stability rewards are combined with task rewards to provide complementary and process-aware feedback. We validate the effectiveness of using ACF and PE rewards by showing their correlation with logic errors on two backbone models. Experiments on four reasoning benchmarks show that StaRPO consistently outperforms compared baselines and can enhance both final-answer accuracy and logical stability.

title: Beyond Reconstruction: Reconstruction-to-Vector Diffusion for Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
summary: While Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection (HAD) excels at identifying sparse targets in complex scenes, existing models remain trapped in a scalar "reconstruction-as-endpoint" paradigm. This reliance on ambiguous scalar residuals consistently triggers sub-pixel anomaly vanishing during spatial downsampling, alongside severe confirmation bias when unpurified anomalies corrupt training weights. In this paper, we propose Reconstruction-to-Vector Diffusion (R2VD), which fundamentally redefines reconstruction as a manifold purification origin to establish a novel residual-guided generative dynamics paradigm. Our framework introduces a four-stage pipeline: (1) a Physical Prior Extraction (PPE) stage that mitigates early confirmation bias via dual-stream statistical guidance; (2) a Guided Manifold Purification (GMP) stage utilizing an OmniContext Autoencoder (OCA) to extract purified residual maps while preserving fragile sub-pixel topologies; (3) a Residual Score Modeling (RSM) stage where a Diffusion Transformer (DiT), guarded by a Physical Spectral Firewall (PSF), effectively isolates cross-spectral leakage; and (4) a Vector Dynamics Inference (VDI) stage that robustly decouples targets from backgrounds by evaluating high-dimensional vector interference patterns instead of conventional scalar errors. Comprehensive evaluations on eight datasets confirm that R2VD establishes a new state-of-the-art, delivering exceptional target detectability and background suppression. The code is available at https://github.com/Bondojijun/R2VD.

title: Phantom Paradoxes: Language Models Treat Unresolved Circular Truth Dependence as Contradiction
comments: v2: major revision with a new title and a confirmatory study. Withdrawn from v1: the attention effective-rank signature and the architecture-invariance claim. Previous title: When Self-Reference Fails to Close: Matrix-Level Dynamics in Large Language Models. 19 pages, 2 figures, 8 tables
summary: Do language models struggle with self-reference itself, or with structures where propagating truth values along references cannot settle a value in finitely many steps? Our results support the latter. In our main test, statements refer to one another's truth in a cycle, yet exactly one consistent assignment exists. Local propagation never settles the queried value, but exhaustive search finds it, so INCONSISTENT (no consistent assignment) is always wrong. We call such misreadings of satisfiable problems phantom paradoxes. Each circular problem has a grounded twin with the same answer but no cycle. To rule out logical difficulty and unfamiliar wording, we added constraint twins (equivalent formulas without talk of truth) and perplexity-matched grounded controls. In confirmatory behavioral tests fixed before any confirmation response, four open models from three families answered INCONSISTENT on average 31.0 percentage points more often on circular problems than on grounded twins, 36.4 more than on constraint twins and 37.1 more than on perplexity-matched controls. In each model, validated layer-wise truth directions, fitted on unrelated arithmetic, recovered the queried value at the question's last token for grounded twins but not for circular problems. Constraint twins, likewise unrecovered, drew INCONSISTENT far less often, so circular truth dependence, not the unrecovered value alone, matters. In a small natural-language bank, self-reference settling in finitely many steps drew INCONSISTENT 23.4 points less often than unsettled self-reference with the same classical solution. Pooled tests did not show the predicted late-layer revision or attention spread. Overall, models treat unresolved circular truth dependence as contradiction. We will release all prompts, outputs and hidden states.

title: UniRec: Bridging the Expressive Gap between Generative and Discriminative Recommendation via Chain-of-Attribute
summary: Generative Recommendation (GR) reframes retrieval and ranking as autoregressive decoding over Semantic IDs (SIDs), unifying the multi-stage pipeline into a single model. Yet a fundamental expressive gap persists: discriminative models score items with direct feature access enabling explicit user-item crossing, whereas GR decodes over compact SID tokens without item-side signal. We formalize this via Bayes' theorem: ranking by p(y|f,u) is equivalent to ranking by p(f|y,u), which factorizes autoregressively over item features, showing that a generative model with full feature access matches its discriminative counterpart, with any practical gap stemming solely from incomplete feature coverage. We propose UniRec with Chain-of-Attribute (CoA) as its core mechanism. CoA prefixes each SID sequence with structured attribute tokens:category, seller, brand, before decoding the SID, recovering the item-side feature crossing that discriminative models exploit. Since items sharing identical attributes cluster in adjacent SID regions, attribute conditioning yields a measurable per-step entropy reduction H(s_k|s<k,a) < H(s_k|s<k), narrowing the search space and stabilizing beam search. We further address two deployment challenges: Capacity-constrained SID introduces exposure-weighted capacity penalties into residual quantization to suppress token collapse and the Matthew effect; Conditional Decoding Context (CDC) combines Task-Conditioned BOS with hash-based Content Summaries to inject scenario signals at each decoding step. A joint RFT and DPO framework aligns the model with business objectives beyond distribution matching. Experiments show UniRec outperforms the strongest baseline by +22.6% HR@50 overall and +15.5% on high-value orders. Deployed on Shopee's e-commerce platform, online A/B tests confirm significant gains in PVCTR (+5.37%), orders (+4.76%), and GMV (+5.60%).

title: Reward Design for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
summary: Physical reasoning over images requires integrating perception, domain knowledge, and multi-step symbolic inference, yet Vision-Language Models (VLMs) fall far short of human performance on physics benchmarks. Reinforcement learning can improve reasoning via reward signals, but it remains unclear whether these signals must come from outside the model or can be derived from the model itself. We compare external rewards, which rely on an outside verifier (rule-based format and answer-correctness checks, or an LLM-judge rubric), with an internal attention-based reward computed from the model's own attention over image regions, requiring no labels or judge. We find that external rewards drive most of the accuracy gains, while preserving more coherent reasoning when rewarded for reasoning tokens. The internal attention-based reward, provides an annotation-free grounding signal that improves spatial-relation reasoning and is complementary to external rewards: adding it to format and accuracy rewards, at no additional annotation cost, improves average accuracy on Molmo~2 while generalizing to out-of-distribution tasks. Our results suggest that internal attention rewards can supplement external supervision and lead to improved physical reasoning.

title: Efficient Thermo-Viscoplastic Analysis Using a Multi-Level hp-Finite Cell Method with Non-Negative Moment Fitting
comments: 40 pages, 30 Figures, 2 Tables Accepted for publication in Finite Elements in Analysis and Design
summary: An extension of the multi-level hp Finite Cell Method is proposed for the simulation of thermoviscoplastic problems with temperature-dependent material behavior. The approach combines hierarchical adaptive refinement with a non-negative moment fitting (NNMF) quadrature scheme for efficient and robust integration of non-linear, history-dependent constitutive models on cut cells. The NNMF formulation yields sparse, positive quadrature rules that significantly reduce the number of integration points while maintaining stability and accuracy. An error-indicator-driven hp-refinement strategy enables localized resolution of strain and thermal gradients during the non-linear solution process. The framework is implemented within a partitioned thermo-mechanical scheme and evaluated on benchmark and application-oriented examples. The results demonstrate improved accuracy and substantial computational savings compared to standard integration approaches.

title: Distributed Optimization with Nesterov Momentum and Finite-Time Quantized Consensus
summary: In modern large-scale networked systems, rapidly solving optimization problems while utilizing communication resources efficiently is critical for addressing complex tasks. In this paper, we consider an unconstrained distributed optimization problem in which information exchange among nodes is governed by a directed communication graph. In our setup we focus on two key challenges. The first is the zigzag phenomenon caused by the objective functions of individual nodes having significantly different curvature along different directions. The second is that the communication channels among nodes are subject to limited bandwidth, which motivates the use of compressed (quantized) messages. To address both challenges simultaneously, we propose QANM, a distributed optimization algorithm that combines Nesterov momentum with a distributed finite-time quantized consensus protocol. Under strong convexity and smoothness assumptions, we show that our proposed algorithm converges linearly to a neighborhood of the optimal solution. Finally, we evaluate QANM on a distributed sensor-fusion problem. With each method's step size tuned separately, QANM exhibits the fastest initial error reduction among the tested methods, including QAGD, Acc-DNGD-SC, and MSDA. Comparisons with QAGD under the same quantized averaging framework illustrate the empirical benefit of momentum, while experiments at two quantization levels demonstrate quantization-dependent error floors.

title: Scaling Human-AI Coding Collaboration Requires a Governable Consensus Layer
summary: Vibe coding turns natural-language intent into working software, but code generation alone does not give humans and agents a shared account of what they are building. As collaboration spans participants, components, and releases, design choices must remain understandable and open to revision. We argue that scaling human and AI coding collaboration requires a governable consensus layer. Agentic Consensus organizes collaboration around a versioned project-state model linking selected intent, structural commitments, executable artifacts, and evidence. Participants can clarify intent before implementation and coordinate proposed changes against commitments that humans can inspect and revise. Bidirectional synchronization connects intended changes to implementation and exposes conflicts or stale evidence as artifacts evolve. We implemented its review workflow in Consensus Control. In a small exploratory human study, 10 participants used the system on projects from their everyday work and reported clearer, faster understanding of agent-submitted changes. A three-condition comparison with the same participants collected 60 responses, with near-ceiling decision scores and measured representation and pipeline costs. Our research agenda asks how shared project state can preserve human understanding and control as agent contributions accumulate.

title: Latent Preference Modeling for Multi-Session Personalized Tool Calling
comments: Under review. 27 pages, 14 figures, 19 tables. v2: revised benchmark construction and extended analysis
summary: Users often omit essential details in their requests to LLM-based agents, resulting in under-specified inputs for tool use. This poses a fundamental challenge for tool-augmented agents, as API execution typically requires complete arguments, highlighting the need for personalized tool calling. To study this problem, we present Multi-Session Personalized Tool Calling (MPT), a benchmark comprising 4,695 instances over 459 multi-session interaction histories that cover three challenges: Preference Recall, Induction, and Transfer. We further propose PRefine, a test-time memory method that maintains the user's latent preference as a textual hypothesis revised through a generate--verify--refine loop. Across five LLMs, existing memory systems often fail to improve on full-history prompting; PRefine outperforms all baselines and alone surpasses it on Preference Transfer. These results indicate that memory for personalized agents must abstract behavior into preferences, rather than simply archive it.

title: Causally-Constrained Probabilistic Forecasting for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
comments: This work is currently under review for possible publication in the IEEE Access journal. All intellectual property rights are retained by IEEE
summary: Anomaly detection in multivariate time series is a central challenge in industrial monitoring, as failures frequently arise from complex temporal dynamics and cross-sensor interactions. While recent deep learning models, including graph neural networks and Transformers, have demonstrated strong empirical performance, most approaches remain primarily correlational and offer limited support for causal interpretation and root-cause localization. This study introduces a causally-constrained probabilistic forecasting framework which is a Causally Guided Transformer (CGT) model for multivariate time-series anomaly detection, integrating an explicit time-lagged causal graph prior with deep sequence modeling. For each target variable, a dedicated forecasting block employs a hard parent mask derived from causal discovery to restrict the main prediction pathway to graph-supported causes, while a latent Gaussian head captures predictive uncertainty. To leverage residual correlational information without compromising the causal representation, a shadow auxiliary path with stop-gradient isolation and a safety-gated blending mechanism is incorporated to suppress non-causal contributions when reliability is low. Anomalies are identified using negative log-likelihood scores with adaptive streaming thresholding, and root-cause variables are determined through per-dimension probabilistic attribution and counterfactual clamping. Experiments on the ASD and SMD benchmarks indicate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art detection performance, with F1-scores of 96.19% on ASD and 95.32% on SMD, and enhances variable-level attribution quality. These findings suggest that causal structural priors can improve both robustness and interpretability in detecting deep anomalies in multivariate sensor systems.
