title: TurboVGGT: Fast Visual Geometry Reconstruction with Adaptive Alternating Attention
summary: Recent feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods, such as visual geometry transformers, have substantially advanced the traditional per-scene optimization paradigm by enabling effective multi-view reconstruction in a single forward pass. However, most existing methods struggle to achieve a balance between reconstruction quality and computational efficiency, which limits their scalability and efficiency. Although some efficient visual geometry transformers have recently emerged, they typically use the same sparsity ratio across layers and frames and lack mechanisms to adaptively learn representative tokens to capture global relationships, leading to suboptimal performance. In this work, we propose TurboVGGT, a novel approach that employs an efficient visual geometry transformer with adaptive alternating attention for fast multi-view 3D reconstruction. Specifically, TurboVGGT employs an end-to-end trainable framework that leverages adaptive sparse global attention guided by adaptive sparsity selection to capture global relationships across frames and uses frame attention to aggregate local details within each frame. In the adaptive sparse global attention, TurboVGGT adaptively learns representative tokens with varying sparsity levels for global geometry modeling, considering that token importance varies across frames, different attention layers operate on tokens at different levels of abstraction, and global dependencies rely on structurally informative regions. Extensive experiments on multiple 3D reconstruction benchmarks demonstrate that TurboVGGT achieves fast multi-view reconstruction while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: GQLA: Group-Query Latent Attention for Hardware-Adaptive Decoding
summary: Decoding efficiency depends on KV-cache traffic, computation, and parallelism. Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) offers absorbed and head-expanded forms, but its head-specific projections limit grouped KV sharing. We introduce Group-Query Latent Attention (GQLA), whose group-shared up-projections preserve a joint latent and enable a shardable expanded cache. The same weights support equivalent MQA-absorb and GQA execution using existing kernels. Roofline analysis relates path preference to GPU compute-to-bandwidth ratio and tensor parallelism (TP): absorption trades traffic for computation and replicates the latent across ranks; GQA shards KV groups. Pretraining with eight query heads per group yields terminal training losses close to MLA's across the tested model scales at matched tokens. TransGQLA converts GQA and MLA checkpoints using calibration data. Without gradient updates, converted DeepSeek-V3.1-Base achieves 77.79% eight-task accuracy versus the source's 77.84%, while WikiText-2 perplexity rises from 3.21 to 6.05. On eight H20-3e GPUs, its GQA path improves output throughput over MQA-absorb by 22.42--34.97% at matched resident batches across 8K--64K inputs. Its smaller per-rank cache permits larger batches, giving 50.07% in a separate capacity-tuned comparison. These results support multiple execution paths as an architectural means of adapting decoding to hardware and parallelism.

title: Njord: A Probabilistic Graph Neural Network for Ensemble Ocean Forecasting
comments: NeurIPS 2026. Code is available at https://github.com/deinal/njord
summary: Ocean dynamics are inherently chaotic, yet existing machine learning ocean models produce only deterministic forecasts. We introduce Njord, a probabilistic data-driven model for ocean forecasting, applicable to both global and regional domains. Njord combines a deep latent variable framework with a graph neural network architecture, enabling sampling each forecast step in a single forward pass. We apply Njord globally at 0.25° resolution and regionally to the Baltic Sea at 2 km resolution. To scale to these large ocean grids we introduce K-means cluster meshes that adapt to irregular sea surface geometry. Experiments demonstrate strong performance on both domains compared to deterministic machine learning baselines, while also providing uncertainty estimates from the sampled ensemble forecasts. On the global OceanBench benchmark, Njord achieves the lowest errors on average across upper-ocean variables when evaluated against real-world observations, with the largest improvements in surface temperature prediction.
comment: NeurIPS 2026. Code is available at https://github.com/deinal/njord

title: Vectorized Generalized Nearest Neighbor Decoding for In-block Memory Channel
summary: This work extends the generalized nearest neighbor decoding (GNND), originally developed as a receiver architecture for memoryless channels, to a vectorized GNND (Vec-GNND) suitable for in-block memory (IBM) channels. Leveraging the generalized mutual information (GMI) as an operational lower bound on the mismatch capacity, an analytical characterization of the optimal Vec-GNND is obtained for general IBM channels with Gaussian codebooks. The formalism further provides closed-form optimality conditions and achievable GMIs for restricted variants of the receiver architecture. Furthermore, we formulate a GMI-based joint design viewpoint for Gaussian codebook covariance and decoding metrics. Since the metric optimization admits a closed-form solution for each fixed covariance, the joint design is reduced to an input-covariance optimization problem; for the diagonal covariance family, we derive first-order self-consistent optimality conditions. Numerical evaluations on block noncoherent AWGN and phase-noise channels demonstrate consistent GMI gains over conventional scaling-based GNND schemes, suggesting potential performance advantages of Vec-GNNDR in practical communication systems.

title: When and Why Adversarial Training Improves PINNs: A Neural Tangent Kernel Perspective
summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are powerful surrogates for differential equations but are notoriously difficult to train due to spectral bias, stiffness, and poor accuracy on high-frequency or multiscale solutions. Adversarial training based on generative adversarial networks (GANs) has recently gained surprisingly strong empirical results in improving training, but the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. To this end, we propose a new analysis framework for adversarially trained PINNs, based on the key observation of how the discriminator in GANs can influence the training dynamics of PINNs. The framework first provides a much needed theoretical grounding to why and when adversarial training is effective in PINNs, then presents a unified analysis of GANs variants in such training, and finally leads to a new, practical, efficient training algorithm for PINNs. Empirical results demonstrate that our method can significantly reduce the pathology of PINNs training, thereby providing better models with superior performances, often several magnitudes more accurate than alternative methods.

title: A unification of graded and substructural logics
summary: Type systems which account for resource sensitive computations can generally be split into two styles: First, substructural logics such as Linear Logic which seek to restrict weakening and contraction and reintroduce them in a controlled manner; And second, graded systems which allow weakening and contraction by default, but track the use of variables quantitatively in some algebraic structure -- usually a semiring. We present GRASS (Graded and substructural), a type system which incorporates mechanisms from both of these approaches, thus allowing maximally flexible control over variable usage. Furthermore, GRASS allows grades from an arbitrary collection of grade algebras to coexist in the same system, thus allowing different variables to be controlled with respect to different notions of resource within the same program. We develop the categorical semantics of GRASS, and find that, on the level of categorical semantics, it subsumes multiple established systems such as LNL, Adjoint Logic, and mGL.

title: OmniSelect: Dynamic Modality-Aware Token Compression for Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Models
summary: Omnimodal large language models (OmniLLMs) have recently gained increasing attention for unified audio-video understanding. However, processing long multimodal token sequences introduces substantial computational overhead, making efficient token compression crucial. Existing methods typically rely on fixed, modality-specific guidance, which fails to account for the varying importance of modalities across different queries. To address this limitation, we propose $\textbf{OmniSelect}$, a training-free, modality-adaptive token pruning framework that dynamically selects appropriate compression strategies for multimodal inputs. Specifically, we leverage a lightweight AudioCLIP model to estimate cross-modal relevance and categorize each input into three pruning regimes: Audio-Centric, Video-Centric, and Uniform pruning. Based on these relevance scores, OmniSelect further performs fine-grained token pruning within each temporal group, adaptively allocating pruning ratios to preserve informative tokens across modalities. By explicitly modeling modality preference and enabling dynamic strategy selection, OmniSelect effectively avoids the pitfalls of one-size-fits-all compression. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves efficient multimodal token reduction while maintaining strong performance, without requiring any additional training.

title: How Far Are We From True Auto-Research?
summary: Recent auto-research systems can produce complete papers, but feasibility is not the same as quality, and the field still lacks a systematic study of how good agent-generated papers actually are. We introduce ResearchArena, a minimal scaffold that lets off-the-shelf agents (Claude Code using Opus 4.6, Codex using GPT-5.4, and Kimi Code using K2.5) carry out the full research loop themselves (ideation, experimentation, paper writing, self-refinement) under only lightweight guidance. Across 13 computer science seeds and 3 trials per agent-domain pair, ResearchArena yields 117 agent-generated papers, each evaluated under three complementary lenses: a manuscript-only reviewer (SAR), an artifact-aware peer review (PR) in which agents inspect the workspace alongside the manuscript, and an human conducted meta-review. Under SAR alone the picture is optimistic: Claude Code obtains the highest score, outperforms Analemma's FARS, and matches the weighted-average human ICLR 2025 submission, suggesting that minimally scaffolded agents can produce papers that look competitive on manuscript-only review. Manual inspection, however, reveals this picture is overstated: SAR scores are poorly aligned with its actual acceptance decisions and reward plausible framing without verifying experimental substance. Under artifact-aware PR scores drop sharply, and manual auditing identifies experimental rigor as the major bottleneck, decomposing into three failure modes (fabricated results, underpowered experiments, and plan/execution mismatch) that are highly agent-dependent: Codex 5%/8% paper-vs-artifact mismatch / fabricated references versus Kimi Code 77%/72%, a $\sim$15$\times$ spread that tracks distinct research personas the agents develop. None of the 117 agent-generated papers reaches the acceptance bar of a top-tier venue. This suggests that we are still gapped from the true auto-research.

title: BrainDyn: A Sheaf Neural ODE for Forecasting and Generating Brain Dynamics
summary: Brain activity unfolds as coordinated patterns across regions over time, and modeling these dynamics is a central goal in computational neuroscience. Because activity is distributed over connected brain regions, it is naturally represented on a graph whose nodes are brain regions or recording electrodes and whose edges capture relationships between these nodes, with message-passing modeling regional communication. However, standard message-passing networks place every node in a single shared feature space and typically aggregate messages from neighbors by scalar summation, which does not align with neurobiological evidence of brain communication. In order to model the heterogeneous nature of the brain, we introduce BrainDyn, a graph ordinary differential equation (ODE) network built on a cellular sheaf with dynamic restriction maps, recomputed from the forecasting context window rather than fixed once, mediating region-to-region communication through learned linear transformations that drive the time evolution of neural activity. We evaluate BrainDyn on resting-state fMRI, EEG, and simulated activity from the NEST simulator. Across these modalities, we test multi-region forecasting and autoregressive generation of brain transients, and, using NEST, prediction of altered transients following controlled perturbations. BrainDyn outperforms competing models across modalities, while analysis of the learned features shows that they are expressive, interpretable, and biologically aligned.

title: MOCHA: Multi-Objective Chebyshev Annealing for Agent Skill Optimization
summary: LLM agents organize behavior through skills -- structured natural-language specifications that govern how an agent reasons, retrieves, and responds. Unlike monolithic prompts, skills are multi-field artifacts with platform limits: descriptions are indexed for routing, instruction bodies are loaded into a shared context window, and every extra line costs the agent context it could spend elsewhere. Skill optimization is therefore inherently multi-objective: a skill should be accurate and economical at once. Existing prompt optimizers collapse these goals into a single score, and we find that this makes them stall: in most of their runs, 1000 rollouts yield zero progress over the seed skill. We introduce MOCHA (Multi-Objective CHebyshev Annealing), which selects skills to improve by Chebyshev scalarization and accepts improvements that expand the Pareto front, annealing from exploration to exploitation. Chebyshev scalarization scores a skill by its largest weighted shortfall from a perfect skill; with random weights, it can select any skill on the Pareto front for improvement, including trade-offs that an average would never favor. Across six diverse skills and two models, MOCHA escapes the seed in nearly every run, achieving 7.9% higher mean accuracy than the strongest baseline (up to 23.7% on DebugBench with GPT 5.5 and 14.9% on FEVER with Claude Haiku 4.5) while discovering Pareto fronts with the highest hypervolume and nearly twice as many Pareto-optimal skills.

title: OScaR: The Occam's Razor for Extreme KV Cache Quantization in LLMs and Beyond
summary: The rapid advancement toward long-context reasoning and multi-modal intelligence has made the memory footprint of the Key-Value (KV) cache a dominant memory bottleneck for efficient deployment. While the established per-channel quantization effectively accommodates intrinsic channel-wise outliers in Key tensors, its efficacy diminishes under extreme compression. In this work, we revisit the inherent limitations of the per-channel quantization paradigm from both empirical and theoretical perspectives. Our analysis identifies Token Norm Imbalance (TNI) as the primary bottleneck to quantization fidelity. We demonstrate that TNI systematically amplifies errors when shared quantization parameters are required to span token groups exhibiting substantial norm disparities. Instead of relying on intricate quantization pipelines (e.g., TurboQuant), we propose OScaR (Omni-Scaled Canalized Rotation), an accurate and lightweight KV cache compression framework for X-LLMs (i.e., text-only, multi-modal, and omni-modal LLMs). Advancing the per-channel paradigm, OScaR employs Canalized Rotation followed by Omni-Token Scaling to mitigate TNI-induced sequence-dimensional variance both effectively and efficiently, further supported by our optimized system design and CUDA kernels. Extensive evaluations across X-LLMs show that OScaR consistently outperforms existing methods and achieves near-lossless performance under INT2 quantization, establishing it as a robust, low-complexity, and universal framework that defines a new Pareto front. Compared with the BF16 FlashDecoding-v2 baseline, our OScaR implementation achieves a notable up to 3.0x speedup in decoding, reduces memory footprint by 5.3x, and increases throughput by 4.1x. The code for OScaR is publicly available at https://github.com/ZunhaiSu/OScaR-KV-Quant.

title: Why Latent Actions Fail, and How to Prevent It
summary: Latent action models (LAMs) aim to learn action-like representations from unlabeled videos by compressing frame-to-frame changes. The frames of in-the-wild videos, however, contain not only the agent's own state but exogenous state such as background clutter. Since the exogenous state introduces changes unrelated to actions, it hinders reliable latent action learning. This paper investigates this problem analytically by extending a linear LAM framework to explicitly model exogenous state. Our analysis reveals two insights: (1) minimizing the standard reconstruction objective produces latent actions that encode exogenous information from future observation; and (2) learning in a representation space that focuses on endogenous components is a key to mitigating the interference of noise. We further show that previously proposed auxiliary objectives, such as action-supervision, provably encourage latent actions to be consistent across exogenous states. These findings are validated through experiments on both linear and nonlinear LAMs, providing a unified theoretical analysis of how exogenous state hinders latent action learning and why common remedies work.

title: Capability $\neq$ Interpretability: Human Interpretability of Vision Foundation Models
summary: How interpretable are the features of leading vision models? The question is increasingly pressing as these models move from research benchmarks into high-stakes deployments, yet existing methods cannot answer it reliably. We address this gap with a framework for measuring and comparing the human interpretability of vision models, built around two complementary psychophysics protocols: (1) localizability---can an observer predict where a feature fires on a novel image?---and (2) semanticity---can an observer accurately describe what the feature represents? Features are recovered via sparse autoencoders, and a chance-anchored scoring function places every model on a common scale. Applying the framework to six vision transformers---two supervised ViTs and four foundation models (DINOv2, DINOv3, CLIP, SigLIP)---we collected more than $15{,}000$ behavioral responses, of which we analyzed $13{,}400$ responses from the $377$ participants who passed our pre-specified quality checks. We find that foundation models are consistently $less$ interpretable than their size-matched supervised counterparts, and the gap is not a capability tradeoff: interpretability does not correlate with downstream task performance on any benchmark we examine. What does correlate is the locality of a feature's activations and coarse-grained semantic alignment with humans---models with focal activations and representations that reflect the world's broad categorical structure tend to produce more interpretable features. The two protocols yield strongly correlated rankings and share the same predictors, establishing interpretability as an independent, measurable dimension of representation quality---and, surprisingly, one on which the foundation models we tested fall below their size-matched supervised baseline. Capability alone cannot close that gap, but locality and coarse-grained alignment might.

title: When Reasoning Supervision Hurts: TTCW-Based Long-Form Literary Review Generation
summary: Automatic evaluation of long-form literary writing remains challenging, particularly for creativity-related dimensions such as originality and flexibility. We address the lack of large-scale supervision for structured Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW)-based evaluation by constructing a dataset of 263{,}911 long-form stories, each paired with scalar scores and meta-synthesised review comments across 14 TTCW-based dimensions. Using this dataset, we study whether reviewer-style reasoning traces improve structured literary review generation across Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Nemotron-8B. Across all three models, no-trace supervision yields higher score imitation fidelity and near-complete report generation, whereas trace supervision reduces completion to $85.9$--$90.9\%$. Failure analysis shows that $88.6\%$ of failed reasoning generations contain semantic repetition loops inside the trace. These loops concentrate in particular story--criterion interactions and progressively harden after onset, while comparable repetition is rare in the supervision data. Our results suggest that, for long-form tasks requiring strictly structured outputs, explicit reasoning traces can introduce generation instability that outweighs their overall benefit.

title: DeTox-Fed: Detecting Toxic Conversations in the Fediverse with Federated Graph Neural Networks
comments: This revised version substantially extends the experimental evaluation by incorporating a Mastodon dataset, additional LLM models (both lightweight and top-tier), and including GraphNLI as an experimental baseline
summary: The rise of decentralized social networks (DSNs), and in particular the rapid uptake of the Fediverse (e.g., Pleroma, Mastodon, Lemmygrad), introduces new challenges in content moderation. Independent instances host their own data, follow different moderation policies, and often observe only partial views of conversations. We present DeTox-Fed, a federated graph-learning framework for detecting toxic conversations in DSNs without requiring instances to share raw conversations or moderation labels. Each instance constructs a local conversation graph, where nodes represent conversation trees and edges capture shared user participation across conversations. A Graph Neural Network is then trained in a federated learning setup, allowing instances to collaboratively learn a toxicity classifier while preserving data locality. Unlike text-only moderation approaches, DeTox-Fed combines conversational structure, user-interaction patterns, conversation-level statistics, and aggregate sentiment signals. We evaluate the framework on a large Pleroma conversation dataset and a second one from Mastodon, showing that it achieves stable toxic conversation detection under limited local labels, partial client participation, and varying moderation thresholds. Our results indicate that federated graph-based moderation is a promising direction for semi-automated moderation in decentralized social networks.
comment: This revised version substantially extends the experimental evaluation by incorporating a Mastodon dataset, additional LLM models (both lightweight and top-tier), and including GraphNLI as an experimental baseline

title: A finite-element-inspired bipartite graph learned simulator for manufacturability assessment in large-deformation sheet forming
summary: Explicit dynamic finite element (FE) simulations are widely used for large-deformation analysis but remain expensive for design-space exploration. In explicit FE analysis, nodal kinematics and element-level deformation measures evolve through a coupled node-element update process. An FE-inspired learned simulator can preserve this structure and learn nodal kinematics and elemental deformation on their native domains. Nodal displacement describes geometry evolution, while elemental thinning identifies local deformation and critical regions. Feeding both outputs back during rollout allows each field to inform subsequent updates of the other. This work proposes CAtt-BiGNN, a cross-attention-based bipartite graph neural network for coupled nodal-elemental learning. The bipartite graph encodes FE-guided state organisation and information flow without imposing equilibrium or constitutive constraints. Mesh nodes and elements are represented as distinct graph entities connected by directed node-element edges, enabling prediction of nodal displacement increments and elemental deformation on their native domains. An edge-aware cross-attention processor dynamically updates edge representations and weights messages using the receiving state and evolving local relations. For larger graphs, CAtt-BiUGNN uses separate nodal and elemental downsampling and upsampling to enhance long-range propagation while preserving their interaction across graph levels. The method is evaluated on dome-shaped cold-forming and corner-shaped hot-forming benchmarks. Comparisons with node-centred baselines, an FE-inspired hypergraph model, a Physics-Attention-based neural operator, a graph Transformer, and attention ablations show improved joint accuracy in nodal displacement and elemental thinning prediction during autoregressive rollout.

title: A Simple Plug-in for Improving Eviction-Based KV Cache Compression
summary: KV cache growth is a major bottleneck for long-context inference in large language models. Existing methods are often dominated by binary eviction or representation approximation, which may underutilize tokens that are not critical for exact retention but are still reconstructable. We present VECTOR, a plug-and-play augmentation for eviction-based pipelines that introduces three-way token routing: retention, approximation, and eviction. VECTOR combines an importance signal from the base scorer with a reconstructability signal from an offline-calibrated regression-based value estimation. By leveraging reconstructability, VECTOR recovers useful value information that would otherwise be irreversibly lost under binary eviction, while preserving key vectors for attention routing stability. On LongBench, RULER with contexts up to 128K tokens, and multi-turn SCBench, VECTOR yields significant gains over its base eviction methods under high compression. At a 90% compression ratio, SnapKV augmented with VECTOR outperforms six competing compression methods, including D2O and RocketKV, on all three evaluated models. Since VECTOR makes all routing decisions at prefill, decoding runs on a standard compressed cache with no measurable overhead.

title: Structured Masked Diffusion for Shared-Codebook Unsourced Random Access Decoding
comments: 57 pages. NeurIPS 2026 camera-ready version; clarified shared-codebook URA scope, expanded evaluation, and updated references
summary: In shared-codebook unsourced random access (URA), a receiver must recover an unordered set of messages from simultaneous transmissions. Its outer decoder assembles ambiguous slot-wise evidence into distinct codewords while enforcing parity constraints. We propose CIDER, a learned outer decoder that combines masked-diffusion refinement with cross-row demixing and parity-aware propagation on the code's Tanner graph. At higher per-bin loads, quality-guided remasking selectively re-decodes low-confidence rows. On the evaluated GF(64) LDPC codes at $K=2$, CIDER has lower measured symbol and codeword error rates than SIC-BP and FFT-BP at all four code lengths. In same-GPU decoder-only measurements, the deployed mixed-precision implementation is $8.2\times$ to $167\times$ faster than our optimized FFT-BP implementation across those lengths. We also evaluate higher loads, estimated user counts, and detector mismatch. Code is available at https://github.com/jiyunyoung/CIDER/tree/neurips-2026.
comment: 57 pages. NeurIPS 2026 camera-ready version; clarified shared-codebook URA scope, expanded evaluation, and updated references

title: C-MIG: Multi-view Information Gain-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Clinical Diagnosis Reasoning
summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) trained with reinforcement learning (RL) is a promising way to ground large language models in medical evidence for clinical diagnosis. However, existing RAG-RL methods face two problems: (1) their process reward is largely singleview, as most methods inherited from opendomain multi-hop QA reward only the quality of the retrieved information; (2) assigning a reliable process reward is hard, as hard matching gives zero to clinically correct but non-verbatim steps such as "Allergic Sinusitis" versus "Allergic Rhinitis", and the alternative of strong-teacher guiding is bounded by the teacher's own medical competence. To address these issues, we propose C-MIG, a Multiview Information Gain-based framework for Clinical diagnosis. We identify two complementary and crucial intermediate steps in clinical diagnosis: what to retrieve and how to refine. We reward both by the information gain each brings, measured as the increase in the predicted likelihood of the ground-truth answer under a base, frozen reference model. The frozen scorer yields a stable and reproducible reward that needs no extra reward model or teacher. Experiments on four medical benchmarks show that C-MIG outperforms RAGRL baselines in and out of domain and stays competitive with far larger medical-specialist and general-purpose LLMs, at only about 3.4% training overhead and no inference-time cost.

title: ConRAG: Consensus-Driven Evidence Flow for Multi-Hop Question Answering
summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing large language models (LLMs) on multi-hop question answering (QA), which requires reasoning over evidence from multiple documents. However, current multi-hop RAG approaches still struggle with evidence selection and information transfer, i.e., retrieving irrelevant passages or failing to pass intermediate information to subsequent reasoning steps, thereby hindering coherent multi-hop reasoning. To this end, we propose ConRAG, a consensus-driven evidence flow framework that effectively boosts LLM performance on complex multi-hop QA. In short, the core of ConRAG is to select relevant evidence via consensus-driven multi-view ranking, and leverage a slot-based mechanism to transfer intermediate information between dependent reasoning steps. Extensive experiments across three multi-hop QA benchmarks show that ConRAG surpasses the baselines by a clear margin. Encouragingly, on Gemma-4-31B-it, ConRAG outperforms the strongest baseline by 5.8 points in average score, while reducing total end-to-end runtime and token consumption by 75.9% and 67.3%, respectively.

title: Unification and Optimization of Robust Supervised Learning
summary: Robust learning methods such as distributionally robust optimization, vicinal risk minimization, Mixup, and label smoothing address different sources of uncertainty, including distribution shift, finite-sample effects, and label uncertainty. In practice, however, several such sources may occur simultaneously, and it remains unclear which robust method or combination of methods to use. We introduce a unified framework that organizes a broad class of robustness methods along explicit design axes and makes their relations and combinations explicit within a shared formulation. Within this framework, we analyze how robustness methods interact: some are redundant under particular modeling assumptions, whereas others yield genuinely distinct solution families, and these relationships can change with the model class or loss. We further derive a tractable training procedure that exposes the design choices and their strengths as tunable hyperparameters. Across vision and reward-modeling tasks, the preferred robustness method depends on the task, target metric, and validation data, while suitably selected combinations often outperform the best single method.

title: T2J-BENCH: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Execution-Grounded PyTorch-to-JAX Repository Migration
summary: Migrating a machine-learning codebase across frameworks--for example from PyTorch to JAX--is a routine but costly engineering task that is fundamentally cross-paradigm: eager, stateful, object-oriented modules must be rewritten as pure, jittable functions over an explicit parameter pytree. We ask whether coding agents can perform such whole-repository migrations correctly, and argue that existing code benchmarks, which grade unit-test pass rates or surface-level similarity to a reference translation, cannot answer this: they neither require the migrated system to \emph{behave} the same nor prevent a JAX reimplementation from faking equivalence by secretly importing PyTorch itself. We introduce T2J-BENCH, a benchmark of 63 whole-repository PyTorch-to-JAX migration tasks spanning 18 model families across both training and serving, where torch-free checkpoint conversion is itself part of the deliverable. T2J-BENCH grades execution-grounded functional equivalence: each candidate is run inside a separate, torch-free, offline verifier and scored against references frozen from the PyTorch original, under a hard independence gate and a continuous, threshold-free reward. Across twenty off-the-shelf agent--model configurations, the strongest recovers only 0.676 of the reward against a 0.980 oracle, with substantial numeric and behavioral divergence despite high spec pass rates. Finally, we contribute TWINHARNESS, a reference-grounded agent harness that turns the agent's executable PyTorch source into legitimate self-verification feedback; applied to an opus-5 agent it raises the reward from 0.649 to 0.723--the highest of any configuration--using only task-visible resources.

title: Masked Diffusion Vision-Language Models for Temporal Action Localization
summary:
Temporal action localization (TAL) requires recognizing the target event and localizing its start and end times precisely in untrimmed videos. Recent vision-language formulations improve semantic reasoning and support language-conditioned outputs, but their autoregressive decoders still generate tokens from left to right, preventing later semantic evidence from revising earlier timestamp predictions.
  We adapt masked diffusion vision-language models (MDVLMs) to TAL so that semantic tokens and boundary tokens remain editable throughout iterative denoising with bidirectional attention, allowing temporal boundaries and semantic content to be refined jointly.
  Direct adaptation, however, creates two TAL-specific mismatches: standard masked diffusion training corrupts all positions uniformly at random, but the time tokens are more reliable when enough semantic context is available; and token-level cross-entropy does not reflect temporal IoU. To address these mismatches, we introduce a Planned Training Objective that uses boundary-aware masking and step-weighted reconstruction to rehearse the late recovery of time tokens, together with a Step-Level IoU Reward that provides overlap-aware supervision during denoising. A standard sequence-level cross-entropy term provides the base reconstruction signal.
  Experiments on ActivityNet-RTL, ActivityNet-1.3, and THUMOS-14 show that MDVLM-TAL improves both temporal reasoning and boundary localization over autoregressive vision-language baselines, with especially strong gains under stricter temporal IoU criteria. The source code is available at https://github.com/ycwfs/MDVLM-TAL .

title: Redundant or Necessary? A Benchmark for Detecting Redundant Steps in Agent Trajectories
summary: Computation cost is a critical challenge for LLM agent systems, as their long-horizon trajectories continuously accumulate computational overhead. While existing studies focus on improving the overall efficiency of agent systems, the efficiency of individual steps remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose and formulate a new research problem: \textbf{redundant step detection}, aiming to detect these steps that consume substantial computational resources while contributing little or nothing to task completion. To support this initiative, we introduce \textbf{RedundancyBench}, a new benchmark that contains 1,920 trajectories collected from 6 different LLMs with 3,613 step-level annotations. Using RedundancyBench, we develop and evaluate 6 frontier LLMs and Jev as redundant step detectors, summarizing their strengths and limitations. Our experiments reveal that the redundant step detection is still challenging even for SOTA models, such as Claude-Opus-5, particularly without prior information. Code and dataset in this paper are both available in https://anonymous.4open.science/r/RedundancyBench-E0CB.

AI.title_translation: 冗余还是必要？一个用于检测智能体轨迹中冗余步骤的基准
AI.tldr: 本文提出了冗余步骤检测这一新问题，并引入了RedundancyBench基准来评估LLM作为冗余步骤检测器。实验表明，即使是SOTA模型，冗余步骤检测仍然具有挑战性。
AI.motivation: LLM智能体系统的计算成本是一个关键挑战，其长期的轨迹会持续累积计算开销。现有研究主要关注提高智能体系统的整体效率，而单个步骤的效率在很大程度上仍未被探索。
AI.method: 本文提出并制定了冗余步骤检测这一新研究问题，旨在检测那些消耗大量计算资源但对任务完成贡献甚微或没有贡献的步骤。为了支持这项工作，本文引入了RedundancyBench，这是一个包含1,920条轨迹的新基准，这些轨迹来自6种不同的LLM，并带有3,613个步骤级别的标注。使用RedundancyBench，本文开发并评估了6个前沿LLM和Jev作为冗余步骤检测器。
AI.result: 实验表明，即使是SOTA模型，如Claude-Opus-5，冗余步骤检测仍然具有挑战性，尤其是在没有先验信息的情况下。
AI.conclusion: 冗余步骤检测是一个具有挑战性的问题，即使对于最先进的模型也是如此，这表明该领域需要进一步的研究和改进。
AI.translation: 计算成本是大型语言模型（LLM）智能体系统面临的一个关键挑战，因为其长期的轨迹会持续积累计算开销。虽然现有研究主要关注提高智能体系统的整体效率，但单个步骤的效率在很大程度上仍未被探索。在本文中，我们提出并制定了一个新的研究问题：**冗余步骤检测**，旨在检测那些消耗大量计算资源但对任务完成贡献甚微或没有贡献的步骤。为了支持这项倡议，我们引入了**RedundancyBench**，这是一个新的基准，包含从6个不同LLM收集的1,920条轨迹，并带有3,613个步骤级别的标注。使用RedundancyBench，我们开发并评估了6个前沿LLM和Jev作为冗余步骤检测器，总结了它们的优势和局限性。我们的实验表明，即使对于SOTA模型，如Claude-Opus-5，冗余步骤检测仍然具有挑战性，尤其是在没有先验信息的情况下。本文的代码和数据集均可在https://anonymous.4open.science/r/RedundancyBench-E0CB获取。
AI.summary: 本文针对LLM智能体系统高计算成本的问题，提出了一个新颖的研究方向——冗余步骤检测。研究旨在识别智能体轨迹中那些资源消耗大但对任务贡献小的步骤。为此，作者构建了RedundancyBench，一个包含多LLM轨迹和详细步骤标注的基准数据集。通过在此基准上评估多个先进LLM作为检测器，研究发现冗余步骤检测即使对最先进的模型来说仍是一项艰巨的任务，尤其是在缺乏先验信息的情况下。
AI.keywords: LLM智能体, 冗余步骤检测, 计算效率, RedundancyBench, 基准测试
AI.comments: 本文的创新之处在于首次明确提出并系统性地研究了LLM智能体轨迹中的“冗余步骤检测”问题，并构建了一个新的、大规模的基准数据集RedundancyBench。这对于解决LLM智能体系统的计算效率瓶颈具有重要意义。然而，实验结果也揭示了当前SOTA模型在该任务上的局限性，表明该领域仍有很大的研究空间和改进潜力。

title: Subspace-Decomposed JEPAs: Disentangling Progression and Content in Latent World Models
comments: Rewritten presentation, corrected method description, new figures, updated related work
summary: World models used for planning learn to predict how a scene evolves, yet they rarely hold a global view of how far a task has progressed. We argue that such a view should be part of the representation, and that it can be compact: describing a scene takes many dimensions, but where the scene stands on its way to the goal can be summarised by only a few. We propose SD-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive world model whose latent is split into a small progression subspace and a large content subspace. A temporal triplet loss keeps consecutive frames of a trajectory close in the progression coordinates and separates different trajectories, while a distributional regulariser keeps the content coordinates from collapsing. On four control benchmarks, the model plans as well as the same architecture without the split. In return, its latent becomes easier to read. A few percent of its dimensions are enough to predict progress within an episode, and the angle they form follows the task, moves backward when the agent backtracks and changes fastest around events such as grasps and releases. Surprise also becomes anchored in the trajectory: when the scene changes mid-episode, the angle spikes and then relocalizes on a new part of the progression, anchoring surprise in the agent's own map of the task.
comment: Rewritten presentation, corrected method description, new figures, updated related work

AI.title_translation: 子空间分解的JEPA：在潜在世界模型中解耦进程与内容
AI.tldr: 本文提出SD-JEPA，一种将世界模型的潜在空间分解为进程子空间和内容子空间的方法。这种方法在规划性能上与传统模型相当，但其潜在表示更易于解读，能有效预测任务进展，并锚定意外事件。
AI.motivation: 现有的世界模型在规划时能预测场景演变，但缺乏对任务进展的全局视图。本文认为这种视图应是表示的一部分，且可以紧凑地由少量维度概括。
AI.method: 提出SD-JEPA，一个联合嵌入预测世界模型。其潜在空间被分解为小的进程子空间和大的内容子空间。使用时间三元组损失使轨迹中连续帧在进程坐标中保持接近并分离不同轨迹，同时使用分布正则化器防止内容坐标崩溃。
AI.result: 在四个控制基准上，SD-JEPA的规划性能与未分解的相同架构相当。其潜在表示更易于解读，少量维度足以预测 эпизод 内的进展，其形成的“角度”遵循任务进程，在智能体回溯时反向移动，并在抓取和释放等事件发生时变化最快。意外事件也被锚定在轨迹中：场景在 эпизод 中途变化时，角度会急剧上升，然后重新定位到进程的新部分。
AI.conclusion: 通过将潜在空间分解为进程和内容子空间，SD-JEPA在保持规划性能的同时，显著提高了潜在表示的可读性和对任务进展及意外事件的感知能力。
AI.translation: 用于规划的世界模型学习预测场景如何演变，但它们很少能对任务进展到何种程度有一个全局的视图。我们认为这样的视图应该是表示的一部分，并且可以是紧凑的：描述一个场景需要许多维度，但场景在实现目标的过程中所处的位置可以用少量维度来概括。我们提出了SD-JEPA，一个联合嵌入预测世界模型，其潜在空间被分解为一个小的进程子空间和一个大的内容子空间。时间三元组损失使轨迹中连续帧在进程坐标中保持接近并分离不同轨迹，同时分布正则化器防止内容坐标崩溃。在四个控制基准上，该模型的规划性能与没有这种分解的相同架构相当。作为回报，其潜在表示变得更容易阅读。其少量维度足以预测 эпизод 内的进展，它们形成的角度遵循任务，在智能体回溯时反向移动，并在抓取和释放等事件（如抓取和释放）发生时变化最快。意外事件也因此被锚定在轨迹中：当场景在 эпизод 中途变化时，角度会急剧上升，然后重新定位到进程的新部分，将意外锚定在智能体自己的任务地图中。
AI.summary: 本文提出了SD-JEPA，一种新的联合嵌入预测世界模型，旨在解决传统世界模型缺乏对任务进展全局视图的问题。SD-JEPA将其潜在空间分解为进程子空间和内容子空间，通过特定的损失函数进行训练。实验表明，该模型在保持规划性能的同时，使潜在表示更易于理解和解读，能够有效预测任务进展，并对意外事件进行定位，从而提供更清晰的任务状态感知。
AI.keywords: 世界模型, 潜在空间, 进程分解, SD-JEPA, 任务进展
AI.comments: 该论文的创新点在于提出了将世界模型的潜在空间分解为进程和内容子空间，这使得模型能够更清晰地理解和表示任务的进展。这种分解不仅提高了潜在表示的可读性，还在不影响规划性能的前提下，为智能体提供了更强的任务感知能力，尤其是在处理意外事件时。这对于开发更智能、更具解释性的AI系统具有重要意义。

title: Fake Plastic Voters: When Political Parties Can Use AI-Simulated Focus Groups
summary: Political parties strive to understand their electorates, and focus groups are a vital tool in these efforts. AI-enhanced simulation technologies (AESTs) enable synthetic focus groups in a fraction of the time (and cost), raising the question of when and how such simulated evidence can be used in campaign research. This paper develops a decision matrix to help party strategists match research needs to appropriate simulation technologies and to identify when to escalate to hybrid or fully human focus groups. The matrix combines three dimensions: strategic purpose, deployment risk, and empirical grounding of the simulation tool. Strategic purpose is the decisive dimension, as it determines what kind of evidence the focus group is meant to produce: observing how political meanings and identities emerge through interaction (Mode 1) or testing and refining campaign messages (Mode 2). The matrix shows that, given documented failure modes such as sycophancy, persona drift, and the suppression of minority viewpoints, AESTs cannot replace human interaction in Mode 1 at any risk level. Within Mode 2, suitability depends instead on deployment risk and on the empirical grounding. Yet even here, we caution that routine reliance on AESTs may erode the qualitative craft on which sound judgment depends.

AI.title_translation: 虚假塑料选民：政党何时能使用AI模拟焦点小组
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一个三维决策矩阵，探讨了政党在竞选研究中使用AI模拟焦点小组的适用场景、风险及局限性，警告AI无法完全替代人类焦点小组且可能侵蚀定性研究判断力。
AI.motivation: 随着人工智能增强模拟技术（AESTs）的出现，政党能够以极低的时间和成本进行合成焦点小组研究，这引发了关于何时以及如何将此类模拟证据应用于竞选研究的问题。
AI.method: 开发了一个三维决策矩阵，将战略目的、部署风险和模拟工具的经验基础相结合，用以匹配研究需求与适当的模拟技术，并判断何时需要转向混合或全人类焦点小组。
AI.result: 研究表明，由于存在谄媚、角色漂移和抑制少数观点等故障模式，AESTs在探索政治意义和身份涌现的场景中无法在任何风险水平下替代人类交互；在测试和完善竞选消息的场景中，其适用性则取决于部署风险和经验基础。
AI.conclusion: 尽管AI模拟焦点小组能节省时间和成本，但由于其存在谄媚、角色漂移和抑制少数观点等缺陷，不能完全替代人类交互。政党策略师应根据战略目的、部署风险和经验基础谨慎使用AESTs，避免盲目依赖。
AI.translation: 政党致力于理解其选民，而焦点小组是实现这一努力的重要工具。人工智能增强模拟技术（AESTs）能够在极短的时间（和成本）内实现合成焦点小组，这引发了关于何时以及如何在竞选研究中使用此类模拟证据的问题。本文开发了一个决策矩阵，以帮助政党策略师将研究需求与适当的模拟技术相匹配，并识别何时升级为混合或全人类焦点小组。该矩阵结合了三个维度：战略目的、部署风险和模拟工具的经验基础。战略目的决定了焦点小组旨在产生的证据类型：观察政治意义和身份如何在互动中涌现（模式1），或测试和完善竞选信息（模式2），因此它是决定性维度。矩阵表明，鉴于记录在案的失败模式（如谄媚、角色漂移和压制少数观点），AESTs在任何风险水平下都无法在模式1中替代人类互动。在模式2中，适用性则取决于部署风险和经验基础。然而，即便在此，我们也警告说，常规依赖AESTs可能会侵蚀健全判断所依赖的定性技术。
AI.summary: 本文研究了政治党派如何利用人工智能模拟焦点小组（AESTs）进行选民研究。通过构建一个三维决策矩阵，论文分析了AI模拟技术在不同战略目的、部署风险和经验基础下的适用边界，指出AESTs不能完全替代人类焦点小组，并警告过度依赖可能会侵蚀定性研究的专业判断力。
AI.keywords: AI模拟焦点小组, 政治营销, 决策矩阵, 竞选研究, 人工智能伦理
AI.comments: 该论文探讨了人工智能模拟焦点小组（AESTs）在政治竞选研究中的应用边界与风险。创新之处在于提出了一个包含战略目的、部署风险和经验基础的三维决策矩阵，明确了AI模拟不能完全替代人类交互（尤其是在探索政治身份和意义涌现的场景中），并对日常依赖AI可能侵蚀定性研究判断力提出了警示。对于理解政治传播与AI伦理具有重要的实践和理论意义。

title: Constrained Whole-Body Tracking for Humanoid Robots
comments: To be presented at the 2026 Conference on Robot Learning, Austin TX
summary: Recent advances in reinforcement learning (RL) have demonstrated impressive whole-body agility for humanoid robots, yet ensuring safety and satisfying constraints -- particularly those specified after training -- remains a challenge. Towards this goal, we present ConstrainedMimic, a control framework that leverages whole-body kinematics and dynamics for real-time constraint enforcement within RL tracking policies. By integrating principles from operational space control and control barrier functions, we enable the satisfaction of arbitrary runtime constraints on both the kinematic reference motion and the underlying dynamics, with efficient computation at frequencies above 1 kHz. In whole-body motion-tracking experiments in simulation and hardware, we demonstrate collision avoidance (both with the robot body and external obstacles), joint limits, and center of mass stability constraints. By remaining consistent with the current contact mode and tracking objectives, we minimally restrict the capabilities of the policy when constraints are active. Project page: https://stanfordasl.github.io/constrainedmimic.
comment: To be presented at the 2026 Conference on Robot Learning, Austin TX

AI.title_translation: 人型机器人受约束全身跟踪
AI.tldr: ConstrainedMimic是一个控制框架，它利用全身运动学和动力学在RL跟踪策略中实时强制执行约束，确保人型机器人的安全性和约束满足。
AI.motivation: 尽管强化学习在人型机器人全身敏捷性方面取得了进展，但在训练后仍难以确保安全性和满足约束条件。
AI.method: 本研究提出了ConstrainedMimic控制框架，该框架利用全身运动学和动力学，通过整合操作空间控制和控制障碍函数原理，在强化学习跟踪策略中实时强制执行运行时约束，并能以高于1 kHz的频率高效计算。
AI.result: 在模拟和硬件全身运动跟踪实验中，ConstrainedMimic成功演示了碰撞避免（包括机器人本体和外部障碍物）、关节限制和质心稳定性约束。在约束激活时，它能最大限度地减少对策略能力的限制，并与当前接触模式和跟踪目标保持一致。
AI.conclusion: ConstrainedMimic框架通过实时强制执行运动学和动力学约束，有效解决了强化学习在人型机器人全身跟踪中安全性和约束满足的挑战，同时最大限度地减少了对策略能力的限制。
AI.translation: 强化学习（RL）的最新进展已证明人型机器人具有令人印象深刻的全身敏捷性，但确保安全性和满足约束——特别是那些在训练后指定的约束——仍然是一个挑战。为此，我们提出了ConstrainedMimic，一个控制框架，它利用全身运动学和动力学在RL跟踪策略中实时强制执行约束。通过整合操作空间控制和控制障碍函数的原理，我们能够在运动学参考运动和底层动力学上满足任意运行时约束，并能以高于1 kHz的频率进行高效计算。在模拟和硬件的全身运动跟踪实验中，我们展示了碰撞避免（包括与机器人本体和外部障碍物的碰撞）、关节限制和质心稳定性约束。通过与当前接触模式和跟踪目标保持一致，我们在约束激活时最大限度地减少了策略的能力限制。项目页面：https://stanfordasl.github.io/constrainedmimic。
AI.summary: 本论文提出了ConstrainedMimic控制框架，旨在解决强化学习在人型机器人全身跟踪中难以确保安全性和满足训练后约束的挑战。该框架结合了操作空间控制和控制障碍函数，利用全身运动学和动力学在RL策略中实时高效地强制执行各种运行时约束，如碰撞避免、关节限制和质心稳定性。实验证明，ConstrainedMimic在满足约束的同时，最大限度地减少了对机器人策略能力的限制。
AI.keywords: 人型机器人, 全身跟踪, 强化学习, 约束控制, 控制障碍函数
AI.comments: 这项工作具有重要意义，它解决了强化学习在机器人控制中长期存在的安全性和约束满足问题。通过将传统控制理论与RL相结合，ConstrainedMimic提供了一种在保持RL敏捷性的同时，确保机器人行为可预测性和安全性的有效方法，尤其对于部署在复杂环境中的人型机器人至关重要。其高效的实时计算能力也是一个显著的创新点。

title: Robust Asynchronous Planning via Auto-Formalization
summary: LLMs can plan by generating schedules directly as a Planner, or by translating a task into a formal specification for a solver as a Formalizer. Most real-world tasks are asynchronous, with non-uniform durations, concurrency, and execution-time changes, yet existing benchmarks hardly cover them. We unify asynchronous planning under one formulation and release three benchmarks spanning task-graph scale, grounded state and resource constraints, and execution-time events. Surprisingly, PDDL2.1, the formalism built for temporal planning, is the weakest pipeline. On AsyncPlan-XXL it averages 30.8% plan accuracy, against 81.7% for the Planner and 94.0% for a CP-SAT Formalizer. The gap widens with scale, and at 100 actions the three pipelines reach 9.0%, 44.5%, and 82.5%, respectively. The formalism is not to blame. Compiled from the same model-extracted intermediate representation, PDDL2.1 and CP-SAT reach nearly identical accuracy (81.6% vs. 81.5%), and gold task graphs reach 100% for both. What remains is a bottleneck shared by every pipeline: recovering the task graph from language. Execution-time events further degrade every pipeline, yet updating only event-induced constraints reaches 81.6% versus 41.6% for full regeneration. Robust asynchronous planning thus hinges not on the expressiveness of the target formalism but on how reliably a model can write and edit it, and a well-chosen interface can let a weaker model match a stronger one.

AI.title_translation: 通过自动形式化实现鲁棒的异步规划
AI.tldr: 该论文研究了利用大语言模型进行异步规划的性能与瓶颈，发现通过CP-SAT形式化器可实现高达94.0%的准确率，而核心瓶颈在于如何可靠地从自然语言中恢复任务图。
AI.motivation: 现有的规划基准很少涵盖现实世界中常见的具有非均匀持续时间、并发性和执行时间变化的异步任务，且需要探究大模型通过直接生成调度或翻译为形式化规范进行规划的有效性与瓶颈。
AI.method: 统一了异步规划的表述，发布了三个涵盖任务图规模、状态与资源约束以及执行时间事件的基准，对比评估了LLM直接规划、PDDL2.1和CP-SAT形式化器的性能，并分析了中间表示和任务图恢复的影响。
AI.result: CP-SAT形式化器表现最好（达到94.0%），而传统的PDDL2.1表现最弱（30.8%）。性能差距主要源于从自然语言中恢复任务图的瓶颈，且针对执行时间事件仅更新诱导约束比完全重新生成效果更好（81.6%对41.6%）。
AI.conclusion: 鲁棒的异步规划不取决于目标形式主义的表达能力，而取决于模型编写和编辑它的可靠性，精心选择的接口可以让较弱的模型匹配较强的模型。
AI.translation: 大模型可以通过作为规划器直接生成调度，或者将任务翻译为求解器的形式化规范作为形式化器来进行规划。大多数真实世界的任务都是异步的，具有非均匀的持续时间、并发性和执行时间变化，但现有的基准几乎没有涵盖它们。我们将异步规划统一在一个公式下，并发布了三个跨越任务图规模、基础状态和资源约束以及执行时间事件的基准。令人惊讶的是，为时间规划构建的形式主义 PDDL2.1 是最弱的管道。在 AsyncPlan-XXL 上，它的平均计划准确率为 30.8%，而 Planner 为 81.7%，CP-SAT 形式化器为 94.0%。随着规模的扩大，差距进一步拉大，在 100 个动作时，这三个管道的准确率分别达到 9.0%、4.4% 和 82.5%。形式主义本身并没有问题。从相同的模型提取的中间表示编译而来，PDDL2.1 和 CP-SAT 达到的准确率几乎相同（81.6% 对 81.5%），并且黄金任务图对两者都达到了 100%。剩下的瓶颈是每个管道共享的：从语言中恢复任务图。执行时间事件进一步降低了每个管道的性能，但仅更新事件引起的约束可达到 81.6%，而完全重新生成则为 41.6%。因此，鲁棒的异步规划的关键不在于目标形式主义的表现力，而在于模型编写和编辑它的可靠性，精心选择的接口可以使较弱的模型与较强的模型相匹配。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了基于大语言模型的鲁棒异步规划，统一了异步规划的表述并推出了三个基准。研究发现，CP-SAT形式化器的表现远优于PDDL2.1和直接规划器，而性能瓶颈在于从自然语言中恢复任务图的能力，而非形式化工具的表达能力。
AI.keywords: 异步规划, 大语言模型, 自动形式化, 任务图, 规划基准
AI.comments: 该论文深入探讨了利用大模型进行异步规划的能力，创新性地统一了异步规划的表述，并发布了三个新基准。研究揭示了形式化语言在实际应用中的瓶颈在于从自然语言中恢复任务图的能力，而非形式化工具本身的表达能力，对未来大模型在复杂规划任务中的应用具有重要指导意义。

title: LEGS: Fine-Tuning Teleop-Free VLAs for Humanoid Loco-manipulation in an Embodied Gaussian Splatting World
summary: Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies for humanoid loco-manipulation is constrained by the high cost and complexity of collecting human teleoperation demonstrations. VLA policies fine-tuned in simulators have so far transferred poorly to humanoid loco-manipulation tasks. We present LEGS (Loco-manipulation via Embodied Gaussian Splatting), a hybrid simulator that composites a mesh foreground (robot, objects, props) over a photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) background reconstructed from a handheld scene capture. LEGS uses a procedural motion-primitive generator to synthesize labeled demonstrations at scale without human teleoperation, and a two-stage color calibration that aligns renders to the deployment camera. On a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, across three pick-and-place tasks of increasing whole-body difficulty and three VLA backbones ($ψ_0$, $π_{0.5}$, GR00T N1.6), a policy trained purely on LEGS data matches or exceeds one trained on human teleoperation demos on every experiment. It also outperforms a mesh-only baseline trained on the same motions without the calibrated 3DGS frontend. Because motion is recorded independently of appearance, the same demonstrations can be re-rendered for a target scene and objects at over 15x lower cost than teleoperation. When both the objects and the scene change, a policy trained on LEGS-AUG data re-rendered for that target maintains task success, while the teleop baseline fails entirely. Code and videos are available at https://hojjunekim.github.io/legs/.

AI.title_translation: LEGS：在具身高斯泼溅世界中微调免遥操作VLA以进行类人机器人运动-操作
AI.tldr: LEGS是一个混合模拟器，通过无遥操作生成数据，可以在类人机器人上有效训练运动-操作VLA策略，性能超越人类遥操作，并显著降低成本。
AI.motivation: 训练类人机器人运动-操作的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略面临人类遥操作演示数据收集成本高、复杂性大，以及模拟器微调的VLA策略在类人机器人运动-操作任务中迁移性差的问题。
AI.method: 提出了LEGS（Loco-manipulation via Embodied Gaussian Splatting），一个混合模拟器，它将网格前景（机器人、物体、道具）与从手持场景捕获重建的光真实3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）背景复合。LEGS使用程序化运动原语生成器大规模合成带标签的演示数据，无需人类遥操作，并采用两阶段颜色校准将渲染与部署摄像头对齐。
AI.result: 在Unitree G1类人机器人上，纯粹使用LEGS数据训练的策略在所有实验中都匹配或超过了人类遥操作演示训练的策略。它还优于在相同动作上训练但没有校准3DGS前端的纯网格基线。相同的演示可以以比遥操作低15倍以上的成本为目标场景和物体重新渲染。当物体和场景都发生变化时，使用LEGS-AUG数据训练的策略保持任务成功，而遥操作基线完全失败。
AI.conclusion: LEGS提供了一种高效且高性能的解决方案，用于训练类人机器人运动-操作的VLA策略，通过结合混合模拟器和无遥操作数据生成，克服了传统遥操作的局限性，并展现出优异的泛化能力。
AI.translation: 训练类人机器人运动-操作的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略受到收集人类遥操作演示数据的高成本和复杂性的限制。迄今为止，在模拟器中微调的VLA策略在类人机器人运动-操作任务中的迁移性很差。我们提出了LEGS（Loco-manipulation via Embodied Gaussian Splatting），一个混合模拟器，它将网格前景（机器人、物体、道具）与从手持场景捕获重建的光真实3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）背景复合。LEGS使用程序化运动原语生成器大规模合成带标签的演示数据，无需人类遥操作，并采用两阶段颜色校准将渲染与部署摄像头对齐。在Unitree G1类人机器人上，跨越三个难度递增的全身抓取-放置任务和三种VLA骨干网络（$ψ_0$, $π_{0.5}$, GR00T N1.6），纯粹使用LEGS数据训练的策略在所有实验中都匹配或超过了人类遥操作演示训练的策略。它还优于在相同动作上训练但没有校准3DGS前端的纯网格基线。由于运动与外观独立记录，相同的演示可以以比遥操作低15倍以上的成本为目标场景和物体重新渲染。当物体和场景都发生变化时，使用为该目标重新渲染的LEGS-AUG数据训练的策略保持任务成功，而遥操作基线完全失败。代码和视频可在https://hojjunekim.github.io/legs/获取。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了LEGS，一个创新的混合模拟器，用于在类人机器人上训练视觉-语言-动作（VLA）运动-操作策略。LEGS通过结合网格前景和光真实3D高斯泼溅背景，并利用程序化运动原语生成器大规模合成无遥操作演示数据，有效解决了传统遥操作数据收集成本高和模拟器到真实世界迁移性差的问题。实验表明，在Unitree G1类人机器人上，使用LEGS数据训练的策略在抓取-放置任务中表现与人类遥操作训练的策略相当或更优，并且在场景和物体变化时具有更强的泛化能力，同时显著降低了数据生成成本。
AI.keywords: 类人机器人, 运动-操作, 视觉-语言-动作策略, 3D高斯泼溅, 混合模拟器
AI.comments: LEGS的创新之处在于其混合模拟器设计，结合了3DGS的真实感背景和程序化数据生成，极大地降低了训练类人机器人VLA策略的数据获取成本和复杂性。它有效地解决了模拟器到真实世界的迁移性问题，并展现了在不同场景和物体下的强大泛化能力，对于推动具身智能和机器人学习领域具有重要意义。

title: A Reproducible UAV-Assisted VANET Dataset Generator for Fragmentation Risk Analysis in Intelligent Transportation Systems
summary: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) are a key component of Intelligent Transportation Systems, enabling cooperative communication among vehicles and between vehicles and roadside infrastructure. However, their highly dynamic topology makes them vulnerable to network fragmentation, particularly in highway scenarios, low-density traffic conditions, localized accident zones, and communication-stressed environments. Although Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have been increasingly investigated as temporary aerial relays for improving VANET connectivity, reusable, future-labeled, and reproducible datasets designed to support short-term fragmentation risk analysis remain limited. This paper proposes a reproducible UAV-assisted VANET dataset generator for short-term fragmentation risk prediction. The proposed framework simulates a two-lane highway scenario in which vehicles move in opposite directions while UAVs operate as aerial support nodes. It incorporates multiple data collection profiles, including free-flow traffic, localized accidents, sparse extended topologies, dense bursty traffic, and mixed stress conditions. During each simulation episode, the generator periodically extracts mobility, topology, UAV coverage, and communication-window features, then assigns each sample a future fragmentation label based on the network state observed after a configurable prediction horizon. An illustrative generated dataset is descriptively characterized in terms of scenario balance, UAV policy balance, future-label distribution, scenario-specific label behavior, and representative feature ranges. By providing a modular, extensible, and reproducible ns-3-based data-generation framework, this work offers a practical basis for future supervised learning studies and connectivity management strategies in UAV-assisted VANETs.

AI.title_translation: 一种可复现的无人机辅助VANET数据集生成器，用于智能交通系统中的碎片化风险分析
AI.tldr: 该论文提出了一种可复现的无人机辅助VANET数据集生成器，用于预测智能交通系统中的短期网络碎片化风险，以支持未来的监督学习研究和连接管理策略。
AI.motivation: 车辆自组织网络（VANETs）的动态拓扑结构使其容易受到网络碎片化的影响，特别是在高速公路场景、低密度交通、局部事故区和通信压力环境下。尽管无人机（UAVs）已被研究作为临时空中中继来改善VANET连接性，但支持短期碎片化风险分析的可复用、带有未来标签且可复现的数据集仍然有限。
AI.method: 该论文提出了一种可复现的无人机辅助VANET数据集生成器。该框架模拟了一个双车道高速公路场景，其中车辆向相反方向移动，无人机作为空中支持节点。它包含了多种数据收集配置文件，包括自由流交通、局部事故、稀疏扩展拓扑、密集突发交通和混合压力条件。在每个模拟回合中，生成器定期提取移动性、拓扑、无人机覆盖范围和通信窗口特征，然后根据可配置预测范围后观察到的网络状态为每个样本分配一个未来碎片化标签。
AI.result: 一个示例性的生成数据集通过场景平衡、无人机策略平衡、未来标签分布、场景特定标签行为和代表性特征范围进行了描述性表征。该工作提供了一个模块化、可扩展和可复现的基于ns-3的数据生成框架。
AI.conclusion: 通过提供一个模块化、可扩展和可复现的基于ns-3的数据生成框架，这项工作为未来无人机辅助VANET中的监督学习研究和连接管理策略提供了实用的基础。
AI.translation: 车辆自组织网络（VANETs）是智能交通系统的关键组成部分，能够实现车辆之间以及车辆与路边基础设施之间的协作通信。然而，其高度动态的拓扑结构使其容易受到网络碎片化的影响，特别是在高速公路场景、低密度交通条件、局部事故区域和通信受压环境中。尽管无人机（UAVs）作为临时空中中继在改善VANET连接性方面得到了越来越多的研究，但旨在支持短期碎片化风险分析的可复用、带有未来标签且可复现的数据集仍然有限。本文提出了一种可复现的无人机辅助VANET数据集生成器，用于短期碎片化风险预测。所提出的框架模拟了一个双车道高速公路场景，其中车辆向相反方向移动，而无人机则作为空中支持节点运行。它包含了多个数据收集配置文件，包括自由流交通、局部事故、稀疏扩展拓扑、密集突发交通和混合压力条件。在每个模拟回合中，生成器定期提取移动性、拓扑、无人机覆盖范围和通信窗口特征，然后根据可配置预测范围后观察到的网络状态为每个样本分配一个未来碎片化标签。一个说明性的生成数据集在场景平衡、无人机策略平衡、未来标签分布、场景特定标签行为和代表性特征范围方面进行了描述性表征。通过提供一个模块化、可扩展和可复现的基于ns-3的数据生成框架，这项工作为未来无人机辅助VANET中的监督学习研究和连接管理策略提供了实用的基础。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种可复现的无人机辅助车辆自组织网络（VANET）数据集生成器，旨在解决智能交通系统中VANETs易受网络碎片化影响的问题。该生成器模拟了高速公路场景，并整合了多种交通条件，通过提取移动性、拓扑、无人机覆盖和通信窗口特征，并基于未来网络状态分配碎片化标签，生成了用于短期碎片化风险预测的数据集。这项工作为未来无人机辅助VANET的监督学习和连接管理策略提供了基础。
AI.keywords: VANET, 无人机, 碎片化风险, 数据集生成器, 智能交通系统
AI.comments: 这项工作的创新之处在于提供了一个模块化、可扩展且可复现的基于ns-3的数据生成框架，专门用于无人机辅助VANETs的碎片化风险分析。其重要性在于解决了当前缺乏支持短期碎片化风险分析的、带有未来标签的数据集的问题，为未来的监督学习研究提供了宝贵资源。

title: C2GA: A Class-Controllable Generative Augmentation Framework for Respiratory Sound Classification
comments: The submitter requests withdrawal due to unresolved authorship and contribution-attribution issues following changes in the original inter-institutional collaboration. The attribution of research contributions requires further clarification. Withdrawal is requested pending resolution of these matters
summary: Background: Respiratory sound classification plays a critical role in the clinical identification of pulmonary pathologies. However, its performance is often hindered by the limited size, severe noise, and class imbalance of real-world auscultation datasets. Although conventional audio augmentation techniques are easy to implement, they may inadvertently distort subtle pathological characteristics. Meanwhile, existing Variational Autoencoder (VAE)- or Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based generative approaches often suffer from limited sample fidelity and insufficient controllability over class semantics, particularly under conditions of scarce supervision. Methods: To overcome these limitations, we propose C2GA, a class-controllable generative augmentation framework. C2GA first constructs a semantically rich discrete latent space using a conditional Vector-Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE), in which local acoustic tokens are explicitly decoupled from global class prototypes. Subsequently, a Transformer-based autoregressive prior is trained to generate label-consistent token sequences. These generated tokens are then fused with the corresponding class prototypes and decoded into high-fidelity Mel-spectrograms for data augmentation. Conclusion: These results indicate that C2GA provides an effective and semantically reliable augmentation strategy for respiratory sound analysis. By enabling controllable and high-quality data generation, the proposed framework offers a promising solution for improving the robustness and generalization of respiratory sound classification in realistic clinical scenarios.

AI.title_translation: C2GA：用于呼吸音分类的类可控生成增强框架
AI.tldr: 本文提出了C2GA框架，通过条件VQ-VAE与自回归Transformer生成高保真且类别可控的呼吸音数据，以解决医疗音频数据稀缺和不平衡问题。
AI.motivation: 呼吸音分类性能常受限于真实听诊数据集规模有限、噪声严重及类别不平衡；传统音频增强易扭曲病理特征，现有VAE/GAN生成方法则存在样本保真度低、类别语义可控性不足的问题。
AI.method: 提出C2GA框架，首先使用条件向量量化变分自编码器（VQ-VAE）构建离散潜在空间（将局部声学标记与全局类原型解耦），然后训练基于Transformer的自回归先验以生成标签一致的标记序列，最后将其与类原型融合并解码为高保真梅尔频谱图用于数据增强。
AI.result: 结果表明，C2GA能够实现可控的高质量数据生成，为提高呼吸音分类在实际临床中的鲁棒性和泛化能力提供了一个有前景的解决方案。
AI.conclusion: C2GA为呼吸音分析提供了一种有效且语义可靠的增强策略，能够显著提升真实临床场景下呼吸音分类的鲁棒性与泛化能力。
AI.translation: 背景：呼吸音分类在肺部病理学临床识别中起着关键作用。然而，其性能往往受到真实世界听诊数据集规模有限、噪声严重以及类别不平衡的阻碍。尽管传统的音频增强技术易于实现，但它们可能会无意中扭曲微妙的病理特征。同时，现有的基于变分自编码器（VAE）或生成对抗网络（GAN）的生成方法往往存在样本保真度有限、对类语义的可控性不足的问题，特别是在监督稀缺的条件下。方法：为了克服这些限制，我们提出了C2GA，一个类可控的生成增强框架。C2GA首先使用条件向量量化变分自编码器（VQ-VAE）构建一个语义丰富的离散潜在空间，在该空间中，局域声学标记与全局类原型被显式解耦。随后，训练基于Transformer的自回归先验以生成标签一致的标记序列。接着，将这些生成的标记与相应的类原型相融合，并解码为高保真度的梅尔频谱图用于数据增强。结论：这些结果表明，C2GA为呼吸音分析提供了一种有效且语义可靠的增强策略。通过实现可控且高质量的数据生成，该框架为提高真实临床场景下呼吸音分类的鲁棒性和泛化能力提供了一个有前景的解决方案。
AI.summary: 该文提出了C2GA——一个用于呼吸音分类的类可控生成增强框架。该框架利用条件VQ-VAE和Transformer自回归先验生成高保真、语义可靠的梅尔频谱图，有效克服了医疗音频数据集中样本少、噪声大和类别不平衡的痛点。
AI.keywords: Respiratory sound classification, Generative augmentation, Class-controllable generation, Vector-Quantized Variational Autoencoder, Transformer
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种面向呼吸音分类的类可控生成增强框架（C2GA），创新性地结合了条件VQ-VAE与基于Transformer的自回归先验，能够解耦局域声学标记与全局类原型，有效解决了现实医疗数据集中样本稀缺、噪声大和类别不平衡的问题。

title: Learning Reusable Agent Subroutines from Experience
comments: v2: major revision; method renamed to ARISE, new experiments, rewritten. 28 pages, 15 figures
summary: Existing methods induce various forms of knowledge from agent traces, from sample workflows to programmatic skills. We propose ARISE (Agent Routine Induction from Successful Experience), which identifies recurring procedures in agent traces and synthesizes them into a reusable library of agent subroutines. Across five tasks in narrative deduction, rule application, and constraint planning, it is shown to be a more effective learning strategy than prompting methods and prose and code artifact induction methods. ARISE outperforms chain-of-thought in all ten model-task settings of the main evaluation. Compared to state-of-the-art methods in agent experience induction, our method scores 6.1 percentage points over the strongest evaluated baselines, and 11.5 percentage points over code-skill induction. In our controlled experiment, ARISE also improves average accuracy by up to 15.6 percentage points compared to formatting the induced knowledge as skills and by up to 19.1 points over rewriting it as code tools.
