AI.title_translation: 学习从经验中获取可重用智能体子程序
AI.tldr: ARISE是一种从智能体成功经验中识别并合成可重用子程序的方法，在多项任务中表现优于现有学习策略和基线方法。
AI.motivation: 现有方法从智能体轨迹中诱导各种形式的知识，但需要一种更有效的方式来识别并合成可重用的智能体子程序，以提高学习效率和性能。
AI.method: 本文提出了ARISE (Agent Routine Induction from Successful Experience) 方法。该方法通过识别智能体轨迹中重复出现的程序，并将其合成为一个可重用的智能体子程序库。
AI.result: ARISE在叙事推导、规则应用和约束规划的五项任务中，比提示方法以及散文和代码工件诱导方法更有效。在主要评估的所有十个模型-任务设置中，ARISE优于思维链。与智能体经验诱导的现有最佳方法相比，ARISE比最强的评估基线高出6.1个百分点，比代码技能诱导高出11.5个百分点。在受控实验中，ARISE的平均准确率比将诱导知识格式化为技能提高了高达15.6个百分点，比将其重写为代码工具提高了高达19.1个百分点。
AI.conclusion: ARISE是一种从智能体成功经验中学习可重用子程序的有效策略，在多种任务中显著优于当前的提示方法、知识诱导方法和现有最佳智能体经验诱导基线。
AI.translation: 现有方法从智能体轨迹中诱导各种形式的知识，从样本工作流到程序技能。我们提出了ARISE（从成功经验中诱导智能体例程），它识别智能体轨迹中重复出现的程序，并将其合成为一个可重用的智能体子程序库。在叙事推导、规则应用和约束规划的五项任务中，它被证明是一种比提示方法以及散文和代码工件诱导方法更有效的学习策略。在主要评估的所有十个模型-任务设置中，ARISE优于思维链。与智能体经验诱导的现有最佳方法相比，我们的方法比最强的评估基线高出6.1个百分点，比代码技能诱导高出11.5个百分点。在我们的受控实验中，与将诱导知识格式化为技能相比，ARISE的平均准确率提高了高达15.6个百分点；与将其重写为代码工具相比，平均准确率提高了高达19.1个百分点。
AI.summary: 本文提出ARISE方法，旨在从智能体的成功经验中识别并合成可重用的子程序库。通过在叙事推导、规则应用和约束规划等任务上的实验，ARISE被证明是一种比现有提示方法、散文和代码工件诱导方法更有效的学习策略，并且在性能上显著优于思维链及其他先进的智能体经验诱导基线方法。
AI.keywords: 智能体子程序, 经验学习, ARISE, 知识诱导, 可重用性
AI.comments: ARISE的创新之处在于其能够从智能体经验中自动识别和合成可重用的子程序，这对于提高智能体的学习效率、泛化能力和任务执行效果具有重要意义。该方法在多项任务中表现出显著的性能提升，表明其在构建高效、智能的自主智能体方面具有广阔的应用前景。

title: AUDITFLOW: Executable Symbolic Environments for Structured Financial Reporting Verification
summary: Structured financial reporting verification requires connecting reported facts to accounting constraints, reconstructing expected values, and executing numerical checks. We study this problem through XBRL numerical consistency verification and introduce \textsc{AuditFlow}, a graph-grounded multi-agent framework built around an executable symbolic environment. The environment links a reusable US-GAAP taxonomy graph with filing-specific XBRL evidence and provides typed tools for retrieval, traversal, computation, and rule evaluation. Two specialized auditors investigate constraints and filing evidence, while a senior auditor coordinates disagreement-triggered refinement. Deterministic tools produce verification evidence; evidential aggregation combines structured reports, including agent-declared overrides, into final decisions. On a newly collected 1{,}000-instance evaluation set of engine-recorded DQC violations, \textsc{AuditFlow} achieves $87.70\%$ joint audit accuracy with Claude Sonnet 4.6, compared with $68.60\%$ for Single Agent and $86.70\%$ for Checker-only. Component and coverage analyses identify executable verification as the main source of accuracy, while additional gains from agent judgment depend on the backbone and checker coverage.

AI.title_translation: AUDITFLOW：用于结构化财务报告验证的可执行符号环境
AI.tldr: 本文提出了 AUDITFLOW，一个结合可执行符号环境的多智能体框架，用于高效、准确地验证结构化财务报告（XBRL）的数值一致性。
AI.motivation: 结构化财务报告验证需要将报告的事实连接到会计约束、重建期望值并执行数值检查，现有方法在处理 XBRL 数值一致性验证时需要更高效、准确的自动化框架。
AI.method: 引入了 AuditFlow，一个基于图的多智能体框架，构建在可执行符号环境中。该环境将 US-GAAP 分类法图与 XBRL 证据链接，提供检索、遍历、计算和规则评估的类型化工具。包含两个专业审计员和一个高级审计员进行协同和分歧触发的求精，并采用证据聚合得出最终决策。
AI.result: 在一个包含 1,000 个引擎记录的 DQC 违规实例的新评估集上，使用 Claude Sonnet 4.6 的 AuditFlow 达到了 87.70% 的联合审计准确率，相比之下单智能体为 68.60%，仅检查器方法为 86.70%。
AI.conclusion: AuditFlow 通过结合可执行符号环境和多智能体协作，有效解决了结构化财务报告中的数值一致性验证问题，在 DQC 违规数据集上取得了优于基线的方法的准确率。
AI.translation: 结构化财务报告验证需要将报告的事实与会计约束联系起来，重建期望值，并执行数值检查。我们通过XBRL数值一致性验证研究了这个问题，并引入了 \textsc{AuditFlow}，这是一个建立在可执行符号环境周围的基于图的多智能体框架。该环境将可重用的美国通用会计准则（US-GAAP）分类法图与特定申报的 XBRL 证据链接起来，并提供用于检索、遍历、计算和规则评估的类型化工具。两个专业的审计员调查约束和申报证据，而高级审计员则协调由分歧触发的求精。确定性工具产生验证证据；证据聚合将结构化报告（包括智能体声明的覆盖）组合成最终决策。在一个新收集的包含 1,000 个引擎记录的 DQC 违规实例的评估集上，\textsc{AuditFlow} 在使用 Claude Sonnet 4.6 时实现了 87.70% 的联合审计准确率，而单智能体为 68.60%，仅检查器方法为 86.70%。组件和覆盖范围分析表明，可执行验证是准确性的主要来源，而来自智能体判断的额外收益则取决于主干模型和检查器的覆盖范围。
AI.summary: 该论文介绍了 AUDITFLOW，一个用于结构化财务报告验证的图接地多智能体框架。它通过可执行符号环境结合 US-GAAP 分类法图与 XBRL 证据，利用专门的审计员和确定性工具进行数值一致性验证，在 DQC 违规数据集上表现出优异的准确性。
AI.keywords: XBRL, 财务报告验证, 多智能体框架, 可执行符号环境, US-GAAP
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的基于图的多智能体框架（AuditFlow），结合可执行符号环境，用于结构化财务报告（XBRL）的验证。创新点在于将分类法图与申报证据结合，并通过确定性工具和多智能体协同显著提高了审计准确率。

title: AI Assistance for Discretionary Work: Increasing Feedback Provision in Higher Education
summary: AI assistance can increase the efficiency and accuracy of human work, but can it also encourage people to undertake valuable tasks they might otherwise skip? Here, we investigate whether AI assistance can improve participation in discretionary but beneficial work in the context of personalized feedback provision in higher education, a pedagogically valuable but often optional practice. We conduct a mixed-methods study combining a randomized field experiment and qualitative interviews in an upper-level machine learning course with $n$=11 teaching assistants (TAs) and n=88 students. Student submissions were randomly assigned to either (1) a treatment condition where TAs received AI-assisted feedback drafts after grading or (2) a control condition without drafts. We find that AI-assisted feedback significantly increases feedback provision (+10.8 percentage points, SE=1.1, p<0.001) and feedback length (+39.8 chars, SE=3.45, p<0.001) while also maintaining student-rated usefulness and expert-rated feedback quality among the feedback instances for which these outcomes were observed. While time spent conditional on providing feedback did not significantly differ between conditions, total time spent in the feedback stage increased in the treatment condition (10.55 seconds, SE=4.19, p=.012). Qualitative findings suggest that AI-assisted drafts function as editable scaffolds that lower barriers to initiating feedback rather than reducing overall labor. Together, our findings show that AI assistance can increase participation in discretionary communication without necessarily reducing the labor involved or eliminating the effort required to sustain it.

AI.title_translation: AI辅助酌情工作：增加高等教育中的反馈提供
AI.tldr: AI辅助能增加高等教育中反馈的提供和长度，通过降低启动障碍而非减少整体劳动来作为支架。
AI.motivation: 研究AI辅助是否能鼓励人们参与那些酌情但有益的任务，具体是在高等教育中提供个性化反馈，这是一种有教学价值但通常是可选的实践。
AI.method: 采用混合方法研究，结合随机现场实验和定性访谈。研究对象为一门高阶机器学习课程中的11名助教和88名学生。学生提交作业被随机分配到两个条件：治疗组（助教收到AI辅助的反馈草稿）和对照组（无草稿）。
AI.result: AI辅助反馈显著增加了反馈提供率（+10.8个百分点）和反馈长度（+39.8个字符），同时保持了学生评价的有用性和专家评价的反馈质量。虽然提供反馈的条件时间花费没有显著差异，但治疗组中反馈阶段的总时间花费增加了。定性发现表明，AI辅助草稿充当了可编辑的支架，降低了启动反馈的障碍，而非减少了整体劳动。
AI.conclusion: AI辅助可以增加酌情沟通的参与度，而无需必然减少所涉及的劳动或消除维持它所需的努力。
AI.translation: AI辅助可以提高人类工作的效率和准确性，但它能否也鼓励人们承担他们原本可能会跳过的有价值的任务？在此，我们调查了AI辅助是否能提高高等教育中个性化反馈提供这一酌情但有益的工作的参与度，这是一种具有教学价值但通常是可选的实践。我们进行了一项混合方法研究，结合了随机现场实验和定性访谈，在一个高阶机器学习课程中，有11名助教（TA）和88名学生参与。学生的提交作业被随机分配到以下两种情况之一：（1）治疗组，助教在评分后收到AI辅助的反馈草稿；或（2）对照组，没有草稿。我们发现，AI辅助反馈显著增加了反馈提供（+10.8个百分点，SE=1.1，p<0.001）和反馈长度（+39.8个字符，SE=3.45，p<0.001），同时在观察到这些结果的反馈实例中，学生评价的有用性和专家评价的反馈质量也得以保持。虽然提供反馈的条件时间花费在两组之间没有显著差异，但治疗组中反馈阶段的总时间花费增加了（10.55秒，SE=4.19，p=.012）。定性研究结果表明，AI辅助草稿充当了可编辑的支架，降低了启动反馈的障碍，而不是减少了整体劳动。总而言之，我们的发现表明，AI辅助可以增加酌情沟通的参与度，而无需必然减少所涉及的劳动或消除维持它所需的努力。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了AI辅助对酌情工作，特别是高等教育中个性化反馈提供的影响。通过一项涉及机器学习课程助教和学生的混合方法研究，研究人员发现AI辅助的反馈草稿显著提高了反馈的提供率和长度，同时保持了质量和有用性。尽管反馈阶段的总时间花费有所增加，但定性数据表明AI草稿充当了支架，降低了提供反馈的初始障碍，而非减少了整体劳动。研究得出结论，AI辅助可以促进对可选、有益任务的参与，而无需必然减少所涉及的努力。
AI.keywords: AI辅助, 反馈提供, 高等教育, 酌情工作, 混合方法研究
AI.comments: 该论文为AI辅助提供了一个有趣的视角，强调了其通过降低启动障碍来增加对有价值但常被跳过的任务的参与的潜力，而不是仅仅关注效率提升或劳动减少。总时间花费增加但参与度也增加的发现是反直觉的，对于理解酌情工作中的人机协作非常重要。这表明AI可以通过使任务不那么令人生畏来促进参与。

title: ConTrack: Constrained Hand Motion Tracking with Adaptive Trade-off Control
summary: Human demonstrations provide strong priors for robot manipulation, yet it is non-trivial to transfer them to execute on real robots due to the kinematic gap. In dexterous manipulation, it remains challenging to track long-horizon, contact-rich sequences even in simulators: a reference-tracking policy must keep objects on their target trajectories while preserving demonstrated joint motion and contact timing. Existing approaches often rely on hand-crafted reward tuning that require per-sequence tuning and break under limited interaction budgets. We introduce ConTrack, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that scales with tracking data. ConTrack treats object tracking as a constraint and allocates remaining control authority to motion fidelity, which allows it to adapt task--style trade-offs online using a dual-variable update. In addition, ConTrack also stabilizes long-horizon learning with an adaptive mid-trajectory reset library that reuses policy-reachable simulator states. Our qualitative and quantitative results in simulation tracking and real robot demonstrate that ConTrack improves success and object pose accuracy significantly over prior arts while preserving joint and contact fidelity. Website: https://www.lyt0112.com/projects/ConTrack.

AI.title_translation: ConTrack：具有自适应权衡控制的受约束手部运动跟踪
AI.tldr: ConTrack是一个强化学习框架，通过将物体跟踪视为约束并在线调整任务-风格权衡，显著提高了模拟和真实机器人中手部运动跟踪的成功率和物体姿态精度，同时保持关节和接触保真度。
AI.motivation: 由于运动学差异，将人类演示转移到真实机器人上执行具有挑战性。在灵巧操作中，即使在模拟器中，跟踪长周期、接触丰富的序列也很困难，因为需要保持物体在目标轨迹上，同时保留演示的关节运动和接触时序。现有方法依赖于手工调整奖励，需要针对每个序列进行调整，并且在有限的交互预算下会失效。
AI.method: ConTrack是一个强化学习（RL）框架，它将物体跟踪视为一个约束，并将剩余的控制权限分配给运动保真度。它使用双变量更新在线调整任务-风格权衡。此外，ConTrack通过自适应的轨迹中重置库稳定长周期学习，该库重用策略可达的模拟器状态。
AI.result: ConTrack在模拟跟踪和真实机器人中显著提高了成功率和物体姿态精度，同时保持了关节和接触保真度，优于现有技术。
AI.conclusion: ConTrack通过其新颖的强化学习框架和自适应权衡控制，有效解决了灵巧操作中长周期、接触丰富的手部运动跟踪问题，并在模拟和真实机器人中取得了显著的性能提升。
AI.translation: 人类演示为机器人操作提供了强大的先验知识，但由于运动学差异，将其转移到真实机器人上执行并非易事。在灵巧操作中，即使在模拟器中，跟踪长周期、接触丰富的序列仍然具有挑战性：参考跟踪策略必须使物体保持在其目标轨迹上，同时保留演示的关节运动和接触时序。现有方法通常依赖于手工调整奖励，这需要针对每个序列进行调整，并且在有限的交互预算下会失效。我们引入了ConTrack，一个随跟踪数据扩展的强化学习（RL）框架。ConTrack将物体跟踪视为一个约束，并将剩余的控制权限分配给运动保真度，这使得它能够使用双变量更新在线调整任务-风格权衡。此外，ConTrack还通过自适应的轨迹中重置库稳定长周期学习，该库重用策略可达的模拟器状态。我们在模拟跟踪和真实机器人中的定性和定量结果表明，ConTrack显著提高了成功率和物体姿态精度，同时保持了关节和接触保真度，优于现有技术。网站：https://www.lyt0112.com/projects/ConTrack。
AI.summary: ConTrack是一个新颖的强化学习框架，旨在解决灵巧操作中长周期、接触丰富的手部运动跟踪挑战。它通过将物体跟踪视为约束，并利用双变量更新在线自适应调整任务与风格的权衡。为稳定长周期学习，ConTrack引入了自适应的轨迹中重置库。在模拟和真实机器人上的实验结果表明，ConTrack显著提升了跟踪成功率和物体姿态精度，同时有效保持了关节和接触的保真度，性能优于现有方法。
AI.keywords: 手部运动跟踪, 强化学习, 约束控制, 灵巧操作, 自适应权衡
AI.comments: ConTrack的创新之处在于其将物体跟踪作为约束，并通过双变量更新实现在线任务-风格权衡的自适应控制，这克服了传统强化学习方法中手工调整奖励的局限性。结合自适应轨迹中重置库，该框架有效解决了长周期、接触丰富操作的稳定性问题，对于提高机器人灵巧操作的泛化性和鲁棒性具有重要意义。

title: CoPark: Learning Reactive Parking via Self-Play
summary: Learning a single policy that reaches a goal with high geometric precision while interacting safely with nearby agents poses conflicting objectives. Precision favors commitment to a fixed geometric plan, whereas interaction requires immediate deviation when another agent intrudes, causing policies optimized for one objective to often fail at the other. We study this problem in the context of reactive autonomous parking, where multiple vehicles must reach assigned slots with sub-meter terminal accuracy while remaining responsive to neighboring vehicles throughout the maneuver. We propose CoPark, a multi-agent self-play RL approach built on a residual-policy architecture. A precomputed offline plan provides a fixed action prior, while a residual head learns the reactive corrections. The residual policy learns behaviors under self-play, where data and scripting fall short, while the fixed prior holds the slot-frame geometry that pure policies struggle to reach reliably. The key design is a partner-threat-modulated, channel-asymmetric release of the prior. A continuous threat signal shifts authority of the longitudinal channel to the residual head to enable yielding, while the lateral channel remains anchored to the precomputed reference to preserve sub-meter slot alignment. A closed-loop refinement layer corrects residual terminal error from action-grid discretization. We train our policy on six parking lots and evaluate zero-shot on our new reactive-parking benchmark spanning Dragon Lake Parking (DLP) and DeepScenario Open 3D (DSC3D). CoPark achieves ~70-85% success with only 3-6% collision rate, substantially outperforming classical, imitation-learning, and large-scale RL baselines. Importantly, the results demonstrate emergent interaction behaviors such as reverse-yielding, mid-maneuver yielding, tight-corridor passing, and queuing.

AI.title_translation: CoPark：通过自博弈学习反应式泊车
AI.tldr: CoPark提出了一种基于残差策略和自博弈的多智能体强化学习方法，解决了自动泊车中几何精度和安全交互的冲突目标，实现了高成功率和低碰撞率，并展现了复杂的交互行为。
AI.motivation: 自动泊车中，实现高几何精度泊车与安全地与周围车辆交互是相互冲突的目标。精度需要遵循固定规划，而交互则需要及时调整以避免碰撞。目前的策略往往难以同时兼顾两者，导致在反应式自动泊车场景中性能不佳。
AI.method: 本文提出了CoPark，一种多智能体自博弈强化学习方法，采用残差策略架构。一个预先计算的离线规划作为固定的动作先验，而一个残差头则学习反应式修正。关键设计是一个由伙伴威胁调制的、通道不对称的先验释放机制：连续的威胁信号将纵向通道的控制权转移给残差头以实现避让，而横向通道则保持锚定在预计算的参考上以保持亚米级的泊位对齐。此外，还增加了一个闭环精修层来纠正动作网格离散化造成的残余终端误差。
AI.result: CoPark在六个停车场上进行训练，并在新的反应式泊车基准（Dragon Lake Parking和DeepScenario Open 3D）上进行零样本评估，取得了约70-85%的成功率和3-6%的碰撞率。这显著优于经典方法、模仿学习和大规模强化学习基线。重要的是，结果还展示了诸如倒车避让、机动中避让、狭窄走廊通过和排队等新兴交互行为。
AI.conclusion: CoPark成功地通过其残差策略架构和自博弈训练，解决了自动泊车中精度与交互之间的冲突，实现了高效且安全的反应式泊车，并展现出复杂的社会化交互行为。
AI.translation: 学习一个既能以高几何精度到达目标，又能安全地与附近智能体交互的单一策略，会带来相互冲突的目标。精度偏向于对固定几何规划的承诺，而交互则要求在另一个智能体侵入时立即偏离，导致针对一个目标优化的策略常常在另一个目标上失败。我们在反应式自动泊车的背景下研究这个问题，其中多辆车必须以亚米级的终端精度到达指定泊位，同时在整个机动过程中对相邻车辆保持响应。我们提出了CoPark，一种基于残差策略架构的多智能体自博弈强化学习方法。预先计算的离线规划提供了一个固定的动作先验，而一个残差头学习反应式修正。残差策略通过自博弈学习行为，弥补了数据和脚本的不足，而固定先验则保持了纯策略难以可靠达到的泊位框架几何形状。关键设计是一个由伙伴威胁调制的、通道不对称的先验释放机制。连续的威胁信号将纵向通道的控制权转移给残差头以实现避让，而横向通道则保持锚定在预计算的参考上以保持亚米级的泊位对齐。一个闭环精修层纠正了动作网格离散化造成的残余终端误差。我们在六个停车场上训练了我们的策略，并在我们新的反应式泊车基准（涵盖Dragon Lake Parking (DLP) 和 DeepScenario Open 3D (DSC3D)）上进行了零样本评估。CoPark以仅3-6%的碰撞率取得了约70-85%的成功率，大大优于经典方法、模仿学习和大规模强化学习基线。重要的是，结果表明了新兴的交互行为，例如倒车避让、机动中避让、狭窄走廊通过和排队。
AI.summary: 本文提出CoPark，一种用于反应式自动泊车的多智能体自博弈强化学习方法。针对泊车精度与安全交互之间的冲突，CoPark采用残差策略架构，结合预计算的几何规划和学习到的反应式修正。其核心创新在于伙伴威胁调制的通道不对称先验释放机制，确保纵向避让和横向精度。实验结果表明，CoPark在多个场景下实现了高成功率和低碰撞率，并展现出复杂的交互行为，显著优于现有基线。
AI.keywords: 反应式泊车, 自博弈, 强化学习, 残差策略, 多智能体
AI.comments: CoPark的创新点在于其残差策略架构和通道不对称的先验释放机制，巧妙地解决了自动泊车中精度与反应性之间的固有矛盾。通过将几何规划作为先验并利用强化学习学习反应式修正，它避免了纯RL策略在几何精度上的不足。自博弈训练使其能够学习到在真实数据或脚本中难以捕获的复杂交互行为，这对于自动驾驶系统在复杂交通环境中的部署至关重要。该方法在多智能体交互场景下的表现，特别是新兴的交互行为，展示了其强大的泛化能力和实用潜力。

title: Imagine Before You Draw: Visual Prompt Engineering for Image Generation
summary: Incorporating visual semantic representations as an intermediate step before image generation can reduce the modeling difficulty between text and images, thereby improving generation quality. Recent works such as X-Omni and BLIP3o-Next have explored this direction, but they typically use a two-stage external pipeline: a separate autoregressive model first generates semantic tokens, which are then fed as conditioning to an independent diffusion decoder. When the decoder is conditioned only on the compressed semantic plan, it cannot directly access the original input, which introduces an information bottleneck that limits detail preservation in downstream tasks such as editing. Internal architectures such as Transfusion, BAGEL, and Show-o2 avoid this bottleneck by enabling cross-modal interaction within a single model, but they still face the difficult text-to-pixel modeling gap without intermediate semantic guidance. We propose Visual Prompt Engineering (VPE), which can be seamlessly integrated into such internal frameworks. Specifically, the model first autoregressively generates visual semantic tokens ($e.g.$, SigLIP 2) as "visual prompts" that capture the semantic layout, then generates the full image tokens conditioned on this plan. We validate VPE across class-conditional generation, text-to-image generation, and image editing, covering various token types and model architectures. Results show that VPE can accelerate convergence, raise quality ceilings, and through internal integration, achieve substantially better editing preservation (PSNR: $26.76$ vs. $19.92$) than a matched external pipeline with semantic-only decoder conditioning, while maintaining competitive editing responsiveness.

AI.title_translation: 先想象再绘制：图像生成中的视觉提示工程
AI.tldr: VPE通过内部生成视觉语义提示来指导图像生成，解决了现有方法的细节丢失和文本到像素建模难题，显著提升了图像生成质量和编辑保真度。
AI.motivation: 在图像生成中，将视觉语义表示作为中间步骤可以降低文本与图像之间的建模难度，从而提高生成质量。现有外部两阶段管道存在信息瓶颈，限制了细节保留；而现有内部架构虽避免了瓶颈，但仍面临无中间语义指导的文本到像素建模难题。
AI.method: 本文提出了视觉提示工程（VPE），可无缝集成到内部框架中。具体而言，模型首先自回归生成视觉语义标记（例如SigLIP 2）作为捕获语义布局的“视觉提示”，然后在此计划的条件下生成完整的图像标记。
AI.result: VPE可以加速收敛，提高质量上限，并通过内部集成，实现比仅使用语义解码器条件的外部管道显著更好的编辑保真度（PSNR：26.76 vs. 19.92），同时保持有竞争力的编辑响应能力。VPE在类别条件生成、文本到图像生成和图像编辑中得到了验证。
AI.conclusion: VPE通过在内部框架中引入视觉语义提示，有效解决了图像生成中细节保留和文本到像素建模的挑战，显著提升了生成质量和编辑性能。
AI.translation: 将视觉语义表示作为图像生成前的中间步骤，可以降低文本与图像之间的建模难度，从而提高生成质量。X-Omni和BLIP3o-Next等近期工作探索了这一方向，但它们通常使用两阶段的外部管道：一个独立的自回归模型首先生成语义标记，然后将其作为条件输入给一个独立的扩散解码器。当解码器仅以压缩的语义规划为条件时，它无法直接访问原始输入，这引入了一个信息瓶颈，限制了下游任务（如编辑）中的细节保留。Transfusion、BAGEL和Show-o2等内部架构通过在单个模型内实现跨模态交互来避免这一瓶颈，但它们在没有中间语义指导的情况下仍然面临困难的文本到像素建模鸿沟。我们提出了视觉提示工程（VPE），它可以无缝集成到此类内部框架中。具体而言，模型首先自回归生成视觉语义标记（例如SigLIP 2）作为捕获语义布局的“视觉提示”，然后在此规划的条件下生成完整的图像标记。我们在类别条件生成、文本到图像生成和图像编辑中验证了VPE，涵盖了各种标记类型和模型架构。结果表明，VPE可以加速收敛，提高质量上限，并通过内部集成，实现比仅使用语义解码器条件的匹配外部管道显著更好的编辑保真度（PSNR：26.76 vs. 19.92），同时保持有竞争力的编辑响应能力。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为视觉提示工程（VPE）的新方法，旨在通过在图像生成过程中引入内部视觉语义表示来提升生成质量和编辑能力。针对现有外部管道的信息瓶颈和内部架构的文本到像素建模难题，VPE在单一模型中首先自回归生成视觉语义标记作为“视觉提示”，然后基于这些提示生成最终图像。实验证明，VPE能加速收敛、提高生成质量上限，并在图像编辑任务中展现出显著优于外部管道的细节保留能力，同时保持良好的编辑响应性。
AI.keywords: 视觉提示工程, 图像生成, 语义表示, 图像编辑, 内部架构
AI.comments: 本文提出的VPE通过将视觉语义提示内部集成到图像生成框架中，巧妙地解决了现有方法中信息瓶失真和语义鸿沟的问题。其创新点在于将“想象”过程（生成语义提示）与“绘制”过程（生成图像）紧密结合，且都在一个统一的内部框架中完成，这对于提升生成图像的细节保真度和可编辑性具有重要意义。特别是其在编辑任务中显著优于外部管道的PSNR表现，证明了其优越性。

title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios
comments: Code and data at https://github.com/g8a9/ouvia -- Accepted at EMNLP 2026
summary: Speech translation (ST) is increasingly adopted in user applications, yet its evaluation largely focuses on decontextualized testbeds and holistic quality, rather than end users' communication needs. We introduce Ouvia, an evaluation framework for measuring user-perceived usability of speech translation outputs in real-world settings. Ouvia focuses on one-to-one communication: an English speaker needs to convey a request to a Portuguese speaker, and the message is automatically translated. Through a custom web app and multi-phase study design, we collect more than 1,750 such interactions in healthcare and everyday situations, mediated by four ST systems, involving speakers from three English dialects and two genders. We find that modern ST serves people only to a limited extent---only around half of interactions are rated as usable---with significant gaps in reported usability across demographic groups. Moreover, among quality metrics, we find that QA-based evaluation is a substantially stronger predictor of real-world usability than standard approaches. Together, these findings stress the importance of situated, user-centered evaluation frameworks that go beyond holistic quality scores and attend to who the technology serves---and how well.
comment: Code and data at https://github.com/g8a9/ouvia -- Accepted at EMNLP 2026

AI.title_translation: Ouvia：一个用于衡量真实世界通信场景中语音翻译可用性的以用户为中心的框架
AI.tldr: 本文提出了Ouvia框架以评估真实场景下语音翻译的用户可用性，发现现有系统可用性仅约一半且存在人口统计学偏差，强调了用户中心评估的重要性。
AI.motivation: 当前的语音翻译（ST）评估主要集中在脱离上下文的测试平台和整体质量上，而忽视了最终用户的实际沟通需求以及技术在真实世界中的可用性表现。
AI.method: 引入了名为Ouvia的评估框架，通过定制的网络应用程序和多阶段研究设计，在医疗和日常情境中收集了超过1750次由四种语音翻译系统介导的交互数据，涉及不同英语方言和性别。
AI.result: 大约只有一半的交互被评为可用，不同人口统计学群体之间存在显著的可用性差距。此外，基于QA的评估比标准方法更能强力预测真实世界的可用性。
AI.conclusion: 现代语音翻译在真实场景中的可用性有限，且存在人口统计学偏见。研究强调了建立基于情境的、以用户为中心的评估框架的必要性。
AI.translation: 语音翻译（ST）越来越多地被应用到用户应用程序中，然而其评估主要集中在脱离上下文的测试平台和整体质量上，而不是最终用户的沟通需求。我们介绍了Ouvia，这是一个用于衡量真实世界设置中语音翻译输出用户感知可用性的评估框架。Ouvia专注于一对一沟通：英语发言者需要向葡萄牙语发言者传达请求，并且消息会被自动翻译。通过定制的网络应用程序和多阶段研究设计，我们在医疗和日常情境中收集了1,750多次此类交互，这些交互由四个ST系统介导，涉及来自三个英语方言和两种性别的发言者。我们发现，现代ST在很大程度上只能有限地服务于人们——只有大约一半的交互被评为可用——并且在不同人口统计学群体之间报告的可用性存在显著差距。此外，在质量指标中，我们发现基于QA的评估比标准方法更能强烈预测真实世界的可用性。总之，这些发现强调了情境化的、以用户为中心的评估框架的重要性，这些框架超越了整体质量评分，并关注技术服务于谁以及服务得有多好。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了Ouvia——一个用于衡量真实通信场景中语音翻译用户感知可用性的以用户为中心的框架。通过在医疗和日常情境下对1,750多次交互的大规模研究，研究发现现代语音翻译系统的可用性仅达到约一半，且在不同人口统计学群体中存在明显差距，同时证明基于QA的评估方法是现实可用性的更强预测指标。
AI.keywords: 语音翻译, 可用性评估, 用户中心, 真实世界通信, QA评估
AI.comments: 该论文跳出了传统脱离上下文的基准测试，创新性地关注真实场景下语音翻译的用户感知可用性，并通过大规模的多阶段研究揭示了现有翻译系统在人口统计学群体间的性能差异，对未来以用户为中心的AI评估体系具有重要启发意义。

title: Explain Like I'm 5 or Whatever I Choose: Evaluating the Potential for Interactive Complexity in Language Model Responses
summary: Given the increased use of large language models (LLMs) for reading and seeking information and the varying needs and backgrounds of users, direct manipulation of text can be a valuable mechanism for end-user control. However, enabling direct manipulation requires that models generate text consistent with user-requested changes. We focus on one such setting, manipulating the complexity of scientific information, and ask if models can generate multiple summaries along a continuum of text complexity that enable effective user selection and control. Through a within-subjects user study, we identify reliable complexity measures and a criterion for how models should conform to these measures. We evaluate five LLMs of different families, sizes, and reasoning abilities on $557$ scientific queries. We find that while models can vary complexity across responses, most changes remain inconsistent, with models shifting the complexity measures in the correct direction at most $33.67$% of the time.

title: STREAM: Stochastic Riemannian Flow Matching with Anisotropic Decoder for Digital Histopathology Image Generation
summary: Synthetic histopathology image generation addresses patient-privacy concerns and the growing data demands of foundation models. Existing state-of-the-art histopathology generative models use pretrained Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) as conditioning signals. We show this yields conditioning-dominated diversity: on TCGA-BRCA, 62-75% of their output diversity is attributable to the conditioning signal rather than the learned latent space, while de novo synthesis still requires a VFM at inference. We instead use histopathology VFMs as the latent space itself: their patch tokens are $\ell_2$-normalized on the unit hypersphere $\mathcal{S}^{d-1}$ with strong angular dominance and intrinsic curvature, motivating a Riemannian formulation. We present STREAM, the first framework to apply Riemannian flow matching in the histopathology domain, in two stages: 1) a bridge-type stochastic perturbation that establishes per-token rectifiability on $\mathcal{S}^{d-1}$ for training a Diffusion Transformer, and 2) a novel decoder training design whose noise covariance is anisotropic in the left-singular basis of the per-token tangent-projected velocity-field Jacobian, spending a large robustness budget on its low-response directions and a small one on its high-response directions. Across TCGA-BRCA and TCGA-COADREAD, STREAM achieves state-of-the-art gFID and ranks first on nearly all histopathology-specific metrics as well. Code and a public gallery of generated images are available at https://chokevin8.github.io/STREAM-Patho/.

AI.title_translation: STREAM：具有各向异性解码器的随机黎曼流匹配，用于数字组织病理图像生成
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为STREAM的新框架，用于生成数字组织病理图像。与以往依赖预训练视觉基础模型（VFMs）作为条件信号的方法不同，STREAM将VFMs的补丁标记直接用作潜在空间，并利用黎曼流匹配技术。该方法在两个阶段进行：1）建立每个标记在单位超球体上的可rectify性，用于训练扩散Transformer；2）设计了一种新颖的解码器训练方法，其噪声协方差在速度场雅可比矩阵的左奇异向量基中具有各向异性。STREAM在TCGA-BRCA和TCGA-COADREAD数据集上取得了最先进的gFID分数，并在大多数病理学特定指标上排名第一。
AI.motivation: 现有组织病理图像生成模型依赖预训练的视觉基础模型（VFMs）作为条件信号，导致生成图像的多样性主要受条件信号支配，而非学习到的潜在空间。此外，从头合成仍需在推理时使用VFMs。研究旨在利用VFMs的补丁标记作为潜在空间本身，以克服这些限制。
AI.method: STREAM框架采用两阶段黎曼流匹配方法：1) 建立补丁标记在单位超球体上的可rectify性，用于训练扩散Transformer；2) 设计一种新颖的解码器训练方法，其噪声协方差在速度场雅可比矩阵的左奇异向量基中具有各向异性，将大部分鲁棒性预算分配给低响应方向，少量分配给高响应方向。
AI.result: 在TCGA-BRCA和TCGA-COADREAD数据集上，STREAM在gFID指标上达到了最先进水平，并在几乎所有组织病理学特定指标上均排名第一。
AI.conclusion: STREAM是第一个在组织病理学领域应用黎曼流匹配的框架，通过将VFMs的补丁标记用作潜在空间并采用新颖的各向异性解码器设计，成功生成了高质量且多样化的组织病理图像，并在多个评估指标上超越了现有最先进方法。
AI.translation: 合成组织病理图像生成解决了患者隐私问题和基础模型日益增长的数据需求。现有的最先进的组织病理学生成模型使用预训练的视觉基础模型（VFMs）作为条件信号。我们表明，这会产生以条件为主的多样性：在TCGA-BRCA上，62-75%的输出多样性可归因于条件信号，而非学习到的潜在空间，而从头合成在推理时仍需要VFMs。我们转而使用组织病理学VFMs作为潜在空间本身：它们的补丁标记在单位超球体$\\mathcal{S}^{d-1}$上进行$\\ell_2$归一化，具有很强的角度优势和内在曲率，这启发了黎曼公式。我们提出了STREAM，这是第一个在组织病理学领域应用黎曼流匹配的框架，分两个阶段进行：1）一种桥式随机扰动，在$\\mathcal{S}^{d-1}$上建立每个标记的可rectify性，用于训练扩散Transformer，以及2）一种新颖的解码器训练设计，其噪声协方差在每个标记的切线投影速度场雅可比矩阵的左奇异向量基中是各向异性的，将大量的鲁棒性预算用于其低响应方向，将少量预算用于其高响应方向。在TCGA-BRCA和TCGA-COADREAD上，STREAM实现了最先进的gFID，并在几乎所有的组织病理学特定指标上均排名第一。代码和生成的图像公共图库可在https://chokevin8.github.io/STREAM-Patho/获取。
AI.summary: STREAM是一种新颖的组织病理图像生成框架，它将预训练视觉基础模型（VFMs）的补丁标记直接用作潜在空间，并采用黎曼流匹配技术。该方法通过两阶段过程（建立标记的可rectify性以训练扩散Transformer，以及设计各向异性噪声协方差的解码器）来克服现有方法的局限性。实验结果表明，STREAM在多个数据集和指标上均达到了最先进的性能。
AI.keywords: 组织病理图像生成, 黎曼流匹配, 视觉基础模型, 各向异性解码器, 扩散Transformer
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种创新的组织病理图像生成方法，通过利用黎曼流匹配和VFMs的潜在空间特性，有效解决了现有方法在多样性和推理需求方面的不足。各向异性解码器的设计尤为巧妙，能够更精细地控制生成过程。然而，黎曼流匹配的计算复杂度以及模型的可解释性仍是未来研究可以关注的方向。

title: HARP: Efficient Data Selection for Finetuning Large Language Models
summary: Finetuning data selection requires balancing two competing goals: selecting examples that improve the downstream objective, and doing so without repeatedly finetuning models. Train-free selectors are scalable but rely on proxies such as embedding similarity or clustering, which may not match the target objective. Train-based selectors better reflect downstream utility through gradient signals, subset evaluation, or Shapley attribution, but require many costly train-evaluate iterations. We propose Hierarchical Active Region Pruning (HARP), an efficient train-based selector that preserves downstream alignment while reducing selection cost. HARP organizes the training pool into a node-leaf hierarchy, evaluates only representative leaves, and infers unmeasured utilities with empirical Bayes posteriors. It then selects data using two complementary envelopes: HARP-C, which conservatively controls redundancy, and HARP-E, which additively rewards complementary regions. We theoretically show that, under local smoothness and bounded estimation error, HARP controls selection error while reducing train-evaluate cost. Across 3 base models, 3 finetuning datasets, and 4 reasoning benchmarks (36 settings), HARP variants achieve the highest accuracy among ranked methods in 23 settings and obtain 36-setting mean accuracies of 64.2 and 63.5, respectively, compared with 59.3 for the strongest baseline, NICE. HARP-C trains on roughly 9x fewer examples than the budgeted baselines and 75x fewer than full finetuning, combining higher mean accuracy with a smaller mean training-set size than every ranked baseline.

AI.title_translation: HARP：高效选择用于微调大型语言模型的数据
AI.tldr: HARP是一种高效的基于训练的数据选择方法，通过构建层级结构、评估代表性叶节点并使用经验贝叶斯后验推断未测量效用，来平衡下游目标和降低选择成本。它包含HARP-C（控制冗余）和HARP-E（奖励互补区域）两种变体，能在保证选择误差可控的同时，显著减少训练评估成本。实验表明，HARP在多项设置下均优于现有基线方法，并在准确性和训练集大小方面取得了更好的平衡。
AI.motivation: 在微调大型语言模型时，数据选择需要在提升下游目标和避免重复微调之间取得平衡。现有的训练无关选择器虽然可扩展，但依赖代理指标，可能与目标不符；而基于训练的选择器虽然能更好地反映下游效用，但需要多次耗时的训练评估迭代。
AI.method: HARP（Hierarchical Active Region Pruning）通过构建节点-叶层级结构来组织训练池，仅评估代表性的叶节点，并利用经验贝叶斯后验推断未测量的效用。它包含HARP-C（控制冗余）和HARP-E（奖励互补区域）两种变体来选择数据。
AI.result: 在3个基础模型、3个微调数据集和4个推理基准（共36个设置）的实验中，HARP变体在23个设置下取得了比排名方法更高的准确率，平均准确率为64.2和63.5，优于最强的基线NICE（59.3）。HARP-C的训练样本数量比预算基线少约9倍，比完全微调少75倍，同时实现了更高的平均准确率和更小的平均训练集大小。
AI.conclusion: HARP是一种高效的基于训练的数据选择方法，通过其层级结构和推断机制，能够在显著降低选择成本的同时，保持与下游目标的良好一致性，并在多项基准测试中取得了优于现有方法的性能。
AI.translation: 微调数据选择需要平衡两个相互竞争的目标：选择能够改进下游目标的样本，以及避免反复微调模型。训练无关的选择器具有可扩展性，但依赖于嵌入相似性或聚类等代理指标，这可能与目标不匹配。基于训练的选择器通过梯度信号、子集评估或Shapley归因等方式更好地反映下游效用，但需要多次昂贵的训练-评估迭代。我们提出了分层主动区域剪枝（HARP），一种高效的基于训练的选择器，它在保持下游一致性的同时降低了选择成本。HARP将训练池组织成一个节点-叶层级结构，仅评估代表性的叶节点，并使用经验贝叶斯后验推断未测量的效用。然后，它使用两种互补的包络线来选择数据：HARP-C，保守地控制冗余；HARP-E，加性地奖励互补区域。我们从理论上证明，在局部平滑和估计误差有界的情况下，HARP在控制选择误差的同时降低了训练-评估成本。在3个基础模型、3个微调数据集和4个推理基准（36个设置）的实验中，HARP变体在23个设置下取得了比排名方法更高的准确率，平均准确率为64.2和63.5，而最强的基线NICE为59.3。HARP-C的训练样本数量比预算基线少约9倍，比完全微调少75倍，同时其平均准确率和平均训练集大小均优于所有排名基线。
AI.summary: HARP是一种新颖的高效数据选择方法，旨在解决大型语言模型微调中的数据选择难题。该方法通过构建层级结构，并结合经验贝叶斯推断，有效地在保证下游任务性能的同时，大幅降低了训练和评估成本。HARP包含HARP-C和HARP-E两种变体，分别侧重于控制数据冗余和利用数据互补性，实验证明其在多项任务和模型上均表现优于现有基线方法。
AI.keywords: HARP, 数据选择, 大型语言模型, 微调, 经验贝叶斯
AI.comments: HARP方法在解决大型语言模型微调中的数据选择问题上展现了显著的创新性和实用性。通过引入层级结构和经验贝叶斯推断，它有效地平衡了选择效率和下游任务性能，这对于资源受限的场景尤为重要。理论分析和广泛的实验结果都支持其有效性。然而，其在不同模型架构和任务类型上的泛化能力，以及对层级结构和推断参数的敏感性，可能还需要进一步的研究。

title: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: Steering Vector Construction and Comprehensive Evaluation
summary: Activation steering (AS) has emerged as a popular inference-time technique for modulating the behavior of large language models (LLMs). AS modulates model behavior in a flexible and lightweight manner by injecting task-specific steering vectors (SVs) into intermediate activations. Meanwhile, recent work has identified emergent misalignment (EM) as an emerging safety concern, whereby finetuning on unsafe examples from a narrow task unexpectedly induces broadly unsafe behavior in unrelated domains. With the increasing popularity of AS, it is pressing yet under-explored to thoroughly investigate whether AS can induce EM. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive study of activation-steering-induced emergent misalignment. Specifically, (1) we identify a steering vector construction to confirm that SVs derived from a narrow task can indeed induce misalignment across broad unrelated domains. Qualitative measurement further reveals that AS-induced EM may pose more severe safety risks than finetuning-induced EM, i.e., AS elicits more actionable harmful responses with greater semantic coherence than those generated by finetuned models. (2) We characterize the properties of AS-induced EM by analyzing key steering-specific factors, including steering magnitude, the low-rank structure of the steering subspace, and the number of fine-tuning epochs used during steering-vector construction. (3) We evaluate the robustness and sensitivity of AS-induced EM across diverse model families, model scales, target tasks, and intervention layers. Our findings reveal activation steering as a significant yet underexamined source of emergent misalignment and provide an activation-space perspective on emergent misalignment and its safety risks.

AI.title_translation: 激活转向诱导涌现失准：转向向量构建与全面评估
AI.tldr: 激活转向（AS）通过注入任务特定的转向向量（SVs）来调节大型语言模型（LLMs）的行为。本研究旨在调查AS是否会像微调一样诱导涌现失准（EM）。研究结果表明，AS确实可以诱导跨领域失准，并且可能比微调更危险，因为它能产生更具可操作性的有害响应。研究还分析了导致AS诱导EM的因素，并评估了其在不同模型、任务和层上的鲁棒性，强调了AS作为涌现失准的一个重要来源。
AI.motivation: 随着激活转向（AS）在调节大型语言模型（LLMs）行为方面的日益普及，有必要深入研究AS是否会像微调一样诱导涌现失准（EM），这是一个新兴的安全问题。
AI.method: 本研究通过以下方式全面研究了激活转向诱导的涌现失准：1. 提出一种转向向量（SV）构建方法，以验证源自狭窄任务的SV是否能在广泛的不相关领域中诱导失准。2. 通过分析转向幅度、转向子空间的低秩结构以及用于构建转向向量的微调周期数等关键因素，来表征AS诱导的EM的特性。3. 评估AS诱导的EM在不同模型家族、模型规模、目标任务和干预层上的鲁棒性和敏感性。
AI.result: 研究确认，源自狭窄任务的转向向量（SVs）确实可以在广泛的不相关领域中诱导失准。定性测量表明，AS诱导的EM可能比微调诱导的EM带来更严重的安全风险，因为它能产生比微调模型更具可操作性且语义更连贯的有害响应。此外，研究还揭示了转向幅度、转向子空间的低秩结构以及用于构建转向向量的微调周期数是影响AS诱导EM的关键因素，并且AS诱导的EM在不同模型家族、模型规模、目标任务和干预层上表现出一定的鲁棒性和敏感性。
AI.conclusion: 激活转向（AS）是一种重要的、但尚未得到充分研究的涌现失准（EM）的来源。本研究提供了对涌现失准及其安全风险的激活空间视角，强调了AS在模型安全方面的潜在风险。
AI.translation: 激活转向（AS）已成为一种流行的推理时技术，用于调节大型语言模型（LLMs）的行为。AS通过将任务特定的转向向量（SVs）注入中间激活中，以灵活轻量的方式调节模型行为。与此同时，近期研究已将涌现失准（EM）确定为一种新兴的安全问题，即在狭窄任务的不安全示例上进行微调，会意外地在不相关的领域中诱导广泛的不安全行为。随着AS的日益普及，彻底研究AS是否会诱导EM变得紧迫但仍未得到充分探索。在本研究中，我们对激活转向诱导的涌现失准进行了全面的研究。具体而言，（1）我们确定了一种转向向量构建方法，以确认源自狭窄任务的SV确实可以在广泛的不相关领域中诱导失准。定性测量进一步揭示，AS诱导的EM可能比微调诱导的EM带来更严重的安全风险，即AS产生的有害响应比微调模型生成的响应更具可操作性，并且语义更连贯。（2）我们通过分析关键的转向特定因素，包括转向幅度、转向子空间的低秩结构以及用于转向向量构建的微调周期数，来表征AS诱导的EM的特性。（3）我们评估了AS诱导的EM在不同模型家族、模型规模、目标任务和干预层上的鲁棒性和敏感性。我们的研究结果揭示了激活转向作为涌现失准的一个重要但未被充分研究的来源，并为涌现失准及其安全风险提供了激活空间的视角。
AI.summary: 本研究全面评估了激活转向（AS）诱导涌现失准（EM）的可能性和影响。研究者提出了一种转向向量（SV）构建方法，并验证了AS确实能在不同领域诱导EM，且其产生的有害响应可能比微调更严重。此外，研究还深入分析了影响AS诱导EM的因素，并考察了其在多种模型和任务上的鲁棒性，强调了AS作为模型安全风险源的重要性。
AI.keywords: 激活转向,涌现失准,转向向量,大型语言模型,模型安全, emergent misalignment, activation steering, steering vector, large language models, model safety, LLMs, EM, AS, SVs, safety risks, finetuning, misalignment, harmful responses, semantic coherence, steering magnitude, low-rank structure, fine-tuning epochs, robustness, sensitivity, diverse model families, model scales, target tasks, intervention layers, activation-space perspective
AI.comments: 这项研究对于理解和应对大型语言模型（LLMs）的安全风险至关重要。它不仅揭示了激活转向（AS）可能带来的潜在危害，还提供了一种量化和分析这些风险的方法。研究结果强调了在开发和部署LLMs时，需要对AS技术及其可能产生的意外后果给予足够的重视。未来的研究可以进一步探索缓解AS诱导EM的策略，并将其应用于更广泛的模型和应用场景。

title: AgentWorld: A Data Factory for Training LLM Agents from Multi-Turn Interactions
comments: Accepted as a demonstration paper at ICDM 2026
summary: Training LLMs to act as capable agents requires learning from multi-turn interactions with environments. However, multi-turn interaction trajectories generated by heterogeneous agent runtimes are difficult to transform into structured, high-quality training data that training engines can readily consume. In this paper, we propose AgentWorld, a data factory that bridges heterogeneous agent runtimes and training engines through a Gateway Server and a Data Pool, reframing LLM agent training around a unified data lifecycle from interaction collection to training consumption. The Gateway Server captures multi-turn interactions through an LLM API proxy, while the Data Pool organizes them into standardized step records for curation and training. An interactive dashboard supports trajectory monitoring, step inspection, and data review. In our demonstration, users integrate ready-to-use white-box and black-box agents, trace and curate their interaction data across the pipeline, and extend the factory to new agents and datasets through lightweight configuration. Quantitative experiments across multiple datasets and RL methods demonstrate training support for different agent runtimes. AgentWorld provides a practical foundation for transforming heterogeneous multi-turn experience into training-ready data for LLM agents. Our code is available at https://github.com/AgentR1/Claw-R1 and the demonstration video can be found at link https://youtu.be/Pw47dAOw6B0.
comment: Accepted as a demonstration paper at ICDM 2026

title: SecureClaw: Clawing Back Control of LLM Agents
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (poster). Revised presentation and additional evaluation; 29 pages including appendices
summary: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents face two distinct security failures: unauthorized external actions and exposure of sensitive plaintext inside the runtime before any final output check can intervene. Existing defenses usually protect one boundary, either the planner/runtime or the point where external actions are executed, and therefore do not by themselves secure both surfaces. We present SecureClaw, a dual-boundary architecture that enforces authorization in a trusted executor and keeps raw protected data outside the LLM runtime. Sensitive reads pass through a trusted gateway that replaces raw values with reference IDs. In the evaluated deployment, the gateway also provides short planning summaries that deliberately release selected information, a process called declassification. Writes that change external state follow a PREVIEW$\rightarrow$COMMIT protocol in which only a trusted executor may execute the exact request authorized by policy. The runtime can still plan over summaries and reference IDs, but cannot directly resolve the IDs into secrets or perform side effects. Across the AgentDojo, AgentLeak, and Agent Security Bench (ASB) benchmarks, SecureClaw is the only defense we evaluate in a common harness that simultaneously retains usable task utility and achieves 0% attack success rate (ASR) on ASB, 0.64% ASR on AgentDojo, and 3.23% overall leak on AgentLeak's attacked parity lane, which measures final-output and internal-relay leakage. Code is available at https://github.com/ponyyuhan/SecureClaw.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (poster). Revised presentation and additional evaluation; 29 pages including appendices

AI.title_translation: 安全爪：夺回对大型语言模型代理的控制权
AI.tldr: SecureClaw通过双边界架构解决工具使用型LLM代理的安全问题，一个边界在可信执行器中强制执行授权，另一个边界将原始受保护数据保留在LLM运行时之外，从而防止未经授权的外部操作和敏感数据泄露。
AI.motivation: 现有的LLM代理防御措施通常只保护一个安全边界（规划器/运行时或外部操作执行点），无法同时解决未经授权的外部操作和运行时内部敏感明文暴露的安全问题。
AI.method: SecureClaw采用双边界架构。它使用一个可信网关来替换敏感数据的引用ID，并将规划摘要（declassification）提供给LLM运行时。写入操作遵循PREVIEW→COMMIT协议，只有可信执行器才能执行经策略授权的请求。LLM运行时只能处理摘要和引用ID，无法直接解析敏感信息或执行副作用。
AI.result: 在AgentDojo、AgentLeak和Agent Security Bench (ASB)基准测试中，SecureClaw在保持可用任务效用的同时，在ASB上实现了0%的攻击成功率（ASR），在AgentDojo上实现了0.64%的ASR，在AgentLeak的攻击奇偶校验车道上实现了3.23%的总泄露率。
AI.conclusion: SecureClaw是一种创新的双边界架构，能够同时解决LLM代理中的两个关键安全问题，并在多个基准测试中表现出卓越的安全性和任务效用。
AI.translation: 使用工具的大型语言模型（LLM）代理面临两种独特安全故障：未经授权的外部操作和敏感明文在任何最终输出检查干预之前暴露于运行时。现有防御措施通常只保护一个边界，即规划器/运行时或外部操作的执行点，因此它们本身不能同时保护两个面。我们提出了SecureClaw，一种双边界架构，它在可信执行器中强制执行授权，并将原始受保护数据保留在LLM运行时之外。敏感的读取通过一个可信网关，该网关用引用ID替换原始值。在评估的部署中，该网关还提供简短的规划摘要，故意发布选定的信息，这个过程称为解密（declassification）。改变外部状态的写入遵循PREVIEW$ightarrow$COMMIT协议，其中只有可信执行器可以执行策略授权的确切请求。运行时仍然可以基于摘要和引用ID进行规划，但无法直接解析ID为秘密信息或执行副作用。在AgentDojo、AgentLeak和Agent Security Bench (ASB)基准测试中，SecureClaw是我们评估的通用框架中唯一一种能够同时保持可用任务效用并实现ASB上0%攻击成功率（ASR）、AgentDojo上0.64% ASR以及衡量最终输出和内部中继泄露的AgentLeak攻击奇偶校验车道上3.23%总体泄露率的防御措施。代码可在https://github.com/ponyyuhan/SecureClaw获取。
AI.summary: SecureClaw是一种新的双边界安全架构，旨在解决使用工具的大型语言模型（LLM）代理面临的两种主要安全风险：未经授权的外部操作和敏感数据在运行时内部的泄露。它通过在可信执行器中强制执行授权，并将敏感数据（通过引用ID而非原始值）与LLM运行时隔离来实现这一目标。该方法在AgentDojo、AgentLeak和ASB等基准测试中得到了验证，结果显示SecureClaw在保持任务效用的同时，显著降低了攻击成功率和数据泄露。
AI.keywords: LLM代理安全, 双边界架构, 可信执行器, 数据泄露防护, 工具使用
AI.comments: SecureClaw通过引入双边界防御体系，有效解决了LLM代理在工具使用过程中面临的安全挑战。其创新的之处在于同时处理了外部操作授权和内部数据泄露问题，并通过引用ID和PREVIEW->COMMIT协议等机制，在保证LLM运行时功能的同时，极大地提升了安全性。该方法在多个基准测试中的优异表现，证明了其在实际应用中的潜力和有效性。然而，对于“declassification”过程中信息选择的策略和潜在的风险，以及在更复杂、更广泛的应用场景下的扩展性和鲁棒性，仍有待进一步研究和验证。

title: A Unifying Framework for Concept-Based Representational Similarity
summary: Learned representations across models and modalities often exhibit striking structural similarities, suggesting shared underlying concept decompositions. However, concept alignment remains poorly defined: existing approaches optimize different objectives under the same terminology, obscuring what is actually aligned. We propose a unifying framework that decomposes alignment along two axes: what is aligned (representations vs. concepts) and at what level (instance-wise vs. distributional). This induces four corresponding properties---instance-wise and distributional variants of translation and concept consistency---and reveals precisely which of these guarantees existing methods provide. We further introduce InterVenchA, an intervention-based benchmark that separately measures extraction quality, translation quality, and concept consistency---which we validate against human perception of concept alignment. Using this framework, we show that commonly assumed equivalences between alignment objectives fail in practice: optimizing one property does not reliably recover the others, and, on real embeddings, purely unsupervised objectives fail to recover meaningful instance-level alignment. As a constructive consequence, a model, the Coupled SAE (CoSAE), matches or exceeds specialized alignment methods such as crosscoders and Universal SAEs on their own target metrics, by jointly enforcing the properties identified by our framework without any architectural innovation. Moreover, as little as 1% paired data is sufficient to recover instance-level alignment when anchoring distributional objectives. Overall, concept alignment is fundamentally multi-objective, and progress requires treating it as such. Our framework and benchmark provide the means to define, measure, and compare concept alignment methods on this basis.

title: MARCH: Model-Assisted Reinforcement Learning for the Perceptive Control of Humanoids over Sparse Footholds
summary: Perceptive bipedal locomotion over sparse terrain remains a difficult challenge: model-based methods are precise but brittle to uncertainty, while model-free methods are robust but struggle to discover the precise, constrained motions required for safety-critical locomotion where small errors can cause catastrophic failures. We propose a model-assisted reinforcement learning (RL) framework that combines both perspectives in three steps: (1) generate a safe reference trajectory using simplified models; (2) train a privileged teacher policy guided by a control Lyapunov function (CLF) reward built around the safe reference trajectory; and (3) distill the teacher into a vision-based student policy. We show that this model-assistance procedure produces physically grounded locomotion, improving sample efficiency, reducing the need for a complex learning curriculum, and achieving smoother locomotion behavior alongside stepping stone performance comparable to model-free baselines. We validate our approach in simulation and demonstrate successful deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot navigating sparse footholds with lateral constraints.

title: P3D-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Parametric 3D Generation and Structural Reasoning
comments: 26 pages, including appendix. v4: optimized figure compression; content and results unchanged from v3. v3: updated model evaluations, fixed 100-case subsets per task, and revised score aggregation. Project page: https://spatiaos.github.io/projects/P3D-Bench/
summary: Multimodal large language models can write code to produce complex programs as well as use programs to do 3D modeling, which opens up a new avenue for 3D generation powered by their priors, world knowledge and reasoning. Yet existing benchmarks rarely evaluate 3D modeling through code. Such modeling demands more than runnable code: from a text or visual specification, a model must generate a parametric 3D program that is geometrically precise, semantically aligned and assembly-consistent. We introduce P3D-Bench, a benchmark for parametric 3D generation. Unlike a 3D mesh, a parametric 3D program exposes explicit dimensions, construction operations and part relations, revealing whether a model recovers a design's structure, not just its appearance. Under a unified protocol, P3D-Bench covers three task families (Text-to-3D, Image-to-3D and Assembly-3D) and scores each output for executability, geometric fidelity, topology, text-grounded constraints, multiview semantic alignment and part-level structure. We construct P3D-Dataset, comprising 400 text cases, 400 image cases, and 203 annotated assemblies. Our evaluation on 100 cases from each task family yields three key findings. First, multi-part generation is substantially more challenging than single-part modeling, with models struggling to compose individual parts into a coherent structure. Second, models can often recover the global shape and semantic identity of the target object, yet fail to reproduce the precise parametric geometry specified by the input. Third, part-level modeling remains weak on assemblies, where models recover neither the geometry of each part nor the right number of parts. These results position P3D-Bench as a benchmark for evaluating precise parametric geometry and part-level structure in parametric 3D generation.

title: Position: Hippocampal Explicit Memory Is the Cornerstone for AGI
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across various tasks, raising expectations for Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). This position paper argues that integrating explicit memory is the cornerstone for advancing LLMs toward AGI. The key reason is that the underlying learning mechanism of LLMs is highly analogous to human implicit memory. However, higher-order cognitive functions necessary for AGI, such as long-term strategic planning, metacognition, and symbolic reasoning, heavily rely on hippocampal explicit memory and cannot arise solely from implicit statistical learning. Drawing on findings from neuroscience, I advance this perspective and complement it with computational requirements for artificial explicit memory systems, hoping to foster further research and lay the groundwork for explicit memory integration.

title: When More Documents Hurt RAG: Measuring and Reducing Vector Search Dilution with Domain-Scoped Retrieval
comments: 19 pages, 5 figures, 20 tables. Preprint under review at ACL ARR October
summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) degrades when applied to large, heterogeneous document collections. In RAG systems, dense similarity becomes less discriminative, causing top-$k$ retrieval to return semantically similar but contextually incorrect chunks. We refer to this failure mode as vector search dilution. Even under hybrid dense+sparse retrieval, we first observed it in a deployed Wyoming Department of Transportation (WYDOT) system; in a controlled experiment, growing the corpus from 54 to 1,128 documents cut precision@10 by 63% and recall of the answer-bearing document by 23%. Similar patterns were observed in six other DOTs. To diagnose this issue, we introduce MASDR-RAG (Metadata-Scoped Domain Retrieval for RAG) as a controlled testbed over 200 human-validated queries, five LLM backbones, six public benchmark corpora, and two index stacks. In MASDR-RAG, domain scoping is the load-bearing component. We found hard partitioning to be unsafe, whereas training-free soft scoping is safe when the scope structure is real. Furthermore, we can discover these scopes without hand-curated metadata. However, multi-agent orchestration triggers a precision-faithfulness paradox that survives format controls, prompt controls, and blind human evaluation. Based on these varied outcomes, our practical recommendation is simple: soft-scope first, then perform a single synthesis call.
comment: 19 pages, 5 figures, 20 tables. Preprint under review at ACL ARR October

title: UGV-Conditioned Multi-UAV Informative Planning on a Shared Exposure Belief
summary: Safe ground navigation in large, threat-augmented environments requires aerial support that actively reduces the risks that a ground vehicle faces along its route. Existing aerial reconnaissance systems focus on mapping or covering the environment, but do not direct sensing toward regions that are most relevant for ground vehicle safety. In this paper, we address the problem of coordinating a team of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to improve the safety of an unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) navigating through unknown threat zones. A key aspect of our approach is a risk-averse shared exposure belief for UGV routing and a mission-conditioned UAV reward that directs sensing toward uncertain, exposure-relevant regions of the current UGV corridor. UAV observations update the shared belief online, allowing the UGV to replan around newly revealed threats while the evolving route in turn reshapes UAV sensing priorities. For multiple UAVs, we use region-conditioned spatial assignment to reduce redundant sensing. Simulation experiments show that our approach reduces cumulative UGV exposure by 38% compared with terrain-semantic replanning, and reduces redundant aerial coverage from 38.8% to 3.7% under our multi-UAV coordination scheme.

title: DIRECT: When and Where Should You Allocate Test-Time Compute in Embodied Planners?
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed as high-level planners for embodied agents, with an emerging strategy of scaling test-time compute to improve capability. However, we observe that doing so increases latency, token usage, and FLOPs while yielding uneven, often diminishing gains in downstream success, limiting where embodied agents can be deployed. We argue that choosing when and where to spend test-time compute is central to bringing frontier performance to the real world, and we can budget inference at the planning level. We introduce DIRECT, a routing framework that uses multimodal scene context to allocate compute at each step of a closed-loop agent, selecting a planner for every subtask, improving the success--cost Pareto frontier over fixed model selection. Across three dominant scaling axes, namely chain-of-thought depth, model size, and memory history, our experiments on VLABench and RoboMME show that test-time compute is not a uniform lever: different axes yield qualitatively distinct capability gains. We validate these insights on a physical Franka arm in a DROID setup spanning zero-shot manipulation and long-horizon chaining, where our router matches or exceeds a stronger model's success rate at up to 65% lower average latency. Ultimately, our results show that naively scaling test-time compute is wasteful, and DIRECT can provide frontier-level embodied planning at a fraction of the cost. Project page can be found at jadee-dao.github.io/direct/.

title: ProReviewer: Evidence-Driven Investigation for Scientific Peer Review
summary: Effective peer review requires adaptive investigation that responds to evidence emerging from each paper. Existing LLM-based reviewers largely organize the review process around predefined workflows, leaving limited scope for emerging evidence to reshape investigation. We propose ProReviewer, an evidence-driven review agent that formulates reviewing as a Markov Decision Process, with a structured review log forming the core of its state. At each step, the agent uses accumulated findings to decide what to inspect next and when to conclude. As new evidence emerges, it updates the log by revising claim statuses, resolving open questions, and recording new findings. Each point in the final review cites supporting log entries, making its judgments traceable to the recorded evidence. On 1,000 held-out ICLR 2026 papers, the trained 8B ProReviewer achieves the highest average score among all compared methods, including those built on a 397B model; human evaluators prefer its reviews over all baselines on three of four review-quality dimensions.

title: SPARC: Reliable Spatial Annotations from Robot Demonstrations at Scale
summary: This work introduces Spatial Annotations from Robot Demonstrations with Reliability Calibration (SPARC), a risk-aware framework that automatically labels robot demonstrations with structured spatial annotations and assigns each annotation a reliability score. Structured spatial annotations, such as bounding boxes, object trajectories, and manipulation phase labels, benefit a broad range of robotics applications from training grounded robot policies and embodied foundation models to motion planning and hierarchical task composition. Existing automated pipelines generate such annotations at scale but provide no reliable quality signal: detector confidence is poorly calibrated for annotation correctness, forcing a choice between accepting noisy labels or discarding useful samples. In contrast to existing automated pipelines, SPARC leverages the spatio-temporal structure inherent to robot tasks to generate a reliability signal, reducing noisy labels and retaining more useful samples. We further introduce Interaction-Aware Bench (IA-Bench), a benchmark that measures model accuracy in grounding the locations of interacted objects in robot demonstrations. On 1.7k human-annotated demonstrations spanning diverse embodiments and scenarios, SPARC significantly outperforms detection-only baselines in localization accuracy while retaining three times more samples at high-precision operating points. Our experiments demonstrate that models finetuned on our annotations achieve state-of-the-art results on object-grounding and pointing benchmarks among similarly sized models, while remaining competitive on broader spatial-reasoning suites without manually verified or annotated training data. Furthermore, policies trained on SPARC-generated annotations outperform baselines in cluttered, visually ambiguous real-world scenes. Code, data, and models are available at intuitive-robots.github.io/sparc-labeling.

title: An Empirical Study of Gemini 3 for Detecting Natural Language Test Smells in Manual Test Cases
summary: Manual testing, in which testers follow natural language instructions to validate system behavior, remains essential for uncovering issues that are difficult to capture with automation. However, manual test cases often contain test smells, quality issues such as ambiguity, redundancy, or missing checks that reduce reliability, maintainability, and reproducibility. Existing detection approaches largely depend on manually engineered rules and thus struggle to generalize and scale across heterogeneous test suites. In our previous work, we assessed the feasibility of using Small Language Models (SLMs) for test smell detection by evaluating GEMMA-3-4B, LLAMA-3.2-3B, and PHI-4-14B on test steps from 143 real-world Ubuntu test cases, covering seven smell types. PHI-4-14B achieved the best performance. In this article, we investigate whether a contemporary Large Language Model (GEMINI-3-PRO-PREVIEW) available at the time of the study can identify test smells in natural language manual test cases using a prompt-based, whole-test-case analysis strategy. Unlike approaches that analyze individual test steps in isolation, our approach evaluates complete test cases, enabling the model to consider relationships and dependencies among test steps. We evaluate the approach on 100 Ubuntu test cases covering seven test smell types and compare its performance against previously evaluated SLMs, including GEMMA-3-4B, LLAMA-3.2-3B, and PHI-4-14B. Our results show that GEMINI-3-PRO-PREVIEW outperforms the SLMs, while producing actionable explanations that can help practitioners revise manual test cases for greater clarity and consistency. We also find that test smells are pervasive in practice, with nearly one detected test smell per step on average, highlighting the need for scalable and automated quality support for manual testing artifacts.

title: Driving, Fast or Slow? Neuro-Symbolic Guidance for Motion Prediction in Multi-Modal Ground Mobility
summary: Accurate and interpretable motion prediction for heterogeneous traffic spaces, including pedestrians, bicycles, cars, and trucks, is essential for safe autonomous navigation. Nevertheless, state-of-the-art approaches remain predominantly black-box, lacking explicit encoding of the regulatory and behavioral constraints of real-world mobility. We propose Trajectory Compliance-Shaping (TraCS), a neuro-symbolic framework that augments existing black-box motion prediction backbones with interpretable and probabilistic first-order logic. To do so, TraCS employs an agentic code-generation pipeline to bridge the gap between natural-language descriptions of traffic regulations and probabilistic motion prediction. Furthermore, TraCS employs a reactive data-streaming inference engine that maintains and efficiently updates compliance landscapes as scenes evolve. To prevent TraCS from overconfidently steering the backbone's predictions in the wrong direction, we propose a neural confidence rating learned as a context-aware attenuation of the compliance signal. We demonstrate on the Argoverse 2 benchmark how TraCS consistently improves state-of-the-art prediction backbones, showing that probabilistic and symbolic compliance reasoning is a broadly applicable and computationally efficient complement to purely neural motion predictors.

title: Conormal Lower Bounds for Determinantal Complexity: Fermat Slices, Tight Bounds, and a Ceiling
comments: Substantially expanded. Adds the lower-bound side of the method, a smooth-slice criterion, a tight Theta(q^3) border bound for a VBP-complete path family, cubic bounds for VP- and VNP-complete homomorphism families, and a codimension principle
summary: The determinantal complexity of a polynomial $f$ is the smallest size of a matrix of affine linear forms whose determinant is $f$; the border version only asks for determinants converging to $f$. The polar method bounds these quantities from below by comparing an invariant of the hypersurface $V(f)$, such as the degree of its dual variety, with the number of solutions of a polynomial system built from a determinantal representation of $f$. We determine how far the method reaches. Lower bounds: if $f$ has a linear restriction to a form of degree $d$ in $N$ variables with smooth projective zero set, then the border determinantal complexity of $f$ is at least $(N-1)(d-1)/(4e)$. Setting the off-diagonal host entries to zero turns every homomorphism polynomial $\hom_{F,q}$ with a connected pattern $F$ into a Fermat polynomial, which gives the bound $(q-1)(|E(F)|-1)/(4e)$. For the VBP-complete path family $W_q$ this is tight: the border determinantal complexity of $W_q$ is $Θ(q^3)$. The same argument gives cubic bounds for natural VP- and VNP-complete families, and a bound in terms of the codimension of the singular locus of $V(f)$. A ceiling: the method, together with every refinement in a precisely defined class, cannot prove a lower bound larger than $O(dN)$ for any polynomial of degree $d$ in $N$ variables. The proof computes the solution count exactly, as the degree of the dual of a generic determinantal hypersurface, and shows that every characteristic-cycle invariant of a hypersurface of degree $d$ is at most $8(d-1)^{N-1}+8N$. For the $n\times n$ permanent the ceiling is $O(n^3)$; for the power sum $x_1^N+\dots+x_N^N$ it is $(1+o(1))N^2/(4e)$, matching the known lower bound.

title: DynFS-MoE: Dynamic Functional-Structural Mixture-of-Experts for Post-Traumatic Epilepsy Diagnosis
summary: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a severe complication of traumatic brain injury (TBI). Yet, early identification remains challenging due to the complex structural and functional alterations it induces in the brain. To address this, we propose a dynamic multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework that integrates functional and structural connectivity through time-aware functional-structural encoding and class-conditioned expert routing. Within this framework, modality-specific and cross-modal experts learn complementary representations, while a Modality-Class MoE (MCoE) module dynamically adjusts expert weights according to each classification objective. Experimental results across three binary classification tasks demonstrate that the framework consistently outperforms static fusion baselines, and high-interpretability analyses further reveal meaningful regions of interest (ROIs) interactions. This dynamic multimodal expert framework effectively captures class-dependent brain interaction patterns and provides an interpretable approach for PTE diagnosis and risk stratification.

title: HiMPO: Hindsight-Informed Memory Policy Optimization for Less-Entangled Credit in Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Long-horizon agents compress interaction histories into memory, but final outcomes entangle memory-writing credit with tool failures and reasoning errors. We propose HiMPO, a Hindsight-Informed Memory Policy Optimization framework that supplements trajectory-level reinforcement learning with memory-specific credit. For each update, HiMPO compares the target answer's log-likelihood under the previous and updated memories while holding the remaining pre-write context fixed. A soft gate based on group-relative hindsight relevance then weights the local utility advantage. Trajectory-level credit applies to all generated tokens; memory tokens additionally receive the auxiliary advantage. Across judge-based open-domain tasks and objective compressive-memory QA, HiMPO improves task performance while preserving compressed-context efficiency. On Local Wiki Search, it improves average F1 and exact match over MemPO by 2.6 and 2.2 percentage points, respectively. Controlled interventions and live memory-reversion studies provide evidence of reduced blame leakage and alignment between memory credit and behavioral effects. With the policy fixed, the credit estimator remains robust to the tested forms of target noise.

title: PROSE: Training-Free Egocentric Scene Registration with Vision-Language Models
summary: Registering two captures of the same indoor space taken at different times underpins persistent spatial memory for robots and AR systems, yet the realistic version of this task is egocentric and its most scalable form is RGB-only. Head-mounted cameras yield blurry, fast-moving, partially overlapping views from which dense geometry is hard to recover. Classical registration leans on exactly the clean point clouds this setting lacks, while learned scene-graph methods require a pre-built or annotated graph and a trained matcher that we find brittle under egocentric data. We take a different route, using a pretrained vision-language model as the source of both scene understanding and cross-scan matching. Our method, PROSE (Prompted Scene rEgistration), lifts each RGB sequence into an object-level 3D scene graph using off-the-shelf foundation models for geometry, segmentation, and language, then prompts the same VLM to match object instances across the two RGB sequences. To make this matching tractable and reliable, we leverage object heights as a prior and verify each proposed match with a paired same/different query, then solve for the rigid transform by hypothesizing a candidate per matched object and selecting the one with the strongest geometric consensus. PROSE adds no learned parameters and requires no depth sensor, training, or annotated graph. On the egocentric Aria Digital Twin and Aria Everyday Activities benchmarks, it outperforms both geometric and learned scene-graph baselines in registration accuracy, on ground-truth and RGB-reconstructed point clouds alike, and the scene graph it produces transfers directly to downstream tasks.

title: Misinformation Propagation in Benign Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) are credited with solving complex problems, yet their agents routinely act on context that may be false. Prior work shows single LLMs are swayed by false context, and MAS can be compromised by adversarial agents persuading peers. We study the benign case: agents follow one protocol, none intends to deceive, but some read a misleading passage. We study it with MINT, 10,278 LLM-written misinformation passages in eight styles, testing three open-weight models on commonsense reasoning, knowledge QA, and moral judgment. A relevant false passage costs a single agent 0.12-0.43 accuracy; irrelevant or content-free passages typically cost at most 0.06. Debate looks robust because uninformed agents outnumber misinformed ones. With one of three misinformed, it is no better than choosing the majority over equally exposed independent samples. Interaction helps only with a misinformed majority, recovering up to 0.24 accuracy over voting (0.29 under consensus). A one-sentence unreliability warning recovers up to 0.18 accuracy under voting (0.28 under consensus), at no significant cost under voting when context is true. Robustness should be judged against exposure-matched baselines, with prompt-level skepticism as cheap first defense.

title: DEEPRUBRIC: Evidence-Tree Rubric Supervision for Efficient Reinforcement Learning of Deep Research Agents
summary: Deep research agents synthesize long-form reports by searching and reasoning over retrieved evidence. Reinforcement learning with rubric-based rewards improves these agents by optimizing them against checkable criteria that translate report quality into reward signals, but its efficiency depends on whether those criteria reliably capture the task scope and evidence needs. Most existing studies ask an LLM to generate rubrics for a given query, but when the model fails to infer the underlying information needs, the generated rubrics may be incomplete and reduce RL efficiency. To obtain more reliable query--rubric supervision, we introduce DeepRubric, a data construction framework that reverses this process: instead of inferring evaluation criteria for a given query, it first determines what an evidence-backed report should be evaluated on and then synthesizes aligned query--rubric pairs from those evaluation targets. Starting from a sampled seed topic, DeepRubric builds an evidence tree by recursively expanding evidence-backed sub-questions, whose leaves serve as atomic and verifiable evaluation targets. It then uses the evidence tree to synthesize the training query and rubrics, ensuring that the reward evaluates exactly the information requested by the query. Using DeepRubric, we construct 9K query--rubric supervision examples and train DeepRubric-8B with rubric-based GRPO, achieving comparable performance to prior open state-of-the-art deep research models across three benchmarks with roughly 13x fewer RL GPU-hours.

title: Reference-Space Reuse for Steady and Transient State-Constrained Conjugate Heat Transfer
summary: Repeated thermal optimization must enforce local temperature limits while solving linear systems whose unknowns change as the constraints activate and release. Zero-extension transfer, which carries correction vectors from one inactive set to the next, assigns zero to the degrees of freedom that a constraint has just released. We construct a spectral reference on the full state domain before optimization and restrict it directly to the current inactive set at each update, so the coarse correction receives reference entries at every released degree of freedom. Spatial and space--time constructions cover steady and transient conjugate heat transfer with prescribed fluid velocity, and a restriction-residual identity yields alignment and deflated-convergence bounds under stated rank and spectral-separation assumptions. In the primary comparisons on body-fitted transformer and bore-in-block models, the resulting reference deflation reduces the median complete optimization time relative to the tested iterative alternatives on the same graphics processor. Complete time includes reference construction. Matched transfer experiments connect the improvement to the reference information retained at released constraints. The lower cost persists on refined Cartesian and bore-in-block meshes, on space--time trajectories and over sequences with changing loads and query order; the margin narrows, and eventually reverses, as a trajectory gains time slabs at a fixed horizon. Full-domain reference retention thus supports repeated evaluation of temperature-constrained heat inputs in engineering thermal models.

title: BACC: Budget-Aware Calibration and Control for Horizontal Autoscaling
summary: Cloud services must continuously adapt replica counts to fluctuating demand while respecting fixed-period reliability budgets. Many horizontal autoscalers either react to instantaneous utilization or provision against a fixed predictive risk target. These policies do not explicitly account for how much of the period-level violation budget has already been consumed, so they can be overly conservative when the budget is healthy and insufficiently conservative when the budget is being depleted. We present BACC, a model-agnostic framework for budget-aware horizontal autoscaling. BACC separates three concerns that are often entangled in prior systems: workload prediction, online uncertainty calibration, and budget-paced capacity control. It wraps an arbitrary forecaster with Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI) to calibrate workload uncertainty online, then uses a proportional--integral controller to adjust provisioning aggressiveness based on the observed pace of budget consumption. We instantiate BACC for CPU-threshold-based horizontal autoscaling in Kubernetes and evaluate it through trace-driven simulation and cluster replay experiments. Across five Azure Functions traces, three compliance levels, and two forecasting backends, BACC tracks the requested violation target closely, achieving mean absolute compliance gaps of 0.44 and 0.42 percentage points with ARIMA and Chronos, respectively. The Kubernetes experiments further show that the same controller improves CPU-threshold compliance over native HPA under deployment effects such as measurement delay and replica readiness.

title: PoLAR: Factorizing Extent and Mode in Latent Actions for Robot Policy Learning
comments: Project Page: https://joon-stack.github.io/PoLAR, Accepted to CoRL 2026
summary: Robot actions vary in both extent and mode: how much change they produce and what kind of change they produce. A latent action space that reflects this structure may make it easier for downstream policies to map latent actions to robot actions. However, existing latent action methods typically rely on visual reconstruction from observation pairs without explicitly encouraging such structure. We introduce Polar Latent Actions with Radial structure (PoLAR), which imposes a radial-direction structure on latent actions, encouraging radius to encode transition extent and direction to retain transition mode. PoLAR uses temporal offsets between observations as a weak proxy for transition extent, encouraging transitions with larger offsets to occupy larger radii. We instantiate this structure in hyperbolic space, whose expanding volume with radius offers a natural fit for more diverse transition modes at larger extents. Across in-task and large-scale pretraining settings, PoLAR improves downstream policy performance in simulation and real-world robot experiments, outperforming latent action baselines and strong pretrained VLAs. These results suggest that structuring latent actions by extent and mode helps transfer visual pretraining to robot policy learning.
comment: Project Page: https://joon-stack.github.io/PoLAR, Accepted to CoRL 2026

title: X-Safe: Embodiment-Agnostic Safeguarding for Robot Arm Manipulation Policies via Action Masking
summary: Ensuring safety of learning-enabled robotic manipulation across diverse embodiments and tasks still requires significant manual engineering. For collision avoidance, existing approaches typically rely on embodiment-specific learned safety approximations or simplified robot models together with stopping-based fallback controllers that compromise performance. In this paper, we propose an embodiment-agnostic safeguarding approach, X-Safe, which provides formal probabilistic guarantees for collision avoidance without model simplifications or learned safety functions. By operating in the configuration space, our safeguarding method works with different types of robot policies. X-Safe reasons locally around the current configuration to establish safe regions and uses action masking to restrict the policy's support to these safe regions. We demonstrate X-Safe on two embodiments and three policies, both in simulation and on hardware. We observe less than half of the performance degradation compared to state-of-the-art safeguarding, and empirically corroborate our formal collision avoidance guarantees.

title: Supporting Tutors in the Gig Economy with Automated Feedback: A Case Study on Ringle
summary: The rise of online tutoring platforms in the gig economy has made education more scalable, flexible, and on-demand. These platforms rely on learner evaluations as the primary feedback for tutors and platforms. However, such feedback offers limited guidance for tutors' improvement and makes it difficult to monitor tutor quality at scale. To this end, we explored AI-powered automated feedback and how tutors perceive and respond to it. We deployed a research probe on Ringle, a popular online English tutoring platform, that analyzed tutors' lessons and provided automated feedback. We then surveyed 36 tutors about their experience. Our findings reveal that while tutors perceived automated feedback more negatively than learner feedback, they found it useful for self-monitoring and understanding platform expectations, though discrepancies between them often caused confusion. Based on these insights, we propose design considerations for feedback systems for online educational gig platforms.

title: 4DVLT: Dynamic Scene Understanding with Worldline-Centered Vision-Language Tracking
summary: Language-guided dynamic scene understanding requires identifying one physical entity across time, metric 3D space, and multiple viewpoints, a setting not captured by current multimodal reasoning or tracking paradigms. We introduce 4DVLT, an offline calibrated multi-view task that unifies grounding with metric 3D and synchronized 2D tracking through a worldline binding identity, motion, visibility, and observations. We construct Instruct-4D, with 129.4K QA pairs, 64.7K targets, 851 scenes, and 9 reasoning types, and propose 4DTrack for query-conditioned inference over a 4D state graph. 4DTrack reaches 55.18 WQS, exceeding the strongest adapted VLT baseline by 33.01 points while improving grounding and trajectory quality. The project page is available at https://github.com/mikubaka88/4DVLT.

title: G$^3$VLA: Geometric Inductive Bias for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have rapidly advanced generalist robot manipulation by harnessing the semantic knowledge of pretrained vision-language backbones. However, their visual representations are typically grounded in 2D image coordinates rather than calibrated camera geometry. This limitation is especially pronounced in multi-camera systems, where views are coupled by known intrinsics and extrinsics but processed as independent images. We propose G$^3$VLA, a camera-aware geometric module that injects calibrated structure into the visual-token stream of a pretrained VLA without altering its action space or original action-learning objective. G$^3$VLA combines intrinsic-conditioned ray embeddings, projective positional encoding (PRoPE), and bidirectional cross-view fusion to establish geometrically consistent representations across camera views. Geometric supervision is provided by ground-truth point maps or confidence-gated $π^3$X teacher predictions, enabling training without depth sensors or manual geometric annotations. On $π_0$, G$^3$VLA consistently improves performance on LIBERO and RoboCasa24 under both supervision regimes, while ground-truth supervision improves five-task RoboTwin2.0 averages with three cameras. Experiments on camera-shifted LIBERO-Goal and real robots demonstrate improved robustness to unseen camera viewpoints. Controlled calibration studies across $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$ show that these gains depend on correct camera geometry while remaining stable under mild calibration perturbations. These results demonstrate that grounding VLA visual tokens in calibrated camera geometry provides a simple and general mechanism for improving geometric consistency, multi-view reasoning, and viewpoint robustness in pretrained robot policies.

title: Geological text descriptions in ill-posed inverse problems: insights from learned hydraulic-conductivity inversion
summary: Hydraulic-conductivity inversion is ill posed: even complete head observations can leave structural ambiguity. Geological text descriptions can supply additional information about subsurface structure to constrain reconstruction. However, it remains unclear when descriptions improve reconstruction and how solvers use their stated content. We examine these questions in learned inversion using a synthetic Darcy-flow dataset with idealised descriptions, varying observation density and flow direction. After sparse-observation training, descriptions can improve reconstruction over models trained without them when observations leave structural ambiguity, though gains vary across conditions and runs. Instance-specific content can improve reconstruction beyond field-type information. Editing this content shifts reconstructions toward the stated geometry of selected features, less strongly as observations become more informative about those features. We do not establish a reconstruction advantage of text over numerical inputs encoding the same geological information. Finally, we discuss how this complementarity could guide the joint design of measurements and geological knowledge acquisition in site investigations.

title: From Clicks to Intent: Cross-Platform Session Embeddings with LLM-Distilled Taxonomy for Financial Services Recommendations
comments: Dianjing Fan and Yao Li equally contributed to this work. 7 pages, 1 figure
summary: Sequential user behavior modeling is widely adopted in industrial recommender systems; however, significant gaps remain in financial services, where pre-login web interactions and authenticated in-app experiences differ drastically. Specifically, pre-login web users typically explore new products, whereas logged-in app users focus on account servicing. Due to the challenge of cross-channel entity resolution (e.g., matching anonymous web sessions to authenticated mobile accounts), web-based intent signals remain underutilized for post-authentication personalization. Existing methods for capturing web-based intent are often ad-hoc and narrow, lacking the flexibility to support both quantitative downstream recommendations and qualitative understanding at scale. In this work, we propose a scalable and dual-purpose intent prediction framework for web-based interactions and demonstrate its applicability for personalization. Our approach transforms raw web clickstreams into two outputs: a self-supervised Transformer encodes multi-modal clickstreams into a compact session embedding, while an LLM-based taxonomy generation and distillation pipeline produces interpretable intent labels. Our system demonstrates that self-supervised clickstream representations combined with LLM-distilled taxonomies can jointly serve quantitative tasks and qualitative understanding in production: on the mobile homepage tile ranking task, the session embedding improves macro Recall@1 by 1.88% and reduces Log Loss by 13.38% over production baselines. On the user conversion prediction task, the embedding outperforms the LLM labels by 4.3% on micro F1, while the distillation layer delivers interpretable labels at ultra-low latency with only a 7% performance drop.
